body.text: Abhidharmasamuccaya
body.translated_text: <s>Abhidharmasamuccaya</s> (Compendium of <s>Abhidharma</s>)

body.text: namo buddhāya
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!

body.text: [atha mūlavastuni tridharmaparicchedaḥ prathamaḥ /]
body.translated_text: [Now, the First Chapter: Determination of the Three <s>Dharmas</s> (Doctrinal Categories) in the Fundamental Topics.]

children.translated_text: The three <s>dharmas</s>: inclusion, association, and succession, as well as characteristics;
in the ascertainment: the <s>dharmas</s> of truth, attainment, and discussion as well.
How many, on what basis, adoption, establishment, and characteristics;
conformity, meaning, illustrations, and distinctions should be known in the compendium.

body.text: skandhā dhātava āyatanāni ca kati / skandhāḥ pañca / rūpaskandho vedanāskandhaḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ saṃskāraskandho vijñānaskandhaśca // dhātavo 'ṣṭādaśa / cakṣurdhātū rūpadhātuścakṣurvijñānadhātuḥ śrotradhātuḥ śabdadhātuḥ śrotravijñānadhāturghrāṇadhāturgandhadhāturghrāṇavijñānadhāturjivhādhātū rasadhāturjivhāvijñānadhātuḥ kāyadhātuḥ spraṣṭavyadhātuḥ kāyavijñānadhāturmanodhāturdharmadhāturmanovijñānadhātuśca // āyatanāni dvadaśa / cakṣurāyatanaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ śrotrāyatanaṃ śabdāyatanaṃ ghrāṇāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ jivhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ kāyāyatanaṃ spraṣṭavyāyatanaṃ manaāyatanaṃ dharmāyatanaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: How many are the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases)? The <s>skandhas</s> are five: the <s>rūpa-skandha</s> (aggregate of form), the <s>vedanā-skandha</s> (aggregate of feeling), the <s>saṃjñā-skandha</s> (aggregate of perception), the <s>saṃskāra-skandha</s> (aggregate of volitional formations), and the <s>vijñāna-skandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness). The <s>dhātus</s> are eighteen: the eye-element (<s>cakṣur-dhātu</s>), form-element (<s>rūpa-dhātu</s>), eye-consciousness-element (<s>cakṣur-vijñāna-dhātu</s>), ear-element (<s>śrotra-dhātu</s>), sound-element (<s>śabda-dhātu</s>), ear-consciousness-element (<s>śrotra-vijñāna-dhātu</s>), nose-element (<s>ghrāṇa-dhātu</s>), smell-element (<s>gandha-dhātu</s>), nose-consciousness-element (<s>ghrāṇa-vijñāna-dhātu</s>), tongue-element (<s>jivhā-dhātu</s>), taste-element (<s>rasa-dhātu</s>), tongue-consciousness-element (<s>jivhā-vijñāna-dhātu</s>), body-element (<s>kāya-dhātu</s>), tangible-element (<s>spraṣṭavya-dhātu</s>), body-consciousness-element (<s>kāya-vijñāna-dhātu</s>), mind-element (<s>mano-dhātu</s>), <s>dharma</s>-element (<s>dharma-dhātu</s>), and mind-consciousness-element (<s>mano-vijñāna-dhātu</s>). The <s>āyatanas</s> are twelve: the eye-base (<s>cakṣur-āyatana</s>), form-base (<s>rūpa-āyatana</s>), ear-base (<s>śrotra-āyatana</s>), sound-base (<s>śabda-āyatana</s>), nose-base (<s>ghrāṇa-āyatana</s>), smell-base (<s>gandha-āyatana</s>), tongue-base (<s>jivhā-āyatana</s>), taste-base (<s>rasa-āyatana</s>), body-base (<s>kāya-āyatana</s>), tangible-base (<s>spraṣṭavya-āyatana</s>), mind-base (<s>mana-āyatana</s>), and <s>dharma</s>-base (<s>dharma-āyatana</s>).

body.text: kimupādāya skandhāḥ pañcaiva / paṃcākārātmavastūdbhāvanatāmupādāya / saparigrahadehātmavastu upabhogātmavastu abhilāpātmavastu sarvadharmādharmābhisaṃskārātmavastu (

children.translated_text: Abhidh-s 2

children.text: ) tadāśrayātmasvastu copādāya // kimupādāya dhātovo 'ṣṭādaśaiva / dvābhyāṃ dehaparigrahābhyāmatītavarttamānaṣaḍākāropabhogadhāraṇatāmupādāya // kimupādāyāyatanāni dvādaśaiva / dvābhyāṃ dehaparigrahābhyāmanāgataṣaḍākāropabhogāyadvāratāmupādāya //
children.translated_text: and the essential reality that is the support of those. On what basis are the <s>dhātus</s> exactly eighteen? On the basis of maintaining the enjoyment of the six modes in past and present, through the two [types of] appropriation of the body. On what basis are the <s>āyatanas</s> exactly twelve? On the basis of being the gateway to future enjoyment of the six modes, through the two [types of] appropriation of the body.

body.translated_text: On what basis are the <s>skandhas</s> exactly five? On the basis of the manifestation of the essential reality (<s>ātmavastu</s>) in five aspects: the essential reality of possession of the body (<s>saparigraha-deha</s>), the essential reality of enjoyment (<s>upabhoga</s>), the essential reality of verbal designation (<s>abhilāpa</s>), the essential reality of the formations of all meritorious and non-meritorious <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarva-dharma-adharma-abhisaṃskāra</s>),

body.text: kasmāt skandhā upādānamityucyante / upādānena sahitatvāt skandhā upādānami tyucyante / upādānaṃ katamat / skandheṣu cchando rāgaśca / kasmāt / ḥcchando rāgaścopādānamityucyate / anāgatavarttamānaskandhānāmabhinirvarttanato 'parihārataśca / anāgate 'bhilāṣād varttamāne 'dhāvasānācca cchando rāgaścopādānamityucyate / kasmād dhātava āyatanāni ca sopādānadharmā ityucyante / tatra skandhavannirddeśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Why are the <s>skandhas</s> called <s>upādāna-skandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging)? Because they are accompanied by clinging (<s>upādāna</s>), the <s>skandhas</s> are called aggregates of clinging. What is clinging? Desire (<s>chanda</s>) and passion (<s>rāga</s>) regarding the <s>skandhas</s>. Why? Why are desire and passion called clinging? Because of the production and non-abandonment of future and present <s>skandhas</s>. Because of longing for the future and because of running after the present, desire and passion are called clinging. Why are the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s> also called <s>dharmas</s> with clinging (<s>sopādāna</s>)? There, the explanation is as for the <s>skandhas</s>.

body.text: kiṃlakṣaṇaṃ rūpam / rūpaṇa lakṣaṇaṃ rūpam / tad dvividham / sparśena rūpaṇaṃ pradeśena rūpaṇaṃ ca / sparśena rūpaṇaṃ katamat / karacaraṇapāṣāṇaśasradaṇḍaśītoṣṇakṣutpipāsāmaśakadaṃśasarpavṛścikādīnāṃ sparśena vyābādhanam / pradeśena rūpaṇaṃ katamat / deśena rūpaṇa midaṃ cedaṃ ca rūpamevaṃ caivaṃ ca rūpamiti praṇihitāpraṇihitacetovitarkeṇa pratibimbacitrīkāratā // kiṃlakṣaṇā vedanā / anubhavalakṣaṇā vedanā / nānāvidhānāṃ śubhaśubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaṃ pratyanubhavantyanenetyanubhavaḥ // kiṃlakṣaṇā saṃjñā / saṃjānanālakṣaṇā saṃjñā / saṃjñā nānādharmapratibimbodgrahaṇa (svabhāvā) yayā draṣṭaśrutamatavijñātānarthān vyavaharati // kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ saṃskāraḥ / abhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaḥ saṃskāraḥ / saṃskārabhisaṃskāra (svabhāvo) yena kuśalākuśalāvyakṛteṣu pakṣeṣu cittaṃ prerayati / kiṃlakṣaṇaṃ (

children.translated_text: Abhidh-s 3

children.text: ) vijñānam / vijānanālakṣaṇaṃ vijñānam / vijñānaṃ yena rūpaśabdagandharasasparśadharmān nānā viṣayān vijānāti //
children.translated_text: <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)? <s>Vijñāna</s> is characterized by discriminating (<s>vijānana</s>). <s>Vijñāna</s> is that by which one discriminates the various objects: form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and <s>dharmas</s>.

body.translated_text: What is the characteristic of <s>rūpa</s> (form)? <s>Rūpa</s> is characterized by being molded (<s>rūpaṇa</s>). It is twofold: molding by contact and molding by spatial location. What is molding by contact? It is the impairment caused by the contact of hands, feet, stones, weapons, sticks, cold, heat, hunger, thirst, gnats, gadflies, snakes, scorpions, and the like. What is molding by spatial location? The diversification through mental reflection, whether directed or undirected, [regarding] images in a location — "this form and that form, such form and such form." What is the characteristic of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling)? <s>Vedanā</s> is characterized by experiencing (<s>anubhava</s>). Experience is that by which one experiences the fruition and ripening of various wholesome and unwholesome <s>karmas</s> (actions). What is the characteristic of <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception)? <s>Saṃjñā</s> is characterized by apprehending (<s>saṃjānana</s>). <s>Saṃjñā</s> has the nature of grasping the images of various <s>dharmas</s>, by which one designates things as seen, heard, thought, or cognized. What is the characteristic of <s>saṃskāra</s> (volitional formation)? <s>Saṃskāra</s> is characterized by conditioning (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>). <s>Saṃskāra</s> has the nature of conditioning, by which the mind is impelled toward the wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate categories. What is the characteristic of

body.text: cakṣurdhātuḥ kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ / yena cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭavān paśyati yacca tasya bījamupacitamālayavijñānaṃ taccakṣuḥ // yathā cakṣurdhātulakṣaṇaṃ tathā śrotraghrāṇajihyakāyamanodhātūnāmapi lakṣaṇāni / rūpadhātuḥ kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ / rūpaṃ yaccakṣuṣā dṛṣṭaṃ dṛśyate ca yacca tatra cakṣurdhātorādhipatyaṃ tadrūpadhātu lakṣaṇam / yathā rūpadhātu lakṣaṇaṃ tathā śabdagandharasasparśadharmadhātūnāmapi lakṣaṇāni / cakṣūrvijñānadhātuḥ kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ / cakṣurāśrayā rūpālambanā rūpaprativijñaptiḥ yacca tasya bījamupacitaṃ / vipākālayavijñānaṃ taccakṣurvijñānadhātulakṣaṇam // yathā cakṣurvijñānadhātulakṣaṇaṃ tathā śrotraghrāṇajivhākāyamanovijñānadhātūnāmapi lakṣaṇāni //
body.translated_text: What is the characteristic of the eye-element (<s>cakṣur-dhātu</s>)? The eye by which one has seen and sees forms, together with its seed accumulated in the <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) — that is the eye. Just as the characteristic of the eye-element, so too are the characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-elements. What is the characteristic of the form-element (<s>rūpa-dhātu</s>)? Form that has been seen and is seen by the eye, together with the sovereignty of the eye-element over it — that is the characteristic of the form-element. Just as the characteristic of the form-element, so too are the characteristics of the sound-, smell-, taste-, tangible-, and <s>dharma</s>-elements. What is the characteristic of the eye-consciousness-element (<s>cakṣur-vijñāna-dhātu</s>)? The cognition of form that depends on the eye and takes form as its object, together with its accumulated seed — the ripening <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) — that is the characteristic of the eye-consciousness-element. Just as the characteristic of the eye-consciousness-element, so too are the characteristics of the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness-elements.

body.text: āyatanaṃ kiṃlakṣaṇam / dhātuvad yathāyogaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: What is the characteristic of an <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base)? It should be understood as for the <s>dhātus</s>, with appropriate adaptations.

body.text: rūpaskandhavyavasthānaṃ katamat / yatkiṃcidrūpaṃ sarvaṃ taccatvāri mahābhūtāni catvāri ca mahābhūtānyupādāya // katamāni catvāri mahābhūtāni / pṛthivīdhātuḥ abdhātuḥ tejodhātuḥ vāyudhātuśca // pṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ / kaṭhinatā // abdhātuḥ katamaḥ niṣyandatā // tejodhātuḥ katamaḥ / uṣṇatā // vāyudhātuḥ katamaḥ / kampanatā // upādāya rūpaṃ katamat / cakṣurindriyaṃ śrotrendriyaṃ ghrāṇendriyaṃ jivhendriyaṃ kāyendriyaṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyānāmekadeśo dharmāyatanasaṃgṛhītaṃ ca rūpam // cakṣurindriyaṃ katamat / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya cakṣuvijñānā śrayo rūpaprasādaḥ // śrotrendriyaṃ katamat / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya śrotravijñānāśrayo rūpaprasādaḥ / ghrāṇendriyaṃ katamat / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya ghrāṇavijñānāśrayo rūpaprasādaḥ // jivhendriyaṃ katamat / catvāri mahabhūtānyupādāya jivhāvijñānaśrayo rūpaprasādaḥ // kāyendriyaṃ katamat / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya kāyavijñānāśrayo rūpaprasādaḥ // rūpaṃ katamat / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya cakṣurindriyagocaro 'rthaḥ / yathā nīlaṃ pītaṃ lohitamavadātaṃ dīrghaṃ hrasvaṃ vṛttaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmamunnatamavanataṃ sātaṃ visātamātapaḥ chāyā āloko 'dhakāramabhraṃ dhūmo rajo mahikā ca / abhyavakāśarūpaṃ vijñaptirūpaṃ nabha ekavarṇaṃ rūpam // tat (

children.translated_text: Abhidh-s 4

children.text: ) punastridhā / śobhanamaśobhanamubhayaviparītaṃ ca // śabdaḥ katamaḥ / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya śrotrendriyabrāhyo 'rthaḥ / manojño vā amanojño vā ubhayaviparīto vā / upāttamahābhūtahetuko vā anupāttamahābhūtahetuko vā tadubhayo bālokaprasiddho vā siddhopanīto vā parikalpito vā āryairdeśito vā tīrthaidaśito vā / gandhaḥ katamaḥ / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya ghrāṇendriyagrāhyo 'rthaḥ / yathā surabhirasurabhiḥ samagandhaḥ sahajagandhaḥ sāṃyogikagandhaḥ pāriṇāmikagandhaśca // rasaḥ katama / catvāri mahābhūtāmyupādāya jivhendriyabrāhyo 'rthaḥ / tikto 'mlo madhuraḥ kaṭuko lavaṇaḥ kaṣāyaśca / manojño vā amanojño vā ubhayaviparīto vā sahajo vā sāṃyogiko vā pāriṇāmiko vā // spraṣṭavyaikadeśaḥ katamaḥ / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya kāyendriya grāhyo 'rthaḥ / ślakṣṇatvaṃ karkaśatvaṃ laghutvaṃ gurūtvaṃ picchilatvaṃ mandatvamamandatvaṃ śītatvamuṣṇatvaṃ jighatsā pipāsā tṛptirbalaṃ daurbalayaṃ mūrcchā kaṇḍūtiḥ pūtirvyādhirjarāmaraṇaṃ klāntirviśrāma ūrjā ca // dharmāyatanasaṃgṛhītaṃ rūpaṃ katamat / pañcavidham / ābhisaṃkṣepikamābhyavakāśiṃkaṃ sāmādānikaṃ parikalpitaṃ vaibhutvikaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: is again threefold: attractive (<s>śobhana</s>), unattractive (<s>aśobhana</s>), and neither — the opposite of both. What is sound? The object that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and is external to the ear-faculty. It is either pleasant, unpleasant, or neither; caused by appropriated <s>mahābhūtas</s>, caused by non-appropriated <s>mahābhūtas</s>, or caused by both; popularly known, brought forward by the accomplished, imagined, taught by the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>), or taught by the non-Buddhists (<s>tīrthikas</s>). What is smell? The object that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and is graspable by the nose-faculty. Such as: fragrant, malodorous, of equal smell, innate smell, conjunctive smell, and transformative smell. What is taste? The object that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and is external to the tongue-faculty. It is bitter, sour, sweet, pungent, salty, and astringent; pleasant, unpleasant, or neither; innate, conjunctive, or transformative. What is a portion of the tangible? The object that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and is graspable by the body-faculty. It is smoothness, roughness, lightness, heaviness, viscosity, slowness, non-slowness, coldness, heat, hunger, thirst, satisfaction, strength, weakness, torpor, itching, decay, disease, old age, death, fatigue, rest, and vitality. What is form included in the <s>dharma</s>-base (<s>dharmāyatana</s>)? It is fivefold: condensed (<s>ābhisaṃkṣepika</s>), spatial (<s>ābhyavakāśika</s>), assumed through commitment (<s>sāmādānika</s>), imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>), and mastered through supernatural power (<s>vaibhutvika</s>).

body.translated_text: What is the establishment of the <s>rūpa-skandha</s> (aggregate of form)? Whatever form there is — all of it consists of the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) and [forms] derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s>. What are the four <s>mahābhūtas</s>? The earth-element (<s>pṛthivī-dhātu</s>), water-element (<s>ap-dhātu</s>), fire-element (<s>tejo-dhātu</s>), and wind-element (<s>vāyu-dhātu</s>). What is the earth-element? Hardness. What is the water-element? Fluidity. What is the fire-element? Heat. What is the wind-element? Motion. What is derived form (<s>upādāya rūpa</s>)? The eye-faculty (<s>cakṣur-indriya</s>), ear-faculty (<s>śrotra-indriya</s>), nose-faculty (<s>ghrāṇa-indriya</s>), tongue-faculty (<s>jivhā-indriya</s>), body-faculty (<s>kāya-indriya</s>), a portion of form, sound, smell, taste, and tangibles, and form included in the <s>dharma</s>-base (<s>dharmāyatana</s>). What is the eye-faculty? The clarity of form (<s>rūpa-prasāda</s>) that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and serves as the support of eye-consciousness. What is the ear-faculty? The clarity of form that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and serves as the support of ear-consciousness. What is the nose-faculty? The clarity of form that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and serves as the support of nose-consciousness. What is the tongue-faculty? The clarity of form that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and serves as the support of tongue-consciousness. What is the body-faculty? The clarity of form that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and serves as the support of body-consciousness. What is [visible] form? The object that is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> and is within the range of the eye-faculty. Such as: blue, yellow, red, white, long, short, round, circular, large, subtle, raised, depressed, pleasant, unpleasant, sunlight, shade, light, darkness, clouds, smoke, dust, and mist. Open-space form, representational form (<s>vijñapti-rūpa</s>), space as a single-colored form. That

body.text: vedanāskandhavyavasthānaṃ katamat / ṣaḍvedanākāyāḥ / cakṣuḥsaṃsparśajā vedanā śrotraghrāṇajivhākāyamanaḥ saṃsparśajā vedanā // evaṃ ṣaḍvedanā kāyāḥ sukhā vā duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā vā // punaḥ sukhā kāyikī vedanā duḥkhā kāyikī vedanā aduḥkhāsukhā kāyikīvedanā sukhā caitasikī vedanā duḥkhā caitasikī vedanā aduḥkhāsukhā caitasikī vedanā sukhā sāmiṣavedanā duḥkhā sāmiṣavedanā aduḥkhāsukhā sāmiṣavedanā sukhā nirāmiṣavedanā duḥkhā nirāmiṣavedanā aduḥkhāsukhā nirāmiṣavedanā punaḥ sukhā gredhāśritavedanā duḥkhā gredhāśritavedanā aduḥkhāsukhā gredhāśritavedanā sukhā naiṣkramyāśritavedanā duḥkhā naiṣkramyāśritavedanā aduḥkhāsukhā naiṣkramyānnitavedanā ca // kāyikī vedanā katamā / paṃcavijñānasaṃprayuktā vedanā // caitasikī vedanā katamā / manovijñānasaṃprayuktā vedanā / sāmiṣavedanā katamā / (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 5

children.translated_text: ) Feeling associated with craving for self-existence (<s>ātmabhāvatṛṣṇā</s>). What is feeling without material attachment? Feeling dissociated from that craving. body.translated_text: What is the classification of the <s>vedanā-skandha</s> (aggregate of feeling)? There are six groups of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling): feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact. Thus there are six groups of feeling — pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant. Furthermore: pleasant bodily feeling, unpleasant bodily feeling, neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant bodily feeling; pleasant mental feeling, unpleasant mental feeling, neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant mental feeling; pleasant feeling with material attachment (<s>sāmiṣa</s>), unpleasant feeling with material attachment, neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant feeling with material attachment; pleasant feeling without material attachment (<s>nirāmiṣa</s>), unpleasant feeling without material attachment, neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant feeling without material attachment; furthermore: pleasant feeling based on craving (<s>gredhāśrita</s>), unpleasant feeling based on craving, neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant feeling based on craving; pleasant feeling based on renunciation (<s>naiṣkramyāśrita</s>), unpleasant feeling based on renunciation, and neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant feeling based on renunciation. What is bodily feeling? Feeling associated with the five sense-consciousnesses. What is mental feeling? Feeling associated with mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>). body.translated_text: What is the classification of the <s>saṃjñā-skandha</s> (aggregate of perception)? There are six groups of <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception): perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact. Thus one perceives with signs (<s>sanimitta</s>), perceives without signs (<s>animitta</s>), perceives the limited (<s>parītta</s>), perceives the exalted (<s>mahadgata</s>), perceives the immeasurable (<s>apramāṇa</s>), and perceives 'there is nothing,' i.e., the base of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>). What is perception with signs? All perception except that of one unskilled in conventional usage, that of one who has attained the signless element (<s>animittadhātu</s>), and that of one who has attained the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). What is perception without signs? That which has been set aside [from the above]. What is limited perception? That by which one perceives the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). What is exalted perception? That by which one perceives the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>). What is immeasurable perception? That by which one perceives the base of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>) and the base of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>). What is nothingness-perception? That by which one perceives the base of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>).

children.translated_text: ) — what is it? It is the mental formation, the action of the mind. Its function is the impelling of mind toward the wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. What is <s>manaskāra</s> (attention)? It is the engagement of the mind. Its function is the holding of the mind upon an object. What is <s>sparśa</s> (contact)? When the triad [of sense-faculty, object, and consciousness] converge, it is the determination of the sense-faculty's transformation. Its function is providing the basis for <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). What is <s>chanda</s> (desire-to-act)? With respect to a desired thing, it is the wish to act, conjoined with that [desire]. Its function is providing the basis for the generation of energy (<s>vīrya</s>). What is <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolve)? With respect to a determined thing, it is the holding [of the mind] according to that determination. Its function is unshakeability. What is <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness)? With respect to a familiar thing, it is the non-loss of mind, and its function is non-distraction. What is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration)? With respect to a thing being examined, it is the one-pointedness of mind. Its function is providing the basis for knowledge. What is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)? With respect to the very thing being examined, it is the discrimination of <s>dharmas</s>. Its function is the removal of doubt. What is <s>śraddhā</s> (faith)? It is the conviction regarding existence, qualities, and capability, along with clarity and aspiration. Its function is providing the basis for <s>chanda</s> (desire-to-act). What is <s>hrī</s> (shame)? It is embarrassment at wrongdoing from one's own [standpoint]. Its function is providing the basis for the restraint from misconduct. What is <s>apatrāpya</s> (moral dread)? It is embarrassment at wrongdoing from the standpoint of others. Its function is the same. What is <s>alobha</s> (non-attachment)? It is non-clinging to existence or to the requisites of existence. Its function is providing the basis for non-engagement in misconduct. What is <s>adveṣa</s> (non-hatred)? It is non-hostility toward beings, toward suffering, and toward <s>dharmas</s> that are the occasion of suffering. Its function is providing the basis for non-engagement in misconduct. What is <s>amoha</s> (non-delusion)? It is knowledge through result (<s>vipāka</s>), through scripture (<s>āgama</s>), or through realization (<s>adhigama</s>), [that is,] analytical understanding. Its function is providing the basis for non-engagement in misconduct. What is <s>vīrya</s> (energy)? It is the zeal of mind toward the wholesome — whether in preparation, in application, in non-shrinking, in non-retreating, or in non-contentment. Its function is the completion and perfection of the wholesome factors. What is <s>praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility)? Through the pacification of the unsuitabilities of body and mind, it is the workability of body and mind. Its function is the removal of all obstructions. What is <s>apramāda</s> (heedfulness)? Based on <s>alobha</s>, <s>adveṣa</s>, <s>amoha</s>, together with energy, it is the cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> and the guarding of the mind from defiled <s>dharmas</s>. Its function is the completion and perfection of mundane and supramundane attainments. What is <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity)? Based on <s>alobha</s>, <s>adveṣa</s>, <s>amoha</s>, together with energy, it is the evenness of mind, the smoothness of mind, and the state of non-engagement of mind, opposed to the defiled mode of abiding. Its function is providing the basis for giving no opportunity to defilements. What is <s>avihiṃsā</s> (non-harming)? (

children.translated_text: Non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>) has compassion (<s>karuṇatā</s>) as its peak. Its function is not-harming. What is attachment (<s>rāga</s>)? It is clinging (<s>anuṇaya</s>) to the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>). Its function is the generation of suffering. What is aversion (<s>pratigha</s>)? It is hostility (<s>āghāta</s>) toward beings, toward suffering, and toward phenomena that are the bases of suffering. Its function is providing the basis for non-peaceful abiding, misconduct, and [unwholesome action]. What is pride (<s>māna</s>)? It is the mind's inflation (<s>unnati</s>), based on the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). Its function is providing the basis for disrespect and the arising of suffering. What is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)? It is non-knowledge (<s>ajñāna</s>) regarding the three realms. Its function is providing the basis for wrong determination regarding phenomena (<s>dharmas</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and the arising of affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>). What is doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>)? It is indecision (<s>vimati</s>) regarding the [four noble] truths. Its function is providing the basis for non-engagement in the wholesome class. What is the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>)? It is the acceptance, inclination, opinion, examination, and view of one who regards the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>) as self or as belonging to a self. Its function is providing the basis for all types of views. What is the extreme view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>)? It is the acceptance, inclination, opinion, examination, and view of one who regards the five aggregates of clinging as either eternal (<s>śāśvata</s>) or annihilated (<s>uccheda</s>). body.translated_text: What is the classification of the <s>saṃskāra-skandha</s> (aggregate of formations)? There are six groups of <s>cetanā</s> (volition): volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact. By which one wills toward the wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), wills toward defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), and wills toward the differentiation of states — this is <s>cetanā</s> (volition). Setting aside <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), the other mental factors (<s>caitasika dharmas</s>) and the formations dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta saṃskāras</s>) are called the <s>saṃskāra-skandha</s> (aggregate of formations). children.translated_text: from how many views should those views be understood? From two, or from all. Those views that are among the four indeterminate [categories] — from how many views should they be understood? From two, or from all. Seeing what fault did the Blessed One reject the self in the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) by five reasons? Seeing the five faults grasped by the view of the perishable collection: the fault of being of different nature, the fault of impermanence, the fault of unwholesomeness, the fault of bodilessness, and the fault of liberation without effort. What is the twentyfold view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) in the five aggregates of clinging? One regards form (<s>rūpa</s>) as self; one regards the self as possessing form; one regards form as belonging to the self; one regards the self as in form. [Similarly with] feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) — one regards consciousness as self; one regards the self as possessing consciousness; one regards consciousness as belonging to the self; one regards the self as in consciousness. Among these, how many are self-views and how many are views of what belongs to a self? Five are self-views; fifteen are views of what belongs to a self. For what reason are there fifteen views of what belongs to a self? By virtue of belonging through relationship, by virtue of belonging through being under control, and by virtue of belonging through inseparable functioning. Should the view of the perishable collection be described as having an ascertained object or as having an unascertained object? It should be described as having an unascertained object — like the cognition of a snake in a rope.

body.translated_text: and view of one who regards a view, and the five aggregates of clinging that are the basis of that view, as foremost, best, distinguished, and supreme. What are these five views? How many of them are superimposition-views (<s>samāropadṛṣṭi</s>) and how many are denial-views (<s>apavādadṛṣṭi</s>)? Four are superimposition-views — by virtue of superimposing a particular nature on the object of knowledge, and by virtue of superimposing supreme purity on a view. One is, for the most part, a denial-view. Those views that pertain to the prior end (<s>pūrvāntakalpikā</s>) and those views that pertain to the posterior end (<s>parāntakalpikā</s>),

children.translated_text: it is the concealing of actual faults, which has attachment and delusion as its components. Its function is obstructing the attainment of correct instruction. What is intoxication (<s>mada</s>)? By reason of health, youth, long life, or obtaining one or another worldly fortune, it is delight and elation, which has attachment (<s>rāga</s>) as its component. Its function is providing the basis for all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>). What is harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>)? It is cruelty, mercilessness, and ruthlessness, which has aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) as its component. Its function is causing harm. What is shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>)? It is not being ashamed of wrongdoing before oneself, which has attachment, hatred, and delusion as its components. Its function is assisting all afflictions and secondary afflictions. What is lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>)? It is not being ashamed of wrongdoing before others, which has attachment, hatred, and delusion as its components. Its function is assisting all afflictions and secondary afflictions.

body.translated_text: What is anger (<s>krodha</s>)? When a present occasion of harm arises, it is the mind's hostility (<s>āghāta</s>), which has aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) as its peak. Its function is providing the basis for violence such as taking up weapons, taking up sticks, etc. What is resentment (<s>upanāha</s>)? It is the non-relinquishing of a grudge, following upon [anger], which has aversion as its peak. Its function is providing the basis for impatience. What is concealment (<s>makṣa</s>)? When rightly admonished, it is the concealing of faults, which has delusion (<s>moha</s>) as its component. Its function is providing the basis for remorse and non-peaceful abiding. What is spite (<s>pradāśa</s>)? It is the mind's hostility (<s>āghāta</s>), which has aversion as its component, preceded by anger and resentment. Its function is providing the basis for harsh, loud, and severe speech, producing demerit and non-peaceful abiding. What is jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>)? When one is intent on gain and honor, it is the mind's agitation regarding the special fortune of others, which has hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) as its component and is caused by intolerance (<s>amarṣa</s>). Its function is unpleasantness and non-peaceful abiding. What is avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>)? When one is intent on gain and honor, it is the mind's clinging to one's possessions, which has attachment (<s>rāga</s>) as its component. Its function is providing the basis for non-contentment. What is deceit (<s>māyā</s>)? When one is intent on gain and honor, it is the displaying of non-existent qualities, which has attachment and delusion as its components. Its function is providing the basis for wrong livelihood. What is hypocrisy (<s>śāṭhya</s>)? When one is intent on gain and honor,

children.text: ) kuśalaprayogaḥ // hauṣṭhulyavikṣepaḥ katamaḥ / ahaṃkāramamakārāsmimānapakṣyaṃ dauṣṭhulyamāganya kuśalaprayuktasyotpannotpanneṣu vediteṣvahamiti vā mameti vā asmīti vā udgraho vyavakiraṇā nimittīkāraḥ // manasikāravikṣepaḥ katamaḥ / samapattyantaraṃ vā yānāntaraṃ vā samāpadyamānasya saṃśrayato vā yo visāraḥ / vairāgyapari panthakarmakaḥ middhaṃ katamat / middhanimittamāgamya mohāṃśikaścetaso 'bhisaṃkṣepaḥ kuśalaḥ akuśalaḥ avyākṛtaḥ kāle vā akāle vā yukto vā ayukto vā / kṛtyāvipattisanniśrayadānakarmakam // kaukṛtyaṃ katamat / yadabhipretānabhipretaṃ kāraṇākāraṇāmāgamya mohāṃśikaścetaso vipratisāraḥ / kuśalamakuśalamavyākṛtaṃ kāle akāle yuktamayuktañca // cittasthitiparipanthakarmakaḥ // vitarkaḥ katamaḥ / cetanāṃ vā niśritya prajñāṃ vā paryeṣako manojalpaḥ / sā ca cittasyaudārikatā // vicāraḥ katamaḥ / cetanāṃ vā niśritya prajñāṃ vā pratyavekṣako manojalpaḥ / sa ca cittasya sūkṣmatā / sparśāsparśavihārasaṃniśrayadānakarmakau / api khalu kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ svavipakṣaprahāṇaṃ karma / kleśopakleśānāṃ svapratipakṣaparipanthanaṃ karma // 0 //

body.translated_text: What is sloth (<s>styāna</s>)? It is the mind's unworkability (<s>akarmaṇyatā</s>), which has delusion (<s>moha</s>) as its component. Its function is assisting all afflictions and secondary afflictions. What is restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>)? When one follows after a sign of the pleasant, it is the mind's non-pacification, which has attachment (<s>rāga</s>) as its component. Its function is obstructing tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>). What is lack of faith (<s>āśraddhya</s>)? It is the mind's non-conviction, non-clarity, and non-aspiration regarding wholesome phenomena (<s>dharmas</s>), which has delusion as its component. Its function is providing the basis for laziness. What is laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>)? By reason of attachment to sleep, lying on one's side, and ease, it is the mind's non-enthusiasm, which has delusion as its component. Its function is obstructing the practice of the wholesome class. What is heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>)? Based on laziness and on attachment, hatred, and delusion, it is the non-cultivation of wholesome phenomena and the non-guarding of the mind from phenomena with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>). Its function is providing the basis for the increase of the unwholesome and the decline of the wholesome. What is forgetfulness (<s>muṣitasmṛtitā</s>)? It is mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) associated with afflictions. Its function is providing the basis for distraction. What is non-alertness (<s>asamprajanya</s>)? It is wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) associated with afflictions, by which the conduct of body, speech, and mind proceeds without awareness. Its function is providing the basis for transgression. What is distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>)? It is the mind's dispersal, which has attachment, hatred, and delusion as its components. body.text: citta viprayuktāḥ saṃskārāḥ katame / prāptirasaṃjñisamāpattinirodhasamāpattirāsaṃjñikaṃ jīvitendriyaṃ nikāyasabhāgatā jātirjarā sthitiranityatā nāmakāyāḥ padakāyāḥ vyañjanakāyāḥ pṛthagjanatvaṃ pravṛttiḥ pratiniyamo yogaḥ javo 'nukramaḥ kālo deśaḥ saṃkhyā sāmagrī ca // prāptiḥ katamā / kuśalakuśalāṃnāṃ dharmāṇāmācayāpacaye prāptiḥ pratilagbhaḥ samanvāgama iti prajñaptiḥ // asaṃjñisamāpattiḥ katamā / śubhakṛtsnavītarāgasyoparyavītarāgasya niḥsaraṇasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa manasikāreṇāsthāvarāṇāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodhe asaṃjñisamāpattiriti prajñaptiḥ // nirodhasamāpattiḥ katamā / ākiṃcanyāyatanavītarāgasya bhavāgrāduccalitasya śāntavihārasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa (

children.text: ) manasikāreṇāsthāvarāṇāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodhe nirodhasamāpattiriti prajñaptiḥ // āsaṃjñikaṃ katamat / asaṃjñisattveṣudeveṣūpapannasyāsthāvarāṇāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodhe āsaṃjñikapriti prajñaptiḥ // jīvitendriyaṃ katamat / nikāyasabhāge pūrvakarmāviddhe sthitikālaniyame āyuriti prajñaptiḥ // nikāyasabhāgaḥ katamaḥ / teṣāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmiṃ stasmin sattvanikāye ātmabhāvasadṛśatāyāṃ nikāyasabhāga iti prajñaptiḥ // jātiḥ katamā / nikāyasabhāge saṃskārāṇāmabhūtvābhāve jātiriti prajñaptiḥ // jarā katamā / nikāyasabhāme saṃskārāṇāṃ prabandhānyathātve jareti prajñaptiḥ // sthitiḥ katamā / nikāyasabhāge prabandhāvipraṇāśe sthitiriti prajñaptiḥ // anityatā katamā / nikāyasabhāge saṃskārāṇāṃ prabandhavināśe anityateti prajñaptiḥ // nāmakāyāḥ katame / dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvādhivacane nāmakāyā iti prajñaptiḥ // padakāyāḥ katame / dharmāṇāṃ viśeṣādhivacane padakāyā iti prajñaptiḥ // vyañjanakāyāḥ katameḥ tadubhayāśrayeṣvakṣareṣu vyañjanakāyā iti prajñaptiḥ / tadubhayābhivyañjanatāmupādāya / varṇo 'pi saḥ / arthasaṃvarṇanatāmupādāya / akṣare punaḥ paryāyākṣaraṇatāmupādāya // pṛthagjanatvaṃ katamat / āryadharmāṇāmapratilābhe pṛthagjanatvamiti prajñaptiḥ // pravṛttiḥ katamā / hetuphala prabandhānupacchede pravṛttiriti prajñaptiḥ / pratiniyamaḥ katamaḥ / hetuphalanānātve pratiniyama iti prajñaptiḥ // yogaḥ katamaḥ / hetuphalānurūpye yoga iti prajñaptiḥ // javaḥ katamaḥ / hetuphalāśupravṛttau java iti prajñaptiḥ // anukramaḥ katamaḥ / hetuphalaikatye pravṛttau anukrama iti prajñaptiḥ // kālaḥ katamaḥ / hetuphalaprabandhapravṛttau kāla iti prajñaptiḥ // deśaḥ katamaḥ / pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarā dharordhvāsu sarvato daśasu dikṣu hetuphala eva deśa iti prajñaptiḥ // saṃkhyā katamā / saṃskārāṇāṃ pratyekaśo bhede saṃkhyeti prajñaptiḥ // sāmagrī katamā / hetuphalapratyayasamavadhāne sāmagrīti prajñaptiḥ // 0 //

children.text: ) cittaṃ katamat / skandhadhātvāyatanavāsanāparibhāvitaṃ sarvavījakamālayavijñānaṃ vipākavijñānamādānavijñānamapi tat / tadvāsanācitatāmupādāya // manaḥ katamat / yannityakālammanyanātmākamālayavijñānaṃ caturbhiḥ kleśaiḥ saṃprayuktamātmadṛṣṭyātmasnehenāsmimānenāvidyayā ca / tacca sarvatragaṃ kuśale 'pyakuśale 'pyavyākṛte 'pi sthāpayitvā mārgasabhmukhībhāvaṃ nirodhasamāpattimaśaikṣa bhūmiṃ ca yacca ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānānāṃ samanantaraniruddhaṃ vijñānam // vijñānaṃ katamat / ṣaḍ vijñānakāyāḥ / cakṣurvijñānaṃ śrotraghrāṇajivhākāyamanovijñānam / cakṣurvijñānaṃ katamat / cakṣurāśrayā rūpālambanā prati vijñaptiḥ // śrotravijñānaṃ katamat / śrotrāśrayā śabdālambanā prativijñaptiḥ // ghrāṇavijñānaṃ katamat / ghrāṇāśrayā gandhālambanā pratibijñaptiḥ / jilhāvijñānaṃ katamat / jivhāśrayā rasālambanā prativijñaptiḥ // kāyavijñānaṃ katamat / kāyāśrayā spraṣṭavyālambanā prativijñaptiḥ // manovijñānaṃ katamat / manaāśrayā dharmālambanā prativijñaptiḥ //

body.text: dhātuvyavasthānaṃ katamat / rūpaskandhā eva daśa dhātavaḥ / cakṣurdhātuḥ rūpadhātuḥ śrotradhātuḥ śabdadhātuḥ ghrāṇadhātuḥ gandhadhātuḥ jivhādhātuḥ rasadhātuḥ kāyadhātuḥ spraṣṭavyadhātuḥ mano dhātvekadeśaśca // vedanāskandhaḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ saṃskāraskandhaśca dharmadhātvekadeśaḥ / vijñānaskandha eca sapta vijñānaghātavaḥ / cakṣurādayaḥ ṣaḍ vijñānadhātavo manodhātuśca // dharmadhātau skandhairasaṃgṛhītaṃ katamat / dharmadhātāvasaṃskṛtā dharmāḥ / te 'saṃskṛtādharmāḥ punaraṣṭadhā / kuśaladharmatathatā akuśaladharmatathatā avyākṛtadharmatathatā ākāśam apratisaṃkhyā nirodhaḥ pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ āniṃjyaṃ saṃjñāvedayitanirodhaśca // kuśaladharmatathatā katamā / nairātmyam / sā punarucyate śūnyatā animittaṃ bhūtakoṭiḥ paramārtho dharmādhātuśca // kimupādāya tathatā tathatocyate / ananyayābhāvatāmupādāya / kimupādāya tathatā nairātmyamucyate / dvividhātmaviprayuktatāmupādāya / kimupādāya tathatā śūnyatocyate / sarvasaṃkleśāpracāratāmupādāya / (

children.text: ) kimupādāya tathatā animittamucyate / sarvanimittopaśamatāmupādāya / kimupādāya tathatā bhūtakāṭirucyate / aviparyāsālambanatāmupādāya / kimupādāya tathatā paramārtha ucyate / paramārthajñānagocarasthānatāmupādāya / kimupādāya tathatā dharmadhāturucyate / sarveṣāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ ca buddha dharmanimittāśrayatāmupādāya // yathā kuśalaladharmatathatā tathā akuśaladharmatathatā avyākṛta dharmatathatā ca jñeyā // ākāśaṃ katamat / rūpābhāvaḥ sarvakṛtyāvakāśatāmupādāya // apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ katamaḥ / yo nirodho na visaṃyogaḥ // pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ katamaḥ / yo nirodho visaṃyogaḥ // ānijyaṃ katamat / śubhakṛtsnavītarāgasyoparyavītarāgasya sukhanirodhaḥ // saṃjñāvedayitanirodhaḥ katamaḥ / ākiṃcanyāyatanavītarāgasya bhāvāgrāduccalitasya śāntavihārasaṃjñāmanasikārapūrvakeṇa asthāvarāṇāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tadekatyānāṃ ca sthāvarāṇāṃ nirodhaḥ // paṃcarūpāṇi vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāraskandhāḥ te 'ṣṭau asaṃskṛtā dharmāścaivaṃ te ṣoḍaśa dharmadhātava ucyante /
children.translated_text: On what basis is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) called <s>animitta</s> (signless)? On the basis of the subsiding of all signs. On what basis is <s>tathatā</s> called <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality)? On the basis of being the object of non-erroneous cognition. On what basis is <s>tathatā</s> called <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality)? On the basis of being the domain and locus of ultimate knowledge (<s>paramārtha-jñāna</s>). On what basis is <s>tathatā</s> called <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>)? On the basis of being the support and ground of the <s>dharmas</s> of Buddhahood for all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary Buddhas). Just as the <s>tathatā</s> of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, so too the <s>tathatā</s> of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and of indeterminate <s>dharmas</s> should be understood. What is <s>ākāśa</s> (space)? The absence of form, on the basis of providing room for all activities. What is <s>apratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (cessation not through deliberation)? That cessation which is not separation. What is <s>pratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (cessation through deliberation)? That cessation which is separation. What is <s>ānijya</s> (imperturbability)? For one who has become free from passion toward the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (All-Beautiful) [heaven] and is [yet] not free from passion toward what is above — the cessation of pleasure. What is <s>saṃjñā-vedayita-nirodha</s> (cessation of perception and feeling)? For one who has become free from passion toward <s>Ākiṃcanyāyatana</s> (the Sphere of Nothingness) and has shifted from the Summit of Existence — preceded by the mental application of the perception of peaceful abiding — the cessation of the non-stable <s>dharmas</s> of mind and mental factors, and of certain stable ones among them. The five [types of] form, the <s>vedanā</s>-<s>saṃjñā</s>-<s>saṃskāra</s> aggregates, and those eight unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> — thus these sixteen are called the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>).

body.text: āyatanavyavasthānaṃ katamat / daśa rūpadhātava eva daśa rūpāyatanāni / sapta vijñānadhātava eva manaāyatunam / dharmadhāturdharmāyatanam // anene nayena skandhadhātvāyatanāni triṣu dharmeṣu saṃgṛhītāni bhavanti / rūpaskandho dharmadhāturmanaāyatanaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: What is the establishment of the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases)? The ten form-elements (<s>rūpa-dhātus</s>) are indeed the ten form-bases. The seven consciousness-elements are indeed the mind-base (<s>mana-āyatana</s>). The <s>dharma</s>-element is the <s>dharma</s>-base. By this method, the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s> are included in the three <s>dharmas</s>: the <s>rūpa-skandha</s>, the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>, and the <s>mana-āyatana</s>.

body.text: yaduktaṃ cakṣuśca cakṣurdhātuśceti / kiṃ syāccakṣuśca cakṣurdhātuśca / āhosvit syāccakṣurdhātuśca cakṣuśca / syāccakṣurna cakṣurdhātuḥ / yathā arhataścaramaṃ cakṣuḥ / syāccakṣardhātu rna cakṣuḥ / yathā aṇḍe vā kalale vā arvude vā peśyāṃ vā mātuḥkukṣau vālabdhaṃ cakṣurlabdhaṃ vā naṣṭam / ārūpyeṣūpapannasya pṛthagjanasya vā yaścakṣurhetuḥ / syāccakṣuścakṣurdhātuśca / śiṣṭāsvavasthāṣu / na syāccakṣurna cakṣurdhātuśca / nirupādhiśeṣanirvāṇadhātusamāpannasya ārūpyeṣūpapannasyāryasya vā // yathā cakṣuśya cakṣurdhātuśca tathā śrotraghrāṇajivhākāya dhātavo yathāyogyaṃ veditavyāḥ // kiṃ syānmano 'pi manodhāturapi ahosvit syānmanodhāturapi mano 'pi / syānmano (

children.translated_text: Abhidh-s 14

children.text: ) na manodhātuḥ / yathā arhataścaramaṃ manaḥ / syānmanodhāturna manaḥ / yathā nirodhasamāpannasya yo manohetuḥ / syānmano 'pi manodhāturapi / śiṣṭāsvavasthāsu / na syānmano 'pi manodhāturapi / yathā nirūpādhiśeṣanirvāṇadhātusamāpannasya /
children.translated_text: not the mind-element — as in the case of the last mind of an <s>arhat</s>. There can be the mind-element but not the mind — as in the case of the mental cause of one who has entered the cessation-attainment. There can be both the mind and the mind-element — in all remaining states. There can be neither the mind nor the mind-element —

body.translated_text: It has been stated: "the eye and the eye-element." Can there be the eye and the eye-element [at the same time]? Or can there be the eye-element and the eye [at the same time]? There can be the eye but not the eye-element — as in the case of the last eye of an <s>arhat</s>. There can be the eye-element but not the eye —

body.text: tadbhūmāvutpannaḥ kiṃ tadbhūmikena cakṣuṣā tadbhūmikāni rūpāṇi paśyati / tadbhūmikena cakṣuṣā tadbhūmikāni rūpāṇi paśyati, anyabhūmikenāpi / kāmadhātāvapapannaḥ māvacareṇa cakṣuṣā kāmāvacarāṇi rūpāṇi paśyati / rūpāvacareṇordhvabhūmikeana cakṣuṣā adharabhūmikānyapi rūpāṇi paśyati / yathā cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi pratigṛṇhāti tatha śrotreṇa śabdaṃ pratigṛṇhāti / yathā kāmadhātāvutpannastathā rūpadhātāvutpannaḥ kāmāvacareṇa ghrāṇena jivhayā kāyena cā kāmāvacarān gandhān jighrati rasānāsvādane sparśān budhyati ca // rūpadhātāvutpanno rūpāvacareṇa kāyena svabhūmikān sparśān budhyati / tasmin dhātau svabhāvato na gandharasau / vijñaptyāhārarāgavirahāt / anena nayena na ghrāṇajivhayo rvijñānam / kāmadhātāvutpannaḥ kāmāvacareṇa manasā traidhātukānanāsravāṃśca dharmāna vijānāti // yadhā kāmadhātāvutpannastathā rūpadhātāvutpannaḥ // ārūpyadhātāvutpanna ārūpyāvacareṇa manasā ārūpyāvacarān svabhūmikānanāsravāṃśca dharmān vijānāti / anāsraveṇa manasā traidhātukānanāsravāṃśca dharmān vijānāti //
body.translated_text: One born in a certain plane (<s>bhūmi</s>) — does he see forms of that plane with the eye of that plane? He sees forms of that plane with the eye of that plane, and also with [an eye] of another plane. One born in the Desire Realm (<s>Kāmadhātu</s>) — with the eye of the Desire Realm,

body.text: kimupādāya skandhānāṃ tathānukramaḥ / vijñānādhiṣṭhānatāmupādāya // catvāri vijñānādhiṣṭhānāni vijñānāni ca pūrvāparāśritāni / yathā rūpaṃ tathā bhavaḥ / yathā vedayate tathā saṃjānīte / yathā saṃjānīte tathā cetayate / yathā cetayate tathā vijñānaṃ tatra tatropagaṃ bhavati / saṃkleśavyavadānataḥ / yatra saṃkliśyate vyavadāyate ca / vedanānimittagrahaṇābhisaṃskāreṇa saṃkleśavyavadānābhyāṃ ca saṃkliśyate vyavadāyate ca / anena nayena skandhānāmukramo nirdiśyate /
body.translated_text: On what basis is the order of the <s>skandhas</s> as given? On the basis of being the foundations of consciousness (<s>vijñāna-adhiṣṭhāna</s>). The four foundations of consciousness, together with the consciousnesses, are based on prior and posterior [relations]. As form is, so is existence; as one feels, so one perceives;

body.text: kathaṃ dhātūnāṃ tathānukramaḥ / laukika vastu vikalpapravṛttitā mupādāya // katamā laukikī vastuvikalpapravṛttiḥ / loke prathamaṃ paśyati / dṛṣṭvā (

children.translated_text: Abhidh-s 15

children.text: ) vyatisārayati / vyatisārya snāpitaṃ gandhaṃ mālyaṃ ca paricarati / tato nānāvidhaṃ praṇītaṃ bhojanaṃ paricarati / tato 'nekaśayyāsanadāsīparikān paricarati / aparato manodhātorapi teṣu teṣu vikalpaḥ // evaṃ ca adhyātmadhātoranukrameṇa bahirdhādhātorvyavasthānam / tadanukrameṇa vijñānadhātorvyavasthānam // yathā dhātūnāmanukrama āyatanānāmapi tadvat //
children.translated_text: one discriminates. Having discriminated, one attends to the bathed one with perfume and garlands. Then one attends to various kinds of excellent food. Then one attends to various beds, seats, servants, and attendants. Furthermore, the mind-element —

body.translated_text: How is the order of the <s>dhātus</s> as given? On the basis of the engagement of worldly conceptual elaboration regarding objects. What is the worldly engagement of conceptual elaboration regarding objects? In the world, first one sees. Having seen,

body.text: skandhārthaḥ katamaḥ / yat kiṃcidrūpam / atītamanāgataṃ pratyutpannamadhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā audārikaṃ vā sūkṣmaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā praṇītaṃ vā yadvā dūre yadvāntike tatsarvamabhisaṃkṣipyocyate rūpaskandhaḥ rāśyarthamupādaya / yathā vittarāśiḥ / evaṃ yāvat vijñānaskandham // āpica duḥkhavaipulya lakṣaṇatāmupādāya skandha ucyate / yathāmahāvṛkṣaskandhaḥ / yaduktaṃ sūtre / yathā aikāntikamahāduḥkhasamudayataḥ // api ca saṃkleśato bhāravahanatāmupādāya skandha ucyate / yathā skandhena bhāramudvahati /
body.translated_text: What is the meaning of <s>skandha</s> (aggregate)? Whatever form there is — past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, whether far or near — all of that is summarized together,

body.text: dhātvarthaḥ katamaḥ / sarvadharmavījārthaḥ / svalakṣaṇadhāraṇārthaḥ / kāryakāraṇa bhāvadhāraṇārthaḥ / sarvaprakāradharmasaṃgra hadhāraṇārthañca /
body.translated_text: What is the meaning of <s>dhātu</s> (element)? It means the seed of all <s>dharmas</s>. It means the maintenance of own-characteristic. It means the maintenance of the cause-and-effect relationship. And it means the maintenance of the inclusion of <s>dharmas</s> of all kinds.

body.text: āyatanārthaḥ katamaḥ / vijñānāyadvārārtha āyatanārthaḥ / yathā buddhena bhāṣitam rūpaṃ budbudopamaṃ vedanā phenopamā saṃjñā marīcikopamā saṃskārāḥ parṇo pamā vijñānaṃ māyopamamiti / kimarthaṃ rūpaṃ budbudopamaṃ yāvad vijñānaṃ māyopamamiti / anātmato 'śucito hīnarasato 'dṛḍhato 'sārataśca /
body.translated_text: What is the meaning of <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base)? The meaning of <s>āyatana</s> is the gate for the arising of consciousness. As the <s>Buddha</s> has spoken: "Form is like a bubble; feeling is like foam; perception is like a mirage; formations are like a plantain tree; consciousness is like an illusion."

body.text: (athamūlavastuni tridharmaparicchede prathame dvitīyo bhāgaḥ /)
body.translated_text: (Now, in the Determination of the Three <s>Dharmas</s> within the Fundamental Topics, the Second Section:)

body.text: punaḥ skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ vikalpāḥ katame / tathācodānam /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, what are the varieties of <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>? And the summary verse:

body.text:
dravyamanto jñeyarūpāṇyāsravotpannakādi ca
atītāḥ pratyayāścaiva kathaṃ kati kimarthibhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Substance, objects of knowledge, form-related, with outflows, originated, caused, and so forth; past [etc.], conditions, and how many, of how many kinds, for what purpose?

body.text: skandhadhātvāyataneṣu kathaṃ dravyamat kati dvayamanti kimarthaṃ dravyamatparīkṣā / abhilāpanirapekṣastadanyanirapekṣaścendriyagocaro dravyamat / sarvaṃ dravyamat / ātmadravyā bhiniveśatyājanārtham // kathaṃ prajñaptimat / kati prajñaptimanti kimarthaṃ prajñaptimatparīkṣā / abhilāpasāpekṣastadanyasāpekṣaścendriyagocaraḥ prajñaptimat / sarvaṃ prajñaptimat / prajñaptimadātmā bhiniveśatyājanārtham / kathaṃ saṃvṛtimat / kati saṃvṛtimanti / kimarthaṃ saṃvṛtimatparīkṣā / saṃkleśālambanaṃ saṃvṛtimat / sarvaṃ saṃvṛtimat / saṃkleśanimittātmābhiniveśatyajanārtham // kathaṃ paramārthasat / kati paramārthasanti / kimarthaṃ paramārthasatparīkṣā / vyavadānālambanaṃ paramārthasat / sarvaṃ paramārthasat / vyavadānanimittātmābhiniveśatyājanārtham //
body.translated_text: Among <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), how is something substantially real (<s>dravyamat</s>)? How many are substantially real? What is the purpose of examining substantial reality? That which is independent of verbal designation and independent of other [things], and which is within the range of the senses — that is substantially real. Everything is substantially real. [This examination is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is a [permanent] substance. How is something conceptually designated (<s>prajñaptimat</s>)? How many are conceptually designated? What is the purpose of examining conceptual designation? That which is dependent on verbal designation and dependent on other [things], and which is within the range of the senses — that is conceptually designated. Everything is conceptually designated. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is a [mere] conceptual designation. How is something conventional (<s>saṃvṛtimat</s>)? How many are conventional? What is the purpose of examining conventionality? That which is the object of defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) is conventional. Everything is conventional. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is the sign of defilement. How is something ultimately real (<s>paramārthasat</s>)? How many are ultimately real? What is the purpose of examining ultimate reality? That which is the object of purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) is ultimately real. Everything is ultimately real. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is the sign of purification.

body.text: kathaṃ jñeyaṃ kati jñeyāni kimarthaṃ jñeyaparīkṣā / jñeyāni paṃca / rūpaṃ cittaṃ caitasikā dharmāścittaviprayuktāḥ saṃskārā asaṃskṛtaṃ ca / yatra saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ vayat saṃkliśyate vyavadāyate vā yaśca saṃkleśayati vyavadāyayati vā yā ca tatrāvasthā yā ca vyavadānatā tadāśrayeṇa sarvaṃ jñeyam // tatra rūpaṃ rūpaskandho daśarūpadhātavo daśa rūpāyatanāni dharmadhātvāyatanasaṃgṛhītāni ca rūpāṇi // cittaṃ vijñānaskandhaḥ saptavijñānadhātavo manaāyatanaṃ ca // caitasikā dharmā vedanāskandhaḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ saṃskāraskandho dharmadhātvāyatanaikadeśaśca / cittaviprayuktāḥ saṃskārāḥ citta viprayuktaḥ saṃskāraskandho dharmadhātvāyatanaikadeśaśca // asaṃskṛtaṃ dharmadhātvāyatanaikadeśaḥ // api khalu jñeyā dharmāḥ adhimuktijñānagocarato 'pi yuktijñānagocarato 'pi avisārajñānagocarato 'pi pratyātmajñānagocarato 'pi parātmajñānagocarato 'pi adharajñānagocarato 'pi ūrdhvajñānagocarato 'pi vidūṣaṇajñānagocarato 'pi (a)samutthānajñānagocarato 'pi anutpādajñānagocarato 'pi jñānajñānagocarato 'pi niṣṭhājñānagocarato 'pi mahārthajñānagocarato 'pi / jānakapaśyakātmābhiniveśatmājanārtham // (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 17

children.text: ) kathaṃ vijñeyaṃ kati vijñeyāni kimarthaṃ vijñeyaparīkṣā / avikalpanato 'pi vikalpanato 'pi hetuto 'pi pravṛttito 'pi nimittato 'pi naimittakato 'pi vipakṣapratipakṣato 'pi sūkṣmaprabhedato 'pi vijñeyaṃ draṣṭavyam / sarvāṇi vijñeyāni / draṣṭā dyātmābhiniveśatyājanārtham // kathamabhijñeyaṃ katyabhijñeyāni kimarthamabhijñeyaparīkṣā / saṃkrāntito 'pi anuśravato 'pi caritapraveśato 'pi āgatito 'pi gatito 'pi niḥsaraṇato 'pi / sarvāṇyabhijñeyāni / sānubhāvātmābhiniveśatyājanartham //
children.translated_text: ) How is something to be fully known (<s>vijñeya</s>)? How many things are to be fully known? What is the purpose of examining what is to be fully known? What is to be fully known should be seen in terms of non-conceptualization, conceptualization, cause, occurrence, sign, what is signified, opponent and counteragent, and subtle distinctions. All are to be fully known. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is a seer. How is something to be directly known (<s>abhijñeya</s>)? How many things are to be directly known? What is the purpose of examining what is to be directly known? [It should be examined] in terms of transmigration, hearsay, entry into conduct, origin, destination, and escape. All are to be directly known. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that has powers.

body.translated_text: How is something knowable (<s>jñeya</s>)? How many knowables are there? What is the purpose of examining the knowable? The knowables are five: form (<s>rūpa</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), mental factors (<s>caitasika dharmas</s>), formations dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta saṃskāras</s>), and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). That in which there is defilement and purification, that which is defiled or purified, that which defiles or purifies, the state therein, and the purification itself — on this basis, everything is knowable. Therein, form is the <s>rūpa-skandha</s>, the ten form-<s>dhātus</s>, the ten form-<s>āyatanas</s>, and the forms included in the <s>dharmadhātu-āyatana</s>. Mind is the <s>vijñāna-skandha</s>, the seven consciousness-<s>dhātus</s>, and the <s>mana-āyatana</s>. Mental factors are the <s>vedanā-skandha</s>, the <s>saṃjñā-skandha</s>, the <s>saṃskāra-skandha</s>, and a portion of the <s>dharmadhātu-āyatana</s>. Formations dissociated from mind are the <s>saṃskāra-skandha</s> dissociated from mind and a portion of the <s>dharmadhātu-āyatana</s>. The unconditioned is a portion of the <s>dharmadhātu-āyatana</s>. Moreover, knowable <s>dharmas</s> should be seen as the domain of conviction-knowledge (<s>adhimuktijñāna</s>), reasoning-knowledge (<s>yuktijñāna</s>), non-confusion-knowledge (<s>avisārajñāna</s>), personal-experience-knowledge (<s>pratyātmajñāna</s>), knowledge of self and others (<s>parātmajñāna</s>), lower knowledge (<s>adharajñāna</s>), higher knowledge (<s>ūrdhvajñāna</s>), deprecation-knowledge (<s>vidūṣaṇajñāna</s>), non-arising-knowledge (<s>asamutthānajñāna</s>), non-production-knowledge (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>), knowledge-of-knowledge (<s>jñānajñāna</s>), final-knowledge (<s>niṣṭhājñāna</s>), and great-purpose-knowledge (<s>mahārthajñāna</s>). [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is a knower and seer. (

body.text: kathaṃ rūpi kati rūpīṇi kimarthaṃ rūpiparīkṣā / rūpi tadātmato 'pi bhūtāśrayato 'pi nandīsamudayato 'pi pradeśato 'pi deśavyāptito 'pi deśopade(śa)to 'pi deśagocarato 'pi dvayasamaya gocarato 'pi sambandhato 'pya nuvandhato 'pi prarūpaṇato 'pi vyābādhanato 'pi saṃprāpaṇato 'pi saṃcayavyavasthānato 'pi vahirmukhato 'pi antarmukhato 'pi āyatato 'pi parichinnato 'pi tatkālato 'pi nidarśanato 'pi rūpi draṣṭavyam / sarvāṇi rūpīṇi yathāyogaṃ vā / rūpyā(tmā)bhiniveśatyājanārtham // kathamarūpi katyarūpīṇi kimarthamarūpiparīkṣā / rūpiviparyayeṇāpyaṃ rūpi / sarvāṇyarūpīṇi yathāyogaṃ vā / arūpyātmābhiniveśatyājanārtham // kathaṃ sanidarśanaṃ kati sanidarśanāni kimarthaṃ sanidarśanaparīkṣā / cakṣurgocaraḥ sanidarśanam / śiṣṭasya rūpivat prabhedaḥ / sarvāṇi sanidarśanāni yathāyogaṃ vā / cākṣuṣātmābhiniveśatyājanā rtham // kathamanirdarśanaṃ katyanidarśanāni kimarthamanidarśanaparīkṣā / sanidarśanaviparyayeṇānidarśanaṃ draṣṭavyam / sarvāṇyanidarśanāni yathāyogaṃ vā / (a)cākṣuṣā tmābhiniveśatyājanārtham / kathaṃ sapratighaṃ kati sapratighāni kimarthaṃ sapratigha parīkṣā / yat sanidarśanaṃ saprati ghamapi tat / api khalu tribhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sapratighaṃ draṣṭavyam / jātito 'pi upacayato 'pi aparikarmakṛtato 'pi tatra jātitaḥ yadya(da)nyo 'nyamāvṛṇotyavriyate ca / tatropacaya(ta)ḥ paramaṇorūrddham / tatrāparikarmakṛtataḥ yanna samādhivaśavarttirūpam / api khalu prakopapadasthānataḥ - sapratigham / sarvāṇi sapratighāni yathāyogaṃ vā / (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 18

children.text: ) asarvagatātmābhiniveśatyājanārtham // kathamapratighaṃ katyapratighāni kimarthamapratighaparīkṣā / sapratighaviparyeṇāpratigham / sarvāṇyapratighāni yathāyogaṃ vā / sarvagatātmābhiniveśatyājanārtham //
children.translated_text: ) [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is all-pervasive. How is something non-resistant (<s>apratigha</s>)? How many non-resistant things are there? What is the purpose of examining non-resistance? By the reverse of resistance, it is non-resistant. All are non-resistant, or as appropriate. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is all-pervasive.

body.translated_text: How is something material (<s>rūpin</s>)? How many material things are there? What is the purpose of examining materiality? The material should be seen in terms of its own nature, its basis in great elements (<s>bhūta</s>), its arising from delight (<s>nandī</s>), location, spatial extent, spatial designation, spatial domain, the domain of the conjunction of two [factors], connection, binding, description, obstruction, impacting, accumulation and arrangement, being outward-directed, being inward-directed, being extended, being delimited, the time thereof, and being visible. All are material, or as appropriate. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a material self. How is something immaterial (<s>arūpin</s>)? How many immaterial things are there? What is the purpose of examining immateriality? By the reverse of materiality, it is immaterial. All are immaterial, or as appropriate. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to an immaterial self. How is something visible (<s>sanidarśana</s>)? How many visible things are there? What is the purpose of examining visibility? That which is in the range of the eye is visible. The analysis of the remainder is as for the material. All are visible, or as appropriate. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is seen by the eye. How is something invisible (<s>anidarśana</s>)? How many invisible things are there? What is the purpose of examining invisibility? By the reverse of visibility, the invisible should be seen. All are invisible, or as appropriate. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self not seen by the eye. How is something resistant (<s>sapratigha</s>)? How many resistant things are there? What is the purpose of examining resistance? What is visible is also resistant. Moreover, resistance should be seen through three causes: by birth, by accumulation, and by being unrefined. There, by birth — whatever mutually obstructs and is obstructed. There, by accumulation — [everything] above the atom. There, by being unrefined — that which is not form subject to the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). Moreover, from the standpoint of the ground of provocation — it is resistant. All are resistant, or as appropriate. (

body.translated_text: How is something with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>)? How many things with outflows are there? What is the purpose of examining [things] with outflows? What has outflows should be seen in terms of the outflow being its own nature, the connection with outflows, the binding by outflows, the conduciveness to outflows, and the succession of outflows. The five <s>upādāna-skandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging) have outflows — fifteen <s>dhātus</s>, ten <s>āyatanas</s>, and a portion of three <s>dhātus</s> and two <s>āyatanas</s>. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is conjoined with outflows. How is something without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>)? How many things without outflows are there? What is the purpose of examining [things] without outflows? By the reverse of having outflows, it is without outflows. The five <s>anupādāna-skandhas</s> (aggregates without clinging), and a portion of three <s>dhātus</s> and two <s>āyatanas</s>. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is separated from outflows. How is something with conflict (<s>saraṇa</s>)? How many things with conflict are there? What is the purpose of examining [things] with conflict? Based on whatever form, through attachment, hatred, and delusion, there arise taking up of weapons, taking up of punishment, quarrels, disputes, conflicts, and contentions — that should be seen as with conflict in terms of its own nature, its connection, its binding, its subsequent binding, its conduciveness, and its succession. As many as have outflows, that many have conflict. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self conjoined with conflict. How is something without conflict (<s>araṇa</s>)? How many things without conflict are there? What is the purpose of examining [things] without conflict? By the reverse of having conflict, it is without conflict. As many as are without outflows, that many are without conflict. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self separated from conflict. How is something with material bait (<s>sāmiṣa</s>)? How many things with material bait are there? What is the purpose of examining [things] with material bait? Based on whatever form, through attachment, hatred, and delusion, one ascertains a renewed existence and self-state — that should be seen as with material bait in terms of its own nature, its connection, its binding, its subsequent binding, its conduciveness, and its succession. As many as have conflict, that many have material bait. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self conjoined with material bait. How is something without material bait (<s>nirāmiṣa</s>)? How many things without material bait are there? What is the purpose of examining [things] without material bait? By the reverse of having material bait, it is without material bait. As many as are without conflict, that many are without material bait. [This is] for the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self separated from material bait. How is something based on craving (<s>gredhāśrita</s>)? How many things based on craving are there? What is the purpose of examining [things] based on craving? children.translated_text: The wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>). How many [types of] wholesome are there? For what purpose is the examination of the wholesome? The wholesome should be viewed from [the perspective of]: intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), association (<s>sambandha</s>), continuation (<s>anubandha</s>), origination (<s>utthāna</s>), ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), attainment through rebirth (<s>upapattilābha</s>), practice (<s>prayoga</s>), veneration (<s>puraskāra</s>), assistance (<s>anugraha</s>), acceptance (<s>parigraha</s>), counteraction (<s>pratipakṣa</s>), pacification (<s>upaśama</s>), and outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>). [It pertains to] a portion of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), ten elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and four sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>). For the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self that is connected with the <s>Dharma</s>. What is the wholesome by intrinsic nature? The eleven mental factors (<s>caitta dharmas</s>) beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). What is the wholesome by association? The phenomena (<s>dharmas</s>) associated with those. What is the wholesome by continuation? The latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of those very [wholesome dharmas]. What is the wholesome by origination? The bodily action (<s>kāyakarma</s>) and verbal action (<s>vākkarma</s>) produced by those. What is the wholesome in the ultimate sense? Suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). What is the wholesome by attainment through rebirth? The ripened fruition (<s>vipākābhinirvṛtti</s>) of such a nature, by virtue of previous habituation of those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — such that inclination naturally and without deliberation abides in those very [dharmas]. What is the wholesome by practice? Coming to associate with true persons (<s>satpuruṣa</s>), hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, proper attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>), practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, and cultivation of the wholesome. What is the wholesome by veneration? Having placed before oneself the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or at a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), or at a manuscript, or at a painting — or having placed before oneself the <s>Dharma</s> — acts of worship at <s>Dharma</s>-supports and manuscripts. What is the wholesome by assistance? Benefiting beings by means of the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>).

children.translated_text: The unwholesome should also be viewed from [the perspective of] opposition (<s>vipakṣa</s>) and obstruction (<s>paripantha</s>). [It pertains to] a portion of the aggregates, ten elements, and four sense-bases. For the purpose of abandoning the clinging to a self connected with non-<s>Dharma</s>. What is the unwholesome by intrinsic nature? Setting aside the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) associated with the mind that pertain to the form and formless realms, it is the other afflictions and secondary afflictions (<s>kleśopakleśa</s>) that produce misconduct. What is the unwholesome by association? The phenomena associated with those very afflictions and secondary afflictions. What is the unwholesome by continuation? The latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of those very [unwholesome dharmas]. What is the unwholesome by origination? The bodily and verbal actions produced [by those]. What is the unwholesome in the ultimate sense? All <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). What is the unwholesome by attainment through rebirth? Just as the ripening through habituation of the unwholesome gives rise to [a rebirth] in which inclination abides only in the unwholesome. What is the unwholesome by practice? Just as, coming to associate with false persons, hearing the untrue <s>Dharma</s>, and improper attention (<s>ayoniśo manaskāra</s>) — one engages in misconduct by body, speech, and mind. What is the unwholesome by veneration? Just as, based on one or another class of deities, one establishes a shrine preceded by harm or preceded by wrong views, or one directs acts of worship there — whereby a great mass of people becomes associated with demerit. What is the unwholesome by harm? Just as one wrongly conducts oneself toward beings by body, speech, and mind. What is the unwholesome by acceptance? For the purpose of abandoning attachment to a self that is not liberated. How is that which is to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśana-prahātavya</s>)? How many things are to be abandoned by seeing? For what purpose is the examination of that which is to be abandoned by seeing? Imagined afflicted views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), the basis of views, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions) that are confused regarding views, the bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> produced by views, and all the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s> leading to lower realms—these should be seen as to be abandoned by seeing. How is that which is to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanā-prahātavya</s>)? How many things are to be abandoned by cultivation? For what purpose is the examination of that which is to be abandoned by cultivation? For one who has attained the path of seeing (<s>darśana-mārga</s>), the <s>dharmas</s> with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) above that, in contrast to what is to be abandoned by seeing. How many things are not to be abandoned? For what purpose is the examination of that which is not to be abandoned? The uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) should be seen as not to be abandoned, except for the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). [It pertains to] a portion of the <s>skandhas</s>, ten <s>dhātus</s>, and four <s>āyatanas</s>. For the purpose of abandoning attachment to a self that is accomplished. How is that which is dependently originated (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>)? How many things are dependently originated? For what purpose is the examination of the dependently originated? The dependently originated should be viewed from [the perspectives of]: characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), division of limbs (<s>aṅga-vibhāga</s>), summary of limbs (<s>aṅga-samāsa</s>), establishment of limbs as conditions (<s>aṅga-pratyayatva-vyavasthāna</s>), establishment of the functions of limbs (<s>aṅga-karma-vyavasthāna</s>), summary of affliction in the limbs (<s>aṅga-saṃkleśa-saṃgraha</s>), meaning (<s>artha</s>), profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>), classification (<s>prabheda</s>), and forward and reverse order (<s>anuloma-pratiloma</s>). For the purpose of abandoning attachment to a self [produced] without cause or from unequal causes. How from [the perspective of] characteristic? By considering that origination is from effortless conditions, from impermanent conditions, and from capable conditions. How from [the perspective of] division of limbs? There are twelve limbs. The twelve-limbed <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) consists of: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), <s>bhava</s> (becoming), <s>jāti</s> (birth), and <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death). How from [the perspective of] summary of limbs? There are projecting limbs (<s>ākṣepaka-aṅga</s>), projected limbs (<s>ākṣipta-aṅga</s>), actualizing limbs (<s>abhinirvartaka-aṅga</s>), and actualized limbs (<s>abhinirvṛtti-aṅga</s>). What are the projecting limbs? <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). What are the projected limbs? <s>Nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), and <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). What are the actualizing limbs? <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), and <s>bhava</s> (becoming). What are the actualized limbs? <s>Jāti</s> (birth) and <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death). How from [the perspective of] establishment of limbs as conditions? children.translated_text: the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). What is the function of the <s>saṃskāras</s>? They distribute beings among the realms of rebirth and serve as conditions for the impregnation of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). What is the function of <s>vijñāna</s>? It maintains the karmic bond of beings and serves as the condition for <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). What is the function of <s>nāmarūpa</s>? It causes beings to grasp a self-existence and serves as the condition for <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense bases). What is the function of <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>? It causes beings to grasp the fulfillment of self-existence and serves as the condition for <s>sparśa</s> (contact). What is the function of <s>sparśa</s>? It engages beings in the enjoyment of objects and serves as the condition for <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). What is the function of <s>vedanā</s>? It engages beings in the enjoyment of births and serves as the condition for <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving). What is the function of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>? It draws beings toward birth and serves as the condition for <s>upādāna</s> (clinging). What is the function of <s>upādāna</s>? For the purpose of taking on rebirth, it makes the consciousness of beings prone to clinging, and serves as the condition for <s>bhava</s> (becoming). What is the function of <s>bhava</s>? It directs beings toward rebirth and serves as the condition for <s>jāti</s> (birth). What is the function of <s>jāti</s>? It produces beings in the sequence of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), and <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), and serves as the condition for <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death). What is the function of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death)? It subjects beings to repeated transformation through aging and transformation of the life-span. How from [the perspective of] summary of affliction in the limbs? <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), and <s>upādāna</s> (clinging)—this is the summary of affliction-contamination (<s>kleśa-saṃkleśa</s>). <s>Saṃskāras</s> (formations), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), and <s>bhava</s> (becoming)—this is the summary of action-contamination (<s>karma-saṃkleśa</s>). The remaining [limbs constitute] the summary of birth-contamination (<s>janma-saṃkleśa</s>). How from [the perspective of] meaning? The meaning of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) is: the meaning of having no agent, the meaning of having causes, the meaning of having no [real] being, the meaning of being other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), the meaning of being stoppable, the meaning of impermanence, the meaning of momentariness, the meaning of the unbroken continuity of cause and effect, the meaning of cause and effect being similar, the meaning of cause and effect being varied, and the meaning of cause and effect being specifically determined. How from [the perspective of] profundity? Profundity should be viewed from [the perspectives of]: profundity of cause, profundity of characteristic, profundity of the aspect of arising, profundity of continuance, and profundity of function. Moreover, dependent origination is momentary yet perceived as continuing; dependent origination has effortless conditions yet is perceived as having capable conditions; dependent origination is without [real] beings yet is perceived as [having] beings. It is not arisen from self, not from another, not from both, and not produced from self-making, other-making, or without cause—hence it is profound. How
[<s>Abhidh-s</s> 28]

children.translated_text: from [the perspective of] classification? Classification should be viewed from [the perspectives of]: classification by arising of consciousness, classification by death and rebirth, classification by growth of external crops, classification by formation and dissolution [of worlds], classification by sustenance through food, classification by division into desirable and undesirable destinies, classification by purification, and classification by power. How from [the perspective of] forward and reverse order? The exposition of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) in forward and reverse order should be viewed from [the perspectives of] forward and reverse order of contamination (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), and forward and reverse order of purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>).
