children.text: ) ekamāyatam // cakṣurdhātuvat śrotradhrāṇajivhākāya rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyabhrātavaḥ // manodhātusaṃgrahe kati skandhāḥ katyāyatanāni / ekaḥ skandha ekamāyatanam // dharmadhātusaṃgrahe kati skandhāḥ katyāyatanāni / trayaḥ skandhā rūpaskandhaikadeśa ekamāyatanam // cakṣurvijñānadhātusaṃgrahe kati skandhāḥ katyāyatanāni vijñānaskandhāmanaāyatanayorekadeśaḥ / cakṣurvijñānavat śrotraghrāṃṇajivhākāyamanovijñānadhātavaḥ // cakṣurāyatanasaṃgrahe kati skandhāḥkati dhātavaḥ / rūpaskandhaikadeśa eko dhātuśca / yathā cakṣurāyatanaṃ tayā śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyarūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāyatanāni // manaāyatanasaṃgrahe kati skandhāḥ kati dhātavaḥ / ekaḥ skandhaḥ sapta dhātavaḥ / dharmāyatanasaṃgrahe katiskandhāḥ kati dhātavaḥ / trayāṇāṃ skandhānā mekadeśa eko dhātuśca // tadvat tadanye dharmāḥ skandhadhātvāyatanairnirdṛśyante anye ca na skandhadhātvāyatanairnirddiśyante / yathā dravyamantaḥ prajñāptimantaḥ saṃvṛtimantaḥ paramārthamanto jñeyā vijñeyā abhijñeyā rūpiṇo 'rūpiṇaḥ sanidarśanā anidarśanā ityevamādayaḥ pūrvaṃ nirdṛṣṭāḥ / (teṣāṃ) yathāyogaṃ skandhadhātvāyatanairitaretarasaṃgraheveditavyaḥ // paramārthasaṃgrahaḥ katamaḥ / skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ tathatāsaṃgrahakuśalaḥ kamanuśaṃsa labhate / ālambane 'bhisaṃkṣepānuśaṃsaṃ pratilabhate / yathā yathā ālambaneṣu cittābhisaṃkṣepaḥ tathā tathā kuśalamūlābhivṛddhiḥ // 0 //

body.text: (atha mahāyānābhidharmasamuccayaśāstre mūlavastuni saṃprayogaparicchedastṛtīyaḥ /)

saṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / samāsataḥ saṃprayogaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / avinirbhāga saṃprayogaḥ miśrībhāva saṃprayogaḥ samavadhānasaṃprayogaḥ sahabhāvasaṃprayogaḥ kṛtyānuṣṭhānasaṃprayogaḥ saṃpratipattisaṃprayogaśca // avinirbhāgasaṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / sarveṣāṃ deśināṃ paramāṇuparyāpannānāṃ rūpāṃśikānāmanyonyamavinirbhāgaḥ // miśrībhāvasaṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / (

children.text: ) paramāṇorūrdhvaṃ sarveṣāṃ deśināṃ rūpāṃśikānāṃ parasparaṃ miśrībhāvaḥ // samavadhānasaṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / deśināmeva samudāyināṃ rūpaparaṃparāyāṃ samavadhānam // sahabhāvasaṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / ekasmin kāye skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ sahakālapravṛttiḥ samamutpatti sthitinirodhāḥ / kṛtyānuṣṭhānasaṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / ekasmin kṛtyāṃnuṣṭhāne parasparaṃ saṃprayogaḥ / yathā dvayorbhikṣvoranyatarabhikṣoḥ kriyānuṣṭhāne anyo 'yaṃ saṃprayogaḥ // saṃpratipatti saṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / cittacaitasikānāmekasminnālambane 'nyonyaṃ saṃpratipattiḥ / sa saṃpratipattisaṃprayogaḥ punaranekārthakaḥ / yathā parabhāvena saṃprayogaḥ na svabhāvena / aviruddhyoḥ saṃprayogo na viruddhayoḥ / sadṛśakālayoḥ saṃprayogo avisadṛśakālayoḥ sabhāgadhātubhūmikayoravisabhāga(dhātu)bhūmikayoḥ // sarvatragasaṃprayogastadyathā vedanā saṃjñācetanāsparśamanaskāra vijñānānām // api khalu kliṣṭasarvatragaḥ saṃprayogo manasi caturṇṇāṃ kleśānām // kādācitkaḥ saṃprayogastadyathā citte śraddhādīnāṃ kuśalānāṃ rāgādīnāṃ ca kleśopakleśānām // āvasthikaḥ saṃprayogaḥ sukhāyā vedanāyāḥ sasaṃprayogāyāḥ / evaṃ duḥkhāyā aduḥkhāsukhāyāḥ // avicchinnaḥ saṃprayogaḥ sacittikāyāmavasthāyām / vicchinnaḥ saṃprayogo 'cittakasamāpattyantaritasya // bahirmukhaḥ saṃprayogo yadbhūyasā kāma pratisaṃyuktānāṃ cittacaitasikānām // antarmukhaḥ saṃprayogaḥ yadbhūyasā samāhitabhūmikānāṃ cittacaitasikānām // ucitaḥ saṃprayogaḥ pārthagjanikānāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ tadekatyānāṃ ca śaikṣāśaikṣāṇām // anucitaḥ saṃprayogaḥ lokottarāṇāṃ cittacaitasikānāmādyataduttarāṇāṃ lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhānāṃ ca // saṃprayogakuśalaḥ kamanuśaṃsaṃ pratilabhate / cittamātre vedanādīnāṃ sāṃkleśikānāṃvyāvadānikānāñca dharmāṇāṃ saṃprayogaṃ jānāti / tacca jānanātmā vedayate saṃjānāti cetayate smarati saṃkliśyate vyavadāyate cetayatya bhiniveśaṃ prajahāti nairātmyamavatarati //

body.text: (athābhidhamasamuccayaśāstre mūlavastuni samanvāgamaparicchedaścaturthaḥ)

samanvāgamaḥ katamaḥ / lakṣaṇataḥ pūrvavat // tatprabhedaḥ punaḥ trividhaḥ / bījasamanvāgamaḥ vaśitāsamanvāgamaḥ samudācārasamanvāgamaśca // vījasamanvāgamaḥ katamaḥ / kāmadhātau jāto bhūtaḥ kāmapratisaṃyuktaiḥ kleśopakleśaiḥ rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktaiśca kleśopakleśairvījasamancāgamena samancāgataḥ upapattiprātilābhikaiśca // kuśalaiḥ // rūpadhātau jāto bhūtaḥ kāmapratisaṃyuktaiḥ klaiśopakleśaiḥ vījasamanvāgamena samanvāgato 'samanvāgataśca vaktavyaḥ / rūpapratisaṃyuktairārūpyapratisaṃyuktaiśca klaiśopakleśaiḥ bījasamanvāgamena samanvāgato 'samanvāgataśca vaktavyaḥ / ārūpyapratisaṃ(yu)ktaiḥ kleśopakleśaiḥ bījasamanvāgamena samanvāgataḥ upapatti(prāti)lābhikaiśca kuśalaiḥ // traidhātu kapratipakṣa lābhī yasya yasya prakārasya pratipakṣa utpannastasya bījasamanvāgamenāsamanvāgataḥ / yasya pratipakṣo notpannastasya bījasamanvāgamena samanvāgataḥ // vaśitāsamanvāgamaḥ katamaḥ / prayogikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vaśitāsamanvāgamena samanvāgataḥ laukikānāṃ lokottarāṇāṃ vā dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyādīnāṃ tadekatyājāṃ(cā) vyākṛtānām // samudācārasamanvāgamaḥ katamaḥ / skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ yo ya eva dharmaḥ saṃmukhībhūtaḥ kuśalo vā akuśalo vā avyākṛto vā tasya samudācārasamanvāgamena samanvāgataḥ // samucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bījasamanvāgamena samanvāgato 'samanvāgataśca vaktavyaḥ // ātyantikaḥ punaḥ saṃkleśasamanvāgamaḥ aparinirvāṇadharmakāṇāmicchantikānāṃ draṣṭavyaḥ / mokṣahetuvaikalyādātyantika eṣāṃ hetvasamanvāgamaḥ // samanvāgamakuśalaḥ kamanuśaṃsaṃ pratilabhate / ācayāpacayajño bhavati dharmāṇām / tathā ācayāpacayajño na kasyāṃ cillaukikyāṃ saṃpattau vipattau vā ekāntikasaṃjñī bhavati yāvadevānunayapratighaprahāṇāya //
abhidharmasamuccaye lakṣaṇasamuccayo nāma prathamaḥ samuccayaḥ //
[athābhidharmasamuccayaśāstre viniścayasamuccaye satyaparicchedaḥ prathamaḥ // ]
viniścayaḥ katamaḥ / satyaviniścayo dharmaviniścayaḥ prāptiviniśca sāṃkathyaviniścayaśca //

satyaviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / catvāyāryasatyāni duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodho mārgaśca / duḥkhasatyaṃ katasat / tatsattvajanmato janmādhiṣṭānataśca veditavyam / sattvajanma katamat / narakasattvajanmatiryakpreteṣu manuṣyeṣu pūrvavideheṣvapagodānīyeṣu jāmbūdvīpeṣu uttareṣu kuruṣu deveṣu caturmā(hā)rājakāyikeṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu yāmeṣu tuṣiteṣu nirmāṇaratiṣu paranirmitavaśavartiṣu brahmapurohiteṣu mahābrāhmeṣuparīttābheṣva (pramāṇābheṣu ābhāsvareṣu parīttaśubheṣva)pramāṇaśubheṣu śubhakṛtsneṣvanabhrakeṣu puṇyaprasaveṣu vṛhatphaleṣva saṃjñisattveṣvabṛheṣvatapeṣu sudṛśeṣu sudarśaneṣvakaniṣṭheṣvākāśānantyāyataneṣu vijñānānantyāyataneṣvākiñcanyāyataneṣu naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyataneṣu //

janmādhiṣṭhānaṃ katamat / bhājanalokaḥ / vāyumaṇḍale apmaṇḍalampratiṣṭhitam / apmaṇḍale pṛthivīmaṇḍalam / pṛthivīmaṇḍale sumeruḥ saptakāñcanaparvatāḥ catvāro dvīpāḥ aṣṭāvantaradvīpāḥ abhyantaraḥ samudro vāhyasamudraścatasraḥ sumerupariṣaṇḍāḥ caturmahārājakāyikānāṃ vāpastriṃśānāṃ sthānāntarāṇi cakracāḍaḥ parvataḥ ākāśe vimānāni yāmānāṃ tuṣitānāṃ nirmāṇaratīnāṃ paranirmitavaśavarttināṃ devānāṃ rūpāvacarāṇāṃ ca asurāṇāṃ sthānāntarāṇi nārakāṇāṃ sthānāntarāṇi / uṣṇanarakāḥśītanarakāḥ pratyekanarakāśca tadekatyānāṃ ca tiryakpretānāṃ sthānāntarāṇi yāvadādityāḥ paricaranto diśo 'vabhāsayante vairocanāstāvatsāhasrake loke sahasraṃ candrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ sūryaṇāṃ sahasraṃ sumerūṇāṃ parvatarājāṇāṃ sahasraṃ caturṇāṃ dvīpānāṃ sahasraṃ caturmahārājakāyikānāṃ devānāṃ sahasraṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sahasraṃ yāmānāṃ sahasraṃ tuṣitānāṃ sahasraṃ nirmāṇaratīnāṃ sahasraṃ paranirmitavaśavarttināṃ sahasraṃ brahmalaukikānāmidamucyate sahasracūḍiko lokadhātuḥ // sahasraṃ sahasracūḍikānāṃ dhātūnāmucyate dvitīyo (

children.text: ) madhyamasāhasro lokadhātuḥ // sahasraṃ madhyamasāhasradhātūnāmucyate tṛtīyo mahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ / evaṃ sa trisāhasro mahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ mahācakravāḍa parvatamaṇḍala pariveṣṭitaḥ / sa ca trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ saprasaṃvarttavivarttaḥ / tathā ca devaḥ cakrākārān vṛṣṭivindūn nirantaraṃ niravacchinna mākāśād varṣati / tathā ca pūrvasyāṃ diśi nirantaraṃ niravacchinna mapramāṇo lokadhātuḥ saṃvarttiṣyate vā vivarttiṣyate vā saṃvarttate vā saṃvṛttastiṣṭhati vā vivarttate vā vivṛttastiṣṭhati vā / yathā pūrvasyāṃ diśi tathā sarvāsu daśasu dikṣu / yaśca sattvaloko yaśca bhājanalokaḥ karmakleśaḥ janitaḥ karmakleśādhipateyaśca sarvamucyate duḥkhasatyam / pariśuddhalokadhātustu na duḥkhasatyasaṃgṛhīḥto na karmakleśa janitaḥ na karmakleśādhipateyaśca / kevalaṃ mahāpraṇidhānena vyavadānakuśalamūlādhipatinā ākṛṣyate tadutpattisthānaṃ cācintyaṃ kevalaṃ buddhena budhyate na dhyāyināṃ dhyānagocaraḥ kiṃ punaḥ cintayatām //

body.text: api khalu duḥkhalakṣaṇaprabhedā aṣṭau / "jātirduḥkhaṃ jarā duḥkhaṃ vyādhiduḥkhaṃ maraṇaṃ duḥkham apriyasaṃprayogo duḥkhaṃ priyaviprayogo duḥkhaṃ yadapīcchanna labhate tadapi duḥkhaṃ saṃkṣiptena pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkham" // jātiḥ kimupādāya duḥkham / saṃbādhaduḥkhatāṃ tadanyaduḥkhāśrayatāṃ copādāya / jarā kimupādāya duḥkham / kāle viparīṇatiduḥkhatāmupādāya // vyādhi kimupādāya duḥkham / bhūteṣu viparīṇatiduḥkhatāmupādāya // maraṇaṃ kimupādāya duḥkham / jīvitavipraṇāśaduḥkhatāmupādāya //

apriyasaṃprayogaḥ kimupādāya duḥkham / saṃyogaja duḥkhatāmupādāya // priyaviprayogaḥ kimupādāya duḥkham / viprayogaja duḥkhatāmupadāya // yadapīcchanna labhate tat kimupādāya duḥkham / kāmyaphalābhāvaja duḥkhatāmupādāya // saṃkṣiptenapañcopādānaskandhāḥ kimupādāya duḥkham / dauṣṭhulyaduḥkhatāmupādāya // evamaṣṭau saṃgṛhītāni ṣaḍ bhavanti / saṃvādhaduḥkhaṃ vipariṇati duḥkhaṃ saṃprayogaduḥkhaṃ viprayogaduḥkhaṃ kāmyaphalābhāvaduḥkhaṃ dauṣṭhulyaduḥkhaṃ ca // evaṃ ṣaḍ bāhulyenāṣṭau bhavanti / (

children.text: ) ṣaḍ samānānyaṣṭau bhavanti // yaduktaṃ tisro duḥkhatāḥ / tāsu aṣṭau duḥkhāni saṃgṛhitāni bhavanti / tatra kathaṃ tisṛṣu saṃgṛhītānyaṣṭau aṣṭasu vā saṃgṛhītāstisraḥ / pāraṃparṣalakṣaṇa saṃgrahāt / jātirdukhaṃ jarā duḥkhaṃ vyādhirduḥkhaṃ maraṇaṃ duḥkham apriyasaṃprayogo duḥkhamiti santānaduḥkhaduḥkhatā / priyaviprayogo duḥkhaṃ yadapīcchanna labhate tadapi duḥkhaṃ tadvipariṇāmaduḥkhatā / saṃkṣiptena pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhaṃ tat saṃskāraduḥkhatā // yaduktaṃ dvividhe duḥkhe iti / tat saṃvṛtisatyena duḥkhaṃ paramārthasatyena duḥkhaṃ ca / katamat saṃvṛtisatyena duḥkhaṃ katamat paramārthasatyena duḥkham / jātirduḥkhaṃ yāvat yadapīcchann labhate tadapi duḥkhamiti saṃvṛtisatyena duḥkham / yaduktaṃ saṃkṣiptena pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhamiti paramārthasatyena duḥkham //

body.text: duḥkhasatyasya sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / anityalakṣaṇaṃ duḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ śūnyalakṣaṇamanātmalakṣaṇaṃ ca // anityalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / samāsato dvādaśavidham / asallakṣaṇaṃ vināśalakṣaṇaṃ vipariṇatilakṣaṇaṃ viyogalakṣaṇaṃ sannihitalakṣaṇaṃdharmatālakṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇalakṣaṇaṃ prabandhalakṣaṇaṃ vyādhyādi lakṣaṇaṃ cittacittākāravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ bhogasaṃpattirvipatti lakṣaṇaṃ bhājanalokasaṃvarttavivarttalakṣaṇam // asallakṣaṇaṃ katamat / skandhadhātvāyataneṣu sarvakāli kātmātmīyatā nityābhāvaḥ // vināśalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / saṃskārāṇāmutpannānāṃ nirodhaḥ / taktālaṃ bhūtvābhāvaḥ // vipariṇatilakṣaṇaṃ katamat / saṃskārāṇāmanyathābhāvaḥ / prabandhāsādṛśyena pravṛttiḥ // viyogalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / saṃskāreṣu vaśitvabhraṃśaḥ paraiḥsvīkaraṇaṃ vā / sannihitalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / samupasthitānityatā / yattadānīmevānubhūyamānānityatā // dharmatālakṣaṇaṃ katamat / āgāminyanityatā / yāmāvaśyamanubhaviṣyati // kṣaṇalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / saṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇādūrddhamanavasthānam // prabandhalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / anādimati saṃskāre utpannaniruddhā nāṃ prabandhāprahāṇam // vyadhyādi lakṣaṇa katamat / (

children.text: ) caturṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ kālopabhogaḥ jīvitavipariṇāmaḥ / cittacittākāra vṛttilakṣaṇaṃ katamat / kadācit sārāgaṃ cittaṃ saṃbhavati kadācid vītarāgaṃ cittaṃ saṃbhavati / yadvat sadveṣaṃ vā vītadveṣaṃ vā samohaṃ vā vītamohaṃ vā saṃkṣiptaṃ vā vihisāṃ vā nimnaṃ vā unnataṃ vā uddhataṃ vā anuddhataṃ vā upaśāntaṃ vā anupaśāntaṃ vā samāhita vā asamāhitaṃ vā / evamādi cittasaṃsāravṛttiḥ // bhogasaṃpattivipatti lakṣaṇaṃ katamat / saṃpattīnāmante vipattirvināśaḥ / bhājanalokasaṃvartta vivartta lakṣaṇaṃ katamat / agnyambuvāyubhistrividhaḥ saṃvarttavivarttaḥ / tisṛṇāṃ saṃvarttarnānāṃ śīrṣāṇi dvitīya tṛtīya caturthadhyānāni / caturthadhyāne vāhyānāṃ vimānānāṃ tu vāhyābhāvat eva saṃvarttavivarttaḥ / kevalaṃ tairdevaiḥ tāni vimānāni saha nirvarttante saha nirudhyante etaducyate saṃvartta vivarttaḥ // api khalu trayo 'ntarakalpāḥ durbhikṣavyādhiśastrairbhavanti / hīnasya trividhakalpāsyānte taiḥ śastrādibhirniryāṇaṃ bhavati / yadālokadhātuḥ saṃvṛtto bhavati / eko 'ntarakalpa prathamaḥ apakarṣaḥ / ekāntarakalpaḥ paścima utkarṣaḥ / aṣṭādaśa antarakalpā utkarṣāpakaya / evaṃ ca viṃśatimantarakalpān lokadhātuḥ saṃvarttate / viṃśatimātarakalpāt lokadhāturvivarttate / viṃśatimantarakalpān lokadhāturvivṛttastiṣṭhati / saṃkalikāścaite 'śītirantarakalpā eko mahākalpo bhavati / tayā kalpasaṃkhyāyā rūpārūpyācarāṇāṃ devānāmāyuḥpramāṇaṃ varṇyate // yaduktam anyatare, sattvā āyuḥkṣayād vā puṇya kṣayād vā karmakṣayād vā tasmādadhiṣṭhānāt cyavante iti / tatra āyudāyaḥ katamaḥ / kāle maraṇam / puṇyakṣayaḥ katamaḥ / akāle maraṇam apuṇyamaraṇam / yena sattvā āsvāda samāpattyāṃ rajyante / puṇyakṣayācca hetoḥ te jīvitāccyavante / karmakṣayaḥ katamaḥ / upapadyavedanīyakarmaṇaḥ aparaparyāvedanīyakarmaṇaśca ubhayo kṣayānmaraṇa /

body.text: duḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / tisro duḥkhatāḥ aṣṭākā vā duḥkhaṃ ṣaḍākāraṃ vā (

children.text: ) duḥkhaṃ bāhulyena pūrvamuktaṃ tad duḥkhaṃ nāma / kiṃ pratītyasūtre uktaṃ yadanityaṃ tad duḥkhamiti / ubhayāṃśikīmanityatāṃ pratītya duḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ prajñāyate / utpādāṃśikīmanityatāṃ pratītya duḥkhaduḥkhatā prajñāyate / vyayāṃśikīmanityatāṃ pratītya vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā prajñāyate / ubhayāṃśīkimanityatāṃ pratītya saṃskāraduḥkhatā prajñāyate // tathā ca saṃskārānityatāṃ saṃskāravipariṇāmatāṃ ca saṃdhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā mayā yatkiṃcid veditamidamatra duḥkhasyeti // api khalu utpādavyayadharmadvayānugateṣu saṃskāreṣu jātyādayo 'ṣṭau duḥkhāni / prajñāyante ityabhisaṃdhāya buddhena bhāṣitaṃ yadanityaṃ tad duḥkhamiti / api ca anityeṣu saṃskāreṣu jātyādikaṃ duḥkhaṃ prajñāyate iti anityato duḥkhaṃ na sarve saṃskārā ityatrādhisandhirveditavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) has been extensively described before. What is that suffering? What was stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering'? Depending on both aspects of impermanence, the characteristic of suffering is discerned. Depending on the aspect of impermanence related to arising, the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>) is discerned. Depending on the aspect of impermanence related to decay, the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>) is discerned. Depending on both aspects of impermanence, the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>) is discerned. And thus, with reference to the impermanence and changeability of conditioned phenomena (<s>saṃskāra</s>), the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Whatever is experienced, that is within suffering.' Furthermore, it should be understood that the <s>Buddha</s> spoke 'whatever is impermanent, that is suffering' with the intention that in conditioned phenomena governed by the duality of arising and decay, the eight sufferings beginning with birth (<s>jāti</s>) are discerned. Moreover, [the statement] that suffering is discerned from impermanent conditioned phenomena beginning with birth means that suffering [is discerned] from impermanence — the implicit meaning here should be understood as not [implying] that all conditioned phenomena [are identical with suffering].

body.text: śūnyatālakṣaṇaṃ katamat / teṣu tasya abhāvaḥ / anena nayena samanupaśyanāśūnyatā / punaḥ teṣu anyasya bhāvaḥ / anena nayena yathābhūtajñānabhāvaḥ / etad vatāraśūnyatocyate / yathābhūtajñānamaviparīto 'rthaḥ / teṣu abhāvaḥ katamaḥ / skandhadhātvāyataneṣu nityadhruvakūṭasthāvipariṇāmadharmātmātmīyābhāvaḥ / anena nayena teṣāṃ śūnyatā / teṣu anyasya bhāvaḥ katamaḥ / te ṣveva nairātmyam / tacca ātmano nāstitā anātmano 'stitā satī śūnyatā // etadabhisaṃdhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā sato yathābhūtajñānaṃ bhāvaḥ / asato yathābhūtajñānamabhāvaḥ // api khalu trividhā śūnyatā / svabhāvaśūnyatā tathābhāvaśūnyatā prakṛtiśūnyatā ca / ādyā parikalpitā draṣṭavyā / tṛtīyā pariniṣpannasvabhāvā draṣṭavyā //
body.translated_text: What is the characteristic of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>)? The absence of that [self] in those [aggregates, etc.]. By this method, one contemplates emptiness. Furthermore, the existence of something else in those [aggregates]. By this method, there is knowledge of things as they truly are (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>). This is called the entrance to emptiness. Knowledge of things as they truly are is the non-erroneous meaning. What is the absence in those? In the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), the absence of a permanent, eternal, unchanging, immutable self (<s>ātman</s>) and what belongs to self (<s>ātmīya</s>). By this method, their emptiness. What is the existence of something else in those? In those very [aggregates, etc.], selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>). And that is: the non-existence of self and the existence of non-self — this being emptiness. With this intention the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Knowledge of things as they truly are regarding what exists is existence; knowledge of things as they truly are regarding what does not exist is non-existence.' Furthermore, emptiness is threefold: emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of that state (<s>tathābhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and emptiness of primordial nature (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>). The first should be regarded as the imagined [nature] (<s>parikalpita</s>). The third should be regarded as the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>).

body.text: anātmalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yathātmavāde sthitasya ātmalakṣaṇasya skandhadhātvāyataneṣu (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 41]

children.text: ) tallakṣaṇasyābhāvaḥ / skandhadhātvāyataneṣu ātmalakṣaṇābhāvatāmupādāya / idamucyate anātmalakṣaṇam // etadabhisaṃghāyoktaṃ bhagavatā sarve dharmā anātmāna iti // api coktaṃ bhagavatā naitat sarvaṃ mama naiṣo 'hamasmi na me sa ātmā iti / evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ saṃprajñāya draṣṭhavyam iti tasya ko 'rtha uktaḥ / bahirdhāvastabhisaṃdhāyoktaṃ naitat sarvaṃ mameti / kuta etat / bahirdhāvastuni kalpitātmīyalakṣaṇam / ataḥ ātmīyaniṣkarṣaṇam / adhyātmavastuni parikalpitātmātmīyalakṣaṇam / ata ātmātmīyobhayaniṣkarṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: the absence of that characteristic. Based on the absence of the characteristic of self in the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, this is called the characteristic of non-self (<s>anātmalakṣaṇa</s>). With this intention the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without self.' Moreover, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'All this is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self' — thus should one see it as it truly is with correct understanding. What is the meaning of that? It was said with reference to external objects: 'All this is not mine.' Why is this? Because in external objects there is the imagined characteristic of 'mine.' Therefore, the extraction of [the notion of] 'mine.' In internal objects there is the imagined characteristic of both self and 'mine.' Therefore, the extraction of both self and 'mine.'

body.translated_text: What is the characteristic of non-self (<s>anātman</s>)? For one established in the doctrine of self (<s>ātmavāda</s>), the characteristic attributed to self, in the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>),

body.text: pūrvamuktam anityaṃ kṣaṇalakṣaṇamiti / tat kathaṃ jñāyate / yathā cittacaitasikānāṃ kṣaṇikatā tathā rūpādīnāmapi kṣaṇikatā draṣṭavyā / cittopāttatāmupādāya cittaikayogakṣematāmupādāya cittavikāratadvikāratāmupādāya cittāśrayatāmudāpādāya cittādhipatyasaṃbhūtatāmupādāya cittvaśavarttināṃ copādāya // api khalu atyantavikāropālabdhitāmupādāya utpannasya cānapekṣya pratyayaṃ svarasavināśitāmupādāya rūpasyāpi kṣaṇikatā draṣṭavyā //
body.translated_text: It was previously stated that impermanence has the characteristic of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇa</s>). How is that known? Just as the momentariness of mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>) [is established], so too should the momentariness of material form (<s>rūpa</s>) and so forth be understood — based on their being taken up by mind, based on their sharing a common fate with mind, based on their transformation following the transformation of mind, based on their being the support of mind, based on their arising through the dominion of mind, and based on their being subject to the power of mind. Furthermore, the momentariness of material form should be understood based on the apprehension of its constant transformation, and based on the self-disintegration of what has arisen without depending on [further] conditions.

body.text: yaduktaṃ yatkiṃcidrūpaṃ sarvantaccatvāri mahābhūtāni catvāri ca mahābhūtānyupādāyeti / tatkiṃ sandhāyoktam / saṃbhavaṃ sandhāyoktam / ekadeśāśrayībhāvārtha upādāyārthaḥ // yatra punaḥ samudāye yadbhūtamupalabhyate tattatrā stiti vaktavya / (asti ekabhautikaḥ asti dvibhautikaḥ) asti yāvatsārvabhautikaḥ / upādāyarūpe 'pi yadupādāyarūpaṃ yasmin samudāya upalabhyate tattatrāstīti veditavyam // yatpunarūcyate paramāṇusaṃcitto rūpa samudāya iti tatra niḥśarīraḥ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 42]

children.text: ) paramāṇurveditavyaḥ / buddhyā paryantaprabhedatastu paramāṇuvyavasthānaṃ piṇḍasaṃjñāvibhāghanatāmupādāya rūpe dravyāḥ pariniṣpattipraveśatāṃ copādāya //
children.translated_text: incorporeal. The designation of atoms is [established] through the ultimate analysis by the intellect, based on the dissolution of the notion of mass (<s>piṇḍasaṃjñā</s>) regarding material form, and based on entering into the true nature of substance (<s>dravya</s>).

body.translated_text: As stated: 'Whatever material form there is, all that is the four great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) and [material form] derived from the four great elements.' With what intention was this said? It was said with reference to origination. The meaning of 'derived' (<s>upādāya</s>) is the sense of being a partial support. Where, furthermore, in a given aggregate a given element is found, it should be said that it exists therein. There are some [forms] with one element, some with two elements, and so on up to those with all elements. Regarding derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) too, whatever derived form is found in whatever aggregate, it should be understood as existing therein. As for the statement that material aggregation is composed of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), therein the atom is to be understood as

body.text: tat punaretad duḥkhamasti vipulamasaṃlikhitaṃ saṃlikhitaṃ saṃlikhitā saṃlikhitaṃ ca // asti madhyamasaṃlikhitam asti tanukamasaṃlikhitam asti tanuttaraṃ saṃlikhitam asti tanutamaṃ saṃlikhitam astyaduḥkhaṃ duḥkhapratibhāsaṃ mahāsaṃlekhapratyupasthānaṃ ca // katamadvipulaṃ duḥkhamasaṃlikhitam / yatkāmāvacaramanupacitakuśalamūlānām // katamatsaṃlikhitam / tadevotpannamokṣabhāgīyānām // katamatsaṃlikhitāsaṃlikhitam / tadeva laukikavairāgyāyāvaropitakuśalamūlānām // katamanmadhyamasaṃlikhitam / rūpadhātūpapannānāṃ vivarjitamokṣabhāgīyānām / katamattanukamasaṃlikhitam // ārūpyopapannānāṃ vivarjitamokṣabhāgīyānām // katamattanuttaraṃ saṃlikhitam / yacchaikṣāṇām // katamattanutamaṃ saṃlikhitam / yadaśaikṣāṇāṃ jīvitendriyapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam // katamadaduḥkhaṃ duḥkhapratibhāsaṃ mahāsaṃlekhapratyupasthānam / yatpāramiprāptānāṃ bodhisattvānāmacintya bhavopapattiṣu //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, this suffering is [classified as follows]: there is extensive and unmitigated, mitigated, mitigated-and-unmitigated. There is moderate-unmitigated, there is slight-unmitigated, there is slighter-mitigated, there is slightest-mitigated, and there is non-suffering that appears as suffering with the presentation of great mitigation. What is extensive and unmitigated suffering? That of beings in the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) who have not accumulated roots of wholesome [conduct]. What is mitigated? That same [suffering] of those in whom the portion leading to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>) has arisen. What is mitigated-and-unmitigated? That same [suffering] of those who have planted roots of wholesome [conduct] for worldly dispassion (<s>laukikavairāgya</s>). What is moderate-unmitigated? That of those reborn in the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) who are devoid of the portion leading to liberation. What is slight-unmitigated? That of those reborn in the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>) who are devoid of the portion leading to liberation. What is slighter-mitigated? That of learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>). What is slightest-mitigated? That of non-learners (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) — the six sense-bases conditioned by the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>). What is non-suffering that appears as suffering with the presentation of great mitigation? That of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have reached perfection (<s>pāramiprāpta</s>) in their inconceivable rebirths in existence.

body.text: yaduktaṃ maraṇaṃ duḥkhamiti / tatra maraṇaṃ trividham / kuśalacittasyāvyākṛtacittasya ca // paṭuke cittaprakāre svakuśala mūlabalādhānato (vā) paropasaṃhārato vā kuśalacittasya maraṇaṃ draṣṭavyam // paṭuka eva cittaprakāre svākuśalamulabalādhā nato vā paropasaṃhārato vā akuśalacittasya maraṇaṃ draṣṭavyam // paṭuke vā cittaprakāre apaṭuke vā tadubhayavai kalyādabhisaṃskārāsamarthasya vā avyākṛtacittasya maraṇaṃ draṣṭavyam // śubhakāriṇaḥ adhaḥkāya statprathamataḥ śītībhavati // aśubhakāriṇaḥ punaḥ ūrdhvaṃkāyaḥ śītībhavati // tatrāśubhakāriṇo 'ntarābhavo 'bhinirvarttate / tadyathā kṛṣṇasya kutapasya nirbhāso 'ndhakāratamisrāyā vā rātryāḥ // aśubhakāriṇastadyathā śuklasya parasya nirbhāsajyotsnāyā vā rātryāḥ / antarābhava(ḥ) kāmadhātau rūpadhātau copapadyamānasyārūpadhātoścayamānasya / (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 43]

children.text: ) sa ca manomayo gandharva ityapi / paraṃ saptāhaṃ tiṣṭhatyantareṇa cyavate / ekadā ca vyāvarttate / tatrasthaśca karmopacinoni sabhāgāṃśca sattvān paśyati / yatra copapadyate tadākṛtirapratihatagatiśca / ṛddhimāniva vāśugāmī upapattyāyatane pratihanyate / upapattyāyatane tulāvanāmonnāmayogena cyavate pratisandhi ca vadhnāti / antarābhavasthaścopapattyāyatane rāgamutpādayati / yadanyaśca kleśaḥ pratyayo bhavati / saharāgeṇāntarābhavo nirudhyate kalalaṃ ca savijñānakamutpadyate // sa ca vipākastata ūrdhvamindriyābhinrivṛttiḥ yathā pratityasamutpāde catṛsṛṣvāyoniṣu / aṇḍajāyāṃ jarayujāyāṃ saṃsvedajāyāmupapadukāyañca // 0 //
children.translated_text: and that [intermediate being] is mind-made (<s>manomaya</s>), also called a <s>gandharva</s>. It lasts at most seven days, after which it passes away. And it changes at once. While in that state, it accumulates <s>karma</s> and sees beings of a similar class. It has the form of the place where it will be reborn, and its movement is unobstructed, like one endowed with supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), swift-going, [until] it is blocked at the place of rebirth. At the place of rebirth, it passes away and takes rebirth through the process of descending and ascending, like a balance. While in the intermediate state, it generates attachment toward the place of rebirth, and whatever other affliction (<s>kleśa</s>) serves as a condition. Together with attachment, the intermediate existence ceases, and the embryonic form (<s>kalala</s>) endowed with consciousness arises. And that is the fruition (<s>vipāka</s>); from then onward is the development of the sense faculties, as [described] in dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) regarding the four types of birth: egg-born (<s>aṇḍaja</s>), womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>), moisture-born (<s>saṃsvedaja</s>), and spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>).

body.translated_text: As stated: 'Death (<s>maraṇa</s>) is suffering.' Therein, death is threefold: [death] with a wholesome mind and with an indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) mind. In a clear state of mind, death with a wholesome mind should be understood as occurring either through the strength of one's own roots of wholesome [conduct] or through the assistance of others. In that same clear state of mind, death with an unwholesome mind should be understood as occurring either through the strength of one's own roots of unwholesome [conduct] or through the influence of others. In either a clear or unclear state of mind, death with an indeterminate mind should be understood for one who is incapable of either [wholesome or unwholesome] volitional formations (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>), due to the absence of both. For one who performs wholesome deeds, the lower body grows cold first. For one who performs unwholesome deeds, the upper body grows cold first. Therein, for the unwholesome doer, the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) manifests like the appearance of dark wool, or like a dark, gloomy night. For the unwholesome [wrongly transcribed — should be wholesome] doer, it is like the appearance of white cloth, or like a moonlit night. The intermediate existence [arises] for one being reborn in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) and the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), and for one passing away from the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>),

body.text: (atha viniścaye satyaparicchede pratheme dvitīyo bhāgaḥ)
body.translated_text: (Now, in the Ascertainment [section], in the chapter on Truths, the second part.)

body.text: samudayasatyaṃ katamat / kleśaḥ kleśādhipateyañca karma // prādhānyanirddeśastu (? śāstu) bhagavatā tṛṣṇā paunarbhavikī nandīrāgasahagatā tatra tatrābhinandinī samudayasatyanirdeśena nirdiṣṭā // prādhānyārthaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ sarvatragārthaḥ // sarvatragārthaḥ katamaḥ / tatha hi tṛṣṇā vastusarvatragā avasthāsarvatragā adhvasarvatragā dhātusarvatragā eṣaṇā sarvatragā prakārasarvatragā ca keśaḥ katamaḥ / parisaṃkhyānato 'pi lakṣaṇato 'pyutthāna to 'pyālambanato 'pi saṃprayogato 'pi paryāyato 'pi vipratipattito 'pi dhatuto 'pi nikāyato 'pi prahāṇato 'pi kleśo draṣṭavyaḥ // parisaṃkhyānaṃ katamat // ṣaṭ kleśā daśa vā // ṣaṭ kleśāḥ katamat / rāgaḥ pratigho māno 'vidyā vicikitsā dṛṣṭiśca // ta eva dṛṣṭeḥ pañcākārjabhedena daśa bhavanti // lakṣaṇaṃ katamat / yo dharma utpadyamāno 'praśāntalakṣaṇa utpadyamānena yena kāya cittaprabandhāpraśamapravṛttiḥ / idaṃ kleśalakṣaṇam / utthānaṃ katamat / kleśānuśayaścāprahīṇo bhavati kleśasthānīyaśca dharma ābhāsagato bhavati / tatra ca ayoniśo manaskāraḥ pratyavasthito bhavati / evaṃ kleśa utpadyate / idamucyate utthānam // ālambanaṃ katamat sarvakleśaprayogaḥ // sarvakleśālambanaṃ sarvakleśavastvālambanaṃ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 44]

children.text: ) ca / api khalu kāmāvacaraḥ kleśaḥ sthāpayitvā avidyā dṛṣṭi vicikitsāṃ ca tadanyaḥ urdhvabhūmyanālambanaḥ / ūrdhvabhūmikaḥ kleśaḥ adhobhūmyanālambanaḥ / tadbhūmito vītarāgatvāt / nirodhamārgasatyā lambanaḥ kleśo nirodhamargālambanānabhiśliṣṭaḥ / tatparikalpastvasyālambanamityucyate // kleśaḥ punardvividhaḥ / avastukālambanaḥ savastukālambanaśca // avastukālambanaḥ katamaḥ dṛṣṭayo dṛṣṭisaṃprayuktāśca dharmāḥ // tadanyaḥ savastukālambana ityucyate //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the affliction belonging to the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>), excluding ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), does not take the higher realms as its object. The affliction of the higher realms does not take the lower realms as its object, because there is freedom from passion (<s>vītarāgatva</s>) with respect to that realm. The affliction that takes cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) and the path (<s>mārga</s>) as its object does not cling to cessation and the path as its object; because it is a mere conceptual construction (<s>parikalpana</s>), it is said to be its object. Furthermore, affliction is of two kinds: that which has a non-existent thing as its object, and that which has an existent thing as its object. Which has a non-existent thing as its object? Views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) and <s>dharmas</s> associated with views. The other is said to have an existent thing as its object.

body.translated_text: What is the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>)? It is the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and <s>karma</s> governed by afflictions. However, as a primary indication, the Blessed One has declared with the exposition of the truth of origination: "It is <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, finding pleasure here and there." What is the meaning of primacy? That which is all-pervasive (<s>sarvatraga</s>). What is all-pervasive? For <s>tṛṣṇā</s> is all-pervasive with respect to objects (<s>vastu</s>), all-pervasive with respect to states (<s>avasthā</s>), all-pervasive with respect to time periods (<s>adhvan</s>), all-pervasive with respect to realms (<s>dhātu</s>), all-pervasive with respect to seeking (<s>eṣaṇā</s>), and all-pervasive with respect to modes. What is an affliction (<s>kleśa</s>)? The affliction should be viewed from [the perspective of]: enumeration (<s>parisaṃkhyāna</s>), characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), arising (<s>utthāna</s>), object (<s>ālambana</s>), association (<s>saṃprayoga</s>), synonyms (<s>paryāya</s>), misconception (<s>vipratipatti</s>), realm (<s>dhātu</s>), class (<s>nikāya</s>), and abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>). What is the enumeration? There are six or ten afflictions. What are the six afflictions? Desire (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and wrong views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). These same become ten through the fivefold division of views. What is the characteristic? Whatever <s>dharma</s>, when arising, has the characteristic of non-tranquility, [and] through its arising there is the occurrence of non-pacification of the continuum of body and mind — this is the characteristic of an affliction. What is the arising? The latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) of the affliction is unabandoned, and the <s>dharma</s> that serves as the basis for the affliction comes into the field [of awareness], and therein improper attention (<s>ayoniśo manaskāra</s>) is present — thus the affliction arises; this is called arising. What is the object? [It is] the engagement of all afflictions. The object of all afflictions is the object-basis of all afflictions,

body.text: saṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / rāgaḥ pratighena na saṃprayujyate / pratighavadvicikitsayāpi na saṃprayujyate / śiṣṭeṣu saṃprayogo labhyate // yathā rāgastathā pratigho 'pi draṣṭavyaḥ // pratigho rāgeṇa mānena dṛṣṭyā ca na saṃprayujyate // mānaḥ pratighena vicikitsayā ca na saṃprayujyate // avidyā dvividhā / sarvakleśasaṃprayuktā avidyā / asāmānyā avidyā / asāmānya avidyā katamā / satyeṣvajñānam // dṛṣṭiḥ pratighena vicikitsayā ca na saṃprayujyate // krodhādaya upakleśā anyo 'nyaṃ na saṃprayujyante // āhrīkyamanapatrāpyaṃ ca sarvatrākuśale sāmānyena saṃprayujyete // styānamauddhatyamāśraddhyaṃ kausīdyaṃ pramādaśca sarvatra kliṣṭe saṃprayujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the association (<s>saṃprayoga</s>)? Desire (<s>rāga</s>) is not associated with aversion (<s>pratigha</s>). Like aversion, it is also not associated with doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>). Association is obtained with the rest. As with desire, so aversion should also be viewed. Aversion is not associated with desire, pride (<s>māna</s>), or views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). Pride is not associated with aversion or doubt. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is of two kinds: ignorance associated with all afflictions, and uncommon ignorance. What is uncommon ignorance? It is non-knowledge regarding the [Four Noble] Truths. Views are not associated with aversion or doubt. The secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>) such as anger (<s>krodha</s>) and the rest are not mutually associated with one another. Shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) are generally associated with everything unwholesome. Torpor (<s>styāna</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), lack of faith (<s>āśraddhya</s>), laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), and heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) are associated with everything afflicted.

body.text: paryāyaḥ katamaḥ / sarvakleśā nānārthāśrayā nānavasthāḥ paryāyāḥ / saṃyojanaṃ bandhanaṃ anuśayaḥ upakleśaḥ paryavasthānam oghaḥ yogaḥ upādānam granthaḥ nivaraṇam khilaḥ malaḥ nighaḥ śalyaḥ kiṃcanaḥ duścaritam āsravaḥ vighātaḥ paridāhaḥ raṇaḥ jvaraḥ vanasaḥ vibandhaḥ //
body.translated_text: What are the synonyms (<s>paryāya</s>)? All afflictions, based on different meanings and different states, have [the following] synonyms: fetter (<s>saṃyojana</s>), bond (<s>bandhana</s>), latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>), secondary affliction (<s>upakleśa</s>), entanglement (<s>paryavasthāna</s>), flood (<s>ogha</s>), yoke (<s>yoga</s>), clinging (<s>upādāna</s>), knot (<s>grantha</s>), hindrance (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>), rigidity (<s>khila</s>), impurity (<s>mala</s>), obstruction (<s>nigha</s>), thorn (<s>śalya</s>), attachment (<s>kiṃcana</s>), misconduct (<s>duścarita</s>), outflow (<s>āsrava</s>), impediment (<s>vighāta</s>), burning (<s>paridāha</s>), strife (<s>raṇa</s>), fever (<s>jvara</s>), thicket (<s>vana</s>), and constriction (<s>vibandha</s>).

body.text: saṃyojanāni kati kathaṃ saṃyojanaṃ kutra saṃyojanam / saṃyojanāni nava / anunayasaṃyojanam pratighasaṃyojanam mānasaṃyojanam avidyāsaṃyojanam dṛṣṭisaṃyojanam parāmarśasaṃyojanam vicikitsāsaṃyojanam īrṣyāsaṃyojanam mātsaryasaṃyojanaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: How many fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) are there? How does one become fettered? Where does one become fettered? There are nine fetters: the fetter of attachment (<s>anunayasaṃyojana</s>), the fetter of aversion (<s>pratighasaṃyojana</s>), the fetter of pride (<s>mānasaṃyojana</s>), the fetter of ignorance (<s>avidyāsaṃyojana</s>), the fetter of views (<s>dṛṣṭisaṃyojana</s>), the fetter of clinging to [wrong] views (<s>parāmarśasaṃyojana</s>), the fetter of doubt (<s>vicikitsāsaṃyojana</s>), the fetter of jealousy (<s>īrṣyāsaṃyojana</s>), and the fetter of miserliness (<s>mātsaryasaṃyojana</s>).

body.text: anunayasaṃyojanaṃ katamat / traidhātuko rāgaḥ / anunayasaṃprayojanena saṃprayuktaḥ traidhātukaṃ nodvejayati / anudvegena kuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalāsamudācāraśca / tena āyatyāṃ duḥkhābhinivṛtto duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the fetter of attachment (<s>anunayasaṃyojana</s>)? It is desire (<s>rāga</s>) pertaining to the three realms. One who is bound by the fetter of attachment does not become disenchanted with the three realms. Due to non-disenchantment, there is engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.text: pratighasaṃyojanaṃ katamat / sattveṣu duḥkhe duḥkhasthānīyeṣu na dharmeṣu cittasya vihiṃsā / pratighasaṃyojanena saṃprayukto pratighanimitteṣu cittaṃ nopekṣate / anupekṣayā ca akuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalāsamudācāraśca / tena āyatyāṃ laukikaduḥkhābhinivṛttau duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the fetter of aversion (<s>pratighasaṃyojana</s>)? It is the hostility of mind toward beings, toward suffering, and toward <s>dharmas</s> that are bases of suffering. One who is bound by the fetter of aversion does not maintain equanimity toward objects that provoke aversion. Due to non-equanimity, there is engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward worldly suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.text: mānasaṃyojanaṃ katamat / sapta mānāḥ / māno 'timāno mānatimāno 'smimāno 'bhimāna ūnamāno mithyāmānaśca / mānaḥ katamaḥ / hīnān śreyānasmi (a) sadṛśena sadṛśo 'smīti vā yā cittasyonnatiḥ / atimānaḥ katamaḥ / sadṛśāt śreyānasmi śreyasā sadṛśo 'smīti vā yā cittasyonnatiḥ / mānātimānaḥ katamaḥ / śreyasaḥ śreyānasmīti yā cittasyonnatiḥ / asmimānaḥ katamaḥ / pañcasūpādānaskandheṣvātmātmīyābhiniveśādyā cittasyonnatiḥ / abhimānaḥ katamaḥ / aprāpta uttare viśeṣā dhigame prāpto mayeti yā cittasyonnatiḥ / ūnamānaḥ katamaḥ / vahvantaraviśiṣṭādalpāntarahīno 'smīti yā cittasyonnatiḥ / mithyāmānaḥ katamaḥ / aguṇavato guṇavānasmīti yā cittasyonnatiḥ / mānasaṃyojanena saṃprayukta ātmātmīyau na saṃjānāti / asaṃjñānāt ātmātmīyagrahaḥ akuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalā samudācāraśca / tenāyatyāṃ duḥkhābhinivṛttau duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the fetter of pride (<s>mānasaṃyojana</s>)? There are seven kinds of pride (<s>māna</s>): pride (<s>māna</s>), excessive pride (<s>atimāna</s>), pride upon pride (<s>mānātimāna</s>), the pride of 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>), conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>), self-deprecating pride (<s>ūnamāna</s>), and perverse pride (<s>mithyāmāna</s>). What is pride? It is the mind's elation [thinking] 'I am superior to the inferior' or 'I am equal to the equal.' What is excessive pride? It is the mind's elation [thinking] 'I am superior to the equal' or 'I am equal to the superior.' What is pride upon pride? It is the mind's elation [thinking] 'I am superior to the superior.' What is the pride of 'I am'? It is the mind's elation due to the clinging to a self and what belongs to a self in the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>). What is conceit? It is the mind's elation [thinking] 'I have attained it' when one has not attained a superior distinctive realization. What is self-deprecating pride? It is the mind's elation [thinking] 'I am only slightly inferior' to one who is far superior. What is perverse pride? It is the mind's elation [thinking] 'I am virtuous' when one is without virtue. One who is bound by the fetter of pride does not recognize self and what belongs to self [as they truly are]. Due to non-recognition, there is grasping at self and what belongs to self, engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.text: avidyāsaṃyojanaṃ katamat / traidhātukamajñānam / avidyasaṃyojanena saṃprayuktā duḥkhadharmān samudayadharmān nādhyavasyati / anadhyavasāyena akuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalāsamudācāraśca / tenāyatyāṃ laukikaduḥsvābhinivṛttau duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the fetter of ignorance (<s>avidyāsaṃyojana</s>)? It is non-knowledge (<s>ajñāna</s>) pertaining to the three realms. One who is bound by the fetter of ignorance does not ascertain the <s>dharmas</s> of suffering and the <s>dharmas</s> of origination. Due to non-ascertainment, there is engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward worldly suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.text: dṛṣṭisaṃyojanaṃ katamat / tisro dṛṣṭhayaḥ / satkāyadṛṣṭirantāgrāhadṛṣṭirmithyāḥdṛṣṭiśca / dṛṣṭisaṃyojanena saṃprayukto mithyāniḥsaraṇaṃ parikalpitavipratisāraṃ paryeṣane abhiniviśate / mithyāniḥsaraṇābhiniveśenākuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalāsamudācāraśca / tenāyatyāṃ laukikaduḥkhabhinivṛttau duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the fetter of views (<s>dṛṣṭisaṃyojana</s>)? There are three views: the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the view of eternalism and nihilism (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), and wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). One who is bound by the fetter of views clings to a wrong means of escape and to a conceptualized [path of] regret in seeking [liberation]. Due to clinging to a wrong means of escape, there is engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward worldly suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.text: parāmarśasaṃyojanaṃ katamat / dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśaśca / (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 46]

children.text: ) parāmarśasaṃyojanena saṃprayukto mithyāniḥsaraṇopāyaṃ kalpayatyabhiniviśate / mithyāniḥsaraṇopāyāminiveśenākuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalāsamudācāraśca / tenāyatyāṃ laukikaduḥkhābhinivṛttau duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
children.translated_text: One who is bound by the fetter of clinging (<s>parāmarśasaṃyojana</s>) constructs and clings to a wrong means of escape. Due to clinging to a wrong means of escape, there is engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward worldly suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.translated_text: What is the fetter of clinging (<s>parāmarśasaṃyojana</s>)? It is clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>) and clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>).

body.text: vicikitsāsaṃyojanaṃ katamat / satyeṣu vimatiḥ / vicikitsāsaṃyojanena saṃprayukto buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu ratneṣu vicikitsate ratnatrayaṃ na samudāvarati / ratnatrayāsamudācāreṇākuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalāsanudācāraśca / tenāyatyāṃ laukikaduḥkhābhinivṛttau duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the fetter of doubt (<s>vicikitsāsaṃyojana</s>)? It is uncertainty (<s>vimati</s>) regarding the [Four Noble] Truths. One who is bound by the fetter of doubt has doubts about the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> — the Three Jewels — and does not engage with the Three Jewels. Due to non-engagement with the Three Jewels, there is engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward worldly suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.text: īrṣyāsaṃyojanaṃ katamat / lābhasatkārādhyavasitasya parasaṃpattāvamarṣakṛtaścetaso vyāroṣaḥ / īrṣyāsaṃyojanena saṃprayukto lābhasatkārān anunayati dharmaṃ na gurukaroti / lābhasatkāragurukāreṇā kuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalāsamudācāraśca / tenāyatyāṃ laukikaduḥkhabhinivṛttau duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the fetter of jealousy (<s>īrṣyāsaṃyojana</s>)? It is the hostility of mind born from resentment toward the success of others by one who is intent on gain and honor. One who is bound by the fetter of jealousy pursues gain and honor and does not revere the <s>Dharma</s>. Due to valuing gain and honor [over <s>Dharma</s>], there is engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward worldly suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.text: mātsaryasaṃyojanaṃ katamat / lābhasatkārādhyavasitasya pariṣkāreṣu cetasa āgrahaḥ / mātsaryasaṃyojanena saṃprayukta upacayamanunayati ta dvarjanatāṃ ca na satkaroti / upacayānunayenākuśalasamudācāraḥ kuśalāsamudācāraśca / tenāyatyāṃ laukikaduḥkhabhinivṛttau duḥkhena saṃyujyate //
body.translated_text: What is the fetter of miserliness (<s>mātsaryasaṃyojana</s>)? It is the mind's possessiveness toward material goods by one who is intent on gain and honor. One who is bound by the fetter of miserliness pursues accumulation and does not honor the [practice of] relinquishment. Due to the pursuit of accumulation, there is engagement in unwholesome [conduct] and non-engagement in wholesome [conduct]. Thereby, in future [lives], being turned toward worldly suffering, one is yoked to suffering.

body.text: bandhanaṃ trividham / rāgabandhanaṃ dveṣabandhanaṃ mohabandhanaṃ ca / rāgabandhanena sattvānāṃ viparīṇāmaduḥkhatāyāṃ bandhanam / dveṣabandhanena sattvānāṃ duḥkhaduḥkhatāyāṃ bandhanam / mohabandhanena sattvānāṃ saṃskāraduḥkhatāyāṃ bandhanam / apica rāgadveṣamohānniśritya kuśalasamudācāreṣu na vaśavarttitāṃ labhate / ata ucyate bandhanam //
body.translated_text: <s>Bandhana</s> (bondage) is threefold: bondage of <s>rāga</s> (attachment), bondage of <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and bondage of <s>moha</s> (delusion). Through the bondage of attachment, beings are bound to the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāma-duḥkhatā</s>). Through the bondage of aversion, beings are bound to the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkha-duḥkhatā</s>). Through the bondage of delusion, beings are bound to the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāra-duḥkhatā</s>). Furthermore, dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion, one does not gain mastery over wholesome activities. Therefore it is called bondage.

body.text: anuśayāḥ sapta / kāmarāgānuśayaḥ pratighānuśayaḥ bhavarāgānuśayaḥ mānānuśayaḥ avidyānuśayaḥ dṛṣṭayanuśayaḥ vicikitsānuśayaśca / kāmarāgānuśayaḥ katamaḥ / kāmarāgapakṣīyaṃ dauṣṭhulyam // pratighānuśayaḥ katamaḥ / pratighapakṣīyaṃ dauṣṭhulyam // bhavarāgānuśayaḥ katamaḥ / rūpārūpyarāgapakṣīyaṃ dauṣṭhulyam // mānānuśayaḥ katamaḥ / mānapakṣīyaṃ doṣṭhulyam // avidyānuśayaḥ katamaḥ avidyāpakṣīyaṃ dauṣṭhulyam // dṛṣṭyanuśayaḥ katamaḥ / dṛṣṭipakṣīyaṃ dauṣṭhulyam // vicikitsānuśayaḥ katamaḥ / vicikitsāpakṣīyaṃ dauṣṭhulyam // kāmaiṣāṇāyā aviratasya kāmarāgapratighānuśayāvanuśayāte / (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 47

children.text: ) bhaveṣaṇāyā aviratasya bhavarāgānuśayo 'nuśete / mithyābrahmacaryaiṣaṇāyā aviratasya mānāvidyādṛṣṭi vicikitsānuśayā anuśerate / te sattvā hīnapratipakṣaṃ labhante mado mānaścotpadyate āryasatyeṣu saṃmohaśca / mithyāmokṣaṃ mokṣopāyaṃ ca saṃtorayanti buddhaśāsanadharmavinayeṣu vimatiḥ vicikitsā ca //
children.translated_text: For one who has not refrained from the pursuit of existence, the latent tendency of desire for existence lies latent. For one who has not refrained from the pursuit of false spiritual practice, the latent tendencies of pride, ignorance, views, and doubt lie latent. Those beings obtain an inferior antidote; intoxication and pride arise, along with confusion regarding the <s>āryasatyas</s> (noble truths). They are satisfied with wrong liberation and wrong means of liberation, and there is uncertainty and doubt regarding the teaching, <s>Dharma</s>, and discipline of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.translated_text: The <s>anuśayas</s> (latent tendencies) are seven: the latent tendency of sensual desire (<s>kāmarāgānuśaya</s>), the latent tendency of hostility (<s>pratighānuśaya</s>), the latent tendency of desire for existence (<s>bhavarāgānuśaya</s>), the latent tendency of pride (<s>mānānuśaya</s>), the latent tendency of ignorance (<s>avidyānuśaya</s>), the latent tendency of views (<s>dṛṣṭyanuśaya</s>), and the latent tendency of doubt (<s>vicikitsānuśaya</s>). What is the latent tendency of sensual desire? It is the proclivity pertaining to the category of sensual desire. What is the latent tendency of hostility? It is the proclivity pertaining to the category of hostility. What is the latent tendency of desire for existence? It is the proclivity pertaining to the category of desire for the form and formless realms. What is the latent tendency of pride? It is the proclivity pertaining to the category of pride. What is the latent tendency of ignorance? It is the proclivity pertaining to the category of ignorance. What is the latent tendency of views? It is the proclivity pertaining to the category of views. What is the latent tendency of doubt? It is the proclivity pertaining to the category of doubt. For one who has not refrained from the pursuit of sensual pleasures, the latent tendencies of sensual desire and hostility lie latent.

body.text: upakleśastu yakleśāste upakleśā api bhavanti / upakleśāstu na kleśāḥ / kleśān sthāpayitvā tadanyaḥ kliṣṭaḥ saṃskāraskandhasaṃgṛhītaḥ sarvaścaitasiko dharmaḥ / sa punaḥ katamaḥ / ṣaḍrāgādīn kleśān sthāpayitvā kliṣṭaḥ saṃskāraskandhasaṃgṛhītaḥ krodhādikaścaitasiko dharmaḥ / api khalu rāgo dveṣo mohaśca caitasikā upakleśā ucyante / yaiścitte upakleśo na vairāgyaṃ na viumokṣo nāvaraṇaprahāṇam / ata ucyante upakleśāḥ / tathā ca bhagavatoktam dīrgharātraṃ vo rāgadveṣamohā upakliśyantui vikṣipanti citraṃ saṃkliśyanti /
body.translated_text: As for <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions), the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are also <s>upakleśas</s>, but <s>upakleśas</s> are not necessarily <s>kleśas</s>. Setting aside the <s>kleśas</s>, every other defiled mental factor included in the aggregate of formations (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>) is an <s>upakleśa</s>. What are they? Setting aside the six <s>kleśas</s> beginning with <s>rāga</s> (attachment), every defiled mental factor included in the aggregate of formations, beginning with <s>krodha</s> (anger), is an <s>upakleśa</s>. Moreover, <s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and <s>moha</s>, being mental factors, are called <s>upakleśas</s>, because through them the mind is afflicted — there is no dispassion, no liberation, no abandonment of obscurations. Therefore they are called <s>upakleśas</s>. Thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'For a long time, attachment, aversion, and delusion afflict you, scatter you, and thoroughly defile the mind.'

body.text: paryavasthānānyaṣṭau / styānaṃ middhamauddhatyaṃ kaukṛtyamīrṣyā mātsaryamāhikyamanapatrāpyaṃ ca / punaḥ punaḥ udvegena cittaṃ paryayanahyantīti paryavasthānāni / tathāca śamathapragrahanimittabhāvanākāle tatsanniśraya brahmacaryā diśuddhi saṃgṛhītaśīla kāle cittaṃ paryavanahyanti //
body.translated_text: The <s>paryavasthānas</s> (entanglements) are eight: <s>styāna</s> (torpor), <s>middha</s> (drowsiness), <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret), <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy), <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness), <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness), and <s>anapatrāpya</s> (recklessness). They are called entanglements because they repeatedly overwhelm the mind with agitation. Thus, at the time of cultivating the signs of <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>pragraha</s> (exertion), and at the time of moral discipline included in the purity of the spiritual life dependent upon them, they overwhelm the mind.

body.text: oghaścaturvidhaḥ / kāmaughaḥ mavaughaḥ dṛṣṭcoghaḥ avidyaughaśca / stroto 'nukūlaḥ pravāhāvartta oghārthaḥ / saṃkeśānvayataḥ / ādyaḥ kāmaiṣaṇābhāvanā / dvitīyaḥ bhavaiṣaṇābhāvanā / aparāvubhau mithyābrahmacaryaiṣaṇābhāvanā / āśrayāśritasaṃbandhayogena //
body.translated_text: The <s>oghas</s> (floods) are fourfold: the flood of sensual desire (<s>kāmaugha</s>), the flood of existence (<s>bhavaugha</s>), the flood of views (<s>dṛṣṭyogha</s>), and the flood of ignorance (<s>avidyaugha</s>). The meaning of 'flood' is a current flowing downstream. In terms of the sequence of afflictions: the first is the non-cultivation regarding the pursuit of sensual pleasures, the second is the non-cultivation regarding the pursuit of existence, and the latter two are the non-cultivation regarding the pursuit of false spiritual practice — through the connection of basis and dependent.

body.text: yogaścaturvidhaḥ / kāmayogaḥ bhavayogaḥ dṛṣṭiyogaḥ avidyāyogaśca / visaṃyogaparipanthakaro yogārthaḥ / viśuddhiviparyayataḥ / te punaryathāyogameṣaṇātrayabhāvanā /
body.translated_text: The <s>yogas</s> (yokes) are fourfold: the yoke of sensual desire (<s>kāmayoga</s>), the yoke of existence (<s>bhavayoga</s>), the yoke of views (<s>dṛṣṭiyoga</s>), and the yoke of ignorance (<s>avidyāyoga</s>). The meaning of 'yoke' is that which obstructs disjunction (<s>visaṃyoga</s>). From the perspective of the opposite of purification, they are again, according to suitability, the cultivation of the three pursuits.

body.text: upādānāni catvāri / kāmopādānaṃ dṛṣṭyupādānaṃ śīlavratopādānamātmavādopādānaṃ ca / vivādamūlopādānaṃ paunarbhavikopādānaṃ copādānaṃ draṣṭavyam / (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 48

children.text: ) tena kiṃ bhavati / kāmarāgavibandhagredhāsaṃkleśahetunā gṛhiṇo 'nyo 'nyaṃ vivadanti / tadu vivādamūlaṃ prathamamupādanam / dṛṣṭirāgavibandhagredhā saṃkleśahetunā pravrajitā anyo 'nyaṃ vivadanti / tad vivādamūlamaparamupādānatrayam // dvāṣaṣṭirdṛṣṭigatayo dṛṣṭyupādānam / nānāvṛtaśīlaiḥ kṛcchraṃ tapaḥ śīlavratopādānam // tadāśritā ca satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ ātmavādopādānam // dṛṣṭiśīlavratopādānābhyāṃ tīrthyā anyo 'nyaṃ vivadanti / ātmavādopādāne tu tīrthyā anyo 'nyaṃ na vivadanti / dhārmikaiḥ sārdhamanyo 'nyaṃ vivadanti // evaṃ ca vivādamūle 'bhiniveśāt paunarbhavikaduḥkhavipākopādānākṣepāccopādānānyucyante /
children.translated_text: What results from that? Due to the cause of affliction consisting of the binding craving of attachment to sensual pleasures, householders dispute with one another — that is the root of disputes, the first attachment. Due to the cause of affliction consisting of the binding craving of attachment to views, renunciants dispute with one another — the root of disputes is the other three attachments. The sixty-two wrong views constitute the attachment to views. The harsh austerities practiced through various ascetic rules and rituals constitute the attachment to rules and rituals. The <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable collection) dependent on them is the attachment to the doctrine of self. Through the attachments to views and to rules and rituals, the <s>tīrthyas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) dispute with one another. But regarding the attachment to the doctrine of self, the <s>tīrthyas</s> do not dispute with one another — they dispute with the followers of the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus, because of clinging to the root of disputes and because of seizing the fruition of suffering through renewed existence, they are called attachments.

body.translated_text: The <s>upādānas</s> (attachments) are four: attachment to sensual pleasures (<s>kāmopādāna</s>), attachment to views (<s>dṛṣṭyupādāna</s>), attachment to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavratopādāna</s>), and attachment to the doctrine of self (<s>ātmavādopādāna</s>). <s>Upādāna</s> should be viewed as the root of disputes and as causing renewed existence.

body.text: granthāścatvāraḥ / abhidhyākāyagranthaḥ vyāpādakāyagranthaḥ śīlavrata parāmarśakāyagranthaḥ tatsatyābhiniveśopādānakāyagranthaśca / samāhitamanaḥsvabhāvasya kāyasya parigranthārthena grantho veditavyaḥ / tena kiṃ bhavati / caturvidhaṃ cittaṃ vikṣipyate / vittādiṣu anunayahetoḥ cittaṃ vikṣipyate / vivādastuṣu apratipattihetoḥ cittaṃ vikṣipyate / duṣkaraśīlavrataduḥkhahetoḥ cittaṃ vikṣipyate / ayoniśo jñeya santīraṇahetoḥ cittaṃ vikṣipyatee //
body.translated_text: The <s>granthas</s> (bodily knots) are four: the bodily knot of covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), the bodily knot of malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), the bodily knot of clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), and the bodily knot of adherence to one's views as truth (<s>tatsatyābhiniveśopādāna</s>). A knot should be understood as that which entangles the body whose nature is a collected mind. What results from that? The mind is scattered in four ways: the mind is scattered due to attachment toward wealth and the like; the mind is scattered due to non-compliance in disputes; the mind is scattered due to the suffering of difficult ascetic rules and rituals; the mind is scattered due to improper investigation of objects of knowledge.

body.text: nivaraṇāni pañca / kāmacchandanivaraṇam vyāpādanivaraṇam styānamiddhanivaraṇam auddhatyakaukṛtyanivaraṇam vicikitsānivaraṇaṃ ca / kuśalapakṣasyāsaṃprakhyānaṃ nivaraṇaṃ draṣṭavyam / tacca pravrajyāyāmabhiratau codanāyāṃ pratipattau śamathe pragrahe upekṣāyāṃ ca //
body.translated_text: The <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances) are five: the hindrance of sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda</s>), the hindrance of malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), the hindrance of torpor and drowsiness (<s>styāna-middha</s>), the hindrance of restlessness and regret (<s>auddhatya-kaukṛtya</s>), and the hindrance of doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>). A hindrance should be viewed as the non-manifestation of the wholesome class. And this pertains to delight in renunciation, exhortation, practice, calm, exertion, and equanimity.

body.text: khilastrividhaḥ / rāgakhilo dveṣakhilo mohakhilaśca / rāgadveṣamohānniśritya pūrvābhyāsena rāgādicaryāpariniṣpādanam / cittasyādāntatayā akarmaṇyatayā durvimokṣatayā ca sattvaistasyāścaryāyā durbhedyatvāt khila ityucyate //
body.translated_text: The <s>khilas</s> (rigidities) are threefold: the rigidity of attachment, the rigidity of aversion, and the rigidity of delusion. Dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion, through previous habituation, there is the non-completion of conduct beginning with attachment — due to the untamed, unworkable, and hard-to-liberate nature of the mind, and because that conduct is difficult for beings to break through, it is called rigidity.

body.text: malāstrayaḥ / rāgamalo dveṣamalo mohamalaśca / tacca rāgadveṣamohānniśritya (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 49

children.text: ) dauśīlam / tat saṃprajānabdiḥ sabrahmacāribhirgrāme vā araṇye vā tathā kurvantaṃ paśyadbhirucyate ayaṃ khalvāyuṣmān karotyevaṃ kṛtyaṃ caratyevamācaritaṃ grāmakaṇṭaka āmiṣo 'śuciḥ / ato malā nāma //
children.translated_text: there is moral misconduct (<s>dauśīlya</s>). When fellow practitioners, whether in the village or in the forest, see one acting thus and conducting oneself thus, they say: 'This venerable one does such deeds, conducts himself in such a manner — he is a thorn of the village, covetous, unclean.' Therefore they are called impurities.

body.translated_text: The <s>malas</s> (impurities) are three: the impurity of attachment, the impurity of aversion, and the impurity of delusion. And dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion,

body.text: nighāstrayaḥ / rāganigho dveṣanigho mohanighaśca / rāgadveṣamohānniśritya dīrghakālaṃ punaḥ punarjātimaraṇeṣu vilaśyante ityucyante nighāḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>nighas</s> (destructions) are three: the destruction of attachment, the destruction of aversion, and the destruction of delusion. Dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion, beings languish in births and deaths again and again for a long time — therefore they are called destructions.

body.text: śalyāstrayaḥ / rāgaśalyo dveṣaśalyo mohaśalyaśca / rāgadveṣamohānniśritya bhave bhavopakaraṇeṣu vā adhyeṣaṇāsamutpādena prabandhānupacchedena buddhe dharme saṃghe duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgeṣu vā vicikitsāsamutpādena vā śalyā nāma //
body.translated_text: The <s>śalyas</s> (thorns) are three: the thorn of attachment, the thorn of aversion, and the thorn of delusion. Dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion, through the arising of longing for existence or the requisites of existence and through the unbroken continuity thereof, or through the arising of doubt regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṅgha</s>, and suffering, its origin, cessation, and the path — they are called thorns.

body.text: kiṃcanāstrayaḥ / rāgakiṃcano dveṣakiṃcano mohakiṃcanaśca / rāgadveṣamohānniśritya vittasaṃcayeṣu sabhayāḥ savairā bhūyo vihāravikṣepāḥ kiṃcanā nāma /
body.translated_text: The <s>kiṃcanas</s> (impediments) are three: the impediment of attachment, the impediment of aversion, and the impediment of delusion. Dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion, with regard to the accumulation of wealth, they are fearful, hostile, and further distracted in their dwelling — they are called impediments.

body.text: duścaritāni trīṇi / rāgaduścaritaṃ dveṣaduścaritaṃ mohaduścaritaṃ ca / rāgadveṣamohānniśritya kāyavāṅmanoduścaritāni carantīti duścaritānītyucyate / punaḥ rāgadveṣamohānniśrityotpannānāṃ bahūnāmakuśaladuścaritānāmakuśalamūlatvena tribhirvyavasthānam / tat katham / sattvā loke āmiṣakiṃcitkahato caranti / loke 'pakāra nimittaparikalpahatoḥ duścaritaṃ caranti / loke mithyādharmābhiniveśahetoḥ duścaritaṃ caranti / iti te rāgadveṣamohā duścaritāni akuśalamūlāni /
body.translated_text: The <s>duścaritas</s> (misconducts) are three: the misconduct of attachment, the misconduct of aversion, and the misconduct of delusion. Dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion, beings engage in misconduct of body, speech, and mind — therefore they are called misconducts. Furthermore, dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion, the many arisen unwholesome misconducts are classified under three as unwholesome roots. How so? Beings in the world engage in misconduct due to being struck by greed for material things. They engage in misconduct in the world due to imagining signs of harm. They engage in misconduct in the world due to adherence to wrong doctrines. Thus attachment, aversion, and delusion are misconducts and unwholesome roots.

body.text: āsravāsrayaḥ / kāmāsravo bhavāsravo 'vidyāsravaśca / cittāvesāraṃ strataṃ kurvantī tyāsravāḥ ityucyante / te punaḥ katham / bahirdhā visāraṃ niśritya kāmāsravaḥ / antardhāvisāraṃ niśritya bhavāsravaḥ / tadubhayāśrayavisāraṃ niśritya avidyāsravaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) are three: the outflow of sensual desire (<s>kāmāsrava</s>), the outflow of existence (<s>bhavāsrava</s>), and the outflow of ignorance (<s>avidyāsrava</s>). They are called outflows because they cause the mind to flow outward. How so? Dependent on outward dispersion, there is the outflow of sensual desire. Dependent on inward dispersion, there is the outflow of existence. Dependent on the dispersion of both bases, there is the outflow of ignorance.

body.text: vighātāstrayaḥ / rāgavighāto dveṣavighāto mohavighātaśca / rāgadveṣamohānniśritya bhave pariṣkareṣu vā eṣaṇā / abhāve vighāte sarvadā dāridya duḥkhādibhiḥ kliṣṭā bhavantīti vighātāḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>vighātas</s> (frustrations) are three: the frustration of attachment, the frustration of aversion, and the frustration of delusion. Dependent on attachment, aversion, and delusion, there is longing for existence or the requisites of existence. In their absence or frustration, beings are always afflicted by the suffering of poverty and the like — therefore they are called frustrations.

body.text: paridāhāstrayaḥ / rāgaparidāho dveṣaparidāho mohaparidāhaśca / rāgadveṣamohasanniśrayeṇa ayoniśo nimittābhiniveśo 'nuvyañjanābhiniveśaśca / tena nimittānuvyañjanābhiniveśena kāyaṃ cittaṃ ca paridahantīti paridāhāḥ //
body.translated_text: The torments (<s>paridāha</s>) are three: the torment of desire (<s>rāga</s>), the torment of hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and the torment of delusion (<s>moha</s>). Based on desire, hatred, and delusion, there is improper grasping at signs (<s>nimitta</s>) and grasping at secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>). Through that grasping at signs and secondary characteristics, they burn the body and mind — thus they are called torments.

body.text: upāyāsāstrayaḥ / rāgopāyāso dveṣopāyāso mohopāyasaśca / rāgadveṣamohasanniśrayeṇa tatra tatra ratiradhyavasānaṃ ca / tadvipariṇāme śokaparidevanāduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyasaiḥ spṛṣṭā bhavantītyu pāyāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: The tribulations (<s>upāyāsa</s>) are three: the tribulation of desire, the tribulation of hatred, and the tribulation of delusion. Based on desire, hatred, and delusion, there is delight and resolve toward various [objects]. When those undergo change, one is struck by sorrow (<s>śoka</s>), lamentation (<s>parideva</s>), suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>), and tribulation — thus they are called tribulations.

body.text: raṇāstrayaḥ / rāgaraṇo dveṣaraṇo moharaṇaśca / rāgadveṣamohasanniśrayeṇa śastrādānadaṇḍādibhiḥ raṇayanti nānāvidhaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalahaṃ kurvantīti rāgādayo raṇā ucyante //
body.translated_text: The conflicts (<s>raṇa</s>) are three: the conflict of desire, the conflict of hatred, and the conflict of delusion. Based on desire, hatred, and delusion, they engage in conflict through taking up weapons, sticks, and the like, creating various kinds of quarrels and disputes — thus desire and the rest are called conflicts.

body.text: jvarāstrayaḥ / rāgajvaro dveṣajvaro moha jvaraśca / rāgadveṣamohasanniśrayeṇa adharmarāgeṇa mahādahanena paridahanti viṣamalobhena mahādahanena paridahanti mithyādharmeṇa mahādahanena paridahantīti jvarā nāma //
body.translated_text: The fevers (<s>jvara</s>) are three: the fever of desire, the fever of hatred, and the fever of delusion. Based on desire, hatred, and delusion — they burn with the great conflagration of passion for non-<s>Dharma</s>, they burn with the great conflagration of uneven greed, and they burn with the great conflagration of false doctrine — thus they are called fevers.

body.text: vanasāstrayaḥ / rāgavanaso dveṣavanaso mohavanasaśca / rāgadveṣamohasanniśrayeṇa jātimaraṇamūleṣu saṃskāreṣu saṃyojayanti saṃjanayanti sattvān nānāvidhakāyeṣu pañcagatisaṃsāreṣu abhinirvarttayantīti rāgādayo vanasā ityucyante //
body.translated_text: The entanglements (<s>vanasa</s>) are three: the entanglement of desire, the entanglement of hatred, and the entanglement of delusion. Based on desire, hatred, and delusion, they bind and generate beings in the formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) rooted in birth and death, bringing them forth in various bodies within the five destinies of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) — thus desire and the rest are called entanglements.

body.text: vibandhāstrayaḥ / rāgavibandho dveṣavibandho mohavibandhaśca / rāgadveṣamohasanniśrayeṇa kāyasāpekṣatā vittasāpekṣatā bodhyabhāvaḥ kolāhalaratiḥ parittakuśaladharmalābhe 'pi santoṣaḥ / taiḥ kuśaladharmānna bhāvayantīti vibandhāḥ ucyante / evamādayaḥ kleśārthānāṃ paryāyā apramāṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: The hindrances (<s>vibandha</s>) are three: the hindrance of desire, the hindrance of hatred, and the hindrance of delusion. Based on desire, hatred, and delusion: concern for the body, concern for possessions, absence of awakening, delight in commotion, and contentment even with obtaining only meager wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — through these one does not cultivate wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, thus they are called hindrances. Such synonyms for the meaning of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) are immeasurable.

body.text: vipratipattiḥ katamā / rāgaḥ pratighaśca dvau kleśau viṣaye dṛṣṭau ca vipratipannau / (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 51]

children.text: ) mānaḥ sattveṣu dṛṣṭau ca vipratipannaḥ / satkāyāntagrāhamithyādṛṣṭayo jñeye vipratipannāḥ / dṛṣṭiparāmarśaśīlavrataparāmarśau dṛṣṭau vipratipannau / vicikitsā pratipakṣe vipratipannā / avidyā sarvatra vipratipannā / daśa kleśā duḥkhe samudaye ca vipratipannāḥ / tannidānapadasthānataḥ / punaḥ daśa kleśā nirodhe mārge ca vipratipannāḥ / taistatrotrāsasaṃjananataḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Māna</s> (pride) goes astray with respect to beings and views. The view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), extreme views (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), and wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) go astray with respect to the knowable. Clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>) and clinging to rules and observances (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>) go astray with respect to views. Doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) goes astray with respect to the antidote. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) goes astray everywhere. The ten afflictions go astray with respect to suffering and origination — because these are the basis and ground of those [afflictions]. Furthermore, the ten afflictions go astray with respect to cessation and the path — because they generate fear toward those.

body.translated_text: What is wrong course (<s>vipratipatti</s>)? <s>Rāga</s> (desire) and <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), these two afflictions, go astray with respect to objects and views.

body.text: dhātu katamaḥ / pratighaṃ sthāpayitvā tadanye sarve traidhātukapratisaṃyuktāḥ / pratighastu kāmadhātupratisaṃyuktaḥ / api khalu rāgaḥ kāmadhātau sukhasaumanasyopekṣābhi saṃprayujyate / yathā kāmadhātau tathā prathamadvitīyadhyānayoḥ / tṛtīyadhyāne sukhopekṣābhyāṃ saṃprayujyate / tadūrdhvamupekṣayā saṃprayujyate // pratigho duḥkhadaurmanasyosukhopekṣābhiḥ saṃprayujyate // mānaḥ kāmadhātau saumanasyopekṣābhiḥ saṃprayujyate / prathamadvitīyadhyānayo sukhasaumanasyopekṣābhiḥ saṃprayujyate / tṛtīyadhyāne sukhopekṣābhyāṃ saṃprayujyate / tadūrdhvamupekṣayaiva saṃprayujyate // yathā mānastathā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ antagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśaśca // mithyādṛṣṭiḥ kāmadhātau daurmanasyasaumanasyopekṣābhiḥ saṃprayujyate / rūpadhātāvārupyadhātau ca yathāveditaṃ saṃprayujyate // vicikitsā kāmadhātau dauramanasyopekṣābhyāṃ saṃprayujyate / rūpadhātāvārūpyadhātau ca yathāveditaṃ saṃprayujyate // avidyā dvividhā / saṃprayuktā asāmānyā ca / sarvakleśasaṃprayogataḥ saṃprayuktā avidyā yathāveditaṃ saṃprayujyate / āsāmānyā avidyā kāmadhātau daurmanasyopekṣābhyāṃ saṃprayujyate / tadūrdhvadhātau yathāveditaṃ saṃprayujyate // kathaṃ sarvakleśā upekṣayā saṃprayujyante / sarvakleśānāmaudāsīnyamāgamyāstagamanatāmupādāya // api khalu rāgaḥ kāmadhātau ṣaḍvijñānakāyikaḥ // yathā rāgastathā pratigho 'vidyā ca // rāgo rūpadhātau caturvijñānakāyikāḥ / ārūpyadhātau manovijñānakāyikaḥ // yathā rāgastathā avidyā // māno dṛṣṭirvicikitsā ca sarvatra manovijñānakāyikāḥ // api khalu rāgaḥ pratigho mānaśca kāmadhātau vastvekadeśapravṛttikāḥ / kāmadhātuvad rūpadhātāvārūpyadhātāvapi śiṣṭāḥ kleśāḥ sarvatra sarvavastu pravṛttikāḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the realm (<s>dhātu</s>)? Setting aside aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), all the others are associated with the three realms. Aversion, however, is associated only with the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). Furthermore, desire (<s>rāga</s>) in the desire realm is conjoined with pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). As in the desire realm, so also in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>. In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, it is conjoined with pleasure and equanimity. Above that, it is conjoined with equanimity alone. Aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) is conjoined with suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). Pride (<s>māna</s>) in the desire realm is conjoined with mental pleasure and equanimity. In the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, it is conjoined with pleasure, mental pleasure, and equanimity. In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, it is conjoined with pleasure and equanimity. Above that, it is conjoined with equanimity alone. As with pride, so also with the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), extreme views (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), and clinging to rules and observances (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). Wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) in the desire realm are conjoined with displeasure, mental pleasure, and equanimity. In the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) and formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>), they are conjoined as previously stated. Doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) in the desire realm is conjoined with displeasure and equanimity. In the form and formless realms, it is conjoined as previously stated. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is twofold: associated (<s>saṃprayuktā</s>) and non-general (<s>asāmānyā</s>). The associated ignorance, through conjunction with all afflictions, is conjoined as previously stated. The non-general ignorance in the desire realm is conjoined with displeasure and equanimity. In the higher realms, it is conjoined as previously stated. How are all afflictions conjoined with equanimity? Because all afflictions reach a state of indifference (<s>audāsīnya</s>) and subsidence. Furthermore, desire in the desire realm pertains to the six consciousness-groups (<s>vijñānakāya</s>). As with desire, so also aversion and ignorance. Desire in the form realm pertains to four consciousness-groups. In the formless realm, it pertains to the mental consciousness-group (<s>manovijñānakāya</s>). As with desire, so also ignorance. Pride, views, and doubt everywhere pertain to the mental consciousness-group. Furthermore, desire, aversion, and pride in the desire realm operate with respect to a portion of objects. As in the desire realm, so also in the form and formless realms. The remaining afflictions everywhere operate with respect to all objects.

body.text: nikāyaḥ katamaḥ / dvau kleśanikāyau / darśanaprahātavyanikāyo bhāvanāprahātavyanikāyaśca / darśanaprahātavyanikāyaḥ punaścaturvidhaḥ / duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyanikāyaḥ samudayadarśanaprahātavyanikāyaḥ / nirodhadarśanaprahātavyanikāyaḥ mārgadarśanaprahātavyanikāyaśca / kāmadhātau duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyā daśa kleśāḥ / duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyavat samudayadarśanaprahātavyāḥ nirodhadarśanaprahātavyā mārgadarśanaprahātavyāśca / rūpadhātau duḥkhādicaturvidhadarśanaprahātavyāḥ pratyekaṃ navakleśāḥ sthāpayitvā pratigham / rūpadhātuvadārūpyadhātāvapi / evaṃ ca darśanaprahātavyakleśanikāyā dvādaśādhikaṃ śataṃ kleśāḥ // kāmadhātau bhāvanā prahātavyāḥ ṣaṭkleśāḥ / sahajā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ antaprāhadṛṣṭiḥ rāgaḥ pratigho māno 'vidyā ca / rūpadhātau bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ pañca kleśāḥ sthāpayitvā pratigham / rūpadhātuvadārūpyadhātāvapi / evaṃ ca bhāvanāprahātavyanikāyāḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ kleśāḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the category (<s>nikāya</s>)? There are two categories of afflictions: the category to be abandoned through seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>) and the category to be abandoned through cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>). The category to be abandoned through seeing is further fourfold: to be abandoned through seeing suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), to be abandoned through seeing origination (<s>samudaya</s>), to be abandoned through seeing cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and to be abandoned through seeing the path (<s>mārga</s>). In the desire realm, there are ten afflictions to be abandoned through seeing suffering. As with those to be abandoned through seeing suffering, so also those to be abandoned through seeing origination, cessation, and the path. In the form realm, there are nine afflictions to be abandoned through each of the four types of seeing — setting aside aversion. As in the form realm, so also in the formless realm. Thus the afflictions of the category to be abandoned through seeing total one hundred and twelve. In the desire realm, there are six afflictions to be abandoned through cultivation: innate view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), innate extreme views (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), desire (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). In the form realm, there are five afflictions to be abandoned through cultivation — setting aside aversion. As in the form realm, so also in the formless realm. Thus the afflictions of the category to be abandoned through cultivation total sixteen.

body.text: prahāṇaṃ katamat / tathā paryāyaprahāṇaṃ tena manaskāreṇa prahāṇam / tasmāt pratilambhāt prahāṇam / tathā paryāyaprahāṇaṃ katamat / parijñānataḥ parivarjanataḥ pratipakṣalābhataśca / parijñānaṃ katamat / tannidānavastuparijñānam svabhāvaparijñānam ādīnavaparijñānaṃ ca / parivarjanaṃ katamat / tatkālotpannasyānādānam / pratipakṣalābhaḥ katamaḥ / anutpannasyānutpādata utpannasya varjanato vā pratipakṣa lābhamārgaḥ // tena manaskāreṇa prahāṇam / kīdṛśena manaskāreṇa kiṃ prajahāti / asaṃbhinnālambanena manaskāreṇa sarvadharmā anātmāna iti paśyati / anityākārā iti kleśān prajahāti / anityākāra parikarmataḥ // tasmāt pratilambhāt prahāṇam / kasmāt pratilambhāt prajahāti / nātītāt niruddhataḥ / nānāgatāt anutpannataḥ / na pratyutpannāt asahabhāvataḥ / kevalaṃ kleśadauṣṭhulyapratilambhāt prajahātīti prahāṇam / yathā yathā dauṣṭhulyamutpadyate tathā tathā pratipakṣa utpadyate yathā yathā pratipakṣa utpadyate tathā tathā dauṣṭhulyanirodhaḥ / samaṃ samam / yathā (
