children.text: ) loke jyotirutpadyate tamaśca nirudhyate / tadvisaṃyogato yadānāgatakleśo 'nutpannadhamaṣu avatiṣṭhate tat prahāṇamucyate //
children.translated_text: in the world, when light arises darkness ceases — so through the disconnection from those [afflictions], when a future affliction abides in the state of non-arising, that is called abandonment.

body.translated_text: What is abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>)? It is [analyzed as]: abandonment through method (<s>paryāya</s>), abandonment through that [specific] mental attention, and abandonment through that attainment. What is abandonment through method? Through full understanding (<s>parijñāna</s>), through avoidance (<s>parivarjana</s>), and through obtaining the antidote (<s>pratipakṣalābha</s>). What is full understanding? Full understanding of the cause and basis of those [afflictions], full understanding of their intrinsic nature, and full understanding of their disadvantages. What is avoidance? Non-appropriation of what arises at that time. What is obtaining the antidote? The path of obtaining the antidote through the non-arising of what has not arisen, or through the abandoning of what has arisen. Abandonment through that mental attention: through what kind of mental attention does one abandon what? Through mental attention with an undivided object, one sees that all <s>dharmas</s> are without self (<s>anātman</s>). One abandons the afflictions through the aspect of impermanence — through the preparatory practice of the impermanence aspect. Abandonment through that attainment: from what attainment does one abandon? Not from the past, because it has ceased. Not from the future, because it has not arisen. Not from the present, because it does not coexist [with the antidote]. Rather, one abandons only from the attainment [of freedom from] the tendency (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) of the afflictions — this is abandonment. To the extent that the tendency arises, to that extent the antidote arises; to the extent that the antidote arises, to that extent there is cessation of the tendency — equally and simultaneously. Just as

body.text: kleśādhipateyaṃ karma katamat / cetanā karma cetayitvā karma ca / sarvaṃ karmalakṣaṇaṃ nāma // punaḥ karma pañcavidham / upalabdhikarma kāritrakarma vyavasāyakarma pariṇatikarma prāptikarma ca / asmiṃstvarthe yad bhūyasā vyavasāyakarmābhipretam // cetanākarma katamat / puṇyakarma apuṇyakarma āniṃjyakarma ca // cetayitvā karma katamat / kāyakarma vākkarma manaskarma ca / tāni trīṇi kāyavāṅmanaskarmāṇi akuśalāni kuśalāni ca / akuśalāni katamāni daśākuśalakarmapathāḥ / prāṇātipātaḥ adattādānam kāmamithyācāraḥ mṛṣāvādaḥ piśunavāk paruṣavāk saṃbhinnapralāpaḥ abhidyā vyāpādaḥ mithyādṛṣṭiśca / kuśalāni katamāni / daśa kuśalakarmāpathāḥ / prāṇātipātād viratiḥ adattādānādviratiḥ kāmamithyācārādviratiḥ mṛṣāvādādviratiḥ piśunavāco viratiḥ paruṣavāco viratiḥ saṃbhinnapralāpādviratiḥ anabhidhyā avyāpādaḥ samyagdṛṣṭiśca // apica prāṇātipātādīnāṃ yathāyogaṃ pañca lakṣaṇaprabhedāḥ / vastutaḥ āśayataḥ prayogataḥ kleśataḥ niṣṭhāgamanataśca //

yaduktaṃ sūtre cetanākarma / katamāni cetanākarmāṇi parājñaptisaṃcetanīyatākarma paramasaṃjñaptisaṃcetatīyatākarma avijñāyasaṃcetanīyatākarma mūlābhiniveśasacetanīyatākarma viparyāsasaṃcetanīyatākarma ca / teṣu mūlābhiniveśasaṃcetanīyatākarma viparyāsaṃcetana yatā karma ca / teṣu mūlābhiniveśasaṃcetanīyatā karmaviparyāsasaṃcetanīyatākarmabhyāṃ yadi kṛtaṃ bhavatyupacitaṃ ca na nāsya vipākaḥ pratisaṃvedyate / kṛtaṃ samudācārasamutthāpitam / upacitaṃ ca vāsanā samupacitam //
yadūktaṃ sūtre niyatavedanīyaṃ karma iti / katame niyaptāḥ karmakiyāniyamaḥ vipākapatisaṃvedanāniyamaḥ avasthāniyamaśca //

tanna daśānāmakuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ vipākaphalaṃ triṣu apāyeṣu / mṛdūmadhyādhimātrāṇāṃ tiryakpretanarakeṣu vipākaḥ / nipyandaphalaṃ pratyekaṃ tadānurūpyeṇa manuṣyeṣūpanannānā mātmabhāvaparigrahayorvipattiḥ / adhipatiphalaṃ pratyekaṃ tadānurūpyeṇaiva vāhyānāṃ bhāvānāṃ vipattiḥ / yathoktaṃ sūtre / daśānāṃ kuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ vipākaphalaṃ devamanuṣyamatiṣūpapadyamānānāṃ deveṣu manuṣyeṣu vā vipākaḥ / niṣyandaphalaṃ tadāyataneṣu pratyekaṃ tadānurūpyeṇa ātmābhāvaparigrahayoḥ saṃpattirabhinirvarttate / adhipattiphalaṃ tadāyataneṣu pratyekaṃ tadānurūpyeṇaiva vāhyānāṃ bhāvānāṃ saṃpattirabhinirvarttate /

kuśalānāmakuśalānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ sugatau durgatau ca vipāko 'bhinirvarttate / taccākṣepakeṇa karmaṇā paripūrakeṇa ca karmaṇā / ākṣepakaṃ karma katamat / yena phala vipāko 'bhinirvarttate / paripūrakaṃ karma katamat / yenopapanna iṣṭāniṣṭaphalaṃ vedayate / yena ekena karmaṇā ekamātmabhavanākṣipati vā anekena karmaṇā ekamātmabhāvamākṣipati vā anekena karmaṇā anekamātmabhāvamākṣipati vā // ekaḥ sattvo 'nekena karmaṇā samanvāgataḥ / tatra vipākaphalavedanāyāḥ kaḥ kramaḥ / kāye yad audārikaṃ pūrvaṃ pacyate cyutikāle pratyupasthitaṃ vā pūrvaṃ bahulīkāratāṃ gataṃ vā atrasamācaritaṃ vā / tadvipākaḥ pūrvaṃ pacyate //

yaduktaṃ sūtre trividhaṃ karma puṇyakarma apuṇya karma āniṃjyakarma ca / puṇyakarma katamat / kāmapratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalaṃ karma / apuṇyakarma katamat / akuśalaṃ karma / āniṃjyakarma katamat / rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalaṃ karma // yaduktaṃ sūtre avidyālambanāḥ saṃskārāḥ puṇyāniṃjyā apuṇyāniṃjyāśceti / katame (

children.text: ) puṇyāniṃjyā avidyālambanāḥ saṃskārā utpadyante / dvividhaḥ saṃmūḍhaḥ / phalavipākasaṃmūḍhaḥ tattvārthasaṃmūḍhaśca / phalavipākasaṃmūḍhasyāpuṇyāḥ saṃskārāḥ / tattvārthasaṃmūḍhasya puṇyāniṃjyāḥ saṃskārāḥ /

body.text: prāṇātipātasya karmapathasya lobhadveṣamohaiḥ prayogaḥ / dveṣeṇaiva niṣṭhā / prāṇātipātavat paruṣavāgavyāpādayorapi karmapathayoḥ / adattādānasya karmapathasya lobhadveṣamohaiḥ prayogaḥ / lobhenaiva niṣṭhā / adattādānavat kāmamithyācārābhidhyayoḥ karmapathayoḥ / mṛṣāvādasya karmapathasya lobhadveṣamohaiḥ prayogaḥ / trayāṇāmanyatamena niṣṭhā / mṛṣāvādavat saṃbhinnapralāpapiśunavācoḥ karmapathayoḥ / mithyādṛṣṭeḥ karmapathasya rāgadveṣamohaiḥ prayogaḥ / mohenaiva niṣṭhā /

yaduktaṃ sūtre sādhāraṇaṃ karma asādhāraṇaṃ karma valavatkarma durvalaṃ karma ca / sādhāraṇaṃ karma katamat / yatkarma bhājanaloke nānāvidhaṃ vikalpaṃ karoti // asādhāraṇaṃ karma katamat / yatkarma sattvaloke nānavidhaṃ vikalpaṃ karoti // api ca sattvānāmanyonyādhipateyaṃ karmāpi / yena karmabalena sattvānāmanyonyādhipatipratyayaḥ proktaḥ / teṣāmanyonyādhipatibalatastadapyucyate sādhāraṇaṃ karma / yataḥ sūtre uktam / yathā sattvānāmānyaiḥ sattvaiḥ saha anyonyaṃ darśanādikaṃ nopabhogo nopalabdhiḥ / balavatkarma katamat / pratipakṣabalavatpugdalasya saṃcetanīyamakuśalaṃ karma / pratipakṣavalaviskāmbhaṇena vedanīyanarakakarmapravṛtteḥ dṛṣṭadharmavedanāyāḥ pariniṣpādanaṃ dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyanarakakarmapravṛtteranutpādaḥ / yena tatkarma balavadityucyate / prātipakṣikakarmabalavataḥ sarvaṃ saṃcetanīyaṃ kuśalaṃ karma balavadityucyate / tatkarma niśrityoktaṃ bhagavatā mamāryaśrāvakā apramāṇavaipulyakarmaṇi cittaṃ kuśalaṃ paribhāvayanti abhisaṃskṛte sapramāṇe karmaṇi nākṣipanti nāvasthāpayanti na parihāpayanti tatsaṃkhyāte / yadapi pratipakṣadurbalapugdalasya saṃcetanīyamakuśalaṃ karma tadapi kuśalātkarmaṇo (

children.text: ) balavadityucyate / yat punaḥ saṃcetanīyaṃ karma niyatavipākamaprahīṇamaparijñātaṃ tad balavat karma ityucyate / tanmanasi nidhāyoktaṃ sarvaṃ ca kuśalākuśalaṃ karma niyatavipākamāryamārgeṇa prahīṇaṃ balavat karma ityucyate / yadapi kāmapratisaṃyuktamakuśalaṃ karma yadapi pūrvamabhyastaṃ yadapi padasthaṃ yadapyasādhyamabhisaṃskṛtaṃ karma aparinirvāṇadharmataḥ tadapi prakṛtyā balavat karma ityucyate / kṣetrato 'pi cittābhisaṃskārato 'pi balavat karma veditavyam / punarnavabhirākārairbalavat karma veditavyam / tadyathā kṣetrataḥ vastutaḥ svabhāvataḥ āśrayataḥ manasikārataḥ āśayataḥ sahāyataḥ bahulīkārataḥ bāhujanyataśca // tadviparyeṇa durbalaṃ karma //

body.text: bhagavatoktaṃ ya evaṃ vadedyathāyaṃ puruṣapugdalaḥ karma karotyupacinoti tathā tathā vipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayata ityevaṃ sati brahmacaryabhāso na bhavatyavakāśaśca na prajñāyate samyag duḥkhakṣayāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai / yastvevaṃ vadedyathāyaṃ puruṣapugdalo yathāvedanīyaṃ karma karotyupacinoti tathā tathā yathāvedanīyaṃ vipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayata ityevaṃ sati brahmacaryabhāso bhavatyavakāśaśca prajñāyate samyag duḥkhakṣayāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai / iti yaduktaṃ sūtre tatra ko 'bhisaṃdhiḥ / tatra buddhā manasyevaṃ mithyāvacanaṃ pratiṣeddhuṃ kāmayante / yat sukhasahagatasya karmaṇaḥ sukhasahagata eva vipāko 'bhinirvarttate duḥkhasahagatasya karmaṇo duḥkhasahagata eva vipāko 'bhinirvarttate aduḥkhāsukhasahagatasya karmaṇastatsahagata eva vipāko 'bhinirvarttate / ityevamuktam / samyagvacanaṃ tvevamanumanyate / sukhasahagatasya karmaṇaḥ sukhavedanīyasya sukhavipāko 'nujñāyate duḥkhavedanīyasya duḥkhavipāko 'nujñāyate aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyasyāduḥkhāsukhavipāko 'nujñāyate / duḥkhasahagatasya karmaṇaḥ sukhavedanīyasya sukhavipāko 'nujñāyate duḥkhavedanīyasya duḥkhavipāko 'nujñāyate aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyasyāduḥkhāsukhavipāko 'nujñāyate / aduḥkhāsukhasahagatasya karmaṇaḥ sukhavedanīyasya (

body.text: api khalu karmaprabhedastrividhaḥ / saṃvarakarma asaṃvarakarma naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvarakarma ca / saṃvarakarma katamat / prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ karma dhyānasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ karma anāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ karma ca // prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ karma katamat / sapta saṃghopapannānāṃ saṃvarāḥ / bhikṣusaṃvaraḥ bhikṣuṇīsaṃvaraḥ śikṣamāṇavasaṃvaraḥ śrāmaṇerasaṃvaraḥ śrāmaṇerī saṃvaraḥ upāsakasaṃvaraḥ upāsikāsaṃvaraḥ upavāsasaṃvaraśca // katamaṃ pugdalamadhikṛtya pravrajitasaṃvaro vyavasthāpitaḥ / duścaritavivekacaritaṃ kāmavivekacaritaṃ pugdalamadhikṛtya / kaṃ pugdalamadhikṛtya upāsakopāsikāsaṃvaro vyavasthāpitaḥ / duścaritavivekacaritamadhikṛtya no tu kāmavivekacaritaṃ pugdalam // kaṃ pugdalamadhikṛtyopavāsasaṃvaro vyavasthāpitaḥ / naiva duścaritavivekacaritaṃ na kāmavivekacaritaṃ pugdalamadhikṛtya // upāsakānāmekatyānāṃ śikṣāsyānīyānāṃ śikṣasamavāgama ityucyate / upāsakasaṃvaro 'samanvāgama ityucyate / uktaḥ samanvāgamaḥ śīlavipattirapyucyate / yathā ṣaṇḍapaṇḍakānām / teṣā mupāsakasaṃvaraḥ pratiṣidhyate na vā / teṣāmupāsakasaṃvaro na pratiṣidhyate / kevalaṃ teṣāmupāsakatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate / bhikṣubhikṣuṇīnāmubhayapravrajitānāṃ saṃghasya pakṣasya saṃsevopāsanāyogyatvāt / paṇḍakaḥ punaḥ pañcavidhaḥ / jātipaṇḍakaḥ īrṣyāpaṇḍakaḥ pakṣapaṇḍakaḥ āsecanakapaṇḍakaḥ āpatpaṇḍakaśca //

dhyānasaṃvarasaṃgṛhitaṃ karma katamat / dauḥśīlyasamutthāpakānāṃ kleśānāṃ vījopaghāte sati kāmebhyo vītarāgasya yā viratiḥ / prathamadhyānavītarāgasya yā viratiḥ / dvitīyadhyanavītarāgasya yā viratiḥ / tṛtīyadhyānavītarāgasya yā viratiḥ / socyate dhyānasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ kāyavākkarma /
anāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ karma katamat / satyadarśanena anāsravamanaskārabalena pratilabdhā anāsravā viratiḥ / socyate anāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ karma //

asaṃvarakarma katamat / abhijanmato vā tatkarmasamādānato vā tatkarmādhyācāraniścayaḥ asaṃvara ityucyate / te punarasaṃvarāḥ katame / aurabhrikāḥ kaukkṛṭikāḥ śaukarikāḥ śākunikāḥ mātsyikāḥ lubdhakāḥ vāgurikāḥ corāḥ ghātakāḥ govaṃdhakāḥ nāgavaṃdhakāḥ māṇḍalikāḥ nāgamaṇḍalikāḥ kārāgārikāḥ sūcakāḥ upaghātakāḥ prabhṛtayaḥ /
naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvara saṃgṛhītaṃ karma katamat / naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvaravihāraḥ kuśalākuśalaṃ karma //

punaḥ karmaprabhedastrividhaḥ / sukhavedanīyaṃ karma duḥkhavedanīyaṃ karma aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ karma ca // sukhavedanīyaṃ karma katamat / kāmāvacarāt tṛtīyadhyānaṃ yāvad yat kuśalaṃ karma // duḥkhavedanīyaṃ karma katamat / akuśalaṃ karma // aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ karma katamat / tṛtīyadhyānādūrdhvaṃ yat kuśalaṃ karma /

karmaprabhedaḥ punastrividhaḥ / dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ karma upapadyavedanīyaṃ karma aparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ karma ca // dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ karma katamat / tatkarma dṛṣṭe dharme yasya vipāko vipacyate / tacca maitrīsamāpatteruccalitasyaṃ parihāṇiṃ vṛddhiṃ vā kurvataḥ dṛṣṭe dharme vipāko labhyate // yathā maitrīsamāpatteruccalitasya tathā araṇasamāpatteruccalitasya niurodhasamāpatteruccalitasya strotāpattiphalāduccalitasya arhattvaphalāduccalitasya ca / buddhapramukhe saṃghe kuśalamakuśalaṃ ca kurvataḥ dṛṣṭe dharme vipāko labhyate // anyeṣāṃ tīvrāśayaprayogeṇa kuśalākuśalakarmapratipannānāmapi dṛṣṭe dharme vipāko labhyate // upapadyavedanīyaṃ karma katamat / tatkarma anantare janmani yasya vipāko vipacyate / (

children.text: ) tadyathā paṃcanāntaryakarmāṇi / api ca yānyanyāni kuśalākuśalāni karmāṇi yeṣāmanantare janmani vipāko vipacyate tatsarvamucyate upapadyavedanīyaṃ karma // aparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ karma katamat / tatkarma yasyānantarajanmano 'paraparyāyeṣu vipāko vipacyate / taducyate 'paraparyāyavedanīyaṃ karma /

body.text: punaḥ karmaprabhedaścaturvidhaḥ / kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavipākaṃ karma śuklaṃ śuklavipākaṃ karma kṛṣṇaśuklaṃ kṛṣṇaśuklavipākaṃ karma akṛṣṇaśuklāvipākaṃ vyāmiśraṃ karma // kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavipākaṃ karma katamat / akuśalaṃ karma // śuklaṃ śuklavipākaṃ karma katamat / traidhātukaṃ kuśalaṃ karma // kṛṣṇaśuklaṃ kṛṣṇaśuklavipākaṃ karma katamat / kāmapratisaṃyuktaṃ karma yat karma vā āśayataḥ prayogato vā śuklaṃ yat karma vā prayogataḥ kṛṣṇamāśayataḥ śuklam // akṛṣṇaśuklāvipākaṃ vyāmiśraṃ karma katamat / prayogānantaryamārge 'nāsravaṃ karma aviśeṣeṇa ca sarvasyānāsravakarmaṇaḥ paripanthamānukūlyasvabhāvamadhikṛtya vaṃkadoṣakaṣāyāṇāṃ śauceyānāṃ mauneyānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ yathākramaṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tathā ca dānāni śauceyāni karmāṇi / dānakarma katamat / nidānataḥ utthānataḥ pradeśataḥ svabhāvataśca dānakarma vikalpyate / nidānam alobho 'dveṣo 'mohaśca kuśalamūlāni // utthānaṃ tānyeva cetanāsahagatāni // pradeśo deyāni vastūni // svabhāvo dānasaṃpattikāle kāyavāṅmanaskarmāṇi // dānasaṃpat katamā / abhīkṣṇadānataḥ apakṣapātadānataḥ icchāparipūraṇadānataśca dānasaṃpad veditavyā / api ca aniśritadānataḥ mahāśucidānataḥ parama prahṛṣṭadānataḥ abhikṣṇadānataḥ kṣetrabhājanadānataḥ navapurāṇasaṃvibhāgadānataśca dānasaṃpad veditavyā // deyasaṃpat katamā / anabhidutadeyavastutaḥ aparāpakṛtadeyavastutaḥ akuthitavimaladeyavastutaḥ śucideyavastutaḥ dharmārjitadeyavastutaśca deyasaṃpad veditavyā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, there is a fourfold classification of <s>karma</s>: dark <s>karma</s> with dark result, bright <s>karma</s> with bright result, dark-and-bright <s>karma</s> with dark-and-bright result, and neither-dark-nor-bright <s>karma</s> with mixed result. What is dark <s>karma</s> with dark result? It is unwholesome <s>karma</s>. What is bright <s>karma</s> with bright result? It is wholesome <s>karma</s> pertaining to the three realms. What is dark-and-bright <s>karma</s> with dark-and-bright result? It is <s>karma</s> connected with sensual desire, or <s>karma</s> that is bright in intention but dark in practice, or <s>karma</s> that is dark in practice but bright in intention. What is neither-dark-nor-bright mixed <s>karma</s> with [no particular] result? It is uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>karma</s> on the path of preparatory practice and the uninterrupted path, and in general, regarding all uncontaminated <s>karma</s>, the classification of <s>karmas</s> that are crooked, faulty, impure, and those that are pure (<s>śauceya</s>) and those of silence (<s>mauneya</s>) should be understood respectively, based on their nature of obstructing and favoring. Likewise, acts of giving (<s>dāna</s>) are pure <s>karmas</s>. What is the <s>karma</s> of giving? The <s>karma</s> of giving is analyzed according to its cause (<s>nidāna</s>), its arising (<s>utthāna</s>), its scope (<s>pradeśa</s>), and its intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). The cause is the wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>): non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>), non-aversion (<s>adveṣa</s>), and non-delusion (<s>amoha</s>). The arising is those [wholesome roots] accompanied by volition (<s>cetanā</s>). The scope is the things to be given. The intrinsic nature is the actions of body, speech, and mind at the time of the perfection of giving. What is the perfection of giving (<s>dānasaṃpat</s>)? It should be understood as the perfection of giving through frequent giving, impartial giving, and giving that fulfills the wishes [of recipients]. Moreover, the perfection of giving should be understood through: giving without attachment, giving with great purity, giving with supreme joy, frequent giving, giving to worthy fields (<s>kṣetra</s>) and vessels (<s>bhājana</s>), and giving that shares both new and old [possessions]. What is the perfection of what is given (<s>deyasaṃpat</s>)? It should be understood as perfection of what is given through: things not solicited, things not harmful to others, things unblemished and pure, things clean, and things acquired through <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tathācoktaṃ sūtre śīlasamanvāgataḥ prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛta ācāragocarasaṃpanno 'ṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu mahābhayadarśī śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu iti // kathaṃ śīlasamanvāgato bhavati / viśuddhaśīlanupkṣaṇopapannataḥ // kathaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛto bhavati / nairyāṇikaśīlasaṃdhāraṇataḥ // kathamācāragocarasaṃpanno bhavati / viśuddhaśīlasahabhāvato 'garhitānām // kathamaṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu mahābhayadarśī bhavati // tīvreṇa gauraveṇa śīlaśikṣaṇataḥ // kathaṃ śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu / śikṣāśīlānāṃ śikṣaṇataḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: "Endowed with morality (<s>śīla</s>), restrained by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint, accomplished in conduct and domain, seeing great danger in the slightest faults, one trains in the training rules." How is one endowed with morality? Through possessing pure morality and [its] observation. How is one restrained by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint? Through maintaining the morality leading to liberation (<s>nairyāṇika</s>). How is one accomplished in conduct and domain? Through the accompaniment of pure morality, which is blameless. How does one see great danger in the slightest faults? Through training in the discipline of morality with intense reverence. How does one train in the training rules? Through the training of the moralities to be trained in.

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ śīlamārabhya yad buddhena sūtreṣu nirdṛṣṭaṃ kāyena saṃvṛto bhavatītyevamādi // kathamucyate kāyena vācā saṃvṛto bhavati / saṃprajanyaparigṛhītataḥ // kathaṃ kāyavāksaṃpattyā saṃpanno bhavati / āpattyanāpattidānataḥ // kathaṃ pariśuddhakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / avipratisārādīnāṃ krameṇa saṃpratipattyā yāvat samādhilābhasanniśraya taḥ // kathaṃ kuśalakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / kliṣṭavitarkavyavatīrṇataḥ // kathamanavadyakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / mithyāpraṇidhiparivarjanena brahmacaryabhāvanātaḥ // kathamavyāvadhyakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / pareṣāmanavajñayā sukhasaṃvāsataḥ / kathamānulomikāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / nirvāṇaprāptyanukūlataḥ / katha manucchavikakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / kuśalasya cchādanato 'kuśalasya prakāśanataśca // kathamaupayikakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / sabrahmacaryagrahaṇaśīlataḥ // kathaṃ pratirūpakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / guruṣu gurusthānīyeṣu cānihitamānataḥ // kathaṃ pradakṣiṇakāyāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / avavāde pradakṣiṇaprāhitataḥ // kathamataptakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / kaṣṭapohīnādhimukti vivarjitataḥ // kathamatanutāpyakāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / samutsṛṣṭabhogakarmāntāvipratisāritaḥ / kathamavipratisārikāyavāksamudācāro bhavati / alpamātreṇāsaṃtuṣṭāvipratisāritayā //
body.translated_text: Hereafter, regarding morality (<s>śīla</s>), what the <s>Buddha</s> has taught in the <s>sūtras</s> beginning with 'one is restrained in body,' and so forth: How is one said to be restrained in body and speech? Through being governed by clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>). How is one accomplished with the excellence of body and speech? Through [knowing] what is an offense and what is not an offense. How is one of purified bodily and verbal conduct? Through the sequential practice beginning with freedom from remorse, up to the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>. How is one of wholesome bodily and verbal conduct? Through having transcended afflicted thought (<s>kliṣṭavitarka</s>). How is one of blameless bodily and verbal conduct? Through cultivating the holy life by avoiding wrong aspirations. How is one of non-injurious bodily and verbal conduct? Through living harmoniously without contempt for others. How is one of conforming bodily and verbal conduct? Through being favorable to the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. How is one of becoming bodily and verbal conduct? Through concealing one's virtues and revealing one's faults. How is one of suitable bodily and verbal conduct? Through being disposed to supporting fellow practitioners of the holy life. How is one of proper bodily and verbal conduct? Through not having a haughty attitude toward teachers and those worthy of a teacher's position. How is one of auspicious bodily and verbal conduct? Through being well-disposed toward instruction. How is one of untormented bodily and verbal conduct? Through avoiding aspirations born of suffering and inferiority. How is one of unrepentant bodily and verbal conduct? Through being generous with possessions and work without regret. How is one of remorse-free bodily and verbal conduct? Through being free of regret by not being content with merely a little.

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhagavatā yathā sattvāḥ / karmasvakā karmadāyādāḥ karmayonīyāḥ karmapratisaraṇāḥ karma sarvān sattvān vibhajati uccanīcatayā hīnapraṇītatayā (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 61]

children.text: ) iti // kathaṃ sattvāḥ karmasvakā bhavanti / svayaṃkṛtakarmanipākapratisaṃvedanātāmupādaya // kathaṃ karmadāyādā bhavanti / svayaṃ kṛtakarmavipākapratisaṃvedanatāyāṃ kuśalākuśalānāṃ karmaṇāmanyonyadāyādatāmupādāya // kathaṃ karmayonīyā bhavanti / sattvānāṃ mahetuviṣamahetuvivarjitayonitāmupādāya // kathaṃ karmapratisaraṇā bhavanti / pratipakṣakarmaviśiṣṭakarmabandhanāśrayatāmupādāya // kathaṃ karmaṇā sattvo uccanīcā bhavanti / yat karmaṇā sugatau durgatau vātmabhāvaprabhedaṃ labhante // kathaṃ hīnapraṇītā bhavanti / yat sattvā guṇadoṣaprabhedena samanvāgatā bhavanti //
children.translated_text: How are beings the owners of their <s>karma</s>? By virtue of experiencing the ripening of <s>karma</s> done by themselves. How are they heirs of their <s>karma</s>? By virtue of the mutual inheritance of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karmas</s> in the experience of the ripening of self-made <s>karma</s>. How are they born of their <s>karma</s>? By virtue of beings' birth being free from a great cause or an unequal cause. How are they related to their <s>karma</s>? By virtue of being dependent on the bondage of <s>karma</s> and the superior <s>karma</s> of the antidote. How does <s>karma</s> make beings high and low? In that through <s>karma</s> they obtain the distinctions of personal existence in good or bad destinies. How do they become inferior and superior? In that beings are endowed with the distinction of virtues and faults.

body.translated_text: As the Blessed One has said: "Beings are the owners of their <s>karma</s>, heirs of their <s>karma</s>, born of their <s>karma</s>, related to their <s>karma</s>; <s>karma</s> divides all beings into high and low, into inferior and superior,

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhagavatā sattvānāṃ karmavipāko 'cintya iti / tatra kathaṃ karmavipākaścintyaḥ kathaṃ karmavipāko 'cintyaḥ / kuśalasya karmaṇo devamanuṣyagatisviṣṭa vipākalā bhaścintyaḥ / akuśalasya karmaṇo hīnāsu tisṛṣu durgatiṣu aniṣṭavipākalābhaścintyaḥ / ayaṃ cintyaḥ // yena karmaṇā sattvānāmātmabhāvavipākavaicitryamabhunirvarttate so 'cintyaḥ / tadeva kuśalākuśalaṃ karmasthānavastuhetuvipākaprakārādiprabhederacintyam / vividhavāhyavastuvaicitryābhinirvarttakaṃ karmācintyam / maṇimantraupadhimuṣṭiyogapratisaṃyuktaṃ karmācintyam / yogināṃ prabhāvakarmacintyuam / bodhisattvānāṃ vaśitābhiḥ kriyamāṇaṃ karmā citnyam / tadyathā āyurvaśitayā cittavaśitayā pariṣkāravaśitayā karmavaśitayā upapattivaśitayā adhimuktivaśitayā praṇidhānavaśitayā ṛddhivaśitayā jñānavaśitayā dharmavaśitayā / evaṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmevamādibhirvaśitābhiryatkarma kriyate tadacintyam / sarveṣāṃ buddhānāṃ vuddhakṛtyānuṣṭhānaṃ karmācintyam //
body.translated_text: As the Blessed One has said: "The ripening of beings' <s>karma</s> is inconceivable." In that regard, how is the ripening of <s>karma</s> conceivable, and how is it inconceivable? The obtaining of desired results of wholesome <s>karma</s> in the destinies of gods and humans is conceivable. The obtaining of undesired results of unwholesome <s>karma</s> in the three lower unfortunate destinies is conceivable — this is the conceivable. That <s>karma</s> by which the diversity of the ripening of beings' personal existence is produced is inconceivable. That very same wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>, with its distinctions of basis, object, cause, result, and mode, is inconceivable. <s>Karma</s> that produces the diversity of various external objects is inconceivable. <s>Karma</s> connected with gems, mantras, medicinal substances, and <s>yoga</s> practices is inconceivable. The powerful <s>karma</s> of <s>yogins</s> is inconceivable. The <s>karma</s> performed through the masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is inconceivable — namely: mastery over lifespan, mastery over mind, mastery over requisites, mastery over <s>karma</s>, mastery over birth, mastery over aspiration, mastery over resolve, mastery over supernatural power, mastery over knowledge, and mastery over <s>Dharma</s>. Thus, whatever <s>karma</s> is performed by great <s>Bodhisattvas</s> through such masteries is inconceivable. The <s>karma</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s> in carrying out Buddha-activities is inconceivable.

body.text: tathā ca samudayasatyaṃ samāsato lakṣaṇaprabhedena caturvidham / hetulakṣaṇaṃ samudayalakṣaṇaṃ prabhavalakṣaṇaṃ pratyalakṣaṇaṃ ca / hetulakṣaṇaṃ katamat / punarbhavavāsanāyā āhārakaṃ kāraṇaṃ heturiti hetulakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam // samudayalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / teṣāṃ teṣāmupacitavāsanānāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmiṃstasmin sattvanikāye udayasya kāraṇamiti (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 62]

children.text: ) samudayalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam // prabhuvalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / pratyātmaṃ santānānāṃ sarvaprakāraprakarṣodbhavasya kāraṇamiti prabhavalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam // pratyalakṣaṇaṃ katamat / sattvānāṣānpaprāptyatyayakāraṇamiti pratyayakāraṇaṃ veditavyam //
children.translated_text: The characteristic of origination should be understood as the cause of the arising of those beings, who have accumulated impressions, in those respective classes of beings. What is the characteristic of production? The cause of the arising of all kinds of intensification within one's own continuum (<s>santāna</s>) should be understood as the characteristic of production. What is the characteristic of condition? The cause of beings' non-attainment and destruction should be understood as the characteristic of condition.

body.translated_text: Likewise, the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>), in brief, is fourfold according to the distinction of characteristics: the characteristic of cause (<s>hetulakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of origination (<s>samudayalakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of production (<s>prabhavalakṣaṇa</s>), and the characteristic of condition (<s>pratyayalakṣaṇa</s>). What is the characteristic of cause? The cause that functions as the nourishing factor of the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) for renewed existence should be understood as the characteristic of cause.

body.text: (atha viniścaye satyaparicchede prathame tṛtīyo bhāgaḥ) /
body.translated_text: (Now, in the ascertainment [section], in the chapter on the truths, the third part of the first [division].)

body.text: nirodhasatyaṃ katamat / lakṣaṇataḥ gāmbhīryataḥ saṃvṛtitaḥ paramārthataḥ aparipūritaḥ paripūritaḥ niralaṃkārataḥ sālaṃkārataḥ śeṣataḥ aśeṣataḥ agrataḥ paryāyataśca nirodhasatyaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: What is the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>)? The truth of cessation should be understood from [the perspective of]: characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>), conventional [truth] (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), ultimate [truth] (<s>paramārtha</s>), unfulfilled, fulfilled, unadorned, adorned, with remainder, without remainder, foremost, and synonyms (<s>paryāya</s>).

body.text: lakṣaṇataḥ katamat / tathatāyāmārya mārge kleśānāmanutpādo yo nirodhāśrayo nirodhako nirodhasvabhāvo vā // tannirodhasatyalakṣaṇam // yaduktaṃ bhagavatā cakṣuḥ śrotre ghrāṇajivhākāyāḥ / manaśca teṣu āyataneṣu nāmarūpayorātyantikanirodho na śeṣaḥ iti / yaccoktaṃ tadāyatanaṃ veditavyaṃ yathā cakṣuśca nirudhyate rūpasaṃjñā ca virajyate yāvat manaśca nirudhyate dharmasaṃjñā ca virajyate iti / anena nayena ālambanānāṃ prāpaṇaṃ tathatāyāmālambanādūrdhvaṃ sāsravāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodhaḥ / tannirodhasatya lakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: What is it from the perspective of its characteristic? In <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), through the <s>āryamārga</s> (noble path), the non-arising of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — that which is the basis of cessation, that which brings about cessation, or that which has the nature of cessation — that is the characteristic of the truth of cessation. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'The eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body, and the mind — in those <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), the complete and final cessation of name-and-form, with no remainder.' And as it has been said: 'That <s>āyatana</s> should be known wherein the eye ceases and the perception of form fades away, up to where the mind ceases and the perception of <s>dharmas</s> fades away.' By this method, the directing of objects — beyond objects in <s>tathatā</s> — is the cessation of <s>dharmas</s> with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>). That is the characteristic of the truth of cessation.

body.text: gāmbhīryataḥ katamat / yat teṣāṃ saṃskārāṇāmuparamānnirodhaḥ / tathoparamāt teṣāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ nirodho nānyo vācyaḥ nānanyo vācyaḥ nāpyanyo nāpyananyo vācyaḥ na naivānyo nānanyo vācyaḥ // kutaḥ / niṣprapañcataḥ / asmiṃstvarthe prapañcotpattiḥ na saṃcintyā na mārgeṇa na nyāyena na kuśalaprayogeṇa cintyā iti / yaduktaṃ bhagavatā teṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ spraṣṭāvyayatanānāṃ kṣayo virāgo nirodho vyupaśamo 'staṃgama ityevamādi / syādanyaḥ syādananyaḥ syādanyo 'pi nānyo 'pi (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 63

children.text: ) syānnaivānyo nānanyo 'pi iti niṣprapañca prapañca utpadyate // yāvat ṣaḍāyatanāni tāvat prapañcāḥ // yadā ṣaḍāyatanānāṃ nirodhaśchedaḥ tadā prapañcānāṃ viratiḥ //
children.translated_text: it might be neither other nor not-other' — thus conceptual elaboration arises regarding that which is beyond elaboration. As long as there are the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), so long there are conceptual elaborations. When there is the cessation and cutting off of the six sense bases, then there is the cessation of conceptual elaborations.

body.translated_text: What is it from the perspective of profundity? That cessation which arises from the subsiding of those <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — because of that subsiding, the cessation of those <s>saṃskāras</s> is not to be called other, not to be called not-other, not to be called both other and not-other, and not to be called neither other nor not-other. Why? Because it is beyond conceptual elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>). In this matter, the arising of conceptual elaboration is not to be thought of, not to be thought of through the path, through reasoning, or through wholesome application. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'The destruction, fading away, cessation, pacification, and disappearance of those six tangible sense bases' and so forth — 'It might be other, it might be not-other, it might be both other and not-other,

body.text: saṃvṛtitaḥ katamat / laukikamārgairvījanigraheṇa yo nirodho labhyate / ato bhagavatā tadāṃśikanirvāṇamityucyate // paramārthataḥ katamat / āryaprajñayā bījanirmūlanena yo nirodho labhyate // aparipūritaḥ katamat / śaikṣāṇāṃ strotāpannaphalasaṃgraheṇa vā sakṛdāgamiphalasaṃgraheṇa vā anāgāmiphalasaṃgraheṇa vā yo nirodhaḥ // paripūritaḥ katamat / aśaikṣyāṇāmarhattvaphalasaṃgraheṇa yo nirodhaḥ // niralaṃkārataḥ katamat / prajñāvimuktānāmarhatāṃ yo nirodhaḥ // sālaṃkārataḥ katamat / ubhayabhāga vimuktānāṃ traividyānāṃ ṣaḍabhijñānāmarhatāṃ yo nirodhaḥ // śeṣataḥ katamat / sopadhiśeṣo yo nirodhaḥ // aśeṣataḥ katamat / nirupadhiśeṣo yo nirodhaḥ // agrataḥ katamat / buddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāmapratiṣṭhitanirvāṇasaṃgraheṇa yo nirodhaḥ / sparśavihāriṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ hitasukhādhiṣṭhānataḥ //
body.translated_text: What is it from the perspective of conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>)? The cessation obtained through worldly paths by the suppression of seeds. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> calls it 'partial <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' What is it from the perspective of ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>)? The cessation obtained through noble wisdom (<s>āryaprajñā</s>) by the eradication of seeds. What is it in its incomplete form? The cessation for learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>), included in the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpanna</s>), the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), or the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmin</s>). What is it in its complete form? The cessation for non-learners (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), included in the fruit of <s>arhatship</s>. What is it without adornment? The cessation of <s>arhats</s> liberated by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>). What is it with adornment? The cessation of <s>arhats</s> liberated in both ways (<s>ubhayabhāgavimukta</s>), possessing the three knowledges (<s>traividya</s>) and the six superknowledges (<s>ṣaḍabhijñā</s>). What is it with remainder? Cessation with a remainder of the basis (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>). What is it without remainder? Cessation without a remainder of the basis (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). What is it in its supreme form? The cessation of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, included in the non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>), based on the establishment of benefit and happiness for all beings while dwelling in direct experience.

body.text: paryāyataḥ katamat / aśeṣaprahāṇaṃ pratiniḥsargaḥ vyantībhāvaḥ kṣayo virāgo nirodho vyupaśamo 'staṃgama ityevamādi // kimupādāyocyate aśeṣaprahāṇam / pariśiṣṭāni padānyupādāya // kimupādāyocyate pratiniḥsargaḥ / paryavasthānapratiniḥsaraṇatāmupādāya // kimupādāyocyate kṣayaḥ / darśanamārgeṇa pratipakṣavisaṃyogalābhatā mupādāya // kimupādāyocyate virāgaḥ / bhāvanāmārgeṇa pratipakṣavisaṃyogalābhatāmupādāya // kimupādāyocyate nirodhaḥ / āyatyāṃ tatphaladuḥkhānutpattitāmupādāya // kimupādāyocyate vyupaśamaḥ / dṛṣṭe dharme tatphalacettaduḥkhāsamudācāratāmupādāya // kimupādāyocyate 'staṃgamaḥ / sopadhiśeṣa nirodhatāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: What is it from the perspective of synonyms? Complete abandonment, relinquishment, disappearance, destruction, fading away, cessation, pacification, disappearance, and so forth. In reference to what is it called 'complete abandonment'? In reference to the remaining terms. In reference to what is it called 'relinquishment'? In reference to the release from entanglements (<s>paryavasthāna</s>). In reference to what is it called 'destruction'? In reference to obtaining disjunction from afflictions through the antidote of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). In reference to what is it called 'fading away'? In reference to obtaining disjunction from afflictions through the antidote of the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>). In reference to what is it called 'cessation'? In reference to the non-arising of the resultant suffering in the future. In reference to what is it called 'pacification'? In reference to the non-occurrence of the resultant suffering and mental suffering in the present life. In reference to what is it called 'disappearance'? In reference to cessation with remainder of the basis.

body.text: kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarasaṃskṛtamityucyate / lakṣaṇatrayavirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punardurdarśa ityucyate / carmacakṣuṣo divyacakṣuṣaśca (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 64

children.text: ) gocarātikamaṇatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaracalamityucyate / matiṣu saṃcārabirahamāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaramata mityucyate / tṛṣṇātrayavirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaramṛtamityucyate / skandhamāravirahatāmupādāya // kimuipādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaranāsravamityucyate / sarva kleśamāravirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarlayanamityucyate / anavadyaprītisukhasaṃniśrayatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punardvīpamityucyate / traidhātukaparicchedatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punastrāṇamityucyate / sarvamahāduḥkhopadravāpagamatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaḥ śaraṇamityucyate / āśayaprayogayoravandhyapadasthānatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaḥ parāyaṇamityucyate / sarvasya paramāryatvasyāgamanapadasthāṇatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaracyutamityucyate / jātivirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodha punarnirvāramityucyate / sarvakleśasantāpavirahatāṃ sarvecchālābhaduḥkhamahāsantāpavirahatāṃ copādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarniṣpadāridāhamiotyute / sarva śokaparidevanāduḥkhadaurmanasya vikṣepavirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaḥ kṣemamityucyate / hiṃsā bhayarahitavihārapadasthānatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaḥ śivamityucyate / lābhavastupadasthāna tāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaḥ sauvarṇikamityucyate paramārthasukhādhiṣṭhānatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaḥ svastyayanamityucyate / tatsukhaprayogaprāptipadasthānatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarogyamityucyate / sarvāvaraṇaro gavirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarārnijyamityucyate / sarvavikṣepavirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarnirvāṇamityucyate / animittaśāntamahā sukhavihārapadasthānatāmupādāya / kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarajātamityucyate / pratisaṃdhyupapattivirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarabhūtamityucyate / taduttarakālotpattivirahatāmupādāya // (
children.translated_text: In reference to what is that cessation further called 'immovable'? In reference to its being free from movement among the afflictions. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'undying'? In reference to its being free from the three types of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). In reference to what is that cessation further called 'deathless' (<s>amṛta</s>)? In reference to its being free from the <s>Māra</s> of the aggregates. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'without outflows' (<s>anāsrava</s>)? In reference to its being free from the <s>Māra</s> of all afflictions. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'a resting place'? In reference to its being the basis of blameless joy and happiness. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'an island'? In reference to its being the demarcation from the three realms. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'protection' (<s>trāṇa</s>)? In reference to its being the departure from all great sufferings and calamities. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'refuge' (<s>śaraṇa</s>)? In reference to its being the ground where intention and practice are not fruitless. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'the final goal' (<s>parāyaṇa</s>)? In reference to its being the ground of attainment of the highest nobility. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'without falling' (<s>acyuta</s>)? In reference to its being free from birth. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'without fever' (<s>nirvāra</s>)? In reference to its being free from the torment of all afflictions and free from the great torment of the suffering of desiring gain. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'without thirst or drought'? In reference to its being free from all grief, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and disturbance. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'security' (<s>kṣema</s>)? In reference to its being the ground of dwelling free from harm and fear. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'auspicious' (<s>śiva</s>)? In reference to its being the ground of the object of attainment. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'golden' (<s>sauvarṇika</s>)? In reference to its being the establishment of ultimate happiness. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'well-being' (<s>svastyayana</s>)? In reference to its being the ground of attainment through the practice of that happiness. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'health' (<s>ārogya</s>)? In reference to its being free from all obscuring afflictions. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'imperturbable' (<s>āñijya</s>)? In reference to its being free from all disturbance. In reference to what is that cessation further called '<s>nirvāṇa</s>'? In reference to its being the ground of dwelling in the great happiness of signless peace. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'unborn' (<s>ajāta</s>)? In reference to its being free from rebirth-linking and re-becoming. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'non-existent' (<s>abhūta</s>)? In reference to its being free from arising at any subsequent time.

children.text: ) kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaraskṛtamityucyate / pūrvāntakarmakleśabalavadā vedhavirahatāmupādāya // kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punarasaṃskṛtamityucyate / vartamānakarma kleśānabhisaṃskāra padasthānatāmupādāya / kimupādāya sa nirodhaḥ punaranutpannamityucyate / anāgatasantatyutpādavirahatāmupādāya //
children.translated_text: In reference to what is that cessation further called 'unmade' (<s>askṛta</s>)? In reference to its being free from the powerful influence of karma and afflictions from past lives. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'unconditioned' (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)? In reference to its being the ground of non-conditioning by present karma and afflictions. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'unarisen' (<s>anutpanna</s>)? In reference to its being free from the arising of a future continuum.

body.translated_text: In reference to what is that cessation further called 'unconditioned' (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)? In reference to its being devoid of the three characteristics. In reference to what is that cessation further called 'hard to see'? In reference to its transcending the range of the fleshly eye and the divine eye.

body.text: tathā nirodhasatyasya samāsataścatvāro lakṣaṇaprabhedāḥ / nirodhalakṣaṇaṃ śāntalakṣaṇaṃ praṇītalakṣaṇaṃ niḥsaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ ca / kimupādāya nirodhalakṣaṇam / kleśavisaṃyogatāmupādāya // kimupādāya śāntalakṣaṇam / duḥkhavisaṃyogatāmupādāya / kimupādāya praṇītalakṣaṇam / sukhaśucyadhiṣṭhānatāmupādāya // kimupādāya niḥsaraṇalakṣaṇam / nityahitādhiṣṭhānatāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: Likewise, in summary, there are four subdivisions of the characteristics of the truth of cessation: the characteristic of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), the characteristic of peace (<s>śānta</s>), the characteristic of excellence (<s>praṇīta</s>), and the characteristic of deliverance (<s>niḥsaraṇa</s>). In reference to what is there the characteristic of cessation? In reference to disjunction from afflictions. In reference to what is there the characteristic of peace? In reference to disjunction from suffering. In reference to what is there the characteristic of excellence? In reference to its being the establishment of happiness and purity. In reference to what is there the characteristic of deliverance? In reference to its being the establishment of eternal benefit.

body.text: (atha viniścaye satyaparicchede prathame caturtho bhāgaḥ)
body.translated_text: (Now the fourth section of the first chapter on truth in the <s>Viniścaya</s>)

body.text: mārgasatyaṃ katamat / yena duḥkhaṃ parijānīte samudayaṃ prajahāti nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti mārgaṃ bhāvayati / etat saṃkṣepeṇa mārgasatyalakṣaṇamityucyate // punaḥ mārgaḥ pañcavidhaḥ / saṃbhāramārgaḥ prayogamārgaḥ darśanamārga bhāvanāmārgaḥ niṣṭhāmārgaśca /
body.translated_text: What is the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>)? That by which one fully knows suffering, abandons its origin, directly realizes cessation, and cultivates the path — this, in brief, is called the characteristic of the truth of the path. Furthermore, the path is fivefold: the path of accumulation (<s>saṃbhāramārga</s>), the path of preparation (<s>prayogamārga</s>), the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), and the path of completion (<s>niṣṭhāmārga</s>).

body.text: saṃbhāramārgaḥ katamaḥ / pṛthagjanānāṃ śīlam indriyadvārarakṣā bhojane mātrājñatā prathamarātrau taduttararātriṣu vā nityamamiddhaṃ vīryabhāvanā śamathavipaśyanā saṃprajanyavihāraśca // yadvā punaranyadaupaniṣadaṃ kuśalam śrutamayī prajñā cintāmayī prajñā bhāvanāmayī prajñā // tadbhāvanayā abhisamayavimokṣasthānabhājanāṃ pratilabhate /
body.translated_text: What is the path of accumulation (<s>saṃbhāramārga</s>)? For ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>): moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), guarding the doors of the sense faculties, moderation in eating, constant vigilance without drowsiness in the first watch and the later watches of the night, cultivation of energy (<s>vīrya</s>), <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), and dwelling in clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>). Or again, any other wholesome conducive quality: wisdom born of hearing (<s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>), wisdom born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>), and wisdom born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>). Through their cultivation, one becomes a suitable vessel for the stages of realization and liberation.

body.text: prayogamārgaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ saṃbhāramārgaḥ sa prayogamārgaḥ / yastu prayogamārgaḥ sana saṃbhāramārgaḥ / saṃbhāramārgopacitāni nirvedhabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlāni ūṣmagataḥ mūrdhānaḥ satyānukūlakṣānti laukikāgradharmaśca // ūṣmagataṃ katamat / pratyātmaṃ satye pvālokalabdhaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā saṃyogaśca // mūrdhānaṃ katamat / pratyātmaṃ satyeṣvālokavṛddhaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā saṃyogaśca // satyānukūlakṣāntiḥ katamā / pratyātmaṃ satyeṣvekadeśapraviṣṭānusṛtaḥ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 66]

children.text: ) samādhiḥ prajñā saṃyogaśca // laukikāgradharmaḥ katamaḥ / pratyātmaṃ satyeṣvānantaryacittasamādhiḥ prajñā saṃyogaśca //
children.translated_text: and follows them. What is the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>? It is the <s>samādhi</s>, wisdom, and their conjunction, in the mind immediately preceding [the supramundane path], personally regarding the truths.

body.translated_text: What is the preparatory path (<s>prayogamārga</s>)? Whatever is the path of accumulation (<s>saṃbhāramārga</s>), that is [also] the preparatory path. But what is specifically the preparatory path is not [merely] the path of accumulation. The wholesome roots leading to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya kuśalamūla</s>), accumulated through the path of accumulation, are: heat (<s>ūṣmagata</s>), summit (<s>mūrdhāna</s>), receptive acceptance of truth (<s>satyānukūlakṣānti</s>), and supreme worldly <s>dharma</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>). What is heat? It is the <s>samādhi</s>, wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), and their conjunction, through which one personally obtains a glimpse of light regarding the truths. What is summit? It is the <s>samādhi</s>, wisdom, and their conjunction, through which the light regarding the truths personally increases. What is receptive acceptance of truth? It is the <s>samādhi</s>, wisdom, and their conjunction, through which one personally enters partially into the truths,

body.text: darśanamārgaḥ katamaḥ / samāsato laukikā gradharmānantaramanupalambhaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā saṃyogaśca // samasamālambyālambanajñāmapi tat / pratyātmamapanītasattvasaṃketadharmasaṃketasarvato 'panītobhayasaṃketālambanadharmajñānamapi tat //
body.translated_text: What is the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>)? In brief, it is the <s>samādhi</s>, wisdom, and their conjunction of non-apprehension, immediately following the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>. It is also knowledge that takes the same object as its referent. It is also knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> personally, with the conventions of beings removed, the conventions of <s>dharmas</s> removed, and the referent with both conventions entirely removed.

body.text: prabhedaśaḥ śunardarśanamārgo laukikāgradharmānantaraṃ duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ, duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ duḥkhe 'nvayajñānaṃ samudaye dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ samudaye dharmajñānaṃ samudaye 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ samudaye 'nvayajñānaṃ nirodhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ nirodhe dharmajñānaṃ nirodhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ nirodhe 'nvayajñānaṃ mārge dharmajñānakṣāntiṃ mārge dharmajñānaṃ mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ mārge 'nvayajñānam // evaṃca ṣoḍaśa jñānakṣāntibhirdarśanamārgaprabhedāḥ //
body.translated_text: In detail, the path of seeing is as follows: immediately following the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>: acceptance of knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of suffering (<s>duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānti</s>), knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of suffering (<s>duḥkhe dharmajñāna</s>), subsequent acceptance of knowledge of suffering (<s>duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣānti</s>), subsequent knowledge of suffering (<s>duḥkhe anvayajñāna</s>), acceptance of knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of origination (<s>samudaye dharmajñānakṣānti</s>), knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of origination, subsequent acceptance of knowledge of origination, subsequent knowledge of origination, acceptance of knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of cessation (<s>nirodhe dharmajñānakṣānti</s>), knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of cessation, subsequent acceptance of knowledge of cessation, subsequent knowledge of cessation, acceptance of knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of the path (<s>mārge dharmajñānakṣānti</s>), knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of the path, subsequent acceptance of knowledge of the path, subsequent knowledge of the path. Thus, through sixteen knowledge-acceptances (<s>jñānakṣānti</s>), the divisions of the path of seeing [are established].

body.text: dukhaṃ katamat / duḥkhasatyam // duḥkhe dharmaḥ katamaḥ / duḥkhasatyādhipateyaḥ śāsanadharmaḥ // dharmajñānaṃ katamat / prayogamārge satyādhipateyaṃ dharmavicāraṇājñānam // jñānakṣāntiḥ katamā / pūrvādhipatibalavicāraṇāmupādāya pratyātmaṃ duḥkhasatye pratyakṣānubhāvinī anāsravā prajñā / yayā prajñāyā duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyān sarvakleśān prajahāti / tasmāducyate duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiriti // duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ katamat / kṣāntyanantaraṃ yena jñānena pūrvoktebhyaḥ kleśebhyo vimuktiṃ sākṣātkaroti / tasmāducyate duḥkhe dharmajñānamiti / duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣāntiḥ katamā / duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntyāṃ duḥkhe dharmajñāne ca pratyātmaṃ pratyakṣānubhāvinī anāsravā prajñā utpadyate yaduttaramanvaya eṣa āryadharmāṇām / tasmāducyate duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣāntiḥ // duḥkhe anvayajñānaṃ katamat / tadanantaramanāsravaṃ jñānamutpadyate / yena jñānena duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣāntimupadhārayati / tad duḥkhe 'nvayajñānamityucyate // tadvadanyeṣu satyeṣu yathāyogyam /
body.translated_text: What is suffering? The truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>). What is the <s>dharma</s> regarding suffering? The doctrinal teaching (<s>śāsanadharma</s>) that has the truth of suffering as its governing [object]. What is knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmajñāna</s>)? On the preparatory path, the knowledge born of investigating the <s>dharma</s> that has truth as its governing [object]. What is acceptance of knowledge (<s>jñānakṣānti</s>)? Based on the prior governing force and the investigation, it is the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) wisdom that personally has direct experience of the truth of suffering, by which wisdom one abandons all afflictions to be abandoned through seeing suffering. Therefore it is called 'acceptance of knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of suffering.' What is knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of suffering? The knowledge immediately following acceptance, by which one directly realizes liberation from the previously mentioned afflictions. Therefore it is called 'knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of suffering.' What is subsequent acceptance of knowledge of suffering (<s>duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣānti</s>)? Through the acceptance of knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of suffering and knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of suffering, undefiled wisdom arises personally with direct experience — that which is a subsequent [application] following the noble <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore it is called 'subsequent acceptance of knowledge of suffering.' What is subsequent knowledge of suffering? The undefiled knowledge that arises immediately after that, by which one confirms the subsequent acceptance of knowledge of suffering. That is called 'subsequent knowledge of suffering.' Likewise for the other truths, as appropriate.

body.text: kṣāntirjñānakṣayo jñeyaḥ / tatra avasthāyāṃ dharmakṣāntijñānaiḥ grāhyāvanoghaḥ / anvayakṣāntijñānairgrāhakāvabodhaḥ / api ca eṣu sarveṣu kṣāntijñāneṣu animittaprekṣāvihārī veditavyaḥ // ime ṣoḍaśa cittakṣaṇā darśanamārga ākhyātaḥ // jñeye jñānotpattiparisamāptirekaścittalakṣaṇo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Acceptance should be understood as the cessation of knowledge. In that state, through <s>dharma</s>-acceptances and knowledges, there is the relinquishing of the apprehended; through subsequent acceptances and knowledges, there is the awakening of the apprehender. Moreover, in all these acceptances and knowledges, one should be understood as abiding in the contemplation of signlessness (<s>animitta</s>). These sixteen mind-moments are declared to be the path of seeing. The completion of the arising of knowledge regarding the knowable should be understood as one mind-characteristic.

body.text: sarvaṃ hi mārgasatyaṃ caturbhiḥ prakārairanugantavyam / vyavasthānataḥ vikalpanataḥ anubhavataḥ paripūritaśca / vyavasthānataḥ katamat / yathāsvamadhigamaniṣṭhāprāptāḥ śrāvakādayaḥ / tatpṛṣṭhalabdhena jñānena prāpaṇanimittapramāṇaiḥ nāmapadavyañjanakāyaiḥ mārgasatyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti / vikalpanataḥ katamat / abhisamayaprayuktā laukikena jñānena yathāvyavasthānaṃ vikalpoyanto yadabhyasyanti // anubhavataḥ katamat / tathābhyasyanto mayā (?yadā)dito darśanamārgākhyāṃ lokottarāṃ niṣprapañcāvasthāṃ pratyātmamanubhavati // paripūritaḥ katamat / tadūrdhvaṃ yāmāśrayaparivṛttiṃ paripūrya yāvadadhigamaniṣṭhāṃ prāpnuvanti / tena punaradhigamaniṣṭhāprāptāstatpṛṣṭhalabdhena jñānena nāmapadavyañjanakāyaiḥ mārgasatyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti //
body.translated_text: For the entire truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) should be approached in four ways: through establishment, through conceptualization, through experience, and through completion. Through establishment — how? <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others who have attained the culmination of their respective realizations establish the truth of the path through the knowledge obtained subsequently, using names, words, and syllables (<s>nāmapadavyañjanakāya</s>) as signs and measures of attainment. Through conceptualization — how? Those engaged in realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>), through worldly knowledge, conceptualize according to the establishment and practice. Through experience — how? Thus practicing, one personally experiences, from the beginning, the supramundane state free from conceptual elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>), called the path of seeing. Through completion — how? From then onward, until they accomplish the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>) and reach the culmination of realization. Having thus attained the culmination of realization, they again establish the truth of the path through subsequently obtained knowledge, using names, words, and syllables.

body.text: yaduktaṃ sūtre virajño vītamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurūdapādi iti / taddarśanamārgamadhikṛtyoktam / tatra dharmakṣāntibhirvirajaḥ dharmajñānairvītamalam parijñayā prahāṇena mārgaśuddhilābhena ca //
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The dustless, stainless <s>dharma</s>-eye arose regarding <s>dharmas</s>' — this was said with reference to the path of seeing. Therein, 'dustless' through <s>dharma</s>-acceptances, 'stainless' through <s>dharma</s>-knowledges — through full understanding (<s>parijñā</s>), through abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>), and through attaining the purity of the path.

body.text: yaduktaṃ sūtre dṛṣṭadharmā prāptadharmā viditadharmā paryavagāḍhadharmā sarvaiḥ tīrṇakāṃkṣaḥ tīrṇavicikitsaḥ aparapratyayaḥ śāstuḥ śāsano 'nanyaneyaḥ dharmeṣu vaiśāradyaprāpta iti tadapi darśanamārgamadhikṛtyoktam / dṛṣṭadharmā dharmakṣāntibhiḥ / prāptadharmā dharmajñānaiḥ / viditadharmā anvayakṣāntibhiḥ / paryavagāḍhadharmā anvayajñānaiḥ / sarvaiḥ tīrṇakāṃkṣaḥ svādhigame kṣāntijñānaiḥ kāṃkṣābhāvena / tīrṇavicikitsaḥ parādhigame tadavasthasya vimatyabhāvena / aparapratyayaḥ mārgabhāvanāyāṃ na parataḥ svayaṃ kuśalāvarjanena / śāstuḥ śāsane 'nanyaneyaḥ buddhaśāsane (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 68]

based on the quality of not being led away by other sectarians. 'Having attained confidence regarding <s>dharmas</s>' — based on having an unshrunken mind regarding <s>dharmas</s> worthy of inquiry concerning realization.

body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One who has seen the <s>Dharma</s>, attained the <s>Dharma</s>, understood the <s>Dharma</s>, penetrated the <s>Dharma</s>, crossed beyond all doubt, gone beyond uncertainty, independent of others, in the Teacher's teaching, not to be led by another, having attained confidence regarding <s>dharmas</s>' — this too was said with reference to the path of seeing. 'One who has seen the <s>Dharma</s>' — through <s>dharma</s>-acceptances. 'Attained the <s>Dharma</s>' — through <s>dharma</s>-knowledges. 'Understood the <s>Dharma</s>' — through subsequent acceptances. 'Penetrated the <s>Dharma</s>' — through subsequent knowledges. 'Crossed beyond all doubt' — through acceptances and knowledges regarding one's own realization, due to the absence of doubt. 'Gone beyond uncertainty' — due to the absence of hesitation of one in that state regarding others' realizations. 'Independent of others' — in the cultivation of the path, through one's own undertaking of what is wholesome, not from others. 'Not to be led by another in the Teacher's teaching' — in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching,

body.text: bhāvanāmārgaḥ katamaḥ / darśanamārgādūrdhvaṃ laukiko mārgo lokottaramārgaḥ mṛdumārgo madhyamārgo 'dhimātro mārgaḥ prayogamārgaḥ ānantaryamārgaḥ vimuktimārgaḥ viśeṣamārgaśca //
body.translated_text: What is the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>)? Above the path of seeing, [there are]: the worldly path (<s>laukika mārga</s>), the supramundane path (<s>lokottaramārga</s>), the gentle path (<s>mṛdumārga</s>), the moderate path (<s>madhyamārga</s>), the intense path (<s>adhimātramārga</s>), the preparatory path (<s>prayogamārga</s>), the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), the path of liberation (<s>vimuktimārga</s>), and the path of distinction (<s>viśeṣamārga</s>).

body.text: laukiko mārgaḥ katamaḥ / laukikaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamākāśānattyāyatanaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanamākiñcatyāyatanaṃ naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ ca // ta ete dhyānārūpyāḥ saṃkleśavyavadānavyavasthāna viśuddhibhirveditavyāḥ // kathaṃ saṃkleśataḥ / catvāryavyākṛtamūlāni tṛṣṇā dṛṣṭirmāno 'vidyā ca // tṛṣṇayā āsvāda saṃkleśena saṃkliśyate // dṛṣṭyā dṛṣṭyuttaradhyāyitayā saṃkliśyate / mānena mānottaradhyāyitayā saṃkliśyate / avidyayā vicikitsottaradhyāyitayā saṃkliśyate / tathā ca saṃkliṣṭacetasāṃ rūpārūpyāvacarāḥ kleśopakleśāḥ pravarttante // kathaṃ vyavadānataḥ / śuddhakā dhyānārūpyāḥ kuśalatvād vyavadātā ityucyante // kathaṃ vyavasthānataḥ / aṅgavyavasthānataḥ samāpattivyavasthānataḥ mātrāvyavasthānataḥ saṃjñākaraṇavyavasthānaśca // kathamaṅgavyavasthānataḥ / prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ pañcāṅgam / pañcāṅgāni vitarko vicāraḥ prītiḥ sukhaṃ cittaikāgratā ca // dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ caturaṅgam / catvāryaṅgāni adhyātmasaṃprasādaḥ prītiḥ sukhaṃ cittaikāpratā ca // tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ pañcāṅgam / pañcāṅgāni upekṣā smṛtiḥ saṃprajanyaṃ sukhaṃ cittaikāgratā ca // caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ caturaṅgam / catvāryaṅgāni upekṣāpariśuddhiḥ smṛtipariśuddhiḥ aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā cittaikāgratā ca // pratipakṣāṅgamupādāya anuśaṃsāṅgamupādāya tadubhayāśrayasvabhāvāṅgaṃ copādāya ārupyeṣvaṅgavyavasthānaṃ nāsti / śamathaikarasatāmupādāya // kathaṃ samāpattivyavasthānataḥ / saptabhirmanaskāraiḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate / evaṃ yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ ca // sapta manaskārāḥ katame / lakṣaṇaprati saṃvedī manaskāraḥ ādhimokṣikaḥ prāvivejaḥ ratisaṃgrāhakaḥ mīmāṃsakaḥ prayoganiṣṭhaḥ prayoganiṣṭhāphalaśca (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 69]

children.text: ) manaskāraḥ // kathaṃ mātrāvyavasthānataḥ / prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ suduparibhāvitaṃ madhyaparibhāvitamadhimātraparibhāvitaśca // [tadyathā] prathamaṃ dhyānametraṃ śiṣṭāni dhyānānyārūpyāśca // mṛdumadhyādhimātraparibhāvitasya prathamasya dhyānasya phalaṃ trividhā prathamā dhyānopapattiḥ / yathā prathamasya dhyānasya evaṃ śiṣṭānāṃ dhyānānāṃ trividhā dhyānopapattiḥ / ārūpyeṣu sthānāntarābhāvamupādāyopapattibhedo nāsti / tatra mṛdumadhyādhimātraparibhāvitatvādārūpyāṇāmupapattāvuccanīcatā hīnapraṇītatā prajñāyate // kathaṃ saṃjñākaraṇavyavasthānataḥ / prathamadhyānasaṃgṛhītānyāvataḥ samādhīn buddhabodhisattvāḥ samāpadyante / teṣāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhā nāmābhijñā api na bhavanti / yathā prathamadhyānasaṃgṛhītānevamavaśiṣṭadhyānasaṃgṛhītānyaduta dhyānapāramitāṃ niśritya // kathaṃ viśuddhitaḥ / prāntakoṭikaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ yāvannaiva saṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ viśuddhirityucyate //
children.translated_text: mental engagement (<s>manaskāra</s>). How from [the perspective of] establishment by degree? The first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation absorption) is weakly cultivated, moderately cultivated, and intensely cultivated. [For example,] take the first <s>dhyāna</s>; the remaining <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments (<s>ārūpya</s>) [are likewise]. The fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s> cultivated to a weak, medium, and intense degree is a threefold rebirth in the first <s>dhyāna</s> realm. Just as with the first <s>dhyāna</s>, so too the remaining <s>dhyānas</s> have a threefold rebirth in [their respective] <s>dhyāna</s> realms. In the formless realms, because there are no distinct levels, there is no differentiation of rebirth; however, because the formless attainments are cultivated to weak, medium, and intense degrees, higher and lower, inferior and superior [states] in rebirth within the formless realms are discerned. How from [the perspective of] establishment by designation? As many <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) as <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attain that are included in the first <s>dhyāna</s>—<s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> do not even know them by name. Just as with those included in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, so too with those included in the remaining <s>dhyānas</s>, based on the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s>). How from [the perspective of] purity? The first <s>dhyāna</s> at the highest limit, up to the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>), is called 'purity.'

body.translated_text: What is the worldly path? The worldly first <s>dhyāna</s>, second, third, fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), and the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). These <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments should be understood through [their aspects of] defilement, purification, establishment, and purity. How regarding defilement? There are four indeterminate roots: craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Through craving, one is defiled by the defilement of relishing. Through views, one is defiled by inclination toward higher [states based on] views. Through pride, one is defiled by inclination toward higher [states based on] pride. Through ignorance, one is defiled by inclination toward higher [states based on] doubt. And thus, for those with defiled minds, the afflictions and secondary afflictions of the form and formless realms operate. How regarding purification? The pure <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments, being wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), are called purified. How regarding establishment? Through establishment of factors, establishment of attainments, establishment of degree, and establishment of designation. How through establishment of factors? The first <s>dhyāna</s> has five factors: applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>), sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), bliss (<s>sukha</s>), and one-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>). The second <s>dhyāna</s> has four factors: inner clarity (<s>adhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>), joy, bliss, and one-pointedness. The third <s>dhyāna</s> has five factors: equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>), bliss, and one-pointedness. The fourth <s>dhyāna</s> has four factors: purity of equanimity (<s>upekṣāpariśuddhi</s>), purity of mindfulness (<s>smṛtipariśuddhi</s>), feeling of neither pain nor pleasure (<s>aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā</s>), and one-pointedness. In the formless attainments, there is no establishment of factors — due to their uniform nature of calm (<s>śamatha</s>). How through establishment of attainments? One enters the first <s>dhyāna</s> through seven mental engagements (<s>manaskāra</s>), and likewise up to the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception. What are the seven mental engagements? The mental engagement that discerns characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī</s>), the engagement of conviction (<s>ādhimokṣika</s>), the engagement of delight-withdrawal, the engagement of gathering delight, the engagement of investigation (<s>mīmāṃsaka</s>), the engagement of the culmination of practice (<s>prayoganiṣṭha</s>), and the fruit of the culmination of practice,

body.text: lokottaro mārgaḥ katamaḥ / bhāvanāmārge duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgajñānāni dharmajñānānvayapakṣyāṇi taiśca saṃprayuktaḥ samādhiḥ prathamaṃ vā dhyānaṃ yāvadākiñcanyāyatanaṃ naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ, laukikameva aparisphuṭaṃ saṃjñāpracāratāmupādāya / tata ścānimittamityucyate // yathoktaṃ bhagavatā yāvadeva saṃjñāsamāpattiḥ tāvadājñāprativedha iti / nirodhasamāpattirlokottarā manuṣyeṣvabhinirhiyate / manuṣyeṣva bhinirhṛtā manuṣyeṣurūpadhātau vā saṃmukhīkriyate / ārūpyeṣva syāḥ saṃmukhībhāvo nāsti / śāntavimokṣavipākavihārīṇāṃ tadyatnānārambhatāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: What is the supramundane path (<s>lokottara-mārga</s>)? On the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā-mārga</s>), the knowledges of suffering, origination, cessation, and path—belonging to the category of <s>dharma-jñāna</s> (knowledge of phenomena) and <s>anvaya-jñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge)—and the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) associated with them, [supported by] the first <s>dhyāna</s> up to the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>). The sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) is merely mundane, because its perceptual activity is unclear. Therefore it is called 'signless' (<s>ānimitta</s>). As the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'As far as the attainment of perception extends, so far does the penetration of final knowledge extend.' The attainment of cessation (<s>nirodha-samāpatti</s>) is supramundane and is first achieved among humans. Having been achieved among humans, it is actualized either among humans or in the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>). In the formless realms, its actualization does not occur, because those who dwell in the fruition of the peaceful liberation (<s>śānta-vimokṣa</s>) do not engage in that effort.

body.text: mṛdumārgaḥ katamaḥ / mṛdumṛdurmṛdumadhyo mṛdvadhimātraśca yena traidhātukāvacarāṇā kleśānāṃ bhūmau bhūmāvadhimātrādhimātramadhimātramadhyamadhimātrāmṛduṃ kleśaprakāra prajahāti //
body.translated_text: What is the mild path (<s>mṛdu-mārga</s>)? It is mild-mild, mild-medium, and mild-intense, by which one abandons the intense-intense, intense-medium, and intense-mild categories of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) pertaining to the three realms, level by level.

body.text: madhyo mārgaḥ katamaḥ / madhyamṛdurmadhyamadhyo madhyādhimātraśca yena traidhātukāvacarāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ bhūmau bhūmau madhyādhimātraṃ madhyamadhyaṃ madhyamṛduṃ kleśaprakāraṃ prajahāti //
body.translated_text: What is the medium path (<s>madhya-mārga</s>)? It is medium-mild, medium-medium, and medium-intense, by which one abandons the medium-intense, medium-medium, and medium-mild categories of afflictions pertaining to the three realms, level by level.

body.text: adhimātro mārgaḥ katamaḥ / adhimātramṛduradhimātramadhyo 'dhimātrādhimātraśca yena traidhātukāvacarāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ bhūmau bhūmau mṛdvadhimātraṃ mṛdumadhyaṃ mṛdumṛduṃ kleśaprakāraṃ prajahāti //
body.translated_text: What is the intense path (<s>adhimātra-mārga</s>)? It is intense-mild, intense-medium, and intense-intense, by which one abandons the mild-intense, mild-medium, and mild-mild categories of afflictions pertaining to the three realms, level by level.

body.text: prayogamārgaḥ katamaḥ / yena kleśaṃ prajahāti // ānantaryamārgaḥ katamaḥ / yasyānantaraṃ nirantaraḥ kleśaḥ prahīṇo bhavati // vimuktimārgaḥ katamaḥ / yena prahīṇe kleśe vimuktiṃ sākṣātkaroti // viśeṣamārgaḥ katamaḥ / tadanyasya kleśaprakārasya prayogānantaryavimuktimārgāḥ viśeṣamārgaḥ / api khalu kleśaprahāṇaprayogaṃ nirākṛtya dharmacintāyāṃ vā prayuktasya dharmavihāre vā samāpattiviśeṣe vā yo mārgaḥ / api khalu vaiśeṣikān guṇānabhinirharato vā yo mārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the application path (<s>prayoga-mārga</s>)? That by which one abandons afflictions. What is the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantarya-mārga</s>)? That immediately after which the affliction becomes abandoned without interval. What is the liberation path (<s>vimukti-mārga</s>)? That by which, the affliction having been abandoned, one directly realizes liberation. What is the special path (<s>viśeṣa-mārga</s>)? The application, uninterrupted, and liberation paths directed at another category of affliction constitute the special path. Moreover, the path of one who, having set aside the effort of abandoning afflictions, is engaged in reflection on the <s>Dharma</s>, or dwelling in the <s>Dharma</s>, or in special attainments—that too [is the special path]. Also, the path of one who is bringing forth exceptional qualities [is the special path].

body.text: mārgabhāvanā katamā / pratilaṃbhabhāvanā niṣevaṇabhāvanā nirdhāvanabhāvanā pratipakṣabhāvanā ca // pratilambhabhāvanā katamā / anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmutpādāya yā bhāvanā // niṣevaṇabhāvanā katamā / utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye asaṃmoṣāya bhūyobhāvāya vṛddhivipulatāyai yā bhāvanā / nirdhāvanabhāvanā katamā / utpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya yā bhāvanā // pratipakṣabhāvanā katamā / anutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśakunāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 71]

children.text: ) yā bhāvanā // api khalu mārga utpadyamānaḥ svāṃ vāsanāmava sthāpayati sā pratilambhabhāvanā / sa eva saṃmukhībhūto bhāvanāṃ gacchati sā niṣevaṇabhāvanā / svamāvaraṇaṃ vijahāti sā nirdhāvanabhāvanā / vihīna ścāvaraṇamāyatyāmanutpattidharmatāyāmavasthāpayati sā pratipakṣabhāvanā // api khalu caturvidhaḥ pratipakṣaḥ vidūṣaṇāpratipakṣaḥ prahāṇapratipakṣaḥ ādhārapratipakṣaḥ dūrībhāvapratipakṣaśca pratipakṣabhāvanetyucyate // vidūṣaṇāpratipakṣaḥ katamaḥ / sāsraveṣu saṃskāreṣvādīnavadarśanam // prahāṇapratipakṣaḥ katamaḥ / prayogāntaryamārgaḥ // ādharapratipakṣaḥ katamaḥ / vimuktimārgaḥ / dūrībhāvapratipakṣaḥ katamaḥ // tadu parimo mārgaḥ //
children.translated_text: that cultivation. Moreover, when the path arises, it establishes its own imprint (<s>vāsanā</s>)—that is cultivation of attainment. That same [path], having become present, undergoes cultivation—that is cultivation of familiarization. It relinquishes its own obstruction—that is cultivation of purification. And having relinquished [that] obstruction, it establishes [it] in the state of non-arising in the future—that is cultivation of antidote. Moreover, there are four types of antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>): degradation antidote (<s>vidūṣaṇā-pratipakṣa</s>), abandonment antidote (<s>prahāṇa-pratipakṣa</s>), support antidote (<s>ādhāra-pratipakṣa</s>), and distancing antidote (<s>dūrībhāva-pratipakṣa</s>)—these are called cultivation of antidote. What is the degradation antidote? Seeing the danger in conditioned phenomena with outflows (<s>sāsrava-saṃskāras</s>). What is the abandonment antidote? The application and uninterrupted paths. What is the support antidote? The liberation path. What is the distancing antidote? The subsequent path.

body.translated_text: What is the cultivation of the path (<s>mārga-bhāvanā</s>)? It is: cultivation of attainment (<s>pratilambha-bhāvanā</s>), cultivation of familiarization (<s>niṣevaṇa-bhāvanā</s>), cultivation of purification (<s>nirdhāvana-bhāvanā</s>), and cultivation of antidote (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanā</s>). What is cultivation of attainment? The cultivation directed toward the arising of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have not yet arisen. What is cultivation of familiarization? The cultivation directed toward the stability, non-loss, increase, and fullness of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have arisen. What is cultivation of purification? The cultivation directed toward the abandonment of evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have arisen. What is cultivation of antidote? That directed toward the non-arising of evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have not yet arisen—

body.text: api khalu vastuparīkṣāmārgaḥ vyāvasāyiko mārgaḥ samādhiparikarmamārgaḥ abhisamayaprāyogiko mārgaḥ abhisamayaśliṣṭo mārgaḥ abhisamayamārgaḥ viśuddhinairyāṇiko mārgaḥ niśrayendriyabhinno mārgaḥ śikṣātrayapariśodhano mārgaḥ sarvaguṇanirhārako mārgaḥ mārgasaṃgrahamārgaśca mārga ityucyate // sa punareṣa yathākramaṃ saptatriṃśadabodhipakṣā dharmāḥ catasraḥ pratipadaḥ catvāri dharmapadāni śamatha(ai) vipaśyanā triṇī cendriyāṇī //
body.translated_text: Moreover, the path is called: the path of examining objects (<s>vastu-parīkṣā-mārga</s>), the path of determination (<s>vyāvasāyika-mārga</s>), the path of preparatory work for concentration (<s>samādhi-parikarma-mārga</s>), the path of preparation for realization (<s>abhisamaya-prāyogika-mārga</s>), the path conjoined with realization (<s>abhisamaya-śliṣṭa-mārga</s>), the path of realization (<s>abhisamaya-mārga</s>), the path leading to purification (<s>viśuddhi-nairyāṇika-mārga</s>), the path differentiated by support and faculties (<s>niśraya-indriya-bhinna-mārga</s>), the path purifying the three trainings (<s>śikṣātraya-pariśodhana-mārga</s>), the path bringing forth all qualities (<s>sarva-guṇa-nirhāraka-mārga</s>), and the path summarizing all paths (<s>mārga-saṃgraha-mārga</s>). These, in order, are: the thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa-dharmas</s>), the four practices (<s>pratipad</s>), the four <s>dharma-padas</s>, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), and the three faculties (<s>indriyas</s>).

body.text: smṛtyupasthānānāmālamvanaṃ svabhāvaḥ sahāyaḥ bhāvanā bhāvanāphalañca veditavyam / yathā smṛtyupasthānānāmevamavaśiṣṭānāṃ bodhipakṣāṇām // smṛtyupasthānānāmālambanaṃ katamat / kāyo vedanā cittaṃ dharmāḥ // api khalvātmāśrayavastu ātmopabhogavastu ātmavastu ātmasaṃkleśavyavadānavastu ca // svabhāvaḥ katamaḥ / prajñā smṛtiśca // sahāyaḥ katamaḥ / tatsaṃprayuktāścittacaitasikā dharmāḥ / bhāvanā katamā / adhyātmaṃ kāyādiṣu kāyādyanupaśyanā // yathā adhyātmamevaṃ bahirdhā adhyātmavahirdhā // adhyātmaṃ kāyaḥ katamaḥ / yānyasmin kāye ādhyatmikāni rūpīṇyāyatanāni // bahirdhākāyaḥ katamaḥ / bahirdhā rūpīṇyāyatanāni // adhyātmavahirddhā kāyaḥ katamaḥ / ādhyātmikāyatanasaṃbaddhāni (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 72]

children.text: ) bāhyānyāyatanāni / indriyādhiṣṭhānāni pārasāntānikāni cādhyātmikāni rūpīṇyāyatayāni / kāye kāyānupaśyanā katamā / yā vikalpapratibimbakāyena prakṛtibimbakāyasya samatāpaśyanā / adhyātmaṃ vedanā katamā / adhyātmaṃ kāyamupādāyotpannā vedanā // bahirddhā vedanā katamā / bahirddhā kāyamupādayotpannā vedanā // adhyātmabahirddhā vedanā katamā / adhyātmābahirddhākāyamupādāyotpannāvedanā // yathā vedanā evaṃ cittaṃ dharmāḥ // yathā kāye kāyānupaśyanā evaṃ vedanādiṣu vedanādyanupaśyanā yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ / api khalu bhāvanā chando vīryaṃ vyāyāma utsāhaḥ utsūḍhiraprativāṇiḥ smṛtiḥ saṃprajanyaṃ apramādaśca // chandabhāvanā amanasikaropakleśapratipakṣeṇa / vīryabhāvanā kausīdyopakleśapratipakṣeṇa / vyāyāmabhāvanā layauddhatyopakleśapratipakṣeṇa // utsāhabhāvanā cetaso 'līnatvopakleśapratipakṣeṇa // utsūḍhibhāvanā viṣādaparisravaparikhedopakleśapratipakṣeṇa // aprativāṇibhāvanā kuśalapakṣeṇa alpamātra saṃtuṣṭyupakleśapratipakṣeṇa // smṛtibhāvanā bhagavataḥ śāsane saṃmoṣopakleśapratipakṣeṇa // saṃprajanyabhāvanā āpattivipratisāropakleśapratipakṣeṇa // apramādabhāvanā kuśaleṣu nikṣiptadhuratopakleśapratipakṣeṇa // bhāvanāphalaṃ katamat / catu rviparyāsaprahāṇaṃ catuḥ satyāvatāraḥ kāyādivisaṃyogaḥ //
children.translated_text: the external sense bases, the bases of the sense faculties, and the internal material sense bases belonging to other [being's] continuums. What is the contemplation of body in the body? The seeing of equality between the conceptually projected body-image and the natural body. What is internal feeling? Feeling arisen in dependence on the internal body. What is external feeling? Feeling arisen in dependence on the external body. What is internal-and-external feeling? Feeling arisen in dependence on the internal-and-external body. Just as with feeling, so too with mind and phenomena. Just as with the contemplation of body in the body, so too the contemplation of feeling and so forth in feelings and so forth should be understood as appropriate. Moreover, cultivation [consists of]: zeal (<s>chanda</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>), enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>), fortitude (<s>utsūḍhi</s>), non-retreat (<s>aprativāṇi</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>), and diligence (<s>apramāda</s>). Cultivation of zeal is the antidote to the affliction of inattention. Cultivation of vigor is the antidote to the affliction of laziness. Cultivation of exertion is the antidote to the affliction of sinking and agitation. Cultivation of enthusiasm is the antidote to the affliction of mental depression. Cultivation of fortitude is the antidote to the afflictions of despair, exhaustion, and weariness. Cultivation of non-retreat is the antidote to the affliction of being content with small measures of wholesome qualities. Cultivation of mindfulness is the antidote to the affliction of forgetting the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching. Cultivation of clear comprehension is the antidote to the affliction of remorse over transgressions. Cultivation of diligence is the antidote to the affliction of abandoning the responsibility for wholesome [practices]. What is the fruit of cultivation? The abandonment of the four inversions (<s>viparyāsas</s>), entry into the four truths (<s>satyas</s>), and separation from body and so forth.

body.translated_text: Regarding the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>), one should understand their object (<s>ālambana</s>), intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), companion (<s>sahāya</s>), cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), and fruit of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā-phala</s>). Just as with the foundations of mindfulness, so too with the remaining factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣas</s>). What is the object of the foundations of mindfulness? Body (<s>kāya</s>), feelings (<s>vedanā</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), and phenomena (<s>dharmas</s>). Moreover, [these are respectively]: the basis of self (<s>ātmāśraya-vastu</s>), the object of self-enjoyment (<s>ātmopabhoga-vastu</s>), the entity of self (<s>ātma-vastu</s>), and the basis of self-contamination and purification (<s>ātma-saṃkleśa-vyavadāna-vastu</s>).
