What is the intrinsic nature? Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>). What is the companion? The mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> associated with them. What is the cultivation? Internally, the contemplation of body and so forth with respect to the body and so forth. Just as internally, so too externally and both internally and externally. What is the internal body? The internal material sense bases (<s>āyatanas</s>) within this body. What is the external body? The external material sense bases. What is the internal-and-external body? The external sense bases connected with the internal sense bases—

body.text: catuḥ samyakprahāṇānāmālambanaṃ katamat / utpannānutpannavipakṣapratipakṣāḥ // svabhāvaḥ katamaḥ / vyāyāmaḥ // sahāyaḥ katamaḥ / tatsaṃprayuktāścittacaitasikā dharmāḥ / bhāvanā katamā / taduktaṃ sūtre chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryamārabhate cittaṃ pragṛṇhāti cittaṃ pradadhāti / ityevamādibhiḥ padaistatravīryāśrayabhāvanā paridīpitā // āśrayaḥ chandaḥ / vīryamudyogaḥ / śamathagragrahopekṣānimittamanasikāreṣu chandaṃ (janayati) layauddhatyāpakarṣaṇe vīryamārabhate evaṃ tadanantaraṃ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 73]

children.text: ) cittaṃ pragṛṇhāti pradadhātīpratyucyate / bhāvanā phalaṃ katamat / aśeṣavipakṣahāniḥ pratipakṣapratilambhaḥ pratipakṣavṛddhiśca // taducyate bhāvanāphalam /
children.translated_text: one takes hold of the mind and applies it — thus it is explained. What is the fruit of cultivation? The complete elimination of all adversaries, the attainment of the antidote, and the increase of the antidote — this is called the fruit of cultivation.

body.translated_text: What is the object of the four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>)? The arisen and unarisen adversaries and antidotes. What is their intrinsic nature? Exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>). What is their companion? The mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> associated with them. What is their cultivation? As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One generates desire, exerts effort, arouses energy, takes hold of the mind, and applies the mind.' Through such terms, the cultivation based on energy and its support is illuminated. The support is desire (<s>chanda</s>). Energy is effort (<s>udyoga</s>). One generates desire with respect to the mental attention directed at the signs of calm (<s>śamatha</s>), holding (<s>graha</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>); one arouses energy for the removal of dullness and agitation — and then immediately

body.text: caturṛddhipādānāmālambanaṃ katamat / niṣpajñena samādhinā yatkaraṇīyaṃ kṛtyam // svabhāvaḥ katamaḥ / samādhiḥ // sahāyaḥ katamaḥ / chandovīryaṃ cittaṃ mīmāṃsā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ // chandasamādhiḥ katamaḥ / yatsatkṛtya prayogamāgamya spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām // vīryasamadhiḥ katamaḥ / yatsātatya prayogamāgamya spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām // cittasamādhiḥ katamaḥ / pūrvasamādhibhāvanāmāgamya svarasena spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām // mīmāṃsāsamādhiḥ katamaḥ / deśanādharmaśravaṇamāgamya pratyātmaṃ pratisaṃkhyāya spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām // punaḥ chandasamādhiḥ yat chandaṃ janayan spṛśati cittasyaikagratām // vīryasamādhiḥ yat vīryamārapramāṇaḥ spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām // cittasamādhiḥ yat cittaṃ pradadhat spṛśati cittasyaigratām // mīmāṃsāsamādhiḥ yat cittaṃ pragṛṇhan spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām // bhāvanā katamā / aṣṭānāṃ prahāṇasaṃskārāṇāmabhyāsaḥ / katame aṣṭau / chandaḥ vyāyāmaḥ śraddhā praśrabdhiḥ smṛtiḥ saṃprajanyaṃ cetanā upekṣā ca / te punaraṣṭau samāsataścaturdhā saṃgṛhyante / vyāyasāyikaḥ anugrāhakaḥ aupanivandhikaḥ prātipakṣikaśca // chandavīryacittamīmāṃsābhāvanā punardvividhā / nidānaṃ saṃkṣepavikṣepa parivarjanabhāvana alīnatvāvikṣepatadubhayāśrayānukūlabhāvanā ca // phalaṃ katamat / kuśalasamādhiparikarmataḥ yathākarmaṃ dharmābhijñā yathācittamabhijñāpradarśanam / api ca teṣu teṣu dharmeṣu adhigamaḥ prātiḥ karmaṇyatā vaśitā kāritraṃ yatheṣṭaṃ nānāvidhānāmṛdudhyādīnāṃ vastūnāṃ niṣpādanamadhiguṇānāṃ nirhāraśca //
body.translated_text: What is the object of the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>)? Whatever task is to be accomplished through perfected <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). What is their intrinsic nature? <s>Samādhi</s>. What is their companion? Desire (<s>chanda</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>), and the mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> associated with them. What is desire-<s>samādhi</s>? When through earnest practice one attains one-pointedness of mind. What is energy-<s>samādhi</s>? When through continuous practice one attains one-pointedness of mind. What is mind-<s>samādhi</s>? When through previous cultivation of <s>samādhi</s>, one spontaneously attains one-pointedness of mind. What is investigation-<s>samādhi</s>? When through hearing the <s>Dharma</s> teaching, having individually analyzed it, one attains one-pointedness of mind. Furthermore, desire-<s>samādhi</s> is when one attains one-pointedness of mind while generating desire. Energy-<s>samādhi</s> is when one attains one-pointedness of mind while arousing measureless energy. Mind-<s>samādhi</s> is when one attains one-pointedness of mind while applying the mind. Investigation-<s>samādhi</s> is when one attains one-pointedness of mind while taking hold of the mind. What is their cultivation? The practice of the eight formations of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasaṃskāra</s>). What are the eight? Desire (<s>chanda</s>), exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), pliancy (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). These eight are summarized in four [types]: pertaining to exertion, pertaining to support, pertaining to commitment, and pertaining to the antidote. The cultivation of desire, energy, mind, and investigation is further twofold: the cultivation that is the cause, and the cultivation that avoids contraction and distraction — [namely] the cultivation based on the support that is favorable to non-dullness, non-agitation, and both together. What is the fruit? Through the preparation of wholesome <s>samādhi</s>, <s>Dharma</s>-cognition and higher cognitions (<s>abhijñā</s>) according to one's actions and according to one's mind. Moreover, with respect to those various <s>dharmas</s>: attainment, satisfaction, workability, mastery, accomplishment, the achievement of various subtle and other objects as desired, and the bringing forth of higher qualities.

body.text: pañcendriyāṇāmālambanaṃ katamat / catvāryāryasatyāni // svabhāvaḥ katamaḥ / śraddhā vīrya smṛtiḥ samādhiḥ prajñā ca // sahāya katamaḥ / tatsaṃprayuktāścittacaitasikā dharmāḥ // bhāvanā katamā / yat śraddhendriyeṇa satyeṣu abhisaṃpratyayasamutthānaṃ prayogabhāvanā / vīryendriyeṇa satyeṣu utpannābhisaṃpratyayasyābhisaṃbodhyarthaṃ vyāyāmasamutthānaprayogabhāvanā / smṛtīndriyeṇa satyeṣu ārabdhavīryasya smṛtisaṃprayogā dharmasaṃmopasamutthānaprayogabhāvanā / samādhīndriyeṇa satyeṣu saṃprayukta smṛteḥ cittaikāgratāsamutthānaprayogabhāvanā / prajñendriyeṇa satyeṣu samāhitacittasya pravicayasamutthānaprayogabhāvanā / bhāvanāphalaṃ katamat / satyābhisamayasamutthānataḥ uṣmagatamūrdhaparikarmataśca kṣāntilaukikāgradharmanirhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the object of the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>)? The four noble truths. What is their intrinsic nature? Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). What is their companion? The mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> associated with them. What is their cultivation? Through the faith-faculty, the practice of generating conviction in the truths. Through the energy-faculty, the practice of generating exertion for the sake of fully awakening to the truths, having generated conviction. Through the mindfulness-faculty, the practice of generating the association with mindfulness for one who has aroused energy regarding the truths, [as an antidote to] the arising of <s>Dharma</s>-confusion. Through the concentration-faculty, the practice of generating one-pointedness of mind for one whose mindfulness is engaged with the truths. Through the wisdom-faculty, the practice of generating discernment for one whose mind is concentrated on the truths. What is the fruit of cultivation? From the arising of realization of the truths, and from the preparation of the stages of heat (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and summit (<s>mūrdha</s>), comes the bringing forth of acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) and the supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>).

body.text: yathā pañcendriyāṇi tathā pañca balāni / eṣāṃ viśeṣaḥ taiḥ vipakṣāntarāyanirllekho 'navamudyateti balānītyucyante //
body.translated_text: As with the five faculties, so also with the five powers (<s>bala</s>). Their distinction is that through them, the adversaries cannot obstruct or overcome [one] — thus they are called powers.

body.text: sapta bodhyaṅgānāmālambanaṃ katamat / caturṇāmāryasatyānāṃ yathābhūtatā / svabhāvaḥ katamaḥ / smṛtiḥ dharmavicayaḥ vīryaṃ prītiḥ praśrabdhiḥ samādhiḥ upekṣā ca // smṛtiḥ saṃniśrayāṅgam / dharmavicayaḥ svabhāvāṅgam / vīryaṃ niryāṇāṅgam / prītiḥ anuśaṃsāṅgam / praśrabdhiḥ / samādhiḥ upekṣā cāsaṃkleśāṅgam / asaṃkleśataḥ asaṃkleśāśrayataḥ asaṃkleśasvabhāvataśca // sahāyaḥ katamaḥ / tatsaṃprayuktāśrittacaitasikā dharmāḥ // bhāvanā katamā / vivekaniśritaṃ virāganiśritaṃ nirodhaniśritaṃ vyavasargapariṇataṃ smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgam / yathā smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ tathā yāvat upekṣāsaṃbodhyaṅgam // ebhiḥ catubhiḥ padairyathākramaṃ catuḥsatyālambanābodhyaṅgabhāvanā paridīpitā / bhāvanāphalaṃ katamat / darśanaheyānāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇam //
body.translated_text: What is the object of the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>)? The true nature (<s>yathābhūtatā</s>) of the four noble truths. What is their intrinsic nature? Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmavicaya</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), pliancy (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). Mindfulness is the factor of support (<s>saṃniśrayāṅga</s>). Investigation of <s>dharmas</s> is the factor of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvāṅga</s>). Energy is the factor of deliverance (<s>niryāṇāṅga</s>). Joy is the factor of benefit (<s>anuśaṃsāṅga</s>). Pliancy, concentration, and equanimity are the factors of non-affliction (<s>asaṃkleśāṅga</s>) — from [the perspective of] non-affliction, the support of non-affliction, and the intrinsic nature of non-affliction. What is their companion? The mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> associated with them. What is their cultivation? The mindfulness factor of awakening that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and matured in relinquishment. As with the mindfulness factor of awakening, so also up to the equanimity factor of awakening. Through these four terms, the cultivation of the factors of awakening based on the four truths as objects is illuminated in sequence. What is the fruit of cultivation? The abandonment of the afflictions to be abandoned through seeing (<s>darśanaheya</s>).

body.text: aṣṭānāmāryamārgāṅgānāmālambanaṃ katamat / taduttarakālaṃ caturṇāmāryasatyānāṃ yathābhūtatā // svabhāvaḥ katamaḥ / samyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyakkarmmāntaḥ samyagājīvaḥ samyagvyāyāmaḥ samyaksmṛtiḥ samyaksamādhiśca // samyagadṛṣṭiuḥ paricchedāṅgam / (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 75]

children.text: ) samyaksaṃkalpa parasaṃprāpaṇāṅgam / samyagvākkarmāntājīvāḥ parasaṃpratyapāṅgam / darśanaśīlājīvaviśuddhitāmupādāya / samyagvyāyāmaḥ kleśāvaraṇaviśodhanāṅgam / samyaksamādhiḥ vaiśeṣikaguṇāvaraṇa viśodhanāṅgam // sahāyaḥ katamaḥ / tatsaṃprayuktāścittacaitasikādharmāḥ // bhāvanā katamā / bhāvanā tu bodhyaṅgavat // bhāvanā phalaṃ katamat / paricchedaḥ parasaṃprāpaṇaṃ parasaṃpratyayaḥ kleśāvaraṇaviśodhanamupakleśāvaraṇaviśodhanaṃ vaiśeṣikaguṇāvaraṇaviśodhanaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>) is the factor of communicating to others. Right speech, right action, and right livelihood are the factors of others' conviction — from the perspective of the purity of view, conduct, and livelihood. Right effort is the factor of purifying the affliction-obstruction (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>). Right concentration is the factor of purifying the obstruction of superior qualities (<s>vaiśeṣikaguṇāvaraṇa</s>). What is their companion? The mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> associated with them. What is their cultivation? The cultivation is as with the factors of awakening. What is the fruit of cultivation? Discernment, communicating to others, others' conviction, purification of the affliction-obstruction, purification of the secondary-affliction-obstruction, and purification of the obstruction of superior qualities.

body.translated_text: What is the object of the eight noble path factors (<s>āryamārgāṅga</s>)? The true nature of the four noble truths at the subsequent time. What is their intrinsic nature? Right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>), right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>). Right view is the factor of discernment (<s>paricchedāṅga</s>).

body.text: catasraḥ pratipadaḥ katamāḥ / duḥkhā pratipad dhandhābhijñā duḥkhā pratipat kṣiprābhijñā sukhā pratipad dhandhābhijñā sukhā pratipat kṣiprābhijñā // prathamā mṛdvindriyāṇāmanupalabdhamauladhyānam / dvitīyā tīkṣṇendriyāṇāmanupalabdhamauladhyānam / tṛtīyā mṛdvindriyāṇāmupalabhamauladhyānam / caturthī tīkṣṇendriyāṇāmupalabdhamaula dhyānam //
body.translated_text: What are the four practices (<s>pratipad</s>)? The painful practice with slow cognition, the painful practice with quick cognition, the pleasant practice with slow cognition, and the pleasant practice with quick cognition. The first is for those with weak faculties who have not attained the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>. The second is for those with sharp faculties who have not attained the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>. The third is for those with weak faculties who have attained the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>. The fourth is for those with sharp faculties who have attained the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: catvāri dharmapadāni katamāni / alobhādveṣāṇāṃ samyak smṛtiḥ samyak samādhiḥ / alobhādveṣāṇāmadhiśīlaśikṣāviśuddhiḥ / samyaksmṛtānāmadhicittaśikṣāviśuddhiḥ / samyaksamādhitānāmadhiprajñaśikṣāviśuddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: What are the four <s>dharma</s>-padas? For those free from desire and hatred: right mindfulness and right concentration. For those free from desire and hatred: purification of the training in higher conduct (<s>adhiśīlaśikṣā</s>). For those with right mindfulness: purification of the training in higher mind (<s>adhicittaśikṣā</s>). For those with right concentration: purification of the training in higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñāśikṣā</s>).

body.text: śamathaḥ katamaḥ / adhyātmaṃ cittasya upanibandhaḥ sthāpanā saṃsthāpanā avasthāpanā upasthāpanā damanaṃ śamanaṃ vyupaśamanam ekotīkaraṇaṃ samādhānaṃ ca // vipaśyanā katamā / yā dharmān vicinoti pravivinoti parivitarkkayati parimīmāṃsamāpataye / ca kāma pratipakṣadauṣṭhulyanimittasaṃyojanataḥ kāmābhibhavānāṃ viparyāsataḥ aviparyastacittasyāvasthāpanataśca // api khalu śamathavipaśyanāmāgamya catvāro mārgāḥ / ekatyaḥ śamathasya lābhī na vipaśyanāyāḥ / tatprakāraṃ śamathaṃ niśritya vipaśyanāmāpanā / ekatyaḥ vipaśyanāyā lābhī na śamathasya / tatprakārāṃ vipaśyanā niśritya śamathabhāvanā / ekatyaḥ na śamathasya lābhī nāpi vipaśyanāyāḥ / tatsaṃbaddhacittasya layau ddhatyāpakarṣaṇād yugapadubhayamārga bhāvanā / ekatyaḥ śamathasya lābhī vipaśyanāyāśca / tasya śamathavipaśyanobhayamārga yuktasya samaṃ yugapat pravṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: What is calm (<s>śamatha</s>)? The internal binding, establishing, stabilizing, settling, and placing of the mind; taming, calming, thorough pacification, unification, and composure. What is insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>)? That which investigates, thoroughly investigates, reflects upon, and examines <s>dharmas</s> — and [functions] in terms of the antidote to the signs of the tendency (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) of desire and the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), in terms of overcoming desires, in terms of the reversal of inversions, and in terms of establishing the mind that is free from inversions. Furthermore, based on <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, there are four paths: One person has attained calm but not insight — depending on that type of calm, one trains in insight. One person has attained insight but not calm — depending on that type of insight, one cultivates calm. One person has attained neither calm nor insight — through the removal of dullness and agitation from one's connected mind, one cultivates both paths simultaneously. One person has attained both calm and insight — for that one who is yoked to both the calm and insight paths, there is equal and simultaneous engagement.

body.text: trīṇīndriyāṇi / ajñātamājñāsyāmīndriyam ājñendriyam ājñātāvīndriyaṃ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 76]

children.text: ) ca // ajñātamājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ katamat / prayogamārge pañcadaśasu ca darśanamārgacittakṣaṇeṣu yadindriyam // ājñendriyaṃ katamat / ṣoḍaśāt darśanamārgacittakṣaṇādrūdhvaṃ sarvasmin śaikṣamārge yadindriyam // ājñātāvīndriyaṃ katamat / aśaikṣamārgeyadindriyam //
children.translated_text: What is the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown' (<s>ajñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s>)? It is the faculty present on the path of preparation and in the fifteen mind-moments of the path of seeing. What is the faculty of knowledge (<s>ājñendriya</s>)? It is the faculty present from the sixteenth mind-moment of the path of seeing onward, throughout the entire path of training (<s>śaikṣamārga</s>). What is the faculty of one who has fully known (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>)? It is the faculty present on the path of the non-learner (<s>aśaikṣamārga</s>).

body.translated_text: The three faculties: the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown' (<s>ajñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s>), the faculty of perfect knowledge (<s>ājñendriya</s>), the faculty of one who has perfect knowledge (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>)

body.text: prathamadhyānabhūmikānāṃ bhāvanāmārge kāmāvacarāṇi kuśalamūlakānyapi bhāvanāṃ gacchanti / teṣu vibhutvalābhataḥ / yathā prathamadhyānabhūmikānāṃ kāmāvacarāṇi kuśalamūlakāni bhāvanāṃ gacchanti tathā sarvepāmūrdvabhūmikānāṃ bhāvanāmārge adhobhūmikāni kuśalamūlakāni bhāvanāṃ gacchanti / teṣu vibhutvalābhataḥ //
body.translated_text: On the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) of those at the level of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the wholesome roots belonging to the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) also undergo cultivation, because mastery over them is obtained. Just as the wholesome roots of the desire realm undergo cultivation for those at the level of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, so too for all those at higher levels, the wholesome roots of the lower levels undergo cultivation on the path of cultivation, because mastery over them is obtained.

body.text: niṣṭhāmārgaḥ katamaḥ / vajropamaḥ samadhiḥ / sarvadauṣṭhulyānāṃ pratipraśrabdheḥ sarvasaṃyogānāṃ prahāṇāt sarvavisaṃyogānāmadhigamācca / tadanantaraṃ nirantarāśrayapravṛttiḥ prāptakṣayajñānam anutpādajñānaṃ daśāśaikṣā dharmāḥ / katame daśa / aśaikṣasya samyagdṛṣṭiryāyada śaikṣasya samyaksamādhiḥ aśaikṣasya samyagvimokṣaḥ aśaikṣasya samyag jñānaṃ ca // evamādayo dharmā niṣṭhāmārga ucyate // katamāni sarvadauṣṭhulyāni / saṃ kṣepataścaturviśatiḥ / tadyathā sarvatragamabhilāpadauṣṭhulyaṃ veditadauṣṭhulyaṃ kleśadauṣṭhulyaṃ karmadauṣṭhulyaṃ vipākadauṣṭhulyaṃ kleśāvaraṇādauṣṭhulyaṃ karmāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ vipākāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ nivaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ vitarkkadauṣṭhulyaṃ āhāradauṣṭhulyaṃ maithunadauṣṭhulyaṃ svapnadauṣṭhulyaṃ vyādhidauṣṭhulyaṃ jarādauṣṭhulyaṃ maraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ pariśramadauṣṭhulyaṃ dṛḍhadauṣṭhulyam audārikadauṣṭhulyaṃ madhyadauṣṭhulyaṃ sūkṣmadauṣṭhulyaṃ samāpattyāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ jñeyāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ ca // saṃyogaḥ katamaḥ / dauṣṭhulyāciteṣu saṃyogalābhateti vijñaptiḥ // visaṃyogaḥ katamaḥ / dauṣṭhulyavikṣipteṣu visaṃyogalābhateti vijñaptiḥ // vajropamaḥ samādhiḥ katamaḥ / bhāvanāmārgagatasya taduttaraṃ saṃyojanaprahāṇamārgavasthāyāṃ yaḥ samādhiḥ prayogamārgasaṃgraho vā ānantaryamārgasaṃgraho vā / prayogamārgasaṃgrahastu tataḥ paraṃ sarvairāvaraṇairacchādyaḥ sarvāvarāṇānāṃ ca bhedaka iti / ānantaryamārgasaṃgrahastu yadanantaraṃ kṣayajñānānutpādajñānotpattiḥ / sa ca samādhiḥ nirantaraḥ dṛḍhaḥ ekarasaḥ vyāpī ca // etadarthapratibimbanārthaṃ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 77]

children.text: ) bhagavatoktaṃ tadyathā mahāśailaparvato 'khaṇḍo 'cchidro 'śuṣira ekaghanaḥ susaṃvṛtto daśadigvātākampyaśca // katamā nāma nirantarāśrayapravṛttiḥ / aśaikṣamārgalābhinaḥ trividhā āśrayapravṛttiḥ / katamāstisraḥ / cittāśrayamapravṛttiḥ māryāśrapapravṛttiḥ dauṣṭhulyāśrayapravṛttiśca // kṣayajñānaṃ katamat / hetukṣayeṇa yad śānaṃ labhyate kṣayaviṣayā lambanaṃ vā // anutpādajñānaṃ katamat / phalaprahāṇena yad jñānaṃ labhyate phalānutpattiviṣayālambanaṃ vā // daśāśaikṣā dharmāstu aśaikṣāṇāṃ śīlaskandhaṃ samādhiskandhaṃ prajñāskandhaṃ vimuktiskandhaṃ vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaṃ cādhikṛtya veditavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: For the purpose of reflecting this meaning, the Blessed One has said: "Just as a great rocky mountain, unbroken, uncleft, unhollow, solidly compact, well-covered, is unshakeable by the winds from the ten directions." What is the transformation of the basis without interruption? For one who has attained the path of the non-learner, there is a threefold transformation of the basis. What are the three? The transformation of the basis of mind (<s>cittāśraya</s>), the transformation of the basis of the path (<s>mārgāśraya</s>), and the transformation of the basis of unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulyāśraya</s>). What is the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>)? It is the knowledge obtained through the destruction of causes, or [the knowledge] that has the domain of destruction as its object. What is the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>)? It is the knowledge obtained through the abandonment of results, or [the knowledge] that has the domain of the non-arising of results as its object. The ten <s>dharmas</s> of a non-learner should be understood with reference to the aggregate of morality (<s>śīlaskandha</s>), the aggregate of concentration (<s>samādhiskandha</s>), the aggregate of wisdom (<s>prajñāskandha</s>), the aggregate of liberation (<s>vimuktiskandha</s>), and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation (<s>vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha</s>) of non-learners.

body.translated_text: What is the path of culmination (<s>niṣṭhāmārga</s>)? It is the diamond-like concentration (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>), [so called] because it pacifies all unsuitabilities (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), abandons all bonds (<s>saṃyoga</s>), and realizes all liberations (<s>visaṃyoga</s>). Immediately after that, there is the transformation of the basis without interruption (<s>nirantarāśrayapravṛtti</s>), the attainment of the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>), the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>), and the ten <s>dharmas</s> of a non-learner. What are the ten? Right view of a non-learner, and so on up to right concentration of a non-learner, right liberation of a non-learner, and right knowledge of a non-learner. Such <s>dharmas</s> and others are called the path of culmination. What are all the unsuitabilities? In brief, there are twenty-four: namely, the unsuitability that is all-pervasive and related to expression, the unsuitability of what is known, the unsuitability of afflictions, the unsuitability of <s>karma</s>, the unsuitability of ripening, the unsuitability of the obstruction of afflictions, the unsuitability of the obstruction of <s>karma</s>, the unsuitability of the obstruction of ripening, the unsuitability of hindrances, the unsuitability of discursive thought, the unsuitability of food, the unsuitability of sexual intercourse, the unsuitability of sleep, the unsuitability of illness, the unsuitability of aging, the unsuitability of death, the unsuitability of fatigue, the unsuitability that is firm, the unsuitability that is gross, the unsuitability that is middling, the unsuitability that is subtle, the unsuitability of the obstruction of attainment, and the unsuitability of the obstruction of the knowable. What is a bond (<s>saṃyoga</s>)? It is the notification that bonds are obtained in [mental continua] accumulated with unsuitability. What is liberation (<s>visaṃyoga</s>)? It is the notification that liberation is obtained in [mental continua] from which unsuitability has been dispelled. What is the diamond-like concentration? It is the concentration of one who has entered the path of cultivation, in the stage of the path of abandoning the highest fetters — whether it belongs to the path of preparation or the uninterrupted path. That which belongs to the path of preparation is unobstructed by all obstructions and is the destroyer of all obstructions. That which belongs to the uninterrupted path is [the concentration] immediately after which the knowledge of destruction and the knowledge of non-arising arise. That concentration is uninterrupted, firm, of one flavor, and all-pervading.

body.text: tathā ca mārgasatyasya catvāraḥ prakārabhedāḥ / mārgalakṣaṇaṃ nyāyalakṣaṇaṃ pratipadlakṣaṇaṃ nairyāṇikalakṣaṇaṃ ca // kimupādāya mārgalakṣaṇam / tattvārthaparimārgaṇatāmupādāya // kimupādāya nyāyalakṣaṇam / kleśapratipakṣatāmupādāya // kimupādāya pratipallakṣaṇam / cittāviparyāsapratipādanātāmupādāya // kimupādāya nairyāṇikalakṣaṇam / nityapadayānatāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: Likewise, there are four distinct characteristics of the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>): the characteristic of the path (<s>mārgalakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of correctness (<s>nyāyalakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of practice (<s>pratipallakṣaṇa</s>), and the characteristic of leading to liberation (<s>nairyāṇikalakṣaṇa</s>). On what basis is it the characteristic of the path? On the basis of being the search for the meaning of reality. On what basis is it the characteristic of correctness? On the basis of being the antidote to afflictions. On what basis is it the characteristic of practice? On the basis of leading the mind to non-distortion. On what basis is it the characteristic of leading to liberation? On the basis of being the vehicle to the eternal state.

body.text: satyeṣu ṣoḍaśākārāḥ laukikā lokottarāśca // laukikānāṃ lokottarāṇāṃ ca katamaḥ prabhedaḥ / jñeye akuśalapraveśakuśalyapraveśastrabhāvaprabhedataḥ sāvaraṇanirāvaraṇasvabhāvaprabhedataḥ savikalpanirvikalpasvabhāvaprabhedataśca // kena hetunā satyeṣu anityaduḥkhādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa lauaukikākārāḥ / tathāgata aprativedhataḥ kleśānuśayataḥ abhilāpamukhena prapañcanataśca // lokottarākārāḥ tadviparyayeṇa / lokottarākāreṣu varttamāno 'nityārthaṃ paśyati sākṣādanubhavati notvanityaṃ paśyati abhilāpaprapañcamukhena / yathā anityākārā anityārthe evaṃ śiṣṭhākarāḥ śiṣṭārtheṣu yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: There are sixteen aspects (<s>ākāra</s>) of the [Four Noble] Truths, both mundane (<s>laukika</s>) and supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>). What is the distinction between the mundane and the supramundane? [It is understood] from the distinction of intrinsic nature as skillful entry into unwholesome and wholesome with regard to the knowable, from the distinction of intrinsic nature as with obstruction and without obstruction, and from the distinction of intrinsic nature as conceptual (<s>savikalpa</s>) and non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>). For what reason are impermanence, suffering, and the other sixteen mundane aspects of the truths [so designated]? Because of non-penetration of the <s>Tathāgata</s>['s realization], because of the latent tendencies of afflictions, and because of conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>) through the medium of verbal expression. The supramundane aspects are the opposite of those. When abiding in the supramundane aspects, one sees the meaning of impermanence and directly experiences it, but does not see 'impermanence' through the medium of verbal conceptual proliferation. As the aspect of impermanence [relates] to the meaning of impermanence, so the remaining aspects should be understood in relation to their respective meanings, as appropriate.

body.text: (atha viniścaye dharmaparicchedo dvitīyo bhāgaḥ /)
body.translated_text: (Now, in the ascertainment [section], the second part of the chapter on <s>dharmas</s>.)

body.text: dharmaviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / āryaśāsanaṃ dvādaśāṅgadharmaḥ / katamāni dvādaśāṅgāni / sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ gāthā udānaṃ nidānam avadānam itivṛtakaṃ jātakaṃ vaipulyam adbhutadharmaḥ upadeśaśca //
body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaviniścaya</s>)? It is the Noble Teaching (<s>āryaśāsana</s>), the <s>Dharma</s> of twelve divisions. What are the twelve divisions? <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>nidāna</s>, <s>avadāna</s>, <s>itivṛttaka</s>, <s>jātaka</s>, <s>vaipulya</s>, <s>adbhutadharma</s>, and <s>upadeśa</s>.

body.text: 1. sūtraṃ katamat / yadabhipretārthaṃ sūcanākāreṇa gadyabhāṣitam / daśānuśaṃsān saṃpaśyan tathāgataḥ sūcanākāreṇa dharmaṃ deśayati sukhaṃ vyavasthāpayati sukhaṃ deśayati / śrotāpi sukhamudgṛṇhāti dharmagauravatayā kṣipraṃ bodhi saṃbhārān paripūrayati āśudharmatāṃ pratividhyati / buddhe 'vetyaprasādaṃ labhate dharme saṃghe cāvetya prasādaṃ labhate / paramadṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāraṃ spṛśati / sāṃkathyaviniścayena satāṃ cittamārādhayati / paṇḍitaḥ paṇḍita iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati //
body.translated_text: 1. What is <s>sūtra</s>? That which is spoken in prose in the manner of indicating the intended meaning. Seeing ten benefits, the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in the manner of indication: it is easy to establish, easy to teach; the listener easily grasps it; through reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, one quickly completes the accumulations for awakening; one penetrates the quality of being swift in <s>Dharma</s>; one obtains unwavering faith in the <s>Buddha</s>; one obtains unwavering faith in the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>; one touches the supreme bliss of abiding in the present <s>Dharma</s>; through discussion and ascertainment, one pleases the minds of the virtuous; and one comes to be reckoned as 'a wise one, a wise one.'

body.text: 2. geyaṃ katamat / sūtrāṇāṃ madhye vā ante vā gāthayā yad gīyate / sūtreṣu anirūpito 'rtho vā yad vyākhyāyate / ato geyamityucyate //
body.translated_text: 2. What is <s>geya</s>? That which is sung in verse in the middle or at the end of <s>sūtras</s>, or that which explains a meaning not analyzed in the <s>sūtras</s>. Therefore it is called <s>geya</s>.

body.text: 3. vyākaraṇaṃ katamat / tat sthāneṣu samatikrāntānāmatītānāmārya śrāvakāṇāṃ prāptyutpattiprabhedavyākaraṇam / api ca sūtreṣu nirūīpitārthasya sphuṭīkaraṇam / vivṛtyābhisandhivyākaraṇāt //
body.translated_text: 3. What is <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (prediction)? It is the prediction of the attainments and rebirths of the noble disciples (<s>āryaśrāvaka</s>) of the past who have transcended [their respective] stages. Moreover, it is the clarification of a meaning established in the <s>sūtras</s>, through the prediction that unfolds [its] hidden intention.

body.text: 4. gāthā katamā / sūtreṣu pādayogena deśyate / dvipadī tripadī catuṣpadī paṃcapadī ṣaṭpadī vā //
body.translated_text: 4. What is <s>gāthā</s> (verse)? That which is taught in the <s>sūtras</s> by means of metrical feet — of two feet, three feet, four feet, five feet, or six feet.

body.text: 5. udānaṃ katamat / sūtreṣu kadācit tathāgatena āttamanaskena yadudāhṛtam //
body.translated_text: 5. What is <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance)? That which the <s>Tathāgata</s> at times, being pleased in mind, has spoken forth in the <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: 6. nidānaṃ katamat / pṛṣṭena yad bhāṣitam / sotpattikaṃ śikṣāprajñāptekaṃ vā / ato 'pi nidānam //
body.translated_text: 6. What is <s>nidāna</s> (introduction)? That which is spoken in response to a question, or that which has an origin — either one that establishes a training rule. This also is <s>nidāna</s>.

body.text: 7. avadānaṃ katamat / sūtreṣu sadṛṣṭāntakaṃ bhāṣitam //
body.translated_text: 7. What is <s>avadāna</s> (narrative illustration)? That which is spoken with similes in the <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: 8. itivṛttakaṃ katamat / yadāryaśrāvakāṇāṃ pūrvalaukikaṃ vṛttaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: 8. What is <s>itivṛttaka</s> (historical account)? That which teaches the past worldly deeds of the noble disciples (<s>āryaśrāvaka</s>).

body.text: 9. jātakaṃ katamat / yat bodhisattvacaritapiṭakasaṃprayuktaṃ vṛttaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: 9. What is <s>jātaka</s> (birth story)? That which teaches deeds connected with the collection of <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct.

body.text: 10. vaipulyaṃ katamat / bodhisattvapiṭakasaṃprayuktaṃ bhāṣitam / yaducyate vaipulyaṃ tad vaidalyamapyucyate vaitulyamapyucyate / kimarthaṃ vaipulyamucyate / sarvasattvānāṃ hitasukhādhiṣṭhānataḥ udāragambhīradharmadeśanātaśca // kimarthamucyate vaidalyam / sarvāvaraṇavidalanataḥ // kimarthamucyate vaitulyam / upamānadharmāṇāṃ tulanābhāvataḥ //
body.translated_text: 10. What is <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive teaching)? That which is spoken in connection with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> collection. What is called <s>vaipulya</s> is also called <s>vaidalya</s> and also called <s>vaitulya</s>. Why is it called <s>vaipulya</s>? Because it is founded on the welfare and happiness of all beings, and because of the teaching of profound and lofty <s>Dharma</s>. Why is it called <s>vaidalya</s>? Because it splits open all obstructions. Why is it called <s>vaitulya</s>? Because there is no comparison for those <s>dharmas</s> that serve as analogies.

body.text: 11. adbhutadharmaḥ katamaḥ / yatra śrāvakabodhisattvatathāgatānāṃ paramā dbhutāścaryadharmāṇāṃ deśanā //
body.translated_text: 11. What is <s>adbhutadharma</s> (marvelous teaching)? That in which there is the teaching of the supremely marvelous and wondrous <s>dharmas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.text: 12. upadeśaḥ katamaḥ / sarvagambhoragūḍha dharmalakṣaṇānāmaviparītaṃ vyākhyānam /
body.translated_text: 12. What is <s>upadeśa</s> (instruction)? It is the correct explanation of the characteristics of all profound and hidden <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: evaṃ sūtrādīni dvādaśāṅgānyāryaśāsanāni triṣu piṭakeṣu saṃgṛhītāni bhavanti / katamāni trīṇi / sūtrapiṭakaṃ vinayapiṭakam abhidharmapiṭakaṃ ca / tāni punardvividhāni / śrāvakapiṭakaṃ bodhisattvapiṭakaṃ ca / sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ gāthā udānaṃ caitāni pañca śrāvakāṇāṃ piṭakasya sūtrapiṭake saṃgṛhītāni bhavanti / nidānamavadānamitivṛttakaṃ jātakaṃ caitāni catvāri dvayoḥ piṭakayoḥ saparivāre vinayapiṭake saṃgṛhītāni bhavanti / vaipulyamadbhutadharmaśca ete dve bodhisattvapiṭakasya sūtrapiṭake saṃgṛhīte bhavataḥ / upadeśa ekaḥ śrāvakabodhisattvapiṭakayoḥ abhidharmapiṭake saṃgṛhīto bhavati /
body.translated_text: Thus the twelve divisions of scripture (<s>dvādaśāṅga</s>) beginning with <s>sūtra</s> — the teachings of the Noble One — are included in the three baskets (<s>tripiṭaka</s>). What are the three? The basket of discourses (<s>sūtrapiṭaka</s>), the basket of discipline (<s>vinayapiṭaka</s>), and the basket of higher doctrine (<s>abhidharmapiṭaka</s>). These are further of two kinds: the basket of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and the basket of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. <s>Sūtra</s> (discourse), <s>geya</s> (mixed prose and verse), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (prophecy), <s>gāthā</s> (verse), and <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance) — these five are included in the <s>sūtrapiṭaka</s> of the <s>śrāvaka</s> basket. <s>Nidāna</s> (narrative of origin), <s>avadāna</s> (heroic tale), <s>itivṛttaka</s> (historical account), and <s>jātaka</s> (birth story) — these four are included in the <s>vinayapiṭaka</s> together with its supplements in both baskets. <s>Vaipulya</s> (extensive teaching) and <s>adbhutadharma</s> (marvelous events) — these two are included in the <s>sūtrapiṭaka</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> basket. <s>Upadeśa</s> (instruction) alone is included in the <s>abhidharmapiṭaka</s> of both the <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>bodhisattva</s> baskets.

body.text: kimupādāya tathāgatasya piṭakatrayavyavasthānam / vicikitsopakleśapratipakṣakā matāmupādāya sūtrapiṭakavyavasthānam / antadvayānuyogopakleśapratipakṣakāmatāmupādāya vinayapiṭakavyavasthānam / svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarśagrahopakleśapratipakṣakāmatāmupādāya abhidharmapiṭakavyavasthānam / punaḥ śikṣātrayavyutpattikāmatāmupādāya sūtrapiṭakavyavasthānam / adhiśīlādhicittaśikṣāniṣpādanakāmatāmupādāya vinayapiṭakavyavasthānam / adhiprajñaśikṣāniṣpādanakāmatāmupādāya abhidharmapiṭakavyavasthānam // punaḥ samyag dharmārthavyutpattikāmatāmupādāya sūtrapiṭakavyavasthānam / (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 80

children.text: ) dharmārthasākṣātkriyāpadasthānaprabhāvitā mupādāya vinayapiṭakavyavasthānam / jñānināṃ sāṃkathyaviniścayadharmasaṃbhogasukha vihārāśrayatāmupādāya abhidharmapiṭakavyavasthānam //
children.translated_text: The <s>vinayapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to the efficacy of being the ground for direct realization of the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>abhidharmapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to being the basis for the happiness of dwelling in the enjoyment of the <s>Dharma</s> through discussion and ascertainment among the wise.

body.translated_text: In reference to what has the <s>Tathāgata</s> established the three baskets? The <s>sūtrapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to the desire to counteract the secondary affliction of doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>). The <s>vinayapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to the desire to counteract the secondary affliction of pursuing the two extremes. The <s>abhidharmapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to the desire to counteract the secondary affliction of grasping one's own views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>). Furthermore, the <s>sūtrapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to the desire for expertise in the three trainings (<s>śikṣātraya</s>). The <s>vinayapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to the desire to accomplish the training in higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>) and higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>). The <s>abhidharmapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to the desire to accomplish the training in higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>). Furthermore, the <s>sūtrapiṭaka</s> is established in reference to the desire for correct expertise in the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning.

body.text: sa eṣa piṭakatrayasaṃgṛhīto dharmaḥ kasya gocaraḥ / śrutamaya cintāmayabhāvanāmayānāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ gocaraḥ // yaduktaṃ sutre cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ sālambanāḥ sākāraḥ sāśrayāḥ sasaṃprayogāśca / teṣāmasmin dharme ālambanaṃ katamat / sūtrādikam // ākāraḥ katamaḥ / skandhādayastatsaṃprayuktāścārthāḥ // āśrayaḥ katamaḥ / paravijñaptiḥ smṛtirvāsanā ca // saṃprayogaḥ katamaḥ / anyo 'nyasahāyabhāvena ālambane ākāraiḥ saṃpratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: This <s>Dharma</s> included in the three baskets — whose domain is it? It is the domain of mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> born of hearing (<s>śrutamaya</s>), reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>), and meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> have objects (<s>sālambana</s>), aspects (<s>sākāra</s>), supports (<s>sāśraya</s>), and associations (<s>sasaṃprayoga</s>).' What is their object in this <s>Dharma</s>? The <s>sūtras</s> and so forth. What is their aspect? The meanings related to the aggregates and so forth, and the objects associated with them. What is their support? The communication of others, memory, and latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). What is their association? The mutual accord in aspects regarding the object through being companions to one another.

body.text: dharme ālambanaprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / saṃkṣepeṇa caturvidhaḥ ākhyātaḥ / vyāpyālambanaṃ caritaviśodhanālambanaṃ kauśalyālambanaṃ kleśaviśodhanālambanaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: What is the classification of objects in the <s>Dharma</s>? In brief, it is declared to be fourfold: the pervasive object (<s>vyāpyālambana</s>), the object for purifying conduct (<s>caritaviśodhanālambana</s>), the object of skill (<s>kauśalyālambana</s>), and the object for purifying afflictions (<s>kleśaviśodhanālambana</s>).

body.text: vyāpyālambanaṃ punaścaturvidham / savikalpapratibimbālambanaṃ nirvikalpaprativimbālambanaṃ vastuparyantālambanaṃ kāryapariniṣpattyālambanaṃ ca // savikalpapratibimbālambanaṃ katamat / adhimuktimanaskāreṇa yat śamathavipaśyanāviṣayālambanam // nirvikalpaprativimbālambanaṃ katamat / tattvamanaskāreṇa yat śamathavipaśyanāviṣayālambanam // vastuparyantālambanaṃ katamat / sarvadharmāṇāṃ kṣayabhāvikatā yathāvadbhāvikatā ca // kṣayabhāvikatā katamā / skandhadhātvāyatanāni // yathāvadbhāvikatā katamā / catvāri āryasatyāni ṣoḍaśākārāḥ tathatā sarve anityāḥ saṃskārāḥ sarve duḥkhā saṃskārāḥ sarve 'nātmāno dharmāḥ nirvāṇaṃ śāntaṃ śūnyamapraṇihitamanimittaṃ ca // kāryapariniṣpattyālambanaṃ katamat / āśrayaparivṛttiḥ / iyamāśrayaparivṛttiracintyā // ṣoḍaśākāreṣu śūnye kati ākārāḥ saṃgṛhītā bhavanti / dvau / apraṇihite kati ākārāḥ saṃgṛhītā bhavanti / ṣaṭ / animitte katyākārāḥ saṃgṛhītā bhavanti / aṣṭau /
body.translated_text: The pervasive object is further fourfold: the object of a conceptual reflection (<s>savikalpapratibimbālambana</s>), the object of a non-conceptual reflection (<s>nirvikalkapratibimbālambana</s>), the object of the limit of reality (<s>vastuparyantālambana</s>), and the object of the accomplishment of the task (<s>kāryapariniṣpattyālambana</s>). What is the object of a conceptual reflection? The object in the domain of <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) through the mental engagement of conviction (<s>adhimuktimanaskāra</s>). What is the object of a non-conceptual reflection? The object in the domain of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> through the mental engagement of reality (<s>tattvamanaskāra</s>). What is the object of the limit of reality? The exhaustive nature (<s>kṣayabhāvikatā</s>) and the 'as-it-is' nature (<s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>. What is the exhaustive nature? The aggregates, elements, and sense bases. What is the 'as-it-is' nature? The four noble truths, the sixteen aspects, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), 'all formations are impermanent,' 'all formations are suffering,' 'all <s>dharmas</s> are non-self,' and '<s>nirvāṇa</s> is peace, emptiness, wishlessness, and signlessness.' What is the object of the accomplishment of the task? The transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>). This transformation of the basis is inconceivable. Among the sixteen aspects, how many aspects are included in emptiness? Two. How many aspects are included in wishlessness? Six. How many aspects are included in signlessness? Eight.

body.text: caritaviśodhanālambanaṃ pañcavidham / bhūyorāgacaritānāmaśubhaviṣayālambanam / bhūyodveṣacaritānāṃ karuṇābhāvanā viṣayālambanam / bhūyomohacaritānāṃ nikāyapratyayatā pratītyasamutpādaviṣayālambanam / madamānacaritānāṃ dhātuprabhedaviṣayālambanam / vitarkkacaritānāmavatārāprativāṇi smṛtiviṣayālambanam //
body.translated_text: The object for purifying conduct is fivefold: for those predominantly inclined toward attachment, the object in the domain of the unattractive (<s>aśubha</s>); for those predominantly inclined toward aversion, the object in the domain of cultivating compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>); for those predominantly inclined toward delusion, the object in the domain of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) and the conditionality of the classes of existence; for those inclined toward intoxication and pride, the object in the domain of the analysis of elements (<s>dhātuprabhedha</s>); for those inclined toward discursive thought, the object in the domain of mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>).

body.text: kauśalyālambanaṃ pañcavidham / skandhakauśalyaṃ dhātukauśalyam āyatanakauśalyaṃ pratītyuasamutpādakauśalyaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalyaṃ ca // sthānāsthānakauśalyena kamarthaṃ paśyati / jñeye pratityasamutpādakauśalyaṃ paśyati // sthānāsthānakauśalyapratītyasamutpādakauśalyayoḥ kaḥ prabhedaḥ / yat dharmā dharmānabhiniṣyandayanti nahyeṣāṃ nirhetuko nāpi viṣamahetuka utpāda itīdaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalyam / hetuphalānurūpye vedayitotpāda itīdaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalyam //
body.translated_text: The object of skill is fivefold: skill in the aggregates (<s>skandhakauśalya</s>), skill in the elements (<s>dhātukauśalya</s>), skill in the sense bases (<s>āyatanakauśalya</s>), skill in dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpādakauśalya</s>), and skill in what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānakauśalya</s>). What does one see through skill in what is possible and impossible? One sees skill in dependent origination regarding the object of knowledge. What is the difference between skill in what is possible and impossible and skill in dependent origination? That <s>dharmas</s> produce other <s>dharmas</s> as their outflow, and that their arising is neither without cause nor from an improper cause — this is skill in dependent origination. That the arising of experience corresponds to the conformity of cause and effect — this is skill in what is possible and impossible.

body.text: kleśaviśodhanalambanaṃ katamat / yad adhobhūmikānāmaudarikatā ūrdhvabhūmikānāṃ śāntatā tathatā catvāryasatyāni ca / etāni kleśaviśodhanālambanāni nāma //
body.translated_text: What is the object for purifying afflictions? The coarseness of the lower planes, the peacefulness of the higher planes, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and the four noble truths — these are called the objects for purifying afflictions.

body.text: tatra dharmamīmāṃsākāmena katibhiryuktibhirvicāryate / catasṛbhiryuktibhiḥ / apekṣāyuktiḥ kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ upapattisādhanayuktiḥ dharmatāyuktiśca // apekṣāyuktiḥ katamā / yā saṃskārāṇāmutpattau pratyayāpekṣā / kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ katamā / pṛthaglakṣaṇānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratyekaṃ kāryakāraṇāni // upapattisādhanayuktiḥ katamā / upapattisādhanārthaṃ sādhyasyārthasya prāmāṇāviruddha upadeśaḥ // dharmatāyuktiḥ katamā / anādikālāt svalakṣaṇasāmānyalakṣaṇasthitadharmeṣu yā dharmatāpariniṣpattiḥ sā dharmatā // iti dharmeṣu vicāraṇā //
body.translated_text: For one who wishes to investigate the <s>Dharma</s>, by how many modes of reasoning (<s>yukti</s>) is it examined? By four modes of reasoning: the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>), the reasoning of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇayukti</s>), the reasoning of proof and establishment (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>), and the reasoning of the nature of things (<s>dharmatāyukti</s>). What is the reasoning of dependence? The dependence on conditions for the arising of formations. What is the reasoning of cause and effect? The individual causes and effects of <s>dharmas</s> having distinct characteristics. What is the reasoning of proof and establishment? An instruction that does not contradict the means of valid knowledge for the purpose of establishing the meaning to be proved. What is the reasoning of the nature of things? The settled nature of <s>dharmas</s> that have abided since beginningless time in their particular and general characteristics — that is the nature of things. Thus is the investigation of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: dharmeṣu katamāḥ paryeṣaṇāḥ saṃbhavanti / catasraḥ paryeṣaṇāḥ saṃbhavanti / nāmaparyeṣaṇā vastuparyeṣaṇā svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā ca // nāmaparyeṣaṇā katamā / dharmeṣu nāmakāyapadakāyavyañjanakāyānāmapariniṣpannaṃ svalakṣaṇamiti (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 82

children.text: ) yā santīraṇā // vastuparyeṣaṇā katamā / dharmāṇāṃ skandhadhātvāyatanānāmapariniṣpakṣaṃ khalakṣaṇamiti yā saṃtīraṇā // svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā katamā / dharmāṇā mabhidhānābhidheyasaṃbandhe svabhāvaprajñaptimātrasya vyavahāranimittatāsantīraṇā // viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā katamā / dharmāṇāmabhidhānābhidheyasambandhe viśeṣaprajñaptimātrasya vyavahāranimittatāsantīraṇā // iti dharmaparyeṣaṇābhāvanā //
children.translated_text: What is the investigation of things? The examination that the own-characteristic of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases of <s>dharmas</s> is not ultimately real. What is the investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature? The examination that in the relationship between signifier and signified regarding <s>dharmas</s>, mere designation of intrinsic nature is the basis of conventional usage. What is the investigation of the designation of distinction? The examination that in the relationship between signifier and signified regarding <s>dharmas</s>, mere designation of distinction is the basis of conventional usage. Thus is the cultivation of the investigation of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.translated_text: What investigations arise regarding <s>dharmas</s>? Four investigations arise: investigation of names (<s>nāmaparyeṣaṇā</s>), investigation of things (<s>vastuparyeṣaṇā</s>), investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>), and investigation of the designation of distinction (<s>viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>). What is the investigation of names? The examination that the own-characteristic of name-groups, phrase-groups, and syllable-groups regarding <s>dharmas</s> is not ultimately real.

body.text: dharmeṣu yathābhūtaparijñānāni katamāni saṃbhavanti / catvāri yathābhūtaparijñānāni / nāmaparyeṣitaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ vastuparyeṣitaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣitaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣitaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ / nāmaparyeṣitaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ katamat / yathābhūtasya nāmānupalabdhijñānam // vastuparyeṣitaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ katamat / yathābhūtasya vastulakṣaṇānupalabdhijñānam // svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣitaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ katamat / yathābhūtasya dravyasvabhāvānupalabdhijñānam // viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣitaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ katamat / yathābhūtasya dravyaviśeṣānupalabdhijñānam /
body.translated_text: What true knowledges arise regarding <s>dharmas</s>? Four true knowledges: the true knowledge investigated through names, the true knowledge investigated through things, the true knowledge investigated through the designation of intrinsic nature, and the true knowledge investigated through the designation of distinction. What is the true knowledge investigated through names? The knowledge of the non-apprehension of names as they truly are. What is the true knowledge investigated through things? The knowledge of the non-apprehension of the characteristics of things as they truly are. What is the true knowledge investigated through the designation of intrinsic nature? The knowledge of the non-apprehension of substantial intrinsic nature as it truly is. What is the true knowledge investigated through the designation of distinction? The knowledge of the non-apprehension of substantial distinction as it truly is.

body.text: dharmamāśritya samādhiprayuktasya yogabhūmiḥ katamā jñeyā / pañcākārāḥ / ādhāraḥ ādhānam ādarśaḥ ālokaḥ āśrayaśca / ādhāraḥ katamaḥ / saṃbhṛtabodhisaṃbhārasya ūṣmagatādiṣu āryasatyeṣu ca yad vāhuśrutyam // ādhānaṃ katamat / tadālambano yoniśo manaskāraḥ // ādarśaḥ katamaḥ / tadālambanaḥ sanimittaḥ samādhiḥ // ālokaḥ katamaḥ / grāhyagrāhakānupalabdhijñānam // etadadhikṛtya suṣṭhu uktaṃ buddhena bhagavatā
body.translated_text: What is the ground of yoga (<s>yogabhūmi</s>) to be known for one engaged in <s>samādhi</s> based on the <s>Dharma</s>? It has five aspects: the foundation (<s>ādhāra</s>), the placing (<s>ādhāna</s>), the mirror (<s>ādarśa</s>), the light (<s>āloka</s>), and the basis (<s>āśraya</s>). What is the foundation? For one who has accumulated the requisites of awakening (<s>bodhisaṃbhāra</s>), it is the extensive learning (<s>vāhuśrutya</s>) regarding the stages beginning with heat (<s>ūṣmagata</s>) and the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>). What is the placing? It is the careful attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>) that takes that as its object. What is the mirror? It is the <s>samādhi</s> that takes that as its object and has a sign (<s>nimitta</s>). What is the light? It is the knowledge of the non-apprehension of the grasped and the grasper (<s>grāhyagrāhakānupalabdhijñāna</s>). Regarding this, it was well spoken by the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>:

children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, concentrated, seeing the reflection in the mind,
Turning away perception of objects, examining one's own perception,

body.text:
evamātmasthacitto 'sau grāhyābhāvaṃ vibodhayet /
tataśca grāhakābhāvaṃ nopalambhaṃ spṛśettataḥ // iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, with mind established in itself, one should awaken to the absence of the grasped; then to the absence of the grasper; and thereby one should touch non-apprehension.

body.text: āśrayaḥ katamaḥ / āśrayaparivṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the basis (<s>āśraya</s>)? It is the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>).

body.text: kathaṃ dharmeṣu dharmakuśalo bhavati / bahuśrutatāmupādāya // kathamarthakuśalo bhavati / abhidharme abhivinaye lakṣaṇajñatāmupādāya // kathaṃ vyañjanakuśalo bhavati / sva niruktavyañjana(jña)tāmupādāya // kathaṃ niruktikuśalo bhavati / ātmātmīyeti janapadaniruktimanabhiniviśyānuvyavahārajñatāmupādāya // kathaṃ pūrvāntāparāntānusandhikuśalo bhavati / pūrvānte udgrahaṇaṃ tāmaparānte niḥsaraṇaṃ tāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: How does one become skilled in <s>dharmas</s> among <s>dharmas</s>? Through extensive learning. How does one become skilled in meaning? Through knowledge of characteristics in the <s>Abhidharma</s> and <s>Abhivinaya</s>. How does one become skilled in expression (<s>vyañjana</s>)? Through knowing one's own etymological expressions. How does one become skilled in etymology (<s>nirukti</s>)? Through not clinging to local etymologies of 'self' and 'belonging to self,' and through knowing conventional usage. How does one become skilled in connecting the past and the future? Through undertaking learning regarding the past and undertaking the path of liberation regarding the future.

body.text: kathaṃ dharmeṣu dharmavihārī bhavati / bhāvanāmanāgamya kevalaśrutacintāprayogeṇa na dharmavihārī bhavati / śrutacintāmanagamya kevalabhāvanāprayogeṇa na dharmavihārī bhavati / ubhayamāgamyobhayavihāreṇa dharmavihārī bhavati // udgrahāya svādhyāyadeśanābhiḥ śrutamayaṃ draṣṭavyam // samadhiprayogāsantuṣṭibhyāṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ draṣṭavyam // prayogaḥ sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogeṇāviparītaprayogeṇa ca draṣṭavyaḥ // asantuṣṭiranāsvāditottaśamayaprayogeṇa draṣṭavyā //
body.translated_text: How does one become a <s>dharma</s>-abider among <s>dharmas</s>? One who has not attained meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), with only the application of learning and reflection (<s>śrutacintā</s>), is not a <s>dharma</s>-abider. One who has not attained learning and reflection, with only the application of meditation, is not a <s>dharma</s>-abider. Having attained both, through abiding in both, one becomes a <s>dharma</s>-abider. That which is born of learning (<s>śrutamaya</s>) should be understood through study, recitation, and teaching, for the sake of retention. That which is born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) should be understood through application to <s>samādhi</s> and non-complacency. Application should be understood through constant and earnest application, and through non-erroneous application. Non-complacency should be understood through application that does not rest content with the quenching of that which has been tasted.

body.text: kena kāraṇena vaipulyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ pāramitāpiṭakamucyate / pāramitānāṃ saṃkhyānirddeśatāmupādāya lakṣaṇanirddeśatāmupādāya kramanirdeśatāmupādāya niruktinirdeśatāmupādāya bhāvanānirdeśatā mupādāya prabhedanirdeśatāmupādāya saṃgrahanirdeśatāmupādāya vipakṣanirdeśatāmupādaya guṇavarṇananirdeśatāmupādāya anyo 'nyaviniścayatāṃ copādāya //
body.translated_text: For what reason is the <s>Vaipulya</s> [literature] called the basket of <s>pāramitās</s> (<s>pāramitāpiṭaka</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Based on the exposition of the enumeration of the <s>pāramitās</s>, the exposition of their characteristics, the exposition of their sequence, the exposition of their etymology, the exposition of their cultivation, the exposition of their divisions, the exposition of their inclusion, the exposition of their opposites, the exposition praising their qualities, and their mutual ascertainment.

body.text: kena kāraṇena vaipulyaṃ audāryaṃ gāmbhīrya ca deśyate / sarvākārajñatā(ma) udāragambhīratāmupādaya // kena kāraṇena vaipulye ekatyā(ḥ) sattvā audāryagāmbhīryaṃ nādhimucyante uttrasanti / dharmatāviyuktatāmupādāya (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 84]

children.text: ) anavaropitakuśalamūlatāmupādāya pāpamitraparigrahatāṃ copādāya // kena kāraṇena vaipulye ekatyāḥ sattvā adhimucyante / (adhimucya)mānā api na niryānti / svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarśa sthāpitayā / idaṃ ca sandhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā mahādharmādarśe dharmaparyāye bodhisattvasya yathāruta mayoniśo dharmānvicinvataḥ aṣṭāviṃśatirasadṛṣṭaya utpadyante // aṣṭāviṃśatirasadṛṣṭayaḥ katamāḥ / nimittadṛṣṭiḥ prajñaptyapavādadṛṣṭiḥ parikalpāpavādadṛṣṭiḥ tattvāpavādadṛṣṭiḥ parigrahadṛṣṭiḥ pariṇatidṛṣṭiḥ anavadyatādṛṣṭiḥ niḥsaraṇadṛṣṭiḥ avajñādṛṣṭiḥ prakopadṛṣṭiḥ viparītadṛṣṭiḥ prasavadṛṣṭiḥ anabhyupagamadṛṣṭiḥ kusṛtidṛṣṭiḥ satkāradṛṣṭi dṛḍhamūḍhatādṛṣṭiḥ mūladṛṣṭiḥ dṛṣṭāvadṛṣṭadṛṣṭiḥ prayoganirākaraṇadṛṣṭiḥ anairyāṇikadṛṣṭiḥ āvaraṇopacayadṛṣṭiḥ apuṇyaprasavadṛṣṭiḥ vaiphalyadṛṣṭiḥ nigrāhyadṛṣṭiḥ abhyākhyānadṛṣṭiḥ akathyadṛṣṭiḥ mahādṛṣṭiḥ abhimānadṛṣṭiśca //
children.translated_text: based on not having planted roots of wholesome [conduct], and based on being under the influence of evil friends (<s>pāpamitra</s>). For what reason do some beings have faith in the <s>Vaipulya</s>, yet even having faith, do not progress? Because they are established in clinging to their own views (<s>svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>). With this intention the <s>Bhagavān</s> said in the <s>Mahādharmādarśa</s> discourse: for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who investigates <s>dharmas</s> unskilfully according to the letter, twenty-eight false views arise. What are the twenty-eight false views? The view of signs (<s>nimittadṛṣṭi</s>), the view denying designations, the view denying the imagined, the view denying reality, the view of grasping, the view of transformation, the view of faultlessness, the view of liberation, the view of contempt, the view of anger, the perverted view, the view of production, the view of non-acceptance, the view of wrong conduct, the view of honor, the view of firm delusion, the view of the root, the view of seeing the unseen as seen, the view rejecting practice, the view of no deliverance, the view of accumulating obscurations, the view producing demerit, the view of futility, the view deserving censure, the view of false accusation, the view of what should not be spoken, the great view, and the view of conceit (<s>abhimānadṛṣṭi</s>).

body.translated_text: For what reason is the <s>Vaipulya</s> taught as vast (<s>audārya</s>) and profound (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>)? Based on the vast and profound nature of omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). For what reason do some beings in the <s>Vaipulya</s> not have faith in the vastness and profundity, and become frightened? Based on being dissociated from the nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>),

body.text: yaduktaṃ vaipulye niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti / tatra ko 'bhisandhiḥ / svayamabhāvatāmupādāya svenātmanābhāvatāmupādāya sve bhāve 'navasthitātma (tā)mupādāya bālagrāhavaccālakṣaṇatāmupādāya // api khalu parikalpite svabhāve lakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatāmupādāya paratantre utpattiniḥsvabhāvatāmupādāya pariniṣpanne paramārthaniḥsvabhāvatāmupādāya // anutpannā aniruddhā ādiśāntā(ḥ) prakṛtiparinirvṛtā iti ko 'bhisandhiḥ / yathā niḥsvabhāvāstathā anutpannāḥ / yathā anutpannāstathā aniruddhāḥ / yathā anutpannāścāniruddhāśca tathā ādiśāntāḥ / yathā ādiśāntā stathā prakṛtiparinirvṛtāḥ //
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Vaipulya</s>: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>)' — what is the implicit meaning there? Based on the absence of self-existence, based on the absence of existence by its own self, based on the non-abiding of self in its own existence, and based on not being characterized as the grasping of the childish. Furthermore, regarding the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>), based on the absence of inherent nature as regards characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatā</s>); regarding the dependent nature (<s>paratantra</s>), based on the absence of inherent nature as regards arising (<s>utpattiniḥsvabhāvatā</s>); regarding the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>), based on the absence of inherent nature in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthaniḥsvabhāvatā</s>). 'Unborn, unceased, quiescent from the beginning, by nature in <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — what is the implicit meaning? Just as they are without inherent nature, so they are unborn. Just as they are unborn, so they are unceased. Just as they are unborn and unceased, so they are quiescent from the beginning. Just as they are quiescent from the beginning, so they are by nature in <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: api khalu catvāro 'bhiprāyāḥ / yairvaipulye tathāgatānāmabhiprāyo 'nugantavyaḥ / samatābhiprāyaḥ kālāntarābhiprāyaḥ arthāntarābhiprāyaḥ pugdalāśayābhiprāyaśca //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, there are four intentions (<s>abhiprāya</s>) by which the intention of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the <s>Vaipulya</s> should be understood: the intention of equality (<s>samatābhiprāya</s>), the intention regarding another time (<s>kālāntarābhiprāya</s>), the intention regarding another meaning (<s>arthāntarābhiprāya</s>), and the intention regarding the disposition of persons (<s>pudgalāśayābhiprāya</s>).

body.text: catvāro 'bhisandhayo yaivapulye tathāgatānāmabhisandhiranugantavyaḥ / avatāraṇābhisaṃdhiḥ lakṣaṇābhisandhiḥ pratipakṣābhisandhiḥ pariṇāmanābhisandhiśca //
body.translated_text: There are four implicit references (<s>abhisandhi</s>) by which the implicit reference of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the <s>Vaipulya</s> should be understood: the implicit reference of introduction (<s>avatāraṇābhisandhi</s>), the implicit reference of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇābhisandhi</s>), the implicit reference of antidote (<s>pratipakṣābhisandhi</s>), and the implicit reference of transformation (<s>pariṇāmanābhisandhi</s>).

body.text: vaipulye dharmasamādhikuśalo bodhisattvaḥ kathaṃ pratyavagantavyaḥ / pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ / pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvadauṣṭhulyāśrayaṃ drāvayati / nānātvasaṃjñāvigatāṃ ca dharmārāmaratiṃ pratilabhate / aparicchinnākāraṃ vāpramāṇāṃ dharmāvabhāsaṃ saṃjñānāti / viśuddhabhāgīyāni cāsyāvikalpitāni nimittāni samudācaranti / dharmakāyaparipūri pariniṣpattaye cottarāduttarataraṃ hetumayaparigrahaṃ karoti /
body.translated_text: How should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> skilled in the <s>dharma</s>-<s>samādhi</s> of the <s>Vaipulya</s> be understood? Through five reasons: at every moment, one dissolves the basis of all rigidity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>); one obtains the delight in the garden of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmārāma</s>), free from the perception of diversity; one perceives the unlimited, uncircumscribed radiance of <s>Dharma</s>; unconstructed signs belonging to the class of purity arise for one; and one produces ever-increasing causal accumulation for the completion and perfection of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>.

body.text: tatra pañcavidhāyāṃ bhāvanāyāṃ phalaṃ pañcavidhaṃ nirvattirtamiti darśayati / pañcavidhā bhāvanā saṃbhinnabhāvanā animittabhāvanā anābhogabhāvanā uttaptabhāvanā parivṛttinibhaḥ(?) bhāvanā yathākramam //
body.translated_text: Therein, [the text] shows that in the fivefold cultivation, a fivefold fruit is produced. The fivefold cultivation is: combined cultivation (<s>saṃbhinnabhāvanā</s>), signless cultivation (<s>animittabhāvanā</s>), effortless cultivation (<s>anābhogabhāvanā</s>), intensified cultivation (<s>uttaptabhāvanā</s>), and cultivation resembling transformation, respectively.

body.text: kena kāraṇena vaipulyadharmo dhūpamālyādibhiḥ pūjyo na tathā śrāvakadharmaḥ sarvasattvahitasukhādhiṣṭhānatāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: For what reason is the <s>Vaipulya Dharma</s> to be worshipped with incense, garlands, and the like, and not so the <s>Śrāvaka Dharma</s>? Because it is established for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings.

body.text: abhidharmasamuccaye dharmaviniścayo nāma tṛtīyaḥ samuccayaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmasamuccaya</s>, [this is] the third collection, called the ascertainment of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaviniścaya</s>).

body.text: (mahāyānābhidharmasamuccayaśāstre viniścaye prāptiparicchede tṛtīye prathamo bhāgaḥ /)
body.translated_text: (In the <s>Mahāyānābhidharmasamuccaya</s> treatise, in the Ascertainment [section], in the chapter on Attainment, the third [chapter], the first part.)

body.text: prāptiviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / saṃkṣepato dvividhaḥ / pudgalavyavasthānataḥ abhisamaya vyavasthāpanataśca draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of attainment (<s>prāptiviniścaya</s>)? In brief, it is twofold: it should be viewed from [the perspective of] the classification of persons (<s>pudgalavyavasthāna</s>) and from the classification of realization (<s>abhisamayavyavasthāpana</s>).

body.text: pudgalavyavasthānaṃ katamat / samāsataḥ saptavidham / roga caritaprabhedataḥ niryāṇaprabhedataḥ ādhāraprabhedataḥ prayogaprabhedataḥ phalaprabhedataḥ dhātuprabhedataḥ caryāprabhedataśca //
body.translated_text: What is the classification of persons? In brief, it is sevenfold: from the division of disposition and conduct (<s>rogacarita</s>), from the division of the vehicle of deliverance (<s>niryāṇa</s>), from the division of the basis (<s>ādhāra</s>), from the division of practice (<s>prayoga</s>), from the division of fruit (<s>phala</s>), from the division of realm (<s>dhātu</s>), and from the division of conduct (<s>caryā</s>).

body.text: rogacaritaprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / saptavidhaḥ / rāgacaritaḥ dveṣacarita mohacaritaḥ mānacaritaḥ vitarkacaritaḥ samabhāgacaritaḥ mandarajaska caritaśca pudgalaprabhedaḥ // niryāṇaprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / trividhaḥ / śrāvakayānikaḥ pratyekabuddhayānikaḥ mahāyānikaśca pudgalaprabhedaḥ // ādhāraprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / trividhaḥ / asaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ saṃbhṛtāsaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraśca pudgalaprabhedaḥ // prayogaprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / śraddhānusārī dharmānusārī ca pudgalaprabhedaḥ // phalaprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / saptaviṃśatividhaḥ / śraddhādhimuktaḥ dṛṣṭiprāptaḥ kāyasākṣī prajñāvimuktaḥ ubhayatobhāgavimuktaḥ strotāpattiphalapratipakṣakaḥ strotaāpannaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannakaḥ sakṛdāgāmī anāgāmiphalapratipannakaḥ anāgāmī arhattvaphalapratipannakaḥ arhan saptakṛdbhavaparamaḥ kulaṃkulaḥ ekavīcikaḥ antarāparinirvāyī upapadyaparinirvāyī anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī ūrddvaṃstrotāḥ parihāṇadharmā arhan cetanādharmā arhan anurakṣaṇādharmā arhan sthitākampyaḥ arhan prativedhadharmā arhan akopyadharmā arhan ca pudgalaprabhedaḥ // dhātuprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / kāmāvacaraḥ pṛthagjanaḥ śīkṣo 'śaikṣaśca / evaṃ trividhaḥ kāmāvacaro rūpāvacara ārupyāvacaraḥ / kāmāvacaro rūpāvacaraśca bodhisattvaḥ kāmāvacaraḥ pratyekabuddhaḥ acintyaśca tathāgataḥ pudgalaprabhedaḥ // caryāprabhedaḥ katamaḥ / saṃkṣepataḥ pañcavidhaḥ / adhimukticārī bodhisattvaḥ adhyāśayacārī bodhisattvaḥ nimittacārī bodhisattvaḥ animittacāri bodhisattvaḥ anabhisaṃskāracārī bodhisattvaśca pudgalaprabhedaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the classification by temperament (<s>carita</s>)? It is sevenfold: the person of desire-temperament (<s>rāgacarita</s>), hatred-temperament (<s>dveṣacarita</s>), delusion-temperament (<s>mohacarita</s>), pride-temperament (<s>mānacarita</s>), discursive-thought-temperament (<s>vitarkacarita</s>), balanced-temperament (<s>samabhāgacarita</s>), and light-dust-temperament (<s>mandarajaskacarita</s>) — this is the classification of persons. What is the classification by vehicle (<s>niryāṇa</s>)? It is threefold: the <s>Śrāvakayānika</s> (one of the Hearers' vehicle), the <s>Pratyekabuddhayānika</s> (one of the Solitary Awakened Ones' vehicle), and the <s>Mahāyānika</s> (one of the Great Vehicle) — this is the classification of persons. What is the classification by foundation (<s>ādhāra</s>)? It is threefold: one who has not accumulated the requisites (<s>asaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāra</s>), one who has partially accumulated the requisites (<s>saṃbhṛtāsaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāra</s>), and one who has fully accumulated the requisites (<s>saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāra</s>) — this is the classification of persons. What is the classification by practice (<s>prayoga</s>)? The faith-follower (<s>śraddhānusārī</s>) and the <s>Dharma</s>-follower (<s>dharmānusārī</s>) — this is the classification of persons. What is the classification by fruit (<s>phala</s>)? It is twenty-seven-fold: the faith-resolved (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>), the view-attainer (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>), the body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣī</s>), the wisdom-liberated (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>), the both-ways-liberated (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>), the stream-entry practitioner (<s>srotāpattiphalapratipannaka</s>), the stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>), the once-returner practitioner (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannaka</s>), the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmī</s>), the non-returner practitioner (<s>anāgāmiphalapratipannaka</s>), the non-returner (<s>anāgāmī</s>), the arhatship practitioner (<s>arhattvaphalapratipannaka</s>), the <s>Arhat</s>, the seven-times-at-most (<s>saptakṛdbhavaparama</s>), the family-to-family (<s>kulaṃkula</s>), the one-intervening (<s>ekavīcika</s>), the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state (<s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>), the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth (<s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>), the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī</s>), the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with effort (<s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī</s>), the one who goes upstream (<s>ūrdhvaṃsrota</s>), the <s>Arhat</s> subject to decline (<s>parihāṇadharma</s>), the <s>Arhat</s> subject to deliberate [death] (<s>cetanādharma</s>), the <s>Arhat</s> subject to guarding (<s>anurakṣaṇādharma</s>), the <s>Arhat</s> who is stable and immovable (<s>sthitākampya</s>), the <s>Arhat</s> subject to penetration (<s>prativedhadharma</s>), and the <s>Arhat</s> who is unshakable (<s>akopyadharma</s>) — this is the classification of persons. What is the classification by realm (<s>dhātu</s>)? A desire-realm ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), a trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>), and one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). Thus threefold for the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is of the desire and form realms. The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> is of the desire realm. The <s>Tathāgata</s> is inconceivable — this is the classification of persons. What is the classification by conduct (<s>caryā</s>)? In brief, it is fivefold: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who courses in aspiration (<s>adhimukticārī</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who courses in superior intention (<s>adhyāśayacārī</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who courses with signs (<s>nimittacārī</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who courses without signs (<s>animittacārī</s>), and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who courses without deliberation (<s>anabhisaṃskāracārī</s>) — this is the classification of persons.

body.text: rāgacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / tīvrā yatarāgaḥ / evaṃ dveṣacarito mohacarito mānacarito vitarkacaritaśca pudgalaḥ tīvrāyataviśiṣṭaḥ // samabhāgacaritaḥ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 87]

children.text: ) pudgalaḥ katamaḥ // prakṛtisthakleśaḥ // mandarajaskacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / prakṛtisthatanutarakleśaḥ //
children.translated_text: — what is that person? One whose afflictions are in their natural state. What is the person of light-dust-temperament? One whose afflictions in their natural state are even more attenuated.

body.translated_text: What is the person of desire-temperament? One whose desire is intense and extensive. Likewise, the person of hatred-temperament, delusion-temperament, pride-temperament, and discursive-thought-temperament is distinguished by intensity and extensiveness. The person of balanced-temperament

body.text: śrāvakayānikaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ samāpanno vā asamāpanno vā śrāvakadharmatāvihārī prakṛtyā mṛdvindriyaḥ svavimuktaye praṇihitaḥ vairāgyabhāvanayā vimuktāśayaḥ śrāvakapiṭakamavalambya vīryabhāvanayā dharmānudharmacārī duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // pratyekabuddhayānikaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ samāpanno vā asamāpanno vā pratyekabuddhadharmatāvihārī prakṛtyā madhyendriyaḥ svavimuktaye praṇihitaḥ vairāgyabhāvanayā vimuktāśayaḥ kevalabhāvanayā cādhigatavodhyāśayaḥ śrāvakapiṭakamavalambya vīryabhāvanayā dharmānudharmacārī anutpāditapūrvanirvedhabhāgīyaḥ utpāditapūrvanirvedhabhāgīyaḥ aprāptapūrvaphalaḥ abuddhalaukikaḥ adhyātma cetanayā ārya mārgasaṃmukhībhūtaḥ khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpaḥ ekavihārī pratyekajinaḥ varggacāri duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // mahāyānikaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / yaḥ samāpanno vā asamāpanno vā bodhisattvadharmatāvihārī prakṛtyā tīkṣṇendriyaḥ sarvasattvavimokṣāya praṇihitaḥ apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇāśayaḥ bodhisattvapiṭakamavalambya vīryabhāvanayā dharmānudharmacārī sattvān paripācayati śuddhāṃ buddhabhūmiṃ bhāvayati vyākaraṇaṃ ca pratilabhate samyaksaṃbodhiṃ ca sākṣātkaroti //
body.translated_text: What is the <s>Śrāvakayānika</s> person? One who, whether accomplished or not yet accomplished, dwells in the nature of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, who by nature has weak faculties, who is directed toward one's own liberation, whose intention is liberation through the cultivation of dispassion, who — relying on the <s>Śrāvaka</s> collection (<s>piṭaka</s>) and cultivating energy — practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and reaches the end of suffering. What is the <s>Pratyekabuddhayānika</s> person? One who, whether accomplished or not yet accomplished, dwells in the nature of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, who by nature has medium faculties, who is directed toward one's own liberation, whose intention is liberation through the cultivation of dispassion, whose intention is awakening through solitary cultivation, who — relying on the <s>Śrāvaka</s> collection and cultivating energy — practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, who has either not previously produced or has previously produced the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), who has not previously attained the fruit, who is not in a world with a <s>Buddha</s>, who through inner mental effort comes face to face with the noble path, who is like the rhinoceros horn (<s>khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpa</s>), dwelling alone, a solitary conqueror (<s>Pratyekajina</s>), traveling in a group — [such a one] reaches the end of suffering. What is the <s>Mahāyānika</s> person? One who, whether accomplished or not yet accomplished, dwells in the nature of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who by nature has sharp faculties, who is directed toward the liberation of all beings, whose intention is non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>), who — relying on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> collection and cultivating energy — practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, matures beings, cultivates the pure <s>Buddha</s>-ground, receives a prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>), and directly realizes perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: asaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / satyādhipateyaṃ dharmamālambya mṛdumātrasamutthitaḥ śuddhaśraddhādhimuktaḥ mṛdumātrāmokṣabhāgīyasamanvāgataḥ aniyatajanmakālikaḥ // saṃbhṛtāsaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / satyādhipateyaṃ dharmamālambya madhyamātrasamutthitaḥ śuddhaśraddhādhimuktaḥ madhyamātramokṣabhāgīyasamanvāgato niyatajanmakālikaḥ // saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / satyādhipatayaṃ dharmamālambya adhimātrasamutthitaḥ śuddhaśraddhādhimuktaḥ adhimātramokṣabhāgīyasamanvāgataḥ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 88]

children.text: ) tajjanmakālikaḥ // punaḥ asaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ satyādhipateyaṃ dharmamālambya satyeṣu mṛdumātrasatya dharmanidhyānakṣāntisamanvāgato mṛdumātra nirvedhabhāgīyasanvāgata anivatajanmakālikaḥ // saṃbhṛtāsaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ satyādhipateyaṃ dharmamālambya satyeṣu madhyamātrasatya dharmanidhyānakṣāntisamanvāgataḥ madhyamātranirvedhabhāgīyasamanvāgato nithatajanmakālikaḥ // saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ satyādhipateyaṃ dharmamālambya satyeṣu adhimātrasatya dharmanidhyānakṣāntisamanvāgataḥ adhimātranirvedhabhāgīyasamanvāgataḥ tajjanmakālikaḥ // tatra trimātranirvedhabhāgīyo laukikāgradharmaṃ sthāpayitvā laukikāgradharmaprakṛtyaiva kṣaṇikaḥ aprāvandhikaḥ // tajjanmakālikaḥ abhisamayaṃ samāpadyamāno 'pūrvavastha mṛdumadhyādhimātramokṣabhāgīyebhyo [nirvedha]bhāgīyebhyaśca parihīyate / tacca samudācāraparihāṇito no tu vāsanāparihāṇitaḥ /
children.translated_text: and whose time [of liberation] is in that very birth. Furthermore, the one who has not accumulated the requisites, having taken as object the <s>Dharma</s> with truth as sovereign, is endowed with slight patient acceptance born of reflection on the truth of <s>dharmas</s> regarding the truths, is endowed with slight aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), and whose time is not determined in terms of births. The one who has partially accumulated the requisites, having taken as object the <s>Dharma</s> with truth as sovereign, is endowed with medium patient acceptance born of reflection on the truth of <s>dharmas</s> regarding the truths, is endowed with medium aids to penetration, and whose time is determined in terms of births. The one who has fully accumulated the requisites, having taken as object the <s>Dharma</s> with truth as sovereign, is endowed with superior patient acceptance born of reflection on the truth of <s>dharmas</s> regarding the truths, is endowed with superior aids to penetration, and whose time is in that very birth. Here, the three levels of aids to penetration — setting aside the supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>) — [apply], for the supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s> by their very nature are momentary and without interval. The one whose time is in that very birth, upon entering realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>), in an unprecedented manner falls away from the slight, medium, and superior roots conducive to liberation and aids to penetration. But that falling away is from active manifestation, not from the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>).

body.translated_text: What is the person who has not accumulated the requisites? One who, having taken as object the <s>Dharma</s> with truth as sovereign, has arisen to only a slight degree, has pure faith and aspiration, is endowed with only slight roots conducive to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>), and whose time [of liberation] is not determined in terms of births. What is the person who has partially accumulated the requisites? One who, having taken as object the <s>Dharma</s> with truth as sovereign, has arisen to a medium degree, has pure faith and aspiration, is endowed with medium roots conducive to liberation, and whose time is determined in terms of births. What is the person who has fully accumulated the requisites? One who, having taken as object the <s>Dharma</s> with truth as sovereign, has arisen to a superior degree, has pure faith and aspiration, is endowed with superior roots conducive to liberation,

body.text: śraddhānusārī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro mṛdvindriyaḥ paropadeśamanusmṛtya yaḥ satyābhisamayāya prayujyate // dharmānusārī katamaḥ / saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārastīkṣṇendriyaḥ svayameva satyādhipateyaṃ dharmamanusmṛtya yaḥ [satyābhi]samayāya prayujyate //
