body.translated_text: What is the faith-follower (<s>śraddhānusārī</s>) person? One who has fully accumulated the requisites, has weak faculties, and who — recollecting the instructions of others — applies oneself to the realization of the truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>). What is the <s>Dharma</s>-follower (<s>dharmānusārī</s>)? One who has fully accumulated the requisites, has sharp faculties, and who — recollecting by oneself the <s>Dharma</s> with truth as sovereign — applies oneself to the realization of the truths.

body.text: śraddhādhimuktaḥ katamaḥ / phalakāle śraddhānusārī yaḥ pugdalaḥ // dṛṣṭiprāptaḥ katamaḥ / phalakāle dharmānusārī yaḥ pudgalaḥ // kāyasākṣī katamaḥ / śaikṣaḥ aṣṭavimokṣadhyāyī yaḥ pudgalaḥ // prajñāvimuktaḥ katamaḥ / kṣīṇāsravo bhotvaṣṭavimokṣadhyāyo yaḥ pugdalaḥ // ubhayatobhāgavimu[ktaḥ kata]maḥ / kṣīṇāsravo 'ṣṭavimokṣadhyāyī yaḥ pudgalaḥ // strotāpattiphalapratipannakaḥ katamaḥ / nirvedhabhāgīyeṣu pañcadaśasu darśanamārgacittakṣaṇeṣu yaḥ pudgalaḥ // strota āpakṣaḥ katamaḥ / ṣoḍaśe darśanamārgacittakṣaṇe yaḥpudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the faith-resolved (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>)? At the time of the fruit, the person who was a faith-follower. What is the view-attainer (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>)? At the time of the fruit, the person who was a <s>Dharma</s>-follower. What is the body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣī</s>)? A trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) who meditates on the eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>). What is the wisdom-liberated (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>)? One whose outflows are exhausted (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>) but who does not meditate on the eight liberations. What is the both-ways-liberated (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>)? One whose outflows are exhausted and who meditates on the eight liberations. What is the stream-entry practitioner (<s>srotāpattiphalapratipannaka</s>)? A person in the fifteen mind-moments of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) among the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). What is the stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>)? A person in the sixteenth mind-moment of the path of seeing.

body.text: darśanamārga(ḥ) satyakatvaniyāmāvakrāntiḥ / dharmābhi[samaye]pi saḥ / kāmeṣvavītarāgaḥ pudgalaḥ samyaktvaniyāmamavakrāman strotaāpanno bhavati // yadbhūyo vītarāgaḥ samyaktvaniyāmamavakrāman sakṛdāgāmī bhavati / kāmebhyo vītarāgaḥ samyaktvaniyāmamavakrāmannanāgāmī bhavati // yadā darśana prahātavyānāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇāt [stota ā]panno bhavati // kena kāraṇena trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāt strotaāpanno bhavati / pradhānasaṃgraha(ta) 'bhavati / prādhānyaṃ kimupādāya / anuccalanakāraṇatāmupādāya / uccalitasya mithyāniryāṇakāraṇatāmupādāya / samyaganiryāṇa(kāraṇa)tāṃ copādāya // api khalu jñeyavipra[tipatti]kāraṇatāmupādāya dṛṣṭivipratipattikāraṇatāmupādāya pratipakṣavipratipattikāraṇatāṃ copādāya // sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannakaḥ katamaḥ / bhāvanāmārge kāmāvacarāṇāṃ pañcaprakārāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇamārge yaḥ pudgalaḥ / sakṛdāgāmī katamaḥ / bhāvanāmārge kāmāvacarasya ṣaṣṭhasya kleśaprakā[rasya pra] hāṇamārge yaḥ pugdalaḥ // anāgāmiphalapratipannakaḥ katamaḥ / bhāvanāmārge kāmāvacarāṇāṃ saptamāṣṭamānāṃ kleśaprakārāṇāṃ prahāṇamārge yaḥ pudgalaḥ // anāgāmī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / bhāvanāmarge kāmāvacarasya navamasya kleśaprakārasya prahāṇamārge yaḥ pudgalaḥ // yadā sarveṣāṃ kāmāvacarā[ṇāṃ bhāva]nāprahātavyānāṃ prahāṇādanāgāmī bhavati // kena kāraṇena pañcānāmavarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanā prahāṇādanāgāmītyucyate / pradhānasaṃgrahamupādāya // prādhānyaṃ kimupādāya / gatyavara kāraṇatāṃ dhātvaparakāraṇatāṃ copādāya // arhattvaphalapratipannakaḥ katamaḥ / yāvadbhāvāgrikāṇāmaṣṭaprakārāṇāṃ [kleśānāṃ] prahāṇamārge yaḥ pudgalaḥ // arhan (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 90]

children.text: ) katamaḥ / bhāvāmrikasya navamasya kleśaprakārasya prahāṇamārge yaḥ pudgalaḥ // yadā traidhātukānāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ sarvvakleśānāṃ prahāṇādarhan bhavati // kena kāraṇenordbhabhāgīyānāṃ prahāṇādarhannityucyate / pradhānasaṃgrahamupādāya / pradhāna saṃgrahaḥ ki[mupādāya] / vimokṣopādāna kāraṇatāmupādāya / ūrddvā parityāgakāraṇatāṃ copādāya / saptakṛdbhavaraparamaḥ katamaḥ / strotaāpanna eva pudgalaḥ saptakṛtvo 'pi miśromiśra devamanuṣyeṣu bhavāt saṃsṛtya yo duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // kulaṃkulaḥ katamaḥ / deveṣu vā kulātkulaṃ gatvā [manuṣye]ṣu vā yo duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // ekavīcikaḥ katamaḥ / sakṛdāgāmī deveṣveva yo duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // antarāparinirvāyī katamaḥ / upapattisaṃyojane prahīṇe abhinivṛttisaṃyojane aprahīṇe antarābhavamabhinirvarttayanneva yo mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti abhinivṛtto vā antarābhave upapattibhavagamanāya cetayannevayo mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti / abhisaṃcetayitvā vā upapattibhavamabhisaṃprasthitaḥ [bhavānu]papatticchandaṃ yo mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // upapadyaparinirvāyī katamaḥ / ubhayasaṃyojane aprahīṇe rūpadhātāvupapannamātra eva yo mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī katamaḥ / upapannaḥ anabhisaṃskāreṇa yo mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // abhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī katamaḥ / upapanno 'bhisaṃskāreṇa yo mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti // ūrdhvaṃstrotāḥ katamaḥ / upapanno rūpāvacarāṇāṃ bhūmau bhūmau yāvadakaniṣṭhagān praviśya tannānāsrava mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti / puna kaścid yāvad bhavāgragān mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya duḥkhasyāntamanuprāpnoti / api ca vyavakīrṇabhāvitasya caturthasya dhyānasya pañcaprakārā prabhedāḥ / mṛduparibhāvitaṃ madhyaparibhāvitamadhimātraparibhāvitamadhimātrādhimātrāparibhāvitamadhyādhimātraparibhāvitaṃ (
children.translated_text: —who is [the arhat]? A person who is on the path of abandoning the ninth category of afflictions at the peak of existence. When, through the abandonment of all afflictions of the three realms, including those of the desire realm, one becomes an <s>arhat</s>. For what reason is one called an <s>arhat</s> through the abandonment of the upper fetters (<s>ūrdhvabhāgīya-saṃyojanas</s>)? By way of a principal summary. A principal summary in what regard? In regard to being the cause of grasping liberation, and in regard to being the cause of abandoning the higher [realms]. Who is the one who returns at most seven times (<s>saptakṛdbhavaparama</s>)? A person who, being a stream-enterer, having transmigrated through existence up to seven times among various gods and humans, reaches the end of suffering. Who is the clan-to-clan (<s>kulaṃkula</s>)? One who, going from clan to clan among gods or among humans, reaches the end of suffering. Who is the one-seeder (<s>ekavīcika</s>)? A once-returner who reaches the end of suffering among the gods alone. Who is the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state (<s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>)? One whose rebirth-fetter is abandoned but whose actualization-fetter is not abandoned, who, while producing the intermediate existence, actualizes the path and reaches the end of suffering; or one who, having been produced in the intermediate existence and intending to go to the rebirth-existence, actualizes the path and reaches the end of suffering; or one who, having intended and set out toward rebirth-existence, [but] with the desire for further existence, actualizes the path and reaches the end of suffering. Who is the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth (<s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s>)? One whose both fetters are not abandoned, who, immediately upon being reborn in the form realm, actualizes the path and reaches the end of suffering. Who is the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>)? One who, having been reborn, without [special] effort actualizes the path and reaches the end of suffering. Who is the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with effort (<s>abhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>)? One who, having been reborn, with effort actualizes the path and reaches the end of suffering. Who is the one who goes upward (<s>ūrdhvasrotas</s>)? One who, having been reborn, progresses level by level through the form-realm levels up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> [heaven], enters it, and there actualizes the uncontaminated path and reaches the end of suffering. Furthermore, some go up to the peak of existence and actualize the path and reach the end of suffering. Moreover, there are five varieties of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> cultivated in a mixed manner: weakly cultivated, moderately cultivated, intensely cultivated, supremely intensely cultivated, and moderately intensely cultivated—
[<s>Abhidh-s</s> 91]

children.text: ) ca / taiḥ vyavakīrṇābhāvitasya caturthadhyānasya pañcaprabhedaiḥ yathākramaṃ paścasu śuddhāvāseṣūpapattiḥ //
children.translated_text: and by these five varieties of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> cultivated in a mixed manner, rebirth occurs in the five Pure Abodes (<s>Śuddhāvāsas</s>) in corresponding order.

body.translated_text: The path of seeing (<s>darśana-mārga</s>) is the entry into the certainty of the truth-making [nature of reality]. It is also [called] the realization of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmābhisamaya</s>). A person who has not yet become free from desire for the sense realm (<s>kāma</s>), upon entering the certainty of the correct [path], becomes a stream-enterer (<s>srota-āpanna</s>). One who is more extensively free from desire, upon entering the certainty of the correct [path], becomes a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>). One who is [entirely] free from desire for the sense realm, upon entering the certainty of the correct [path], becomes a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>). When, through the abandonment of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) to be abandoned by seeing, one becomes a stream-enterer—for what reason is one called a stream-enterer through the abandonment of three fetters (<s>saṃyojanas</s>)? By way of a principal summary. Principal in what regard? In regard to being the cause of non-wavering, in regard to being the cause of wrong departure for one who has wavered, and in regard to being the cause of correct departure. Moreover, in regard to being the cause of confusion about the knowable, in regard to being the cause of confusion about views, and in regard to being the cause of confusion about the antidote. Who is one practicing toward the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmi-phala</s>)? A person who is on the path of abandoning five categories of afflictions of the desire realm on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā-mārga</s>). Who is the once-returner? A person who is on the path of abandoning the sixth category of afflictions of the desire realm on the path of cultivation. Who is one practicing toward the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmi-phala</s>)? A person who is on the path of abandoning the seventh and eighth categories of afflictions of the desire realm on the path of cultivation. Who is the non-returner? A person who is on the path of abandoning the ninth category of afflictions of the desire realm on the path of cultivation. When, through the abandonment of all afflictions of the desire realm to be abandoned by cultivation, one becomes a non-returner. For what reason is one called a non-returner through the abandonment of the five lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya-saṃyojanas</s>)? By way of a principal summary. Principal in what regard? In regard to being the cause of [rebirth in] lower destinies and in regard to being the cause of [rebirth in] lower realms. Who is one practicing toward the fruit of arhatship? A person who is on the path of abandoning up to eight categories of afflictions at the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). The <s>arhat</s>

body.text: parihāṇadharmā arhan katamaḥ / mṛdvindriyaprakṛtiko vikṣipto vā avikṣipto vā cetayitvā vā acetayitvā vā dṛṣṭadharmasukha vihārāt parihāṇameti // cetanādharmā arhan katamaḥ / mṛdvindriyaprakṛtiko vikṣipto vā avikṣipto vā acetayitvā dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāt parihāṇameti cetayitvā na parihāṇameti // anurakṣaṇādharmā arhan katamaḥ / mṛdvindriyaprakṛtiko vikṣipto dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāt / parihāṇameti avikṣipto na parihāṇameti // sthitākampyaḥ arhan katamaḥ / mṛdvindriya prakṛtiko vikṣipto vā avikṣipto vā dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāt na parihāṇameti nāpi indriyāṇyuttāpayati // prativedhanādharmā arhan katamaḥ / mṛdvindriyāprakṛtiko vikṣipto vā avikṣipto vā dṛṣṭadharmasukhaviharāt na parihāṇameti kevala mindriyā ṇyuttāpayati // akopyadharmā arhan katamaḥ / tīkṣṇendriyaprakṛtiko vikṣipto va avikṣipto vā na dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāt parihāṇameti //
body.translated_text: Who is the <s>arhat</s> liable to regression (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>)? One who is naturally of weak faculties, whether distracted or undistracted, whether intentionally or unintentionally, regresses from the pleasant abiding in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharma-sukha-vihāra</s>). Who is the <s>arhat</s> of the intention type (<s>cetanādharman</s>)? One who is naturally of weak faculties, whether distracted or undistracted, who regresses unintentionally from the pleasant abiding in the present life but does not regress when acting intentionally. Who is the <s>arhat</s> of the guarding type (<s>anurakṣaṇādharman</s>)? One who is naturally of weak faculties, who when distracted regresses from the pleasant abiding in the present life, but when undistracted does not regress. Who is the <s>arhat</s> who is stable and immovable (<s>sthitākampya</s>)? One who is naturally of weak faculties, whether distracted or undistracted, does not regress from the pleasant abiding in the present life, yet does not sharpen the faculties either. Who is the <s>arhat</s> of the penetrating type (<s>prativedhanādharman</s>)? One who is naturally not of weak faculties, whether distracted or undistracted, does not regress from the pleasant abiding in the present life, and solely sharpens the faculties. Who is the <s>arhat</s> of the unshakeable type (<s>akopyadharman</s>)? One who is naturally of sharp faculties, whether distracted or undistracted, does not regress from the pleasant abiding in the present life.

body.text: kāmāvacaraḥ pṛthagjanaḥ katamaḥ / kāmadhātāvupapanno bhavati āryadhaprāptaḥ pudgalaḥ ca // kāmāvacaraḥ śaikṣaḥ katamaḥ / kāmādhātāvupapanno bhavati adharmaṃ ca prāptaḥ pudgalaḥ / saṃyojanaṃ cāvaśiṣyate // kāmāvacaro 'śaikṣaḥ katamaḥ / kāmādhātāvupapanno bhavati āryadharmaṃ ca prāptaḥ pudgalaḥ / saṃyojanaṃ nāvaśiṣyate // yathā kāmāvacarāstrayaḥ tathā rūpāvacarā ārupyavacarā api // kāmāvacaro rūpāvacaro bodhisattvaḥ katamaḥ / ārūpyadhātuvyavakarṣitena dhyānena saṃprayukto dhyānasukhairviharatīti kāmadhātāvapyupapanno rūpadhātāvapyupapannaḥ pudgala kāmāvacaraḥ pratyekabuddhaḥ katamaḥ / abuddhabhave kāmadhātau svataḥ pratyekabuddhabodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ // (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 92]

children.text: ) acintyaḥ tathāgataḥ katamaḥ / kāmadhātau tuṣitabhavanayāsamārabhya yāvat mahāparinirvāṇaṃ darśayati sarvāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ buddhacaryāṃ mahācaryāṃ darśayatīti pudgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who is the inconceivable <s>Tathāgata</s>? A person who, beginning from [his descent from] the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, up to the display of the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, displays the entire conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the conduct of a <s>Buddha</s>, and the great conduct.

body.translated_text: Who is the ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) of the desire realm? A person who is born in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) and has not attained the noble <s>Dharma</s>. Who is the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) of the desire realm? A person who is born in the desire realm and has attained the noble <s>Dharma</s>, but in whom fetters (<s>saṃyojanas</s>) still remain. Who is the non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) of the desire realm? A person who is born in the desire realm and has attained the noble <s>Dharma</s>, and in whom no fetters remain. Just as there are these three in the desire realm, so too in the form realm and the formless realm. Who is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the desire realm and form realm? A person who, endowed with <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) drawn from the formless realm, dwells in the bliss of meditation—thus even one born in the desire realm or born in the form realm [is such a person]. Who is the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> of the desire realm? One who, in the absence of a <s>Buddha</s>, in the desire realm, by himself awakens to the enlightenment of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.

body.text: adhimukticārī bodhisattvaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / adhimukticaryābhūmau sthito mṛdumadhyādhimātrabodhisattvakṣāntisamanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ // adhyāśayacārī bodhisattvaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / daśasu bhūmiṣu sthito yo bodhisattvaḥ // sanimittacārī bodhisattvaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / pramuditāvimalāprabhākaryarciṣmatīsudurjayābhimukhībhūmiṣu sthito yo bodhisattvaḥ // animittacārī bodhisattvaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ / duraṃgamabhūmau sthito yo bodhisattvaḥ // anabhisaṃskāracārī bodhisattvaḥ pudgalaḥ katamataḥ / acalā sādhumatīdharmameghāsu bhūmiṣu sthito yo bodhisattvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Who is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> person practicing through aspiration (<s>adhimukticārin</s>)? A person who abides on the level of aspiration-practice (<s>adhimukticaryā-bhūmi</s>) and is endowed with weak, medium, and intense <s>Bodhisattva</s> patience (<s>kṣānti</s>). Who is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> person practicing through superior intention (<s>adhyāśayacārin</s>)? A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who abides on the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>). Who is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> person practicing with signs (<s>sanimittacārin</s>)? A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who abides on the stages of <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful), <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless), <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous), <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Radiant), <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Difficult to Conquer), and <s>Abhimukhī</s> (Facing Forward). Who is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> person practicing without signs (<s>animittacārin</s>)? A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who abides on the <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (Far-Going) stage. Who is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> person practicing without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāracārin</s>)? A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who abides on the <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable), <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence), and <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma) stages.

body.text: punaḥ khalu strotaāpannaḥ pugdalo yaduktaḥ sa dvividhaḥ / kramanairyāṇikaḥ sakṛnnairyāṇikaśca / krasanairyāṇiko yathā purvamuktaḥ // sakṛnnairyāṇikaḥ satyābhisamayamabhisaṃpraviṣṭaḥ aprāpta samāpattimāśritya adhigatena lokottaramāgreṇa sakṛta traidhātukāvacarān sarvakleśān prajahāti prakāraśaḥ prajahāti / dvayoḥ phalayo strotāpattiphalārhattvaphalayoḥ prajñāpyate / sa ca pudgalo bhūyo dṛṣṭe dharme maraṇakāle ājñāmārāgayati / yadi nārāgayati praṇidhānavaśena / tarhi praṇidhānavaśena kāmadhātāvevopapannaḥ avuddhabhave pratyekajinobhavati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) person as described is of two kinds: one who progresses gradually to liberation (<s>kramanairyāṇika</s>) and one who attains liberation at once (<s>sakṛnnairyāṇika</s>). The one who progresses gradually is as previously described. The one who attains liberation at once, having entered the realization of the truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>), relying on an unattained meditative attainment, through the supreme supramundane [path] already realized, abandons at once all afflictions pertaining to the three realms, abandoning them by types. He is designated [as having attained] two fruits: the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>) and the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> (<s>arhattvaphala</s>). That person further attains final knowledge either in the present life or at the time of death. If he does not attain it [then], through the power of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), being reborn in the desire realm by the power of aspiration, in a Buddha-less existence he becomes a solitary victor (<s>pratyekajina</s>).

body.text: (atha viniścaye prāptiparicchede tṛtīye dvitīyo bhāgaḥ)
body.translated_text: (Now, in the ascertainment [section], in the chapter on attainment, the second part of the third [division].)

body.text: abhisamayavyavasthānaṃ katamat / samāsato daśavidham / dharmābhisamayaḥ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 93]

children.text: ) arthābhisamayaḥ tattvābhisamayaḥ pṛṣṭhābhisamayaḥ ratnābhisamayaḥ asamudācārābhisamayaḥ niṣṭhābhisamayaḥ śrāvakābhisamayaḥ pratyekabuddhābhisamayaḥ bodhisattvābhisamayaśca //
children.translated_text: realization of meaning (<s>arthābhisamaya</s>), realization of reality (<s>tattvābhisamaya</s>), subsequent realization (<s>pṛṣṭhābhisamaya</s>), realization of the [Three] Jewels (<s>ratnābhisamaya</s>), realization of non-engagement [in unwholesome conduct] (<s>asamudācārābhisamaya</s>), realization of culmination (<s>niṣṭhābhisamaya</s>), realization of the <s>śrāvaka</s> (<s>śrāvakābhisamaya</s>), realization of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (<s>pratyekabuddhābhisamaya</s>), and realization of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>bodhisattvābhisamaya</s>).

body.translated_text: What is the classification of realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>)? In brief, it is tenfold: realization of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmābhisamaya</s>),

body.text: dharmābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / satyādhipateyeṣu dharmeṣu adhimātrasya adhimuktiprasādasya pratilambhaḥ yathāsaṃpratyayaṃ caryā ca //
body.translated_text: What is the realization of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmābhisamaya</s>)? It is the attainment of intense aspiration and faith (<s>adhimukti-prasāda</s>) in the <s>dharmas</s> governed by the truths, and conduct in accordance with that conviction.

body.text: arthābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ satyādhipateyeṣu dharmeṣu adhimātrāyāḥ satyeṣu dhamanidhyānakṣānteḥ pratilambhaḥ / sā kṣānti nirvedhabhāgīyāvasthāṃ gatā / sā punastrividhena yoniśo manaskāreṇa prabhāvitā / sa trividhastu adhimātramṛduḥ adhimātramadhyo 'dhimātrādhimātraśca //
body.translated_text: What is the realization of meaning (<s>arthābhisamaya</s>)? It is the attainment of intense patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) in the contemplation of the truths regarding the <s>dharmas</s> governed by the truths. That patient acceptance has reached the stage of the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). It is, moreover, developed through a threefold proper attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>). That threefold [attention] is: intensely mild, intensely moderate, and intensely intense.

body.text: tattvābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / ṣoḍaśe darśanamārgacittakṣaṇe ya āryamārgaṃ pratilabhate / darśanamārge punaḥ satye vyavasthāpanādyabhisamayāntikāni saṃmukhīkaroti / bhāvanāmārge tatsaṃvṛtijñānāni pratilabhate na tu saṃmukhīkaroti / bhāvanāmārge tatsaṃvṛtijñānabalena saṃmukhīkaroti /
body.translated_text: What is the realization of reality (<s>tattvābhisamaya</s>)? It is when one attains the noble path at the sixteenth mind-moment of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). On the path of seeing, one directly faces the [realizations] from the establishment [of the truths] up to the final realization regarding the truths. On the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), one attains the conventional knowledges (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>) pertaining to those [truths] but does not directly face them. On the path of cultivation, one directly faces them through the power of those conventional knowledges.

body.text: pṛṣṭhābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / sarvo bhāvanāmārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is subsequent realization (<s>pṛṣṭhābhisamaya</s>)? It is the entire path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>).

body.text: ratnābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / buddhe 'vetya prasādaḥ dharme 'tya prasādaḥ saṃghe 'vetya prasādaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the realization of the [Three] Jewels (<s>ratnābhisamaya</s>)? It is unwavering faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, unwavering faith in the <s>Dharma</s>, and unwavering faith in the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: asamudācārābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / akāraṇasaṃvaralābhāt śikṣāgatasya yadātmano narakakṣayaṃ tiryagyonikṣayaḥ pretayonikṣayaḥ avāṅpatanadurgatikṣayaḥ iti / na punarupādāya tad durgatikarma durgativipāko 'bhinirvarttate /
body.translated_text: What is the realization of non-engagement (<s>asamudācārābhisamaya</s>)? Through obtaining the restraint without [specific] cause, one who has entered the training [recognizes]: 'For me, the [rebirth in] the hells is exhausted, the animal realm is exhausted, the realm of hungry ghosts is exhausted, the downfall into unfortunate destinies is exhausted.' One no longer produces, on the basis of clinging, the <s>karma</s> leading to unfortunate destinies nor the ripening in unfortunate destinies.

body.text: niṣṭhābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / yathā mārgasatye niṣṭhāmārga uktaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the realization of culmination (<s>niṣṭhābhisamaya</s>)? It is as the path of culmination was described under the truth of the path.

body.text: śrāvakābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / pūrvoktaḥ saptavidho 'bhisamayaḥ / śrāvakāṇāṃ parato ghoṣamāgamya pratilambhataḥ śrāvakābhisamaya ityucyate //
body.translated_text: What is the realization of the <s>śrāvaka</s> (<s>śrāvakābhisamaya</s>)? It is the sevenfold realization previously described. Because <s>śrāvakas</s> attain it by relying on the voice of another, it is called the realization of the <s>śrāvaka</s>.

body.text: pratyekabuddhābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / pūrvoktāḥ saptābhisamayāḥ / parato ghoṣamanāgamya pratilambhataḥ pratyekabuddhābhisamaya ityucyate //
body.translated_text: What is the realization of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (<s>pratyekabuddhābhisamaya</s>)? It is the seven realizations previously described. Because it is attained without relying on the voice of another, it is called the realization of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>.

body.text: bodhisattvābhisamayaḥ katamaḥ / pūrvokteṣu saptābhisamayeṣu yā samudāgamakṣāntiḥ no tu sakṣātkiryā / kevalaṃ bodhisattva pramuditābhūmau bodhisattvasya samyaktvaniyāmāvakrāntiḥ / sā bodhisattvābhisamayo veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the realization of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>bodhisattvābhisamaya</s>)? Among the seven realizations previously described, it is the patient acceptance of accomplishment (<s>samudāgamakṣānti</s>) but not direct realization. It is solely the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s entry into the certainty of correctness (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>) on the Joyful Ground (<s>pramuditābhūmi</s>). This should be understood as the realization of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: śrāvakābhisamayāt bodhisattvābhisamayasya ko viśeṣaḥ / saṃkṣepata ekādaśa / ālambanaviśeṣaḥ upastambhaviśeṣaḥ prativedhaviśeṣaḥ abhyupagamaviśeṣaḥ niryāṇaviśeṣaḥ parigrahaviśeṣaḥ vyavasthānaviśeṣaḥ pratiṣṭhāparivāraviśeṣaḥ abhijanmaviśeṣaḥ janmaviśeṣaḥ phalaviśeṣaśca / phalaviśeṣaḥ punardaśavidhaḥ / āśrayaparivṛttiviśeṣataḥ guṇasamṛddhiviśeṣataḥ pañcākāraviśeṣataḥ trikāyaviśeṣataḥ nirvāṇaviśeṣataḥ miśropamiśrajñānaśaktilābhaviśeṣataḥ āvaraṇaviśuddhiviśeṣataḥ miśropamiśrakarmakriyāviśeṣataḥ abhisaṃbodhinirvāṇasandarśanopāyaviśeṣataḥ pañcākāraparitrāṇaviśeṣataśca veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the distinction of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s realization from the <s>śrāvaka</s>'s realization? In brief, there are eleven [distinctions]: distinction of object (<s>ālambana</s>), distinction of support (<s>upastambha</s>), distinction of penetration (<s>prativedha</s>), distinction of acceptance (<s>abhyupagama</s>), distinction of emergence (<s>niryāṇa</s>), distinction of embracing (<s>parigraha</s>), distinction of classification (<s>vyavasthāna</s>), distinction of attendant retinue of the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhāparivāra</s>), distinction of noble birth (<s>abhijanma</s>), distinction of birth (<s>janma</s>), and distinction of fruit (<s>phala</s>). The distinction of fruit is further tenfold, and should be understood from: the distinction of the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>), the distinction of the fullness of qualities, the distinction of five aspects, the distinction of the three bodies (<s>trikāya</s>), the distinction of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the distinction of obtaining the power of mixed and unmixed knowledge, the distinction of purification from obstructions, the distinction of mixed and unmixed activity of <s>karma</s>, the distinction of the means of manifesting awakening and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and the distinction of protection through five aspects.

body.text: apramāṇādivaiśeṣikaguṇānāṃ katamairabhisamayaiḥ saṃgrahaḥ / pṛṣṭhābhisamayaniṣṭhābhisamayābhyāṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ // teṣāṃ saṃgrahaḥ punaḥ katamaḥ / apramāṇāni vimokṣāḥ abhibhvāyatanāni kṛtsāyatanāni araṇāpraṇīdhijñānam pratisaṃvidaḥ abhijñā lakṣaṇānuvyañjanāni pariśuddhayaḥ valāni vaiśāradyāni smṛtyupasthānāni arakṣāṇi asaṃpramoṣadharmatā vāsanāsamuddhātaḥ mahākaruṇā āveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ sarvākārajñatā ityevamādayo guṇā yathā sūtrāntareṣu nirdiṣṭāḥ //
body.translated_text: Through which realizations are the special qualities such as the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) and so forth subsumed? They should be understood as subsumed under the subsequent realization (<s>pṛṣṭhābhisamaya</s>) and the realization of culmination (<s>niṣṭhābhisamaya</s>). What are those [special qualities] that are subsumed? The immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), the totality bases (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>), the knowledge of conflict-free [meditation] and aspiration (<s>araṇāpraṇidhijñāna</s>), the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the marks and minor marks (<s>lakṣaṇānuvyañjana</s>), the purifications (<s>pariśuddhi</s>), the powers (<s>bala</s>), the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the protections (<s>arakṣā</s>), the quality of non-forgetfulness (<s>asaṃpramoṣadharmatā</s>), the eradication of latent tendencies (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the exclusive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>), and omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) — such qualities and others as taught in the various <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: apramāṇāni katamāni / catvāri apramāṇāni / maitrī katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya sattvāḥ sukhena saṃprayujyeranniti vihārasamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ // karuṇā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya sattvā duḥkhena viyujyeranniti vihārasamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // muditā katamā / (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 95]

children.text: ) dhyānaṃ niśritya sattvāḥ sukhena na viyujyeranniti vihārasamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // upekṣā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya sattvā hita labheranniti vihārasamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
children.translated_text: What is sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, [wishing that] 'May beings not be separated from happiness' — the concentration, the wisdom, and the rest as before. What is equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, [wishing that] 'May beings obtain benefit' — the concentration, the wisdom, and the rest as before.

body.translated_text: What are the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>)? There are four immeasurables. What is loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, [wishing that] 'May beings be united with happiness' — the concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), and the mental and mental-associated <s>dharmas</s> connected therewith, in the accomplishment of that abiding. What is compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, [wishing that] 'May beings be separated from suffering' — the concentration, the wisdom, and the rest as before.

body.text: vimokṣāḥ katame / aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ / kathaṃ rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatīti / dhyānaṃ niśritya adhyātmaṃ draṣṭari rūpasaṃjñāyā avibhāvānād draṣṭarī rūpasaṃjñāyāḥ saṃniveśanād vā dṛśya rūpādi paśyatīti vihārasamṛddho samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ yāvad nirmāṇāvaraṇād vimuktiḥ // kathamadhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī vahirddhā rūpāṇi paśyati / dhyānaṃ niśritya draṣṭari rūpasaṃjñāyā vibhāvanād arūpasaṃjñāyāḥ saṃniveśanādvā dṛśya rūpāṇi paśyatīti vihārasamṛddhau samādhi prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // kathaṃ śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtyopasaṃpadya viharatīti / dhyānaṃ niśritya adhyātmaṃ śubhāśubheṣu rūpeṣu anyonyāpekṣāsaṃjñāyā anyonyānugamasaṃjñāyā anyonyaikarasasaṃjñāyāśca labhāt tatra labdhe vihārasamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat yāvat śubhaśubhanirmāṇāt saṃkleśotpattyāvaraṇācca vimuktiḥ // ākāśānantyāyatanavimokṣaḥ katamaḥ / vimokṣānukūlā kāśānantyāyatanavimokṣaḥ tathā vijñānānantyāyatanākiṃcanyāyatananaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanavimokṣā api draṣṭavyaḥ yāvat vimokṣaḥ śānto vimokṣaḥ asaktyāvaraṇaṃ ca // saṃjñāvedayitanirodhavimokṣaḥ katamaḥ / naivasaṃjñānasaṃjñāyatanavimokṣaṃ niśritya samatikrāntānāṃ śiṣṭe śānte vimokṣe mokṣānusadṛśo vihāraḥ vihārasamṛddhau ca cittacaitasikānāṃ nirodhaḥ saṃjñāvedayitanirodhāvaraṇād vimuktyartham //
body.translated_text: What are the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>)? There are eight liberations. How does 'one with form see forms'? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, because the perception of form (<s>rūpasaṃjñā</s>) has not been removed internally from the perceiver, or because the perception of form has been established in the perceiver, [one] sees external forms and so forth — the concentration, the wisdom, and the mental and mental-associated <s>dharmas</s> connected therewith, in the accomplishment of that abiding, up to liberation from the obstruction of manifestation. How does 'one who internally has no perception of form see forms externally'? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, because the perception of form has been removed from the perceiver, or because the perception of formlessness has been established, [one] sees external forms — the concentration, the wisdom, and the rest as before. How does one 'having realized the beautiful liberation, dwell having directly witnessed it with the body'? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, through attaining the perception of mutual dependence, the perception of mutual following, and the perception of mutual single-taste regarding internally beautiful and ugly forms — the concentration, the wisdom, and the rest as before in the accomplishment of that attained abiding, up to liberation from the obstruction of affliction's arising through the manifestation of beautiful and ugly [forms]. What is the liberation of the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>)? It is the liberation conforming to liberation at the sphere of infinite space. Likewise the liberations of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception should also be viewed — up to liberation that is peaceful liberation and [freedom from] the obstruction of attachment. What is the liberation of the cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāvedayitanirodha</s>)? Based on the liberation of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, having transcended it, in the remaining peaceful liberation, it is an abiding similar to liberation; in the accomplishment of that abiding, it is the cessation of mental and mental-associated [<s>dharmas</s>], for the purpose of liberation from the obstruction of the cessation of perception and feeling.

body.text: abhibhvāyatanāni katamāni / aṣṭāvabhibhvāyatanāni / pūrvāṇī catvāri abhibhvāyatanāni dvābhyāṃ vimokṣābhyāṃ vyavasthāpyante / uttarāṇi catvāri abhibhvāvatanāni ekena vimokṣeṇa vyavasthāpyante / tatra vimokṣairālambanamadhimucyate abhibhvāyataneṣu ālambanaprabhibhavati / vaśavarttanatā mupādāya // sattvasaṃkhyātāni asattvasaṃkhyātāni cāśritya rūpāṇi parittādhimātrāṇyucyante / śubhāśubhānyāśritya rūpāṇi suvarṇadurvarṇānyucyante / mānuṣyakadivyānyāśritya rūpāṇi hīnapraṇītānyucyante // śiṣṭāni yathā vimokṣeṣūktāni // ālambanābhibhavanatāmupādāya abhibhvāyatanānītyucyante //
body.translated_text: What are the bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>)? There are eight bases of mastery. The first four bases of mastery are established through two liberations. The latter four bases of mastery are established through one liberation. Among those, through the liberations one resolves upon the object, and in the bases of mastery one masters the object — by virtue of exercising control. Forms are called 'limited and extensive' with reference to those counted as sentient and those counted as non-sentient. Forms are called 'well-colored and ill-colored' with reference to beautiful and ugly. Forms are called 'inferior and superior' with reference to human and divine. The rest is as stated under the liberations. They are called bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>) by virtue of mastering the object.

body.text: kṛtsnāyatanāni katamāni / daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni / kṛtsnaspharaṇālambanatāmupādāya kṛtsnāyatanānītyucyate / kṛtsnaspharaṇavihārasamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ kṛtsnāyatanānītyucyante // kimupādāya kṛtsnāyataneṣu pṛthivyādivyavasthāpanam / taiḥ kṛtsnāyatanaiḥ āśrayāśritarūpāṇi paśyatīti kṛtsnaspharaṇatāmupadaya / śiṣṭāni yathāyogaṃ vimokṣavat // tathā ca kṛtsnāyatanaiḥ pariniṣpattirvimokṣāṇām //
body.translated_text: What are the totality bases (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>)? There are ten totality bases. They are called totality bases in reference to having an object that pervades entirely. The <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and the associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> that accomplish dwelling in total pervasion are called totality bases. In reference to what are earth and the others established among the totality bases? Through those totality bases, one sees the forms that are basis and dependent — in reference to total pervasion. The rest should be understood according to suitability, as with the liberations. And thus, through the totality bases, the liberations are perfected.

body.text: araṇā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya kleśotpattyanurakṣāvihārasamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: What is <s>araṇā</s> (non-contention)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), it is the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, and associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> that accomplish dwelling in the guarding against the arising of afflictions.

body.text: praṇidhijñānaṃ katamat / dhyānaṃ niśritya jñeya jñānapraṇidhisamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What is <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (knowledge of aspiration)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the aspiration for knowledge of the knowable. The remainder is as before.

body.text: pratisaṃvidaḥ katamāḥ / catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ / dharmapratisaṃvid katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya sarvadharma paryāyeṣu avyāghātasamṛddhau samādhīḥ prajñāśeṣaṃ pūrvavat // arthapratisaṃvid katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya lakṣaṇe abhiprāye (

children.translated_text: <s>Abhidh-s</s> 97

children.text: ) cāvyāghātasamṛddau samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // niruktipratisaṃvid katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya janapadabhāpāyāmanuvyavahāre dharmanirvacane ca avyāghāta samṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // pratibhānapratisaṃvid katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya dharmaprabhedeṣu avyāghātasamṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
children.translated_text: The remainder is as before. What is <s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of etymology)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish unimpeded mastery regarding discourse in regional languages and the definition of <s>dharmas</s>. The remainder is as before. What is <s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of eloquence)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish unimpeded mastery regarding the distinctions of <s>dharmas</s>. The remainder is as before.

body.translated_text: What are the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges)? There are four analytical knowledges. What is <s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of teachings)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish unimpeded mastery regarding all categories of <s>dharmas</s>. The remainder is as before. What is <s>arthapratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of meaning)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish unimpeded mastery regarding characteristics and intentions.

body.text: abhijñā katamāḥ / ṣaḍabhijñāḥ / ṛddhyabhijñā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya vicitrarddhivikurvita samṛddhau samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ // divyaśrotrābhijñā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya vicitrāṇāṃ śabdānāmanuśravasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // cetaḥparyāyābhijñā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya parasattveṣu cittacaritaparyāya praveśasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhi prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // pūrvanivāsānusmṛtyabhijñā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya pūrvāntacaryānusmaraṇasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // cyutyupapādābhijñā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya sattvānāṃ cyutyupapādaprakāra saṃdarśanasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // āsravakṣayābhijñā katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya āsravakṣayajñānasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: What are the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges)? There are six superknowledges. What is the superknowledge of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhyabhijñā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, and associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> that accomplish various miraculous transformations. What is the superknowledge of the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotrābhijñā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the hearing of various sounds. The remainder is as before. What is the superknowledge of reading others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāyābhijñā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish penetration into the mental dispositions of other beings. The remainder is as before. What is the superknowledge of recollection of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛtyabhijñā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the recollection of past conduct. The remainder is as before. What is the superknowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings (<s>cyutyupapādābhijñā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the display of the various modes of passing away and rebirth of beings. The remainder is as before. What is the superknowledge of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣayābhijñā</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, and associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> that accomplish the knowledge of the destruction of outflows.

body.text: lakṣaṇānuvyañjanāni katamāni / dhyānaṃ niśritya lakṣaṇānuvyañjanairvibhrājamānasandarśanasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayūktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ tatsamutthitavipākāśca //
body.translated_text: What are the marks and minor marks (<s>lakṣaṇānuvyañjana</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, they are the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s>, and their resultant fruitions that accomplish the display of radiance through the marks and minor marks.

body.text: pariśuddhayaḥ katamāḥ / catasraḥ pariśuddhayaḥ / āśrayapariśuddhiḥ katamāḥ / dhyānaṃ niśritya yathākāmamaśrayasyopādāne sthānaparityāgānāṃ samṛddhau yaḥ samādhīḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ // ālambanapariśuddhiḥ katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya yathākāmamālambananirmāṇapariṇāmanajñānānāṃ samṛddhau yaḥ samādhi prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // cittapariśuddhiḥ katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya yathākāmaṃ samādhimukhavaśavarttisamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // jñānapariśuddhiḥ katamā / dhyānaṃ niśritya yathākāmaṃ dhāraṇīmukhasandhāraṇasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What are the purities (<s>pariśuddhi</s>)? There are four purities. What is the purity of the basis (<s>āśrayapariśuddhi</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, and associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> that accomplish the taking up, maintaining, and relinquishing of the basis at will. What is the purity of the object (<s>ālambanapariśuddhi</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the creation, transformation, and knowledge of objects at will. The remainder is as before. What is the purity of mind (<s>cittapariśuddhi</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish mastery over the various gates of <s>samādhi</s> at will. The remainder is as before. What is the purity of knowledge (<s>jñānapariśuddhi</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the retention through the various gates of <s>dhāraṇī</s> at will. The remainder is as before.

body.text: balāni katamāni / baśa tathāgatabalāni / sthānāsthānabalaṃ katamat dhyānaṃ niśritya sarvaprakāra sthānāsthānajñānasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ // karmasvakajñānabalaṃ katamat / dhyānaṃ niśritya sarvaprakāra karmasvakajñānasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // śiṣṭāni balāni yathāyogaṃ veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: What are the powers (<s>bala</s>)? There are ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers. What is the power of knowing what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānabala</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, and associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> that accomplish the knowledge of what is possible and impossible in all its aspects. What is the power of knowing the results of one's own karma (<s>karmasvakajñānabala</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the knowledge of the results of one's own karma in all its aspects. The remainder is as before. The remaining powers should be understood according to suitability.

body.text: vaiśāradyāni katamāni / catvāri vaiśāradyāni // abhisaṃbodhivaiśāradyaṃ katamat / dhyānaṃ niśritya svārthamevārabhya sarvākārajñeyābhisaṃbodhipratijñāpratiṣṭhāpanasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ // āsravakṣayavaiśāradyaṃ katamat / dhyānaṃ niśritya svārthamevārabhya sarvākārasravakṣayapratijñā pratiṣṭhāpanasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // antarāyikadharmavaiśāradyaṃ katamat / dhyānaṃ niśritya parārthamārabhya sarvākārāntarāyikadharmapratijñāpratiṣṭhāpanasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat // nairyāṇikapratipadavaiśāradyaṃ katamat / dhyānaṃ niśritya parārthamārabhya sarvākāra nairyāṇikamārgadharma pratijñāpratiṣṭhāpanasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What are the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>)? There are four fearlessnesses. What is the fearlessness of perfect awakening (<s>abhisaṃbodhivaiśāradya</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, concerning one's own benefit, it is the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, and associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> that accomplish the establishment of the claim to awakening regarding all knowable things in all their aspects. What is the fearlessness of the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayavaiśāradya</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, concerning one's own benefit, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the establishment of the claim to the destruction of all outflows in all their aspects. The remainder is as before. What is the fearlessness regarding obstructive <s>dharmas</s> (<s>antarāyikadharmavaiśāradya</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, concerning the benefit of others, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the establishment of the claim regarding all obstructive <s>dharmas</s> in all their aspects. The remainder is as before. What is the fearlessness regarding the path leading to deliverance (<s>nairyāṇikapratipadavaiśāradya</s>)? Based on <s>dhyāna</s>, concerning the benefit of others, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the establishment of the claim regarding the <s>dharmas</s> of the path leading to deliverance in all their aspects. The remainder is as before.

body.text: smṛtyupasthānāni katamāni / trīṇyeva smṛtyupasthānāni / gaṇaparikarṣaṇe sarvākārasaṃkleśāsamudācārasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ purvavat //
body.translated_text: What are the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)? There are just three foundations of mindfulness. In guiding an assembly, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the non-occurrence of all forms of affliction in all their aspects. The remainder is as before.

body.text: arakṣāṇi katamāni / trīṇyeravārakṣāṇi // gaṇaparikarṣaṇe yathākāmamavavādānuśāsanīprayogasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What are the unguarded qualities (<s>arakṣāṇi</s>)? There are just three unguarded qualities. In guiding an assembly, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the application of instruction and admonition at will. The remainder is as before.

body.text: asaṃpramoṣadharmatā katamā / sarvākārasya yathāvat kṛtassa bhāṣitasya cābhilapanasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What is the nature of non-forgetfulness (<s>asaṃpramoṣadharmatā</s>)? It is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the utterance of everything done and spoken in all its aspects as it truly is. The remainder is as before.

body.text: vāsanāsamudghātaḥ katamaḥ / sarvajñasya sataḥ asarvajñaceṣṭitāsamudācārasamṛddau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What is the eradication of latent impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>)? For one who is omniscient, it is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the non-occurrence of conduct unbecoming of an omniscient one. The remainder is as before.

body.text: mahākaruṇā katamā / nirantaraṃ sarvaprakāraduḥkhālambanakaruṇāvihārasamṛddau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What is great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>)? It is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the uninterrupted dwelling in compassion having all forms of suffering as its object. The remainder is as before.

body.text: āveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ katame / aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ // asādhāraṇa kāyavāṅganaskarthapariśuddhi samṛddau sāśrayāṇāṃ saphalānāṃ tathāgatendriyāṇamaprāptyāmaparihāṇisamṛddhau asādhāraṇa karmasamudācārasamṛddhau asādhāraṇajñānavihārasamṛddhau ca yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā śeṣaṃ pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: What are the exclusive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>)? There are eighteen exclusive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. It is the <s>samādhi</s> and <s>prajñā</s> that accomplish the exclusive purity of activities of body, speech, and mind, the non-loss and non-decline of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s faculties which have a basis and bear fruit, the exclusive conduct of action, and the exclusive dwelling in knowledge. The remainder is as before.

body.text: sarvākārajñatā katamā / skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ sarvākārajñatāsamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā tatsaṃprayuktāśca cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>)? It is the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, and associated mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> that accomplish the knowledge of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases in all their aspects.

body.text: eteṣāṃ guṇānamabhinirhāraḥ katamaḥ / viśuddhāni catvāri dhyānāni niśritya anyatīrthīyaḥ śrāvako bodhisattvo vā abhinirharati catvāri apramāṇānyevaṃ pañcābhijñāḥ / śeṣān guṇān prāntakoṭikaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya śrāvako bodhisattvastathāgato vābhinirharati // tatpunaḥ kimupādāya / dhyānasanniśrayeṇa yathāvyavasthānamanasikāravahulīkāratāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: What is the production of these qualities? Based on the four purified <s>dhyānas</s>, a non-Buddhist, a <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer), or a <s>bodhisattva</s> produces the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) and the five superknowledges. The remaining qualities are produced by a <s>śrāvaka</s>, <s>bodhisattva</s>, or <s>Tathāgata</s> based on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> at the ultimate limit. Furthermore, in reference to what? In reference to the prevalence of mental engagement according to the proper order, dependent on <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: ta ete guṇā dvividhāḥ / svakāritrapratyupasthānāśca vaihārikāśca // ye svakāritrapratyupasthānāḥ te lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhāḥ saṃvṛtijñānasvabhāvā draṣṭavyāḥ // ye punarvaihārikāste lokottarajñānasvabhāvā draṣṭavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: These qualities are of two kinds: those that arise for the accomplishment of one's own task, and those that are operative. Those that arise for the accomplishment of one's own task should be viewed as having the nature of conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>) obtained subsequent to the supramundane. Those that are operative should be viewed as having the nature of supramundane knowledge (<s>lokottarajñāna</s>).

body.text: apramāṇaiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / vipakṣaṃ jahāti / anukampāvihāritayā puṇya saṃbhāraṃ paripūrayati sattvaparipāke ca na parikhidyate // vimokṣaiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / nirmāṇakarmābhinirharati / śubhanirmāṇe na saṃkliśyate śānteṣu vimokṣeṣu na sajjati / paramapraśāntena cāryavihāreṇa viharati / adhimucyanatā mupādāya // abhibhvāyatanaiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / trayāṇāṃ vimokṣāṇāmālambanaṃ vaśe varttayatyālambanābhibhavanatāmupādāya // kṛtsnāyatanaiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / vimokṣālambanaṃ pariniṣpādayati kṛtsnaspharaṇatāmupādāya // araṇayā kiṃ karma karoti / ādeyavacano bhavati // praṇidhijñānena kiṃ karma karoti / bhūtabhavyavarttamānaṃ vyākaroti bahumataśca bhavati lokasya // pratisaṃvidbhiḥ kiṃ karma (

children.text: ) karoti / deśanayā sattvacittāni saṃtoṣayati // abhijñābhiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / śāsane kāyakarmaṇā āvarjayati / vākkarmaṇā cittādeśanayāvarjayati sattvacaritaṃ ca jñātvā āgatiṃ ca gatiṃ ca niḥsaraṇe sattvān yathāvadavavadate // lakṣaṇānuvyañjanaiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / darśanamātrakeṇa mahāpuruṣatve saṃpratyayaṃ janayati cittānyabhiprasādayati // pariśuddhibhiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / saṃcintya bhavopapattiṃ parigṛṇhāti / ākāṅkṣayankalpaṃ vā kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā tiṣṭhati āyuḥsaṃskārān vā utsṛjati / dharmavaśavarttī bhavati samādhivaśavartī saddharmaṃ ca sandhārayati // balaiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / ahetuviṣamahetuvādaṃ pratyākhāyākṛtābhyāgamavāde ca samyaga bhyudayamārgaṃ deśayati sattvacittacaritāni cānupraviśya deśanābhājanatāṃ cāśayaṃ cānuśayaṃ cālambanaṃ ca saṃbhāraṃ ca bhavyatāṃ ca niḥsaraṇaṃ ca yathāvanniḥśreyasamārgaṃ deśayati / sarvamārāṃśca nigṛṇhāti sarvatra ca praśnaṃ pṛcchati pṛṣṭo vyākaroti // vaiśāradyaiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / parṣadi samyagātmanaḥ śāstṛtvaṃ vyavasthāpahati codakāṃścānyatīrthyānnigṛṇhāti // smṛtyupasthānaiḥ kiṃ karma gaṇamavavadate samanuśāsti // asaṃmoṣadharmatayā kiṃ karma karoti / buddhakṛtyaṃ na hāpayati // vāsanāsamudghātena kiṃ karma karoti / niḥkleśaḥ kleśapratirūpāṃ ceṣṭānna(da)rśayati // mahākaruṇayā kiṃ karma karoti / ṣaṭkṛtvo rātriṃdivasena lokaṃ vyavalokayati // āveṇikairbuddhadharmaiḥ kiṃ karma karoti / sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhān kāyavāṅmanaskarmapariśuddhyā prāptyā cāreṇa vihāreṇa vābhibhavati // (
children.translated_text: Through teaching, one delights the minds of beings. What function does one perform with the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>)? In the teaching, one attracts through bodily action; one attracts through verbal action and through reading minds; and knowing the conduct of beings, their coming and going, one properly instructs beings in liberation. What function does one perform with the marks and minor characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇānuvyañjana</s>)? By mere sight, one generates confidence in one's being a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣa</s>) and inspires faith in minds. What function does one perform with the purifications (<s>pariśuddhi</s>)? One intentionally takes on rebirth in existence; as one wishes, one remains for an eon or the remainder of an eon, or one relinquishes the life-formations (<s>āyuḥsaṃskāra</s>); one comes under the power of <s>Dharma</s>, under the power of <s>samādhi</s>, and upholds the true <s>Dharma</s>. What function does one perform with the powers (<s>bala</s>)? Having refuted the doctrines of no cause and wrong cause, one properly teaches the path of good destiny in the doctrine of actions not going to waste; and entering into the mental conduct of beings, one teaches the path to the highest good as it truly is, knowing their receptivity to teaching, their disposition, latent tendencies, objects, accumulations, potential, and means of liberation; one subdues all <s>Māras</s> and asks questions everywhere and answers when asked. What function does one perform with the confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>)? In the assembly, one properly establishes oneself as teacher and subdues objecting sectarians. What function does one perform with the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)? One instructs and admonishes the assembly. What function does one perform with the quality of not losing (<s>asaṃmoṣadharmatā</s>)? One does not neglect the Buddha-activity. What function does one perform with the eradication of latent impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>)? Though free from afflictions, one displays behaviors resembling afflictions. What function does one perform with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>)? Six times day and night, one surveys the world. What function does one perform with the unique qualities of a Buddha (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>)? One surpasses all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> through the purity of bodily, verbal, and mental action, through attainment, conduct, and abiding.
[<s>Abhidh-s</s> 101]

children.text: ) sarvākārajñatayā kiṃ karma karoti / sarvasattvānāṃ sarvasaṃśayāṃ śchinatti dharmanetrīñca dīrghakālamavasthāpayati yena paripakṣā (? kṣyāḥ) sattvāḥ paripacyante paripakāśca vimucyante // eṣvabhisamayeṣūttarottaraṃ viśiṣṭaṃ mārgaṃ labhamānaḥ pūrvakaṃ hīnaṃ mārgaṃ vijahāti saṃkalanaprahāṇaṃ ca sākṣātkaroti / nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau śrāvakaḥ sarvammārgasamavasargavihānyā vijahāti no tu bodhisattvaḥ // ataeva bodhisattvā akṣayakuśalamūlā akṣa(ya)guṇā ityucyante //
children.translated_text: What function does one perform with omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>)? One cuts through all doubts of all beings, and establishes the lamp of <s>Dharma</s> for a long time, so that beings ready to be matured are matured, and those matured are liberated. In these realizations, obtaining ever more distinguished paths, one abandons the earlier, inferior path and directly realizes the abandonment through integration. In the <s>nirvāṇa</s> realm without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>), the <s>Śrāvaka</s> abandons the abiding in association with all paths, but not so the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. For this very reason, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are said to have inexhaustible roots of wholesome [conduct] and inexhaustible qualities.

body.translated_text: What function does one perform with the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>)? One abandons their opposites; through abiding in compassion, one fulfills the accumulation of merit (<s>puṇyasaṃbhāra</s>) and does not become weary in maturing beings. What function does one perform with the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>)? One carries out the work of magical creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>); one is not defiled in pure creation, one does not become attached to the peaceful liberations, and one abides in the supremely peaceful noble abiding, based on one's conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>). What function does one perform with the bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>)? One brings the objects of the three liberations under control, based on mastery over objects. What function does one perform with the totality bases (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>)? One perfects the objects of liberation, based on pervading everything. What function does one perform with the non-conflict (<s>araṇā</s>)? One's words become worthy of acceptance. What function does one perform with the knowledge of aspiration (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>)? One elucidates past, future, and present, and becomes honored by the world. What function does one perform with the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>)?

body.text: yānyavyākṛtavastūni vyavasthāpitāni kimupādāya / ayoniśaḥparipraśna tāmupādāya // (ayoniśaḥ paripraśnatā kimupādāya /) hetuphalasaṃkleśavyavadānacintāpasrivarjanatāmupādāya // 0 //
body.translated_text: On what basis were the indeterminate matters (<s>avyākṛtavastu</s>) established? Based on unskilful questioning. And what is unskilful questioning based on? Based on avoiding reflection on cause, effect, defilement, and purification.

body.text: kena kāraṇena bodhisattvo bodhimanava vadyāmavakrāntaḥ strotāpanno na bhavati / strotaḥpratipattyapariniṣpannatāmupādāya // kena kāraṇena sakṛdāgāmī na bhavati / apramāṇasaṃcintya bhavopaprattiparigrahatāmupādāya // kena kāraṇenānāgāmī na bhavati / dhyānairvihṛtya kāmadhātāvupapadyānatāmupādāya / bodhisattvaḥ satyānyabhi samayena labdhvā daśasu mūmiṣu bhāvanāmārgeṇa jñeyāvaraṇapratipakṣamārgaṃ bhāvayati na kleśāvaraṇapratipakṣamārgam // tathā ca bodhiprāptaḥ kleśāvaraṇaṃ jñeyāvaraṇaṃ ca vijahāti arhan tathāgataśca saṃpadyate // sa ca bodhisattvaḥ sarvakleśāprahāṇāt mantroṣadhayo viṣamiva sarvakleśān abhibhavati sarvān kleśān doṣāṃśca notpādayati sarvāsu bhūmiṣu arhanniva kleśān prajahāti /
body.translated_text: For what reason does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has irreversibly entered upon awakening not become a stream-enterer (<s>strotāpanna</s>)? Because the practice of the stream has not been fully accomplished. For what reason does one not become a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>)? Because one takes on immeasurable and inconceivable rebirths in existence. For what reason does one not become a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>)? Because having dwelt in the <s>dhyānas</s>, one is reborn in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). A <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having obtained the truths through realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>), cultivates the path that counteracts the cognitive obscuration (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) through the path of meditation on the ten stages (<s>bhūmi</s>), not the path that counteracts the afflictive obscuration (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>). And thus, having attained awakening, one abandons both the afflictive obscuration and the cognitive obscuration, and becomes an <s>Arhat</s> and a <s>Tathāgata</s>. And that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, without having abandoned all afflictions, overpowers all afflictions like mantras and medicines overpower poison, does not produce the faults of any afflictions, and on all stages abandons afflictions like an <s>Arhat</s>.

body.text: api khalu bodhisattvo jñeyeṣu bhāvanākuśalo bhavati upāyeṣu bhāvanākuśalo bhavati abhūtaparikalpeṣu bhāvanākuśalo bhavati nirvikalpeṣu bhāvanākuśalo bhavati tena kālena kālamindriyāṇyuttāpayati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes skilled in meditation regarding the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>), skilled in meditation regarding skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), skilled in meditation regarding unreal conceptualizations (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>), and skilled in meditation regarding the non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>). In that way, from time to time, one sharpens the faculties (<s>indriya</s>).

body.text: jñeyaṃ katamat / saṃkṣepeṇa ṣaḍvidham / bhrāntiḥ bhrāntyāśrayaḥ abhrāntyāśrayaḥ bhrāntyabhrāntiḥ abhrāntiḥ abhrāntiniṣyandaśca // upāyakauśalyaṃ katamat / saṃkṣeparāścaturvidham / (
