children.text: ) sattvaparipākakauśalyaṃ buddhadharmaparipuraṇakauśalyaṃ kṣiprābhijñākauśalyaṃ mārgānupacchedakauśalyaṃ ca // abhūtaparikalpaḥ katamaḥ / saṃkṣepato daśavidhaḥ / mūlavikalpaḥ nimittivikalpaḥ nimittapratibhāsavikalpaḥ nimittavikāravikalpaḥ nimittipratibhāsavikāravikalpaḥ paropanītavikalpaḥ ayoniśovikalpaḥ yoniśovikalpaḥ abhiniveśavikalpaḥ vikṣepavikalpaśca // sa punaḥ daśavidhaḥ / abhāvavikalpa bhāvavikalpaḥ samāropavikalpaḥ apavādavikalpaḥ ekatvavi kalpaḥ pṛthaktvavikalpaḥ svabhāvavikalpaḥ viśeṣavikalpaḥ yathānāmārthavikalpaḥ yathārthanāmavikalpaśca // nirvikalpatā katamā / samāsatastrividhā / santuṣṭinirvikalpatā aviparyāsanirghikalpatā niṣprapañcanirvikalpatā ca // tā imāstitraḥ pṛthagjanaśrāvakabodhisattvānāṃ yathākramaṃ veditavyāḥ // yāsau nimittato niṣprapañcanirvikalpatā tasyāḥ punaḥ abhāvasya pañca nimittāni / na amanasikārataḥ na manasikārasamatikramataḥ na vyupaśamataḥ na svabhāvataḥ na ālambane 'bhisaṃskārataśca / api khalu ālaṃbane 'nabhisaṃskārataḥ / bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyā tīkṣṇendriyaḥ kathaṃ punaḥ indriyāpyuttāpayatīti / tīkṣṇamṛdvindriyamāśritya tīkṣṇamadhyendriyamabhinirharati / punaḥ tīkṣṇamadhyendriyamāśritya tīkṣṇatīkṣṇendriyamabhinirharati //
children.translated_text: skill in maturing beings (<s>sattvaparipākakauśalya</s>), skill in fulfilling the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhadharmaparipūraṇakauśalya</s>), skill in swift superknowledge (<s>kṣiprābhijñākauśalya</s>), and skill in not interrupting the path (<s>mārgānupacchedakauśalya</s>). What is unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>)? In brief, it is tenfold: root conceptualization (<s>mūlavikalpa</s>), conceptualization with signs (<s>nimittivikalpa</s>), conceptualization of the appearance of signs, conceptualization of the transformation of signs, conceptualization of the transformation of appearance of signs, conceptualization introduced by others, unskilful conceptualization, skilful conceptualization, conceptualization of clinging (<s>abhiniveśavikalpa</s>), and conceptualization of distraction (<s>vikṣepavikalpa</s>). And again it is tenfold: conceptualization of non-existence, conceptualization of existence, conceptualization of superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>), conceptualization of denial (<s>apavāda</s>), conceptualization of unity, conceptualization of diversity, conceptualization of inherent nature, conceptualization of distinction, conceptualization of the meaning according to the name, and conceptualization of the name according to the meaning. What is non-conceptuality (<s>nirvikalpatā</s>)? In brief, it is threefold: non-conceptuality of contentment (<s>santuṣṭinirvikalpatā</s>), non-conceptuality of non-error (<s>aviparyāsanirvikalpatā</s>), and non-conceptuality free from elaboration (<s>niṣprapañcanirvikalpatā</s>). These three should be understood as belonging to ordinary beings, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> respectively. Regarding the non-conceptuality free from elaboration with respect to signs — its non-existence has five characteristics: not from non-attention, not from transcending attention, not from quiescence, not from inherent nature, and not from fabrication regarding the object. Rather, it is from non-fabrication regarding the object. Since a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is by nature one of sharp faculties, how does one further sharpen the faculties? Relying on mildly sharp faculties, one develops moderately sharp faculties; then relying on moderately sharp faculties, one develops supremely sharp faculties.

body.translated_text: What is the knowable? In brief, it is sixfold: error (<s>bhrānti</s>), the basis of error (<s>bhrāntyāśraya</s>), the basis of non-error (<s>abhrāntyāśraya</s>), error and non-error (<s>bhrāntyabhrānti</s>), non-error (<s>abhrānti</s>), and the outflow of non-error (<s>abhrāntiniṣyanda</s>). What is skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>)? In brief, it is fourfold:

body.text: (iti abhidharmasamuccaye prāptiviniścayo nāma caturthaḥ samuccayaḥ //) //
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Abhidharmasamuccaya</s>, the fourth collection, called the ascertainment of attainment (<s>prāptiviniścaya</s>).)

body.text: (atha mahāyānabhidharmasamuccayaśāstre viniścayabhāge sāṃkathyaparicchedaścaturthaḥ)
body.translated_text: (Now, in the <s>Mahāyānābhidharmasamuccaya</s> treatise, in the Ascertainment section, the fourth chapter on Discussion (<s>sāṃkathyapariccheda</s>).)

body.text: sāṃkathyaviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / saṃkṣepataḥ saptavidhaḥ / arthaviniścayaḥ vyākhyāviniścayaḥ prabhidyasaṃdarśanaviniścayaḥ saṃpraśnaviniścayaḥ saṃgrahaviniścayaḥ vādaviniścayaḥ abhisandhiviniścayaśca //
body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of discussion (<s>sāṃkathyaviniścaya</s>)? In brief, it is sevenfold: ascertainment of meaning (<s>arthaviniścaya</s>), ascertainment of exposition (<s>vyākhyāviniścaya</s>), ascertainment of demonstrating distinctions (<s>prabhidyasaṃdarśanaviniścaya</s>), ascertainment of questioning (<s>saṃpraśnaviniścaya</s>), ascertainment of inclusion (<s>saṃgrahaviniścaya</s>), ascertainment of debate (<s>vādaviniścaya</s>), and ascertainment of implicit meaning (<s>abhisandhiviniścaya</s>).

body.text: arthaviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / yatra ṣaḍarthānārabhya viniścayo bhavati // katame (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 103]

children.text: ) ṣaḍarthāḥ / svabhāvārthaḥ hetvarthaḥ phalārthaḥ karmārthaḥ yogārthaḥ vṛttyarthaśca // svabhāvārthastraṃyaḥ svabhāvāḥ // hetvarthastrayo hetavaḥ // utpattihetuḥ pravṛttihetuḥ siddhihetuśca // phalārthaḥ pañcaphalāni / vipākaphalaṃ niṣyandaphalaṃ adhipatiphalaṃ puruṣakāraphalaṃ visaṃyogaphalaṃ ca // karmārthaḥ pañca karmāṇi / upalabdhikarma kāritrakarma vyāvasāyakarma pariṇatikarma prāptikarma ca // yogārthaḥ pañca yogāḥ / sāmūhiko yogaḥ ānubandhiko yogaḥ sāṃbandhiko yogaḥ āvasthiko yogaḥ vaikāriko yogaśca // vṛttyarthaḥ pañca vṛttayaḥ / lakṣaṇavṛttiḥ avasthānavṛttiḥ viparyāsavṛttiḥ aviparyāsavṛttiḥ prabhedavṛttiśca //
children.translated_text: There are six meanings (<s>artha</s>): the meaning of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvārtha</s>), the meaning of cause (<s>hetvārtha</s>), the meaning of fruit (<s>phalārtha</s>), the meaning of action (<s>karmārtha</s>), the meaning of connection (<s>yogārtha</s>), and the meaning of function (<s>vṛttyartha</s>). The meaning of intrinsic nature: the three intrinsic natures. The meaning of cause: the three causes — the cause of arising (<s>utpattihetū</s>), the cause of continuation (<s>pravṛttihetū</s>), and the cause of accomplishment (<s>siddhihetū</s>). The meaning of fruit: the five fruits — the ripened fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>), the outflow fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>), the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>), the fruit of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>), and the fruit of disconnection (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>). The meaning of action: the five actions — the action of apprehension (<s>upalabdhikarma</s>), the action of function (<s>kāritrakarma</s>), the action of determination (<s>vyāvasāyakarma</s>), the action of transformation (<s>pariṇatikarma</s>), and the action of attainment (<s>prāptikarma</s>). The meaning of connection: the five connections — collective connection (<s>sāmūhika</s>), sequential connection (<s>ānubandhika</s>), relational connection (<s>sāṃbandhika</s>), circumstantial connection (<s>āvasthika</s>), and transformative connection (<s>vaikārika</s>). The meaning of function: the five functions — function of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇavṛtti</s>), function of abiding (<s>avasthānavṛtti</s>), function of inversion (<s>viparyāsavṛtti</s>), function of non-inversion (<s>aviparyāsavṛtti</s>), and function of classification (<s>prabhedavṛtti</s>).

body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of meaning? Where ascertainment occurs regarding six [types of] meaning. What are

body.text: vyākhyāviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / yena sūtrāntān vyācaṣṭe // sa punaḥ katamaḥ / saṃkṣepeṇa ṣaḍvidhaḥ / parijñeyavastu parijñeyo 'rthaḥ parijñopaniṣad parijñā parijñāphalam tatpravedanā ca // api khalu caturdaśa mukhāni vyākhyāviniścayasya / katamāni caturdaśa / vyākhyāsaṃgrahamukham vastusaṃgrahamukham aṅgopāṅgamukham uggarottaranirhāramukham pratikṣepamukham akṣarapariṇāmamukham nāśānāśamukham pudgalavyavasthānamukham prabhedavyavasthānamukham nayamukham parijñādimukham balā balamukham pratyāhāramukham abhinirhāramukhaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of explanation (<s>vyākhyāviniścaya</s>)? That by which one explains the <s>sūtrāntas</s>. What is it? In brief, it is sixfold: the object to be fully understood (<s>parijñeyavastu</s>), the meaning to be fully understood (<s>parijñeyārtha</s>), the prerequisite for full understanding (<s>parijñopaniṣad</s>), full understanding itself (<s>parijñā</s>), the fruit of full understanding (<s>parijñāphala</s>), and its communication (<s>pravedanā</s>). Furthermore, there are fourteen methods (<s>mukha</s>) of the ascertainment of explanation. What are the fourteen? The method of summary of explanation, the method of summary of topics, the method of limbs and sub-limbs, the method of drawing out the higher and further meaning, the method of refutation, the method of interpretation of words, the method of destruction and non-destruction, the method of establishing persons, the method of establishing classifications, the method of approach, the method beginning with full understanding, the method of strength and weakness, the method of condensation, and the method of accomplishment.

body.text: prabhidyasaṃdarśanaviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / yathānirdiṣṭeṣu skandhādiṣu dharmeṣu yathāyogamekāvacarakaḥ pūrvapadakaḥ paścātpadakaḥ dvikoṭikaḥ trikoṭikaḥ catuṣkoṭikaḥ oṃkāritaḥ prātikṣepika ityevamādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of manifold demonstration (<s>prabhedasaṃdarśanaviniścaya</s>)? With respect to the <s>dharmas</s> such as the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) and so forth as taught, as appropriate: single-domain, with a prior member, with a subsequent member, two-pointed, three-pointed, four-pointed, [answering with] 'oṃ', refutational — and so forth.

body.text: saṃpraśnaviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / aṣṭākārakāyadeśena aṣṭākārayāyadeśane ca (

children.translated_text: [<s>Abhidh-s</s> 104]

children.text: ) praśnavyākaraṇena sarvasatyamithyā viniścayaḥ / api khalu catvāraḥ saṃpraśna viniścayamārgāḥ / dūṣakaḥ pratiṣṭhāpakaḥ chedakaḥ bodhakaśca //
children.translated_text: through the answering of questions, there is the ascertainment of all truth and falsity. Furthermore, there are four paths of the ascertainment of inquiry: the refuting [path] (<s>dūṣaka</s>), the establishing [path] (<s>pratiṣṭhāpaka</s>), the cutting [path] (<s>chedaka</s>), and the enlightening [path] (<s>bodhaka</s>).

body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of inquiry (<s>saṃpraśnaviniścaya</s>)? Through the eight-aspect method of teaching the body and the eight-aspect method of teaching the path,

body.text: saṃgrahaviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / daśabhiḥ sthānaiḥ saṃgṛhīto viniścayaḥ // katamāni daśa sthānāni / kṛtyānuṣṭhānaviniścayasthānam avatāraviniścayasthānam adhimuktiviniścayasthānam yuktiviniścayasthānam sāṃkathyaviniścayasthānam prativedhaviniścayasthānam viśuddhiviniścayasthānam abhinirhārapadaprabhedaviniścayasthānam anābhogābhogamātrasarvārthasiddhiviniścayasthānaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of compilation (<s>saṃgrahaviniścaya</s>)? The ascertainment compiled through ten bases. What are the ten bases? The base of ascertainment of accomplishment of duties, the base of ascertainment of entry, the base of ascertainment of aspiration, the base of ascertainment of reasoning, the base of ascertainment of discussion, the base of ascertainment of penetration, the base of ascertainment of purification, the base of ascertainment of the classifications of the stages of accomplishment, and the base of ascertainment of the accomplishment of all aims through mere effortless effort.

body.text: vādaviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / saṃkṣepataḥ saptavidhaḥ / vādaḥ vādādhikaraṇaṃ vādādhiṣṭhānaṃ bādālaṃkāraḥ vādanigrahaḥ vādaniḥsaraṇaṃ bāde bahukarā dharmāśca //
body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of debate (<s>vādaviniścaya</s>)? In brief, it is sevenfold: debate (<s>vāda</s>), the tribunal of debate (<s>vādādhikaraṇa</s>), the basis of debate (<s>vādādhiṣṭhāna</s>), the adornment of debate (<s>vādālaṃkāra</s>), defeat in debate (<s>vādanigraha</s>), escape from debate (<s>vādaniḥsaraṇa</s>), and the <s>dharmas</s> that are helpful in debate.

body.text: prathamo vādaḥ punaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / vādaḥ pravādaḥ vivādaḥ apavādaḥ anuvāda avavāśca // vādaḥ sarvalokavacanam // pravādaḥ lokānuśruto vādaḥ / lokajñānapravādataḥ // vivādaḥ parasparaṃ viruddhayorvāde 'vasthānam // apavādaḥ parasparaṃ kopasaṃrambhapāruṣyanacanam // anuvādaḥ viśuddhajñānadarśanānukūlaḥ sāṃkathyaviniścayaḥ // avavādaḥ sattvānāṃ asamāhitacittānāṃ cittasamādhānāya samāhitacittānāṃ vimokṣalābhāya deśanāvādaḥ //
body.translated_text: The first, debate, is further sixfold: speech (<s>vāda</s>), report (<s>pravāda</s>), dispute (<s>vivāda</s>), reproach (<s>apavāda</s>), approving speech (<s>anuvāda</s>), and admonition (<s>avavāda</s>). Speech is all worldly discourse. Report is speech that is commonly heard in the world — from worldly conventional discourse. Dispute is taking a stand when two parties hold mutually opposing positions. Reproach is speaking with anger, hostility, and harshness to one another. Approving speech is the ascertainment of discussion that accords with purified knowledge and insight. Admonition is teaching-speech for the purpose of composing the minds of beings whose minds are not composed, and for the attainment of liberation for those whose minds are composed.

body.text: dvitīyaṃ vādādhikaraṇaṃ rājakulaṃ vā prajākulaṃ vā prāmāṇikānāṃ sahāyakānāṃ dharmārthakuśalānāṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇānāṃ nādasabhā vā /
body.translated_text: The second, the tribunal of debate, is either a royal court, or an assembly of the people, or an assembly of authoritative and helpful <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are skilled in <s>Dharma</s> and meaning.

body.text: tṛtīyaṃ vādādhiṣṭhānaṃ yadadhiṣṭhāya vādaḥ kriyate / saṃkṣepato dvividham / sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ ca / sādhyaṃ dvividham / svabhāvo viśeṣaśca // sādhanāni aṣṭau / pratijñā hetuḥ dṛṣṭāntaḥ upanayaḥ nigamanaṃ pratyakṣaṃ anumānaṃ āptāgamaśca // sādhyasya svabhāvaḥ ātmasvabhāvo dharmasvabhāvo vā / viśeṣaḥ ātmaviśeṣo dharmaviśeṣo vā // pratijñā sādhyasya svarucitārthasya parasaṃprāpaṇavijñāpanā / hetuḥ tasminneva sādhye apratītasyārthasya saṃpratyayanimittaṃ pratyakṣopalambhānupalambhasamākhyānam // dṛṣṭānta dṛṣṭa antena adṛṣṭāsya antasya samīkaraṇasamākhyānam // upanayaḥ śiṣṭatajjātīya rmmāpagamāya nayatvasamākhyānam // nigamanaṃ niṣṭhāgamanasamākhyānam // prasvasatprakāśābhrānto 'rthaḥ // anumānaṃ pratyakṣaśiṣṭasaṃpratyayaḥ // āptāgamaḥ taduviruddhopadeśaḥ //
body.translated_text: The third, the basis of debate, is that upon which debate is conducted. In brief, it is twofold: the thesis to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) and the proof (<s>sādhana</s>). The thesis is twofold: intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) and distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>). The proofs are eight: assertion (<s>pratijñā</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), application (<s>upanaya</s>), conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>), direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and reliable testimony (<s>āptāgama</s>). The intrinsic nature of the thesis is the intrinsic nature of the self or the intrinsic nature of the property. The distinction is the distinction of the self or the distinction of the property. An assertion is the communication to others of the meaning of the thesis that one wishes to establish. A reason is the statement of the cause for engendering conviction regarding the unaccepted meaning in that very thesis, through the statement of what is directly perceived or not perceived. An example is the statement that equates the unseen end with a seen end. An application is the statement of the method for arriving at [the conclusion regarding] the remainder of that same class. A conclusion is the statement of reaching the final determination. Direct perception is a meaning that is clear, present, and non-erroneous. Inference is conviction regarding the remainder based on direct perception. Reliable testimony is instruction that is not contradicted by those [means of knowledge].

body.text: caturtho vādālaṃkāraḥ vādādhiṣṭhāne samyagyuktibhiḥ vādasabhāyāṃ gambhīro nipuṇaśca bhavatīti vādālaṃkāra ityucyate / sa punaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / svaparasamayajñatā vākkaraṇasaṃpad vaiśaradyaṃ pratibhānaṃ sthairyaṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: The fourth, the adornment of debate, is that through which one is profound and skilled in the debate assembly by means of correct reasoning regarding the basis of debate — thus it is called the adornment of debate. It is further sixfold: knowledge of one's own and others' doctrines (<s>samaya</s>), excellence of speech, confidence (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>), steadfastness (<s>sthairya</s>), and skillful conduct (<s>dākṣiṇya</s>).

body.text: pañcamo vādanigrahaḥ kathātyāgaḥ kathāsādaḥ kathādoṣaśca // kathātyāgaḥ svāvādadoṣābhyupagamaḥ paravāaguṇābhyupagamaśca // kathāsādaḥ anyavastupratisaraṇena vyāvṛttiḥ bāhyavastuvacanena mūlaparatijñāparityāgaḥ krodhamadamānamrākṣādi pradarśanaṃ ca // yathoktaṃ sūtre / kathādoṣaḥ saṃkṣepeṇa navavidhaḥ / ākulaṃ saṃrabdham agamakam amitam anarthakam akālam asthiram apradīptam apravaddhaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: The fifth, defeat in debate, consists of: abandonment of the discussion, disgrace in the discussion, and faults in the discussion. Abandonment of the discussion is accepting the faults of one's own position and accepting the merits of the opponent's position. Disgrace in the discussion is: evasion by resorting to a different topic, abandoning one's original thesis by speaking about an external matter, and displaying anger, intoxication, pride, malice, and the like. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, the faults of discussion are, in brief, ninefold: confused, hostile, inconclusive, immeasurable, purposeless, untimely, unstable, unilluminating, and undeveloped.

body.text: ṣaṣṭhaṃ vādaniḥsaraṇaṃ guṇadoṣau vicārya vādānniḥsaratyakaraṇena vā prativādityabhājanatāṃ parṣado vaiguṇyamātmano 'kauśalyaṃ ca jñātvā vādaṃ na karoti / prativādini bhājanatāṃ parṣado guṇavattvamātmanaḥ kauśalyaṃ ca jñātvā vādaṃ karoti //
body.translated_text: The sixth, escape from debate: having examined the merits and faults, one escapes from debate by not engaging. Knowing the non-receptivity of the opponent, the deficiency of the assembly, and one's own lack of skill, one does not debate. Knowing the receptivity of the opponent, the quality of the assembly, and one's own skill, one engages in debate.

body.text: vāde bahukarā dharmāḥ samāsatastrayaḥ / svaparasamayajñatā yayā sarvatra nipuṇo vādaṃ karoti / vaiśāradyaṃ yena nipuṇaḥ samagraparṣadi vādaṃ karoti / pratimānaṃ yena nipuṇaḥ sarvāṃn kaṭhinān praśnān vyākaroti //
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> that are helpful in debate are, in brief, three: knowledge of one's own and others' doctrines, by which one debates skillfully in all [contexts]; confidence (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), by which one debates skillfully in a full assembly; and quick-wittedness (<s>pratibhāna</s>), by which one skillfully answers all difficult questions.

body.text: api khalu svahitasukha kāmena vādeṣu abhijñātuṃ pravarttitavyaṃ na paraiḥ vivādaṃ kartum / taduktaṃ bhagavatā mahāyānā bhidharmasutre / bodhisattvena vīryamārabhamāṇena kuśalapakṣaprayuktena pratipattisārakeṇa dharmānudharmacāriṇā sarvasattvasaṃgrāhakeṇa kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyak saṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyatā dvādaśasthānadharmān samanupaśyatā na paraiḥ saha vivādaḥ kāryaḥ // katame dvādaśa / anuttarārthaparamadharmadeśanāyāṃ saṃpratyayo durlabhaḥ / prāśnikānāmavavādagrāhakaṃ cittaṃ durlabham / sabhyā guṇadoṣavicārakāśca durlabhā / vāde prayuktānāṃ ṣaḍdoṣaviraho durlabhaḥ / katame ṣaṭ / asatpakṣabhiniveśadoṣaḥ kusṛtivacanadoṣaḥ akālikavākkaraṇadoṣaḥ kathāsādadoṣaḥ pārupyavacatadoṣaḥ cittāghātadoṣaśca / vāde saṃrambhābhāvo durlabhaḥ / vāde paracittānurakṣaṇaṃ durlabham / vāde anurakṣaṇe 'pi cittasamādhidurlabhaḥ / vāde cittasya nikārsaparotkarṣakāmatā durlabhā / nikarṣaparotkarṣayorapi cittasyāsaṃkleśo durlabhaḥ / saṃkliṣṭe tu citte sparśavihāro durlabhaḥ / asparśavihāre tu kuśaladharmabhāvanā durlabhā / nirantaraṃ kuśaladharme 'bhāvite tu asamāhicittasya kṣipraṃ samādhilābhaḥ samāhitacittasya vā kṣipraṃ vimokṣalābho durlabhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, one who desires one's own welfare and happiness should engage in debates in order to understand, not to dispute with others. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated in the <s>Mahāyānābhidharmasūtra</s>: 'A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who arouses energy, is engaged in the wholesome, takes practice as essential, practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, gathers all beings, and quickly and fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening — seeing these twelve points — should not dispute with others. What are the twelve? (1) Conviction in the unsurpassed and supreme <s>Dharma</s>-teaching is difficult to obtain. (2) A mind that accepts admonition is difficult to find among questioners. (3) Judges who examine merits and faults are difficult to find. (4) Freedom from six faults is difficult for those engaged in debate. What are the six? The fault of clinging to a wrong position, the fault of deceitful speech, the fault of untimely discourse, the fault of disgrace in discussion, the fault of harsh speech, and the fault of mental hostility. (5) Absence of hostility in debate is difficult. (6) Protecting the other's mind in debate is difficult. (7) Even when protecting [the other's mind], composure of one's own mind is difficult. (8) In debate, the desire to lower oneself and elevate the other is difficult. (9) Even in lowering and elevating, non-affliction of the mind is difficult. (10) When the mind is afflicted, comfortable abiding is difficult. (11) Without comfortable abiding, cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> is difficult. (12) When wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are not continuously cultivated, quick attainment of concentration for one whose mind is not composed, or quick attainment of liberation for one whose mind is composed, is difficult.'

body.text: abhisandhiviniścayaḥ katamaḥ / uktādanyo 'rthaḥ / nāmapadavyañjanakāyānāṃ channasyābhisandheḥ anyārthābhivyañjane vipariṇāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is the ascertainment of hidden intention (<s>abhisandhiviniścaya</s>)? A meaning other than what is stated — a transformation in indicating a different meaning through the hidden intention concealed within the collections of words, phrases, and syllables.

children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ hatvā rājānaṃ dvau bahuśrutau /
children.translated_text: Having slain mother and father, the king, and two learned ones,

children.text: rāṣṭraṃ sānucaraṃ hatvā naro viśuddha ucyate //
children.translated_text: having slain the kingdom together with its followers — that person is said to be pure.
And it is further stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:
One who is faithless, ungrateful, and a breaker of bonds,
one who has destroyed opportunity and vomited food — he indeed is the supreme person.
And it is further stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:
Those who perceive essence in what is without essence, and who are well-established in perversion,
and who are thoroughly afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), attain the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

body.text: api coktaṃ sūtre bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pañcabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato dānapāra mitāyāṃ kṣipraṃ paripūriṃ labhate / katame pañca / mātsaryadharmatāmanuvṛṃhayati / dānena ca parikhidyate / yācanakaṃ ca dveṣṭi / na kiṃcit kadācid dadāti / dūre ca bhavati dānasya // punaścoktaṃ sūtre / bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pañcadharmasamanvāgato brahmacārī bhavati parameṇa viśuddhena brahmacaryeṇa samanvāgataḥ // katame pañca // nānyatra maithunyānmaithunasya niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣate / maithunaprahāṇenopekṣako bhavati / utpannaṃ ca maithunarogamadhivāsayati / maithunapratipakṣeṇa ca dharmeṇottrasyati / abhīkṣṇaṃ ca dvayadvayaṃ samāpadyate //
body.translated_text: Moreover, it is stated in a <s>sūtra</s>: 'A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) endowed with five <s>dharmas</s> quickly obtains the fulfillment of the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>). What are the five? He cultivates the nature of miserliness, he grows weary of giving, he despises the one who asks, he never gives anything at any time, and he is far removed from generosity.' Furthermore, it is stated in a <s>sūtra</s>: 'A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> endowed with five <s>dharmas</s> is a celibate endowed with the supreme and pure spiritual life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). What are the five? He does not seek escape from sexual conduct except through sexual conduct itself. He remains equanimous through the abandonment of sexual conduct. He tolerates the disease of sexual desire that has arisen. He is frightened by the <s>dharma</s> that is the antidote to sexual conduct. And he repeatedly enters into the union of pairs.'

body.text: kimupādāyedaṃ śāstramabhidharmasamuccaya iti nāma labhate / saṃkṣepatastribhirarthaiḥ / sametyoccayatāmupādāya samantāduccayatāmupādāya samyaguccayatāṃ copādāya //
body.translated_text: In reference to what does this treatise obtain the name <s>Abhidharmasamuccaya</s> (Compendium of Higher Doctrine)? In brief, for three reasons: in reference to being a collection brought together (<s>sametyoccayatā</s>), in reference to being a collection from all sides (<s>samantāduccayatā</s>), and in reference to being a correct collection (<s>samyaguccayatā</s>).

body.text: (iti abhidharmasamuccaye sāṃkathyaviniścayo nāma pañcamaḥ samuccayaḥ //) //
body.translated_text: (Thus ends the fifth compendium, called the Ascertainment through Discussion (<s>Sāṃkathyaviniścaya</s>), in the <s>Abhidharmasamuccaya</s>.)
